pairs.english: And Jacob journeyed to Succoth, and he built himself a house;
and for his kine he made booths (succoth),
wherefore the place was called Succoth.

pairs.hebrew: וַיָּבֹא֩ יַעֲקֹ֨ב שָׁלֵ֜ם עִ֣יר שְׁכֶ֗ם אֲשֶׁר֙ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ כְּנַ֔עַן
pairs.english: And Jacob came complete to the city of Shchem in the land of Canaan [complete in his body (having recovered from his limp), complete in his wealth, complete in his Torah],
when he came from Padan Aram, [having emerged unscathed from his encounters with Lavan and Esau],
and he encamped before the city.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּ֜קֶן אֶת־חֶלְקַ֣ת הַשָּׂדֶ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֤ר נָֽטָה־שָׁם֙ אׇהֳל֔וֹ
pairs.english: And he bought the part of the field where he had pitched his tent

pairs.hebrew: מִיַּ֥ד בְּנֵֽי־חֲמ֖וֹר אֲבִ֣י שְׁכֶ֑ם בְּמֵאָ֖ה קְשִׂיטָֽה׃
pairs.english: from the sons of Chamor the father of Shchem for a hundred kesitah.
And he erected an altar there,
and he called it "The Almighty is the G d of Israel" (i.e., Jacob.)

pairs.hebrew: וַתֵּצֵ֤א דִינָה֙ בַּת־לֵאָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר יָלְדָ֖ה לְיַעֲקֹ֑ב
pairs.english: And Dinah the daughter of Leah ["Like mother, like daughter" — Leah also "went out" (30:16)], whom she had borne to Jacob, went out
to see the daughters of the land.

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּ֨רְא אֹתָ֜הּ שְׁכֶ֧ם בֶּן־חֲמ֛וֹר הַֽחִוִּ֖י נְשִׂ֣יא הָאָ֑רֶץ
pairs.english: And Shchem the son of Chamor, the Chivi, the prince of the land, saw her,
and he took her and he lay with her [naturally], and he afflicted her [unnaturally].
And his soul cleaved to Dinah the daughter of Jacob,
and he loved the maiden and he spoke to the heart of the maiden [by suasion].
And Shchem said to Chamor, his father:
Take this girl for me as a wife.

pairs.hebrew: וְיַעֲקֹ֣ב שָׁמַ֗ע כִּ֤י טִמֵּא֙ אֶת־דִּינָ֣ה בִתּ֔וֹ
pairs.english: And Jacob heard that he had defiled Dinah his daughter,
and his sons were with his herds in the field,
and Jacob remained silent until they came.
And Chamor the father of Shchem went out to Jacob
to speak to him.
And the sons of Jacob came from the field when they heard,
and the men were saddened and greatly angered,

pairs.hebrew: כִּֽי־נְבָלָ֞ה עָשָׂ֣ה בְיִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל לִשְׁכַּב֙ אֶת־בַּֽת־יַעֲקֹ֔ב וְכֵ֖ן לֹ֥א יֵעָשֶֽׂה׃
pairs.english: for he had done a shameful thing in Israel to lie with the daughter of Jacob, and such [(to afflict virgins)] was not to be done, [the nations having "fenced themselves" against illicit relations after the flood].

pairs.hebrew: וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר חֲמ֖וֹר אִתָּ֣ם לֵאמֹ֑ר שְׁכֶ֣ם בְּנִ֗י חָֽשְׁקָ֤ה נַפְשׁוֹ֙ בְּבִתְּכֶ֔ם
pairs.english: And Chamor spoke with them, saying: My son, Shchem, desired your daughter.
Give her to him, I pray you, as a wife.
And intermarry with us.
Give us your daughters [as you choose], and our daughters take for yourselves [as you choose].
And dwell with us and the land shall be before you.
Sit and trade in it, and gain a holding in it.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר שְׁכֶם֙ אֶל־אָבִ֣יהָ וְאֶל־אַחֶ֔יהָ אֶמְצָא־חֵ֖ן בְּעֵינֵיכֶ֑ם
pairs.english: And Shchem said to her father and to her brothers: Let me find favor in your eyes,
and what you tell me shall I give.

pairs.hebrew: הַרְבּ֨וּ עָלַ֤י מְאֹד֙ מֹ֣הַר וּמַתָּ֔ן וְאֶ֨תְּנָ֔ה כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר תֹּאמְר֖וּ אֵלָ֑י
pairs.english: Heap upon me much dowry and gift, and I will give it, as you tell me,
but give me the maiden as a wife.

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּעֲנ֨וּ בְנֵֽי־יַעֲקֹ֜ב אֶת־שְׁכֶ֨ם וְאֶת־חֲמ֥וֹר אָבִ֛יו בְּמִרְמָ֖ה וַיְדַבֵּ֑רוּ
pairs.english: And the sons of Jacob answered Shchem and Chamor his father with subtlety, and they spoke [thus rightfully],
for he had defiled Dinah their sister.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ אֲלֵיהֶ֗ם לֹ֤א נוּכַל֙ לַעֲשׂוֹת֙ הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֔ה
pairs.english: And they said to them: We shall not be able to do this thing,
to give our sister to a man with a foreskin,
for it is an abomination to us.
Only with this will we consent to you,

pairs.hebrew: אִ֚ם תִּהְי֣וּ כָמֹ֔נוּ לְהִמֹּ֥ל לָכֶ֖ם כׇּל־זָכָֽר׃
pairs.english: if you will be like us — to have all your males circumcised.
Then we will give our daughters to you [as we choose], and your daughters [i.e., those we choose] shall we take for ourselves.
And we will dwell with you and we will be one people.
And if you do not heed us to circumcise yourselves,
then we will take our daughter and go.
And their words were good in the eyes of Chamor
and in the eyes of Shchem the son of Chamor.

pairs.hebrew: וְלֹֽא־אֵחַ֤ר הַנַּ֙עַר֙ לַעֲשׂ֣וֹת הַדָּבָ֔ר כִּ֥י חָפֵ֖ץ בְּבַֽת־יַעֲקֹ֑ב
pairs.english: And the young man did not delay doing the thing, for he desired the daughter of Jacob,
and he was the most highly honored in his father's house.

pairs.hebrew: וַיָּבֹ֥א חֲמ֛וֹר וּשְׁכֶ֥ם בְּנ֖וֹ אֶל־שַׁ֣עַר עִירָ֑ם
pairs.english: And Chamor and Shchem his son came to the gate of their city
and they spoke to the men of their city, saying:

pairs.hebrew: הָאֲנָשִׁ֨ים הָאֵ֜לֶּה שְֽׁלֵמִ֧ים הֵ֣ם אִתָּ֗נוּ וְיֵשְׁב֤וּ בָאָ֙רֶץ֙ וְיִסְחֲר֣וּ אֹתָ֔הּ
pairs.english: These men are whole-hearted with us. Let them dwell in the land and trade in it;
the land is "broad-handed" [i.e., ample] before them [You will lose nothing by their presence.]

pairs.hebrew: אֶת־בְּנֹתָם֙ נִקַּֽח־לָ֣נוּ לְנָשִׁ֔ים וְאֶת־בְּנֹתֵ֖ינוּ נִתֵּ֥ן לָהֶֽם׃
pairs.english: Their daughters shall we take for ourselves as wives [by our choice], and our daughters shall we give to them [by our choice].

pairs.hebrew: אַךְ־בְּ֠זֹ֠את יֵאֹ֨תוּ לָ֤נוּ הָאֲנָשִׁים֙ לָשֶׁ֣בֶת אִתָּ֔נוּ לִהְי֖וֹת לְעַ֣ם אֶחָ֑ד
pairs.english: Only with this will the men consent to dwell with us, to be one people,

pairs.hebrew: בְּהִמּ֥וֹל לָ֙נוּ֙ כׇּל־זָכָ֔ר כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר הֵ֥ם נִמֹּלִֽים׃
pairs.english: by all of our males being circumcised as they are circumcised.

pairs.hebrew: מִקְנֵהֶ֤ם וְקִנְיָנָם֙ וְכׇל־בְּהֶמְתָּ֔ם הֲל֥וֹא לָ֖נוּ הֵ֑ם
pairs.english: Their herds, their possessions, and all of their beasts — are they not ours?
Let us but consent to them [to be circumcised], and they will dwell with us.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּשְׁמְע֤וּ אֶל־חֲמוֹר֙ וְאֶל־שְׁכֶ֣ם בְּנ֔וֹ כׇּל־יֹצְאֵ֖י שַׁ֣עַר עִיר֑וֹ
pairs.english: And they hearkened to Chamor and to Shchem his son, all that went out of the gate of his city,
and all the males were circumcised, all that went out of the gate of his city.
And it was on the third day, when they were in pain,

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּקְח֣וּ שְׁנֵֽי־בְנֵי־יַ֠עֲקֹ֠ב שִׁמְע֨וֹן וְלֵוִ֜י אֲחֵ֤י דִינָה֙ אִ֣ישׁ חַרְבּ֔וֹ
pairs.english: that two of Jacob's sons [(Though they were Jacob's sons, they did not consult him)], Shimon and Levi, the brothers of Dinah, [risking their lives for her], took each man his sword,
and came upon the city secure, [in that the men were ailing], and they killed every male.
And Chamor and Shchem his son they slew by the sword,
and they took Dinah from the house of Shchem and they went out.
The sons of Jacob came upon the slain [to strip them],
and they despoiled the city that had defiled their sister.
Their sheep, their cattle, and their asses,
and what was in the city and what was in the field they took.
And all of their possessions, and all of their little ones, and their wives, they took captive and they plundered,
and all that was in the house.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יַעֲקֹ֜ב אֶל־שִׁמְע֣וֹן וְאֶל־לֵוִי֮ עֲכַרְתֶּ֣ם אֹתִי֒ לְהַבְאִישֵׁ֙נִי֙ בְּיֹשֵׁ֣ב הָאָ֔רֶץ בַּֽכְּנַעֲנִ֖י וּבַפְּרִזִּ֑י
pairs.english: And Jacob said to Shimon and to Levi: You have sullied me, to make me odious with the inhabitant of the land, the Canaani and Perizi.
And I am but few in number,

pairs.hebrew: וְנֶאֶסְפ֤וּ עָלַי֙ וְהִכּ֔וּנִי וְנִשְׁמַדְתִּ֖י אֲנִ֥י וּבֵיתִֽי׃
pairs.english: and they will gather against me and smite me, and I will be destroyed, I and my house.
And they said:
Shall they make our sister as an abandoned one!

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֱלֹהִים֙ אֶֽל־יַעֲקֹ֔ב ק֛וּם עֲלֵ֥ה בֵֽית־אֵ֖ל וְשֶׁב־שָׁ֑ם
pairs.english: And G d said to Jacob: Arise, and go up to Bethel, [(You have been punished through your daughter for having tarried upon the way)], and abide there,
and make there an altar to the G d who appeared to you
when you fled from Esau your brother.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יַעֲקֹב֙ אֶל־בֵּית֔וֹ וְאֶ֖ל כׇּל־אֲשֶׁ֣ר עִמּ֑וֹ
pairs.english: And Jacob said to his household and to all who were with him:
Remove the strange gods that are with you [from the spoil of Shchem]
and cleanse yourselves [of idolatry], and change your garments, [lest you have a vestment devoted to idolatry].
And let us arise and go up to Bethel,

pairs.hebrew: וְאֶֽעֱשֶׂה־שָּׁ֣ם מִזְבֵּ֗חַ לָאֵ֞ל הָעֹנֶ֤ה אֹתִי֙ בְּי֣וֹם צָֽרָתִ֔י
pairs.english: and I will make an altar there to the G d who answered me in the day of my affliction
and who was with me in the way in which I went.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּתְּנ֣וּ אֶֽל־יַעֲקֹ֗ב אֵ֣ת כׇּל־אֱלֹהֵ֤י הַנֵּכָר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּיָדָ֔ם
pairs.english: And they gave to Jacob all the strange gods which were in their hands
and the rings which were in their ears,

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּטְמֹ֤ן אֹתָם֙ יַעֲקֹ֔ב תַּ֥חַת הָאֵלָ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר עִם־שְׁכֶֽם׃
pairs.english: and Jacob buried them under the terebinth near Shchem.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּסָּ֑עוּ וַיְהִ֣י ׀ חִתַּ֣ת אֱלֹהִ֗ים עַל־הֶֽעָרִים֙ אֲשֶׁר֙ סְבִיב֣וֹתֵיהֶ֔ם
pairs.english: And they journeyed, and the terror of G d was on the cities around them,
and they did not pursue the sons of Jacob.

pairs.hebrew: וַיָּבֹ֨א יַעֲקֹ֜ב ל֗וּזָה אֲשֶׁר֙ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ כְּנַ֔עַן הִ֖וא בֵּֽית־אֵ֑ל
pairs.english: And Jacob came to Luz in the land of Canaan (the same as Bethel),
he and all the people that were with him.
And he built an altar there,
and he called the place "The Almighty is in Bethel";

pairs.hebrew: כִּ֣י שָׁ֗ם נִגְל֤וּ אֵלָיו֙ הָֽאֱלֹהִ֔ים בְּבׇרְח֖וֹ מִפְּנֵ֥י אָחִֽיו׃
pairs.english: for G d had revealed Himself to him there when he fled from his brother.
And Devorah, Rivkah's nurse, [(whom Rivkah had sent to Padan Aram to tell Jacob to return)], died.
And she was buried beneath Bethel, [i.e., at the foot of the mountain on which Bethel was built], on the slope terrace;
and he called its name Alon Bachuth ("the plain of weeping").

pairs.hebrew: וַיֵּרָ֨א אֱלֹהִ֤ים אֶֽל־יַעֲקֹב֙ ע֔וֹד בְּבֹא֖וֹ מִפַּדַּ֣ן אֲרָ֑ם
pairs.english: And G d appeared to Jacob again, [a second time in this place (once in his going; the other, in his returning)] when he came from Padan Aram,
and He blessed him [(the mourners' blessing)].
And G d said to him: Your name — Jacob —

pairs.hebrew: לֹֽא־יִקָּרֵא֩ שִׁמְךָ֨ ע֜וֹד יַעֲקֹ֗ב כִּ֤י אִם־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ יִהְיֶ֣ה שְׁמֶ֔ךָ
pairs.english: your name shall no longer be called "Jacob" [connoting deviousness], but "Yisrael" [connoting lordship] shall be your name;
and He called his name Yisrael.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֩אמֶר֩ ל֨וֹ אֱלֹהִ֜ים אֲנִ֨י אֵ֤ל שַׁדַּי֙ פְּרֵ֣ה וּרְבֵ֔ה
pairs.english: And He said to him: I am the G d Shaddai [It becomes Me (ani kedai) to bless, all blessings being Mine]: Be fruitful and multiply [(Benjamin had not yet been born)].
A nation [Benjamin] and a congregation of nations [Menasheh and Ephraim] shall come forth from you;
and kings [Saul and Ish Bosheth (of the tribe of Benjamin)] shall issue forth from your loins.

pairs.hebrew: וְאֶת־הָאָ֗רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֥ר נָתַ֛תִּי לְאַבְרָהָ֥ם וּלְיִצְחָ֖ק לְךָ֣ אֶתְּנֶ֑נָּה
pairs.english: And the land that I gave to Abraham and to Isaac, to you will I give it,
and to your seed after you will I give the land.
And G d ascended from (over) him
in the place where He spoke with him.

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּצֵּ֨ב יַעֲקֹ֜ב מַצֵּבָ֗ה בַּמָּק֛וֹם אֲשֶׁר־דִּבֶּ֥ר אִתּ֖וֹ מַצֶּ֣בֶת אָ֑בֶן
pairs.english: And Jacob set up a monument in the place where He spoke with him, a monument of stone,
and he poured a libation thereon,
and he poured oil thereon.
And Jacob called the name of the place

pairs.hebrew: אֲשֶׁר֩ דִּבֶּ֨ר אִתּ֥וֹ שָׁ֛ם אֱלֹהִ֖ים בֵּֽית־אֵֽל׃
pairs.english: where G d spoke with him Bethel.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּסְעוּ֙ מִבֵּ֣ית אֵ֔ל וַֽיְהִי־ע֥וֹד כִּבְרַת־הָאָ֖רֶץ לָב֣וֹא אֶפְרָ֑תָה
pairs.english: And they traveled from Bethel, and there was yet a kivrah of land to come to Efrath,
when Rachel gave birth, travailing in labor.
And it was, as she travailed in labor,

pairs.hebrew: וַתֹּ֨אמֶר לָ֤הּ הַמְיַלֶּ֙דֶת֙ אַל־תִּ֣ירְאִ֔י כִּֽי־גַם־זֶ֥ה לָ֖ךְ בֵּֽן׃
pairs.english: that the midwife said to her: Do not fear, for this, too [in addition to Joseph], is a son for you.

pairs.hebrew: וַיְהִ֞י בְּצֵ֤את נַפְשָׁהּ֙ כִּ֣י מֵ֔תָה וַתִּקְרָ֥א שְׁמ֖וֹ בֶּן־אוֹנִ֑י
pairs.english: And it was, as her soul departed in death, that she called his name Ben Oni ["son of my travail"];
and his father called him Binyamin ["son of the south," (Canaan, where he was born, being south of Aram Naharayim, whence Jacob had come)].
And Rachel died,

pairs.hebrew: וַתִּקָּבֵר֙ בְּדֶ֣רֶךְ אֶפְרָ֔תָה הִ֖וא בֵּ֥ית לָֽחֶם׃
pairs.english: and she was buried on the way to Efrath, which is Bethlehem.
And Jacob set a monument upon her grave,
the monument of Rachel's grave until this day.
And Israel journeyed
and he pitched his tent beyond Migdal Eder.
And it was, when Israel dwelt in that land, [delaying coming to his father Isaac in Chevron],

pairs.hebrew: וַיֵּ֣לֶךְ רְאוּבֵ֗֔ן וַיִּשְׁכַּ֕ב֙ אֶת־בִּלְהָ֖ה֙ פִּילֶ֣גֶשׁ אָבִ֑֔יו וַיִּשְׁמַ֖ע יִשְׂרָאֵ֑͏ֽל׃ {פ}
pairs.english: that Reuven went and lay with Bilhah, his father's concubine, and Israel heard;
and the sons of Jacob [after the birth of Benjamin] were twelve [the full complement of the tribes].
The sons of Leah: the first-born of Jacob, Reuven [first-born in respect to inheritance, Divine service, and numeration (of the tribes)],
Shimon, Levi, Judah, Issachar and Zevulun.
The sons of Rachel,
Joseph and Benjamin.
And the sons of Bilhah, the handmaid of Rachel,
Dan and Naftali.

pairs.hebrew: וּבְנֵ֥י זִלְפָּ֛ה שִׁפְחַ֥ת לֵאָ֖ה גָּ֣ד וְאָשֵׁ֑ר
pairs.english: And the sons of Zilpah, the handmaid of Leah, Gad and Asher.

pairs.hebrew: אֵ֚לֶּה בְּנֵ֣י יַעֲקֹ֔ב אֲשֶׁ֥ר יֻלַּד־ל֖וֹ בְּפַדַּ֥ן אֲרָֽם׃
pairs.english: These are the sons of Jacob, who were born to him in Padan Aram.

pairs.hebrew: וַיָּבֹ֤א יַעֲקֹב֙ אֶל־יִצְחָ֣ק אָבִ֔יו מַמְרֵ֖א קִרְיַ֣ת הָֽאַרְבַּ֑ע הִ֣וא חֶבְר֔וֹן
pairs.english: And Jacob came to Isaac his father, to [the plain of] Mamre, [to the city of] Kiryath Ha'Arba, which is Chevron,
where Abraham and Isaac lived.
And the days of Isaac were
a hundred and eighty years.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּגְוַ֨ע יִצְחָ֤ק וַיָּ֙מׇת֙ וַיֵּאָ֣סֶף אֶל־עַמָּ֔יו זָקֵ֖ן וּשְׂבַ֣ע יָמִ֑ים
pairs.english: And Isaac expired and he died, and he was gathered to his people, old and sated with days.
And Esau and Jacob his sons buried him.
And these are the progeny of Esau,
who is Edom:
Esau took his wives from the daughters of Canaan:
Adah, the daughter of Elon the Chitti [same as Basmath (26:34)]
and Ahalivamah [same as Yehudith (Ibid.)], the daughter of Anah, the daughter of Tzivon, the Chivi [i.e., the daughter of Tzivon by the wife of his son Anah (see 36:24)].
And Basmath the daughter of Ishmael [same as Machlath (38:9)],
the sister of Nevayoth, [thus referred to here because Nevayoth gave her in marriage after Ishmael's death].
And Adah bore to Esau, Elifaz;
and Basmath bore Reuel.
And Ahalivamah bore Yeush and Ya'alam and Korach.

pairs.hebrew: אֵ֚לֶּה בְּנֵ֣י עֵשָׂ֔ו אֲשֶׁ֥ר יֻלְּדוּ־ל֖וֹ בְּאֶ֥רֶץ כְּנָֽעַן׃
pairs.english: These are the sons of Esau who were born to him in the land of Canaan.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּקַּ֣ח עֵשָׂ֡ו אֶת־נָ֠שָׁ֠יו וְאֶת־בָּנָ֣יו וְאֶת־בְּנֹתָיו֮ וְאֶת־כׇּל־נַפְשׁ֣וֹת בֵּיתוֹ֒
pairs.english: And Esau took his wives and his sons and his daughters and all the souls of his house,

pairs.hebrew: וְאֶת־מִקְנֵ֣הוּ וְאֶת־כׇּל־בְּהֶמְתּ֗וֹ וְאֵת֙ כׇּל־קִנְיָנ֔וֹ אֲשֶׁ֥ר רָכַ֖שׁ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ כְּנָ֑עַן
pairs.english: and his herds and all of his beasts, and all of his possessions which he had acquired in the land of Canaan,
and he went to a land [i.e., to live wherever he could find room] away from Jacob his brother.
For their possessions were too great to (allow them to) remain together,

pairs.hebrew: וְלֹ֨א יָֽכְלָ֜ה אֶ֤רֶץ מְגֽוּרֵיהֶם֙ לָשֵׂ֣את אֹתָ֔ם מִפְּנֵ֖י מִקְנֵיהֶֽם׃
pairs.english: and the land of their sojourning could not contain them because of [the pasture land required for] their cattle.
And Esau dwelt in Mount Seir.
Esau is Edom.
And these are the generations of Esau the father of Edom, [which his sons begot]
in [i.e., after he went to] the mountain of Seir.
These are the names of the sons of Esau:
Elifaz, the son of Adah, the wife of Esau;
Reuel, the son of Basmath, the wife of Esau.
And the sons of Elifaz were
Teman, Omar, Tz'fo, Ga'atam, and Kenaz.

pairs.hebrew: וְתִמְנַ֣ע ׀ הָיְתָ֣ה פִילֶ֗גֶשׁ לֶֽאֱלִיפַז֙ בֶּן־עֵשָׂ֔ו וַתֵּ֥לֶד לֶאֱלִיפַ֖ז אֶת־עֲמָלֵ֑ק
pairs.english: And Timna was concubine to Elifaz the son of Esau, and she bore to Elifaz, Amalek.
These are the sons of Adah, the wife of Esau.

pairs.hebrew: וְאֵ֙לֶּה֙ בְּנֵ֣י רְעוּאֵ֔ל נַ֥חַת וָזֶ֖רַח שַׁמָּ֣ה וּמִזָּ֑ה
pairs.english: And these are the sons of Reuel: Nachath and Zerach, Shammah and Mizzah.

pairs.hebrew: אֵ֣לֶּה הָי֔וּ בְּנֵ֥י בָשְׂמַ֖ת אֵ֥שֶׁת עֵשָֽׂו׃
pairs.english: These were the sons of Basmath, the wife of Esau.

pairs.hebrew: וְאֵ֣לֶּה הָי֗וּ בְּנֵ֨י אׇהֳלִיבָמָ֧ה בַת־עֲנָ֛ה בַּת־צִבְע֖וֹן אֵ֣שֶׁת עֵשָׂ֑ו
pairs.english: And these were the sons of Ahalivamah the daughter of Anah the daughter of Tzivon, the wife of Esau.
She bore to Esau Yeush and Ya'alam and Korach.
These are the chiefs [i.e., the heads of families] of the sons of Esau.
The sons of Elifaz, the first-born of Esau:

pairs.hebrew: אַלּ֤וּף תֵּימָן֙ אַלּ֣וּף אוֹמָ֔ר אַלּ֥וּף צְפ֖וֹ אַלּ֥וּף קְנַֽז׃
pairs.english: Chief Teman, Chief Omar, Chief Tzefo, Chief Kenaz.
Chief Korach, Chief Ga'atam, Chief Amalek.

pairs.hebrew: אֵ֣לֶּה אַלּוּפֵ֤י אֱלִיפַז֙ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ אֱד֔וֹם אֵ֖לֶּה בְּנֵ֥י עָדָֽה׃
pairs.english: These are the chiefs of Elifaz in the land of Edom. These are the sons of Adah.

pairs.hebrew: וְאֵ֗לֶּה בְּנֵ֤י רְעוּאֵל֙ בֶּן־עֵשָׂ֔ו אַלּ֥וּף נַ֙חַת֙ אַלּ֣וּף זֶ֔רַח אַלּ֥וּף שַׁמָּ֖ה אַלּ֣וּף מִזָּ֑ה
pairs.english: And these are the sons of Reuel the son of Esau: Chief Nachath, Chief Zerach, Chief Shammah, Chief Mizzah.
These are the chiefs of Reuel in the land of Edom.
These are the sons of Basmath, the wife of Esau.
And these are the sons of Ahalivamah the wife of Esau:

pairs.hebrew: אַלּ֥וּף יְע֛וּשׁ אַלּ֥וּף יַעְלָ֖ם אַלּ֣וּף קֹ֑רַח
pairs.english: Chief Yeush, Chief Ya'alam, Chief Korach.

pairs.hebrew: אֵ֣לֶּה אַלּוּפֵ֞י אׇהֳלִֽיבָמָ֛ה בַּת־עֲנָ֖ה אֵ֥שֶׁת עֵשָֽׂו׃
pairs.english: These are the chiefs of Ahalivamah the daughter of Anah the wife of Esau.
These are the sons of Esau, and these are their chiefs.
He is Edom.
These are the sons of Seir the Chori, the inhabitants of the land [before Esau came there]:
Lotan, Shoval, Tzivon, and Anah.
And Dishon and Etzer and Dishan.

pairs.hebrew: אֵ֣לֶּה אַלּוּפֵ֧י הַחֹרִ֛י בְּנֵ֥י שֵׂעִ֖יר בְּאֶ֥רֶץ אֱדֽוֹם׃
pairs.english: These are the chiefs of the Chori, the sons of Seir in the land of Edom.
And the sons of Lotan were Chori and Hemam,
and the sister of Lotan [by his mother, but not by his father, Seir (20)] was Timna.
And these are the sons of Shoval:
Alvan and Manachath and Eval, Shefo and Onam.
And these are the sons of Tzivon: Ayah and Anah.

pairs.hebrew: ה֣וּא עֲנָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר מָצָ֤א אֶת־הַיֵּמִם֙ בַּמִּדְבָּ֔ר
pairs.english: This is the Anah [mentioned above (20) as the brother of Tzivon (Tzivon lived with his mother and begot Anah)], who "found" the yemim [(lit., "fearful ones," white mules, whose kick is dreaded)], in the desert
when he grazed [i.e., mated] the asses belonging to Tzivon his father [with horses. (Being a bastard, he gendered bastards.)]
And these are the children of Anah: Dishon
and Ahalivamah the daughter of Anah.
And these are the sons of Dishan:
Chemdan, Eshban, Yithran, and Ch'ran.
These are the sons of Etzer:
Bilhan, Za'avan, and Akkan.
These are the sons of Dishan:
Utz and Aran.
These are the chiefs of the Chori:

pairs.hebrew: אַלּ֤וּף לוֹטָן֙ אַלּ֣וּף שׁוֹבָ֔ל אַלּ֥וּף צִבְע֖וֹן אַלּ֥וּף עֲנָֽה׃
pairs.english: Chief Lotan, Chief Shoval, Chief Tzivon, Chief Anah.

pairs.hebrew: אַלּ֥וּף דִּשֹׁ֛ן אַלּ֥וּף אֵ֖צֶר אַלּ֣וּף דִּישָׁ֑ן
pairs.english: Chief Dishon, Chief Etzer, Chief Dishan.

pairs.hebrew: אֵ֣לֶּה אַלּוּפֵ֧י הַחֹרִ֛י לְאַלֻּפֵיהֶ֖ם בְּאֶ֥רֶץ שֵׂעִֽיר׃ {פ}
pairs.english: These are the chiefs of the Chori according to their chiefs in the land of Seir.

pairs.hebrew: וְאֵ֙לֶּה֙ הַמְּלָכִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר מָלְכ֖וּ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ אֱד֑וֹם
pairs.english: And these are the kings that reigned in the land of Edom
before a king reigned over the children of Israel.
And there reigned in Edom Bela the son of Be'or;
and the name of his city was Dinhavah.
And Bala died,
and there reigned in his stead Yovav the son of Zerach from Batzrah [a Moavite city].
And Yovav died,
and there reigned in his stead Chisham from the land of the Temani.
And Chusham died,

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּמְלֹ֨ךְ תַּחְתָּ֜יו הֲדַ֣ד בֶּן־בְּדַ֗ד הַמַּכֶּ֤ה אֶת־מִדְיָן֙ בִּשְׂדֵ֣ה מוֹאָ֔ב
pairs.english: and there reigned in his stead Haddad the son of Bedad, who smote Midian in the field of Moav, [Edom joining forces with Moav against Midian].
And the name of his city was Avith.
And Haddad died,
and there reigned in his stead Samlah from Masrekah.
And Samlah died,
and there reigned in his stead Shaul from Rechovoth Hanahar.
And Shaul died,
and there reigned in his stead Bal Chanan the son of Achbor.

pairs.hebrew: וַיָּ֘מׇת֮ בַּ֣עַל חָנָ֣ן בֶּן־עַכְבּוֹר֒ וַיִּמְלֹ֤ךְ תַּחְתָּיו֙ הֲדַ֔ר
pairs.english: And Bal Chanan the son of Achbor died, and there reigned in his stead Haddad.
And the name of his city was Pau;

pairs.hebrew: וְשֵׁ֨ם אִשְׁתּ֤וֹ מְהֵֽיטַבְאֵל֙ בַּת־מַטְרֵ֔ד בַּ֖ת מֵ֥י זָהָֽב׃
pairs.english: and the name of his wife was Mehetavel the daughter of Matred, the daughter of Mei Zahav [= mahu zahav — "Of what value is gold?" (gold being of no significance to him in the enormity of his wealth)].

pairs.hebrew: וְ֠אֵ֠לֶּה שְׁמ֞וֹת אַלּוּפֵ֤י עֵשָׂו֙ לְמִשְׁפְּחֹתָ֔ם לִמְקֹמֹתָ֖ם בִּשְׁמֹתָ֑ם
pairs.english: And these are the names of the chiefs of Esau, according to their families, after their places by their [the places'] names [the kingship having ended with Haddad]:

pairs.hebrew: אַלּ֥וּף תִּמְנָ֛ע אַלּ֥וּף עַֽלְוָ֖ה אַלּ֥וּף יְתֵֽת׃
pairs.english: the chief of Timna, the chief of Avlah, the chief of Yetheth.
Chief Ahalivamah,
Chief Elah, Chief Pinon.
Chief Kenaz,
Chief Teman, Chief Mivtzar.
Chief Magdiel [Rome], Chief Iram.

pairs.hebrew: אֵ֣לֶּה ׀ אַלּוּפֵ֣י אֱד֗וֹם לְמֹֽשְׁבֹתָם֙ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ אֲחֻזָּתָ֔ם
pairs.english: These are the chiefs of Edom by their habitations in the land of their holding.
This is Esau the father of Edom.
And Jacob dwelt in the land of his father's sojournings,
in the land of Canaan.
[And] these [(following the abbreviated chronicles of Esau)] are the [habitations and wanderings of the] generations of Jacob [until they came to a permanent settlement]:

pairs.hebrew: יוֹסֵ֞ף בֶּן־שְׁבַֽע־עֶשְׂרֵ֤ה שָׁנָה֙ הָיָ֨ה רֹעֶ֤ה אֶת־אֶחָיו֙ בַּצֹּ֔אן
pairs.english: Joseph, when he was seventeen years old, grazed the flock with his brothers.

pairs.hebrew: וְה֣וּא נַ֗עַר אֶת־בְּנֵ֥י בִלְהָ֛ה וְאֶת־בְּנֵ֥י זִלְפָּ֖ה נְשֵׁ֣י אָבִ֑יו
pairs.english: And he was a lad [He would do callow things, preening and primping himself], (associating) with the sons of Bilhah and the sons of Zilpah, the wives of his father. [His brothers scorned them, and he befriended them.]
And Joseph brought evil report of them [the sons of Leah] to their father.

pairs.hebrew: וְיִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל אָהַ֤ב אֶת־יוֹסֵף֙ מִכׇּל־בָּנָ֔יו כִּֽי־בֶן־זְקֻנִ֥ים ה֖וּא ל֑וֹ
pairs.english: And Israel loved Joseph more than all his sons, for he was the son of his old age.
And he made him a robe of fine wool.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּרְא֣וּ אֶחָ֗יו כִּֽי־אֹת֞וֹ אָהַ֤ב אֲבִיהֶם֙ מִכׇּל־אֶחָ֔יו
pairs.english: And his brothers saw that his father loved him more than all his brothers,

pairs.hebrew: וַֽיִּשְׂנְא֖וּ אֹת֑וֹ וְלֹ֥א יָכְל֖וּ דַּבְּר֥וֹ לְשָׁלֹֽם׃
pairs.english: and they [being "one in mouth and one in heart"] could not speak peaceably to him.
And Joseph dreamed a dream and he told (the dream) to his brothers,
and they hated him even more.
And he said to them:
Hear, I pray you, this dream which I have dreamed.

pairs.hebrew: וְ֠הִנֵּ֠ה אֲנַ֜חְנוּ מְאַלְּמִ֤ים אֲלֻמִּים֙ בְּת֣וֹךְ הַשָּׂדֶ֔ה
pairs.english: And, behold, we were binding sheaves in the midst of the field,
and, behold, my sheaf arose and remained standing,
and behold, your sheaves surrounded it and bowed down to my sheaf.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֤אמְרוּ לוֹ֙ אֶחָ֔יו הֲמָלֹ֤ךְ תִּמְלֹךְ֙ עָלֵ֔ינוּ
pairs.english: And his brothers said to him: Will you reign over us?
Will you rule over us?

pairs.hebrew: וַיּוֹסִ֤פוּ עוֹד֙ שְׂנֹ֣א אֹת֔וֹ עַל־חֲלֹמֹתָ֖יו וְעַל־דְּבָרָֽיו׃
pairs.english: And they hated him even more for his dreams and for his words [the evil report (2)].

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּחֲלֹ֥ם עוֹד֙ חֲל֣וֹם אַחֵ֔ר וַיְסַפֵּ֥ר אֹת֖וֹ לְאֶחָ֑יו
pairs.english: And he dreamed another dream, and he told it to his brothers,
and he said: Behold, I have dreamed another dream,

pairs.hebrew: וְהִנֵּ֧ה הַשֶּׁ֣מֶשׁ וְהַיָּרֵ֗חַ וְאַחַ֤ד עָשָׂר֙ כּֽוֹכָבִ֔ים מִֽשְׁתַּחֲוִ֖ים לִֽי׃
pairs.english: and, behold, the sun and the moon and eleven stars bowing down to me.
And he told it to his father and to his brothers [together, after having told it to his brothers]. And his father rebuked him [for arousing hatred to himself]

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ל֔וֹ מָ֛ה הַחֲל֥וֹם הַזֶּ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר חָלָ֑מְתָּ
pairs.english: and he said to him: What is this dream which you have dreamed?

pairs.hebrew: הֲב֣וֹא נָב֗וֹא אֲנִי֙ וְאִמְּךָ֣ וְאַחֶ֔יךָ לְהִשְׁתַּחֲוֺ֥ת לְךָ֖ אָֽרְצָה׃
pairs.english: Shall I and your mother and your brothers come to bow down to you to the earth? [i.e., How can this be if your mother is dead! (Jacob not knowing that it would be fulfilled through Bilhah, who had reared Joseph as a mother.)]
And his brothers envied him,
and his father awaited the [materialization of] the thing.
And his brothers went
to graze their father's flock in Shchem.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל אֶל־יוֹסֵ֗ף הֲל֤וֹא אַחֶ֙יךָ֙ רֹעִ֣ים בִּשְׁכֶ֔ם
pairs.english: And Israel said to Joseph: Are your brothers not grazing in Shchem?
Go, and I will send you to them.
And he said to him: I am here [at your service (though knowing that his brothers hated him)].

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ל֗וֹ לֶךְ־נָ֨א רְאֵ֜ה אֶת־שְׁל֤וֹם אַחֶ֙יךָ֙ וְאֶת־שְׁל֣וֹם הַצֹּ֔אן וַהֲשִׁבֵ֖נִי דָּבָ֑ר
pairs.english: And he said to him: Go now, and see how your brothers fare and how the flock fares, and return word to me.
And he sent him from [i.e., towards realization of] the deep [counsel of the one (Abraham) buried in] Chevron, [viz. (15:13): "For your seed shall be a stranger, etc."],
and he came to Shchem.
And a man [the angel Gabriel] found him, and, behold, he was straying in the field.
And the man asked him: What are you seeking?
And he said: I am seeking my brothers;
tell me, I pray you, where they are grazing.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר הָאִישׁ֙ נָסְע֣וּ מִזֶּ֔ה כִּ֤י שָׁמַ֙עְתִּי֙ אֹֽמְרִ֔ים נֵלְכָ֖ה דֹּתָ֑יְנָה
pairs.english: And the man said: They have departed from this [i.e., from brotherhood]. For I heard them saying: Let us go to Dothan.
And Joseph went after his brothers,
and he found them in Dothan.
And they saw him from afar.

pairs.hebrew: וּבְטֶ֙רֶם֙ יִקְרַ֣ב אֲלֵיהֶ֔ם וַיִּֽתְנַכְּל֥וּ אֹת֖וֹ לַהֲמִיתֽוֹ׃
pairs.english: And before he approached them they schemed against him to put him to death.
And each said to the other:
Behold, this dreamer of dreams is coming.

pairs.hebrew: וְעַתָּ֣ה ׀ לְכ֣וּ וְנַֽהַרְגֵ֗הוּ וְנַשְׁלִכֵ֙הוּ֙ בְּאַחַ֣ד הַבֹּר֔וֹת
pairs.english: And now, let us go to slay him, and let us cast him in one of the pits.
And we will say: An evil beast devoured him,
and [(the Holy Spirit thus saying)]: We will see what will be his dreams [i.e., whether your words will be fulfilled or Mine].
And Reuven heard and he rescued him from their hand,
saying: Let us not strike him a death blow.
And Reuven said to them: Do not spill blood.

pairs.hebrew: הַשְׁלִ֣יכוּ אֹת֗וֹ אֶל־הַבּ֤וֹר הַזֶּה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בַּמִּדְבָּ֔ר וְיָ֖ד אַל־תִּשְׁלְחוּ־ב֑וֹ
pairs.english: Cast him into this pit, which is in the desert, but do not send a hand against him, [Reuven saying this (thus the testimony of the Holy Spirit)]

pairs.hebrew: לְמַ֗עַן הַצִּ֤יל אֹתוֹ֙ מִיָּדָ֔ם לַהֲשִׁיב֖וֹ אֶל־אָבִֽיו׃
pairs.english: in order to rescue him from their hands, to return him to his father.
And it was, when Joseph came to his brothers,

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּפְשִׁ֤יטוּ אֶת־יוֹסֵף֙ אֶת־כֻּתׇּנְתּ֔וֹ אֶת־כְּתֹ֥נֶת הַפַּסִּ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָלָֽיו׃
pairs.english: that they stripped Joseph of his robe, the robe of fine wool that was upon him.
And they took him and cast him into a pit,
and the pit was empty; there was no water in it, [but there were snakes and scorpions in it.]
And they sat down to eat bread,

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּשְׂא֤וּ עֵֽינֵיהֶם֙ וַיִּרְא֔וּ וְהִנֵּה֙ אֹרְחַ֣ת יִשְׁמְעֵאלִ֔ים בָּאָ֖ה מִגִּלְעָ֑ד
pairs.english: and they lifted their eyes and they saw, and, behold, a caravan of Ishmaelites coming from Gilead,

pairs.hebrew: וּגְמַלֵּיהֶ֣ם נֹֽשְׂאִ֗ים נְכֹאת֙ וּצְרִ֣י וָלֹ֔ט הוֹלְכִ֖ים לְהוֹרִ֥יד מִצְרָֽיְמָה׃
pairs.english: and their camels laden with spicery, balm, and laudanum [(rather than the usual foul-smelling load — providentially, for Joseph's benefit)], going to take it down to Egypt.
And Judah said to his brothers:

pairs.hebrew: מַה־בֶּ֗צַע כִּ֤י נַהֲרֹג֙ אֶת־אָחִ֔ינוּ וְכִסִּ֖ינוּ אֶת־דָּמֽוֹ׃
pairs.english: What [monetary] profit if we kill our brother and conceal his death?

pairs.hebrew: לְכ֞וּ וְנִמְכְּרֶ֣נּוּ לַיִּשְׁמְעֵאלִ֗ים וְיָדֵ֙נוּ֙ אַל־תְּהִי־ב֔וֹ כִּֽי־אָחִ֥ינוּ בְשָׂרֵ֖נוּ ה֑וּא
pairs.english: Let us go and sell him to the Ishmaelites, and let our hand not be against him, for he is our brother, our flesh;
and his brothers acquiesced.
And Midianite merchants passed by;
and they [Joseph's brothers] pulled and raised Joseph out of the pit,

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּמְכְּר֧וּ אֶת־יוֹסֵ֛ף לַיִּשְׁמְעֵאלִ֖ים בְּעֶשְׂרִ֣ים כָּ֑סֶף וַיָּבִ֥יאוּ אֶת־יוֹסֵ֖ף מִצְרָֽיְמָה׃
pairs.english: and they sold Joseph to the Ishmaelites for twenty pieces of silver [and the Ishmaelites sold him to the Midianites] and they brought Joseph to Egypt.

pairs.hebrew: וַיָּ֤שׇׁב רְאוּבֵן֙ אֶל־הַבּ֔וֹר וְהִנֵּ֥ה אֵין־יוֹסֵ֖ף בַּבּ֑וֹר
pairs.english: And Reuven returned to the pit, [it having been his day to pay attendance upon his father], and, behold, Joseph was not in the pit,
and he rent his garments.
And he returned to his brothers and he said:
The youth is not here, and I, where shall I come? [i.e., Whither shall I flee from my father's grief?]
And they took Joseph's robe,

pairs.hebrew: וַֽיִּשְׁחֲטוּ֙ שְׂעִ֣יר עִזִּ֔ים וַיִּטְבְּל֥וּ אֶת־הַכֻּתֹּ֖נֶת בַּדָּֽם׃
pairs.english: and they slaughtered a kid of goats, [whose blood is similar to a man's], and they dipped the robe in the blood.
And they sent the robe of fine wool and they brought it to their father.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּאמְר֖וּ זֹ֣את מָצָ֑אנוּ הַכֶּר־נָ֗א הַכְּתֹ֧נֶת בִּנְךָ֛ הִ֖וא אִם־לֹֽא׃
pairs.english: And they said: This we found. Recognize, now, whether or not it is your son's robe.
And he recognized it, and he said: The robe of my son.

pairs.hebrew: חַיָּ֥ה רָעָ֖ה אֲכָלָ֑תְהוּ טָרֹ֥ף טֹרַ֖ף יוֹסֵֽף׃
pairs.english: A wild beast has devoured him; Joseph has been torn.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּקְרַ֤ע יַעֲקֹב֙ שִׂמְלֹתָ֔יו וַיָּ֥שֶׂם שַׂ֖ק בְּמׇתְנָ֑יו
pairs.english: And Jacob rent his garments and placed sackcloth on his loins,
and he mourned his son many days [twenty-two years].
And all his sons and all his daughters arose to console him [(one view: a twin girl was born with each son, and each married a step-sister. Another view: "daughters" here are daughters-in-law)].
And he refused to be consoled, [consolation not "taking" for a living person who is thought dead.]
And he said: For I will go down to the grave mourning over my son.
And his father [Isaac] bewept him [Jacob (for his grieving)].
And the Medanites sold him to Egypt
to Potiphar, an officer of Pharaoh, head of the slaughterers.

pairs.hebrew: וַֽיְהִי֙ בָּעֵ֣ת הַהִ֔וא וַיֵּ֥רֶד יְהוּדָ֖ה מֵאֵ֣ת אֶחָ֑יו
pairs.english: And it was at that time that Judah was brought down [from his greatness] by his brothers [(When they beheld their father's grief, they said to him: You told us to sell him; if you had told us to return him, we would have heeded you)],
and he turned [away from his brothers] to [partnership with] an Adulamite man by the name of Chirah.

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּרְא־שָׁ֧ם יְהוּדָ֛ה בַּת־אִ֥ישׁ כְּנַעֲנִ֖י וּשְׁמ֣וֹ שׁ֑וּעַ
pairs.english: And Judah saw there the daughter of a merchant by the name of Shua.
And he took her and lived with her.
And she conceived and she bore a son
and he called his name Er.
And she conceived again and she bore a son
and she called his name Onan.

pairs.hebrew: וַתֹּ֤סֶף עוֹד֙ וַתֵּ֣לֶד בֵּ֔ן וַתִּקְרָ֥א אֶת־שְׁמ֖וֹ שֵׁלָ֑ה
pairs.english: And she again bore a son and she called him Shelah.
And he was in Keziv ["cessation" (from bearing)] when she bore him.
And Judah took a wife for Er, his first-born,
whose name was Tamar.

pairs.hebrew: וַיְהִ֗י עֵ֚ר בְּכ֣וֹר יְהוּדָ֔ה רַ֖ע בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהֹוָ֑ה
pairs.english: And Er, the first-born of Judah, was evil in the eyes of the L rd, [destroying his seed to preserve his wife's beauty],
and the L rd killed him.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוּדָה֙ לְאוֹנָ֔ן בֹּ֛א אֶל־אֵ֥שֶׁת אָחִ֖יךָ וְיַבֵּ֣ם אֹתָ֑הּ
pairs.english: And Judah said to Onan: Come to your brother's wife and take her in levirate marriage,
and establish seed for your brother, [the son being called by the latter's name].

pairs.hebrew: וַיֵּ֣דַע אוֹנָ֔ן כִּ֛י לֹּ֥א ל֖וֹ יִהְיֶ֣ה הַזָּ֑רַע
pairs.english: And Onan knew that not his would be the seed.

pairs.hebrew: וְהָיָ֞ה אִם־בָּ֨א אֶל־אֵ֤שֶׁת אָחִיו֙ וְשִׁחֵ֣ת אַ֔רְצָה
pairs.english: And it was, when he came to his brother's wife, that he destroyed [the seed] to the ground ["threshing within and winnowing without"],
not to give seed to his brother.
And it was evil in the eyes of the L rd what he had done,
and He killed him too.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוּדָה֩ לְתָמָ֨ר כַּלָּת֜וֹ שְׁבִ֧י אַלְמָנָ֣ה בֵית־אָבִ֗יךְ עַד־יִגְדַּל֙ שֵׁלָ֣ה בְנִ֔י
pairs.english: And Judah said to Tamar his daughter-in-law [as a pretext for not giving Shelah to her]: Remain a widow in your father's house until Shelah my son grows up.
For he said (to himself): Lest he, too, die as his brothers.
And Tamar went and she sat in her father's house.
And in the course of time, the daughter of Shua, Judah's wife, died.
And Judah was consoled

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּ֜עַל עַל־גֹּֽזְזֵ֤י צֹאנוֹ֙ ה֗וּא וְחִירָ֛ה רֵעֵ֥הוּ הָעֲדֻלָּמִ֖י תִּמְנָֽתָה׃
pairs.english: and he went up to [supervise] his sheep shearers, he and Chirah his companion, the Adulamite, to Timnah.
And it was told to Tamar, saying:

pairs.hebrew: הִנֵּ֥ה חָמִ֛יךְ עֹלֶ֥ה תִמְנָ֖תָה לָגֹ֥ז צֹאנֽוֹ׃
pairs.english: Behold, your father-in-law has gone up to Timnah to shear his sheep.

pairs.hebrew: וַתָּ֩סַר֩ בִּגְדֵ֨י אַלְמְנוּתָ֜הּ מֵֽעָלֶ֗יהָ וַתְּכַ֤ס בַּצָּעִיף֙ וַתִּתְעַלָּ֔ף
pairs.english: And she removed her widow's weeds, and she donned a veil and covered her face,

pairs.hebrew: וַתֵּ֙שֶׁב֙ בְּפֶ֣תַח עֵינַ֔יִם אֲשֶׁ֖ר עַל־דֶּ֣רֶךְ תִּמְנָ֑תָה
pairs.english: and she sat at the crossroads on the way to Timnah.

pairs.hebrew: כִּ֤י רָאֲתָה֙ כִּֽי־גָדַ֣ל שֵׁלָ֔ה וְהִ֕וא לֹֽא־נִתְּנָ֥ה ל֖וֹ לְאִשָּֽׁה׃
pairs.english: For she saw that Shelah had grown and that she had not been given to him as a wife. [(And Tamar was desirous of perpetuating Judah's line)]
And Judah saw her and he thought her to be a harlot, [for she sat at the crossroads],
for she had covered her face [that he not be able to recognize her].

pairs.hebrew: וַיֵּ֨ט אֵלֶ֜יהָ אֶל־הַדֶּ֗רֶךְ וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ הָֽבָה־נָּא֙ אָב֣וֹא אֵלַ֔יִךְ
pairs.english: And he detoured to her to the way [on which she sat]. And he said: Ready yourself that I may come to you.

pairs.hebrew: כִּ֚י לֹ֣א יָדַ֔ע כִּ֥י כַלָּת֖וֹ הִ֑וא
pairs.english: (For he did not know that she was his daughter-in-law.)
And she said to him: What will you give me for coming to me?
And he said: I shall send a goat-kid from the flock.
And she said: If you give me a pledge until you send it.
And he said: What is the pledge that I shall give you?

pairs.hebrew: וַתֹּ֗אמֶר חֹתָֽמְךָ֙ וּפְתִילֶ֔ךָ וּמַטְּךָ֖ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּיָדֶ֑ךָ
pairs.english: And she said: Your signet and your cloak and the staff that is in your hand.
And he gave it to her and he came to her and she conceived to him [i.e., strong ones like him: righteous ones like him].
And she arose, and she went, and she removed her veil from her,
and she donned her widow's garments.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּשְׁלַ֨ח יְהוּדָ֜ה אֶת־גְּדִ֣י הָֽעִזִּ֗ים בְּיַד֙ רֵעֵ֣הוּ הָֽעֲדֻלָּמִ֔י לָקַ֥חַת הָעֵרָב֖וֹן מִיַּ֣ד הָאִשָּׁ֑ה
pairs.english: And Judah sent the goat-kid with his friend the Adulamite to take the pledge from the woman,
and he did not find her.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּשְׁאַ֞ל אֶת־אַנְשֵׁ֤י מְקֹמָהּ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר אַיֵּ֧ה הַקְּדֵשָׁ֛ה הִ֥וא בָעֵינַ֖יִם עַל־הַדָּ֑רֶךְ
pairs.english: And he asked the men of her place: Where is the harlot of the crossroads?
And they said: There was no harlot here.
And he returned to Judah and he said: I did not find her,

pairs.hebrew: וְגַ֨ם אַנְשֵׁ֤י הַמָּקוֹם֙ אָֽמְר֔וּ לֹא־הָיְתָ֥ה בָזֶ֖ה קְדֵשָֽׁה׃
pairs.english: and the men of the place also said: There was no harlot here.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוּדָה֙ תִּֽקַּֽח־לָ֔הּ פֶּ֖ן נִהְיֶ֣ה לָב֑וּז
pairs.english: And Judah said: Let her take it [what she had], lest we be put to shame [i.e., exposed by our oversolicitous inquiry].

pairs.hebrew: הִנֵּ֤ה שָׁלַ֙חְתִּי֙ הַגְּדִ֣י הַזֶּ֔ה וְאַתָּ֖ה לֹ֥א מְצָאתָֽהּ׃
pairs.english: Behold, I sent this kid and you did not find her. [What more could I have done?]

pairs.hebrew: וַיְהִ֣י ׀ כְּמִשְׁלֹ֣שׁ חֳדָשִׁ֗ים וַיֻּגַּ֨ד לִֽיהוּדָ֤ה לֵאמֹר֙
pairs.english: And it was, with the tripling of the months [the greater part of the first, the greater part of the last, and all of the middle] that it was told to Judah:

pairs.hebrew: זָֽנְתָה֙ תָּמָ֣ר כַּלָּתֶ֔ךָ וְגַ֛ם הִנֵּ֥ה הָרָ֖ה לִזְנוּנִ֑ים
pairs.english: Tamar your daughter-in-law has played the harlot, and she is also pregnant by harlotry.
And Judah said: Take her out and let her be burned, [Tamar being the daughter of Shem, a Cohein (see Rashi on 14:18 and Leviticus 21:9)].

pairs.hebrew: הִ֣וא מוּצֵ֗את וְהִ֨יא שָׁלְחָ֤ה אֶל־חָמִ֙יהָ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר
pairs.english: As she was being taken out [to be burned], she sent to her father-in-law, saying,
I am with child by the man to whom these belong.

pairs.hebrew: וַתֹּ֙אמֶר֙ הַכֶּר־נָ֔א לְמִ֞י הַחֹתֶ֧מֶת וְהַפְּתִילִ֛ים וְהַמַּטֶּ֖ה הָאֵֽלֶּה׃
pairs.english: And she said: Recognize, I pray you, whose are this signet and cloak and staff.
And Judah recognized them and he said: She is right. [She is with child] by me.
For [she acted] justly [in that] I did not give her to Shelah my son.
And he did not live with her again.
And it was, at the time of her bearing,
that, behold, there were twins in her womb.
And it was, as she bore, that one put forth his hand.

pairs.hebrew: וַתִּקַּ֣ח הַמְיַלֶּ֗דֶת וַתִּקְשֹׁ֨ר עַל־יָד֤וֹ שָׁנִי֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר זֶ֖ה יָצָ֥א רִאשֹׁנָֽה׃
pairs.english: And the midwife took and tied a red string on his hand, saying: This one came out first.

pairs.hebrew: וַיְהִ֣י ׀ כְּמֵשִׁ֣יב יָד֗וֹ וְהִנֵּה֙ יָצָ֣א אָחִ֔יו
pairs.english: And it was, when he drew back his hand, that his brother came out.
And she said: How you have girded yourself with strength [paretz]!
And he called his name Paretz.

pairs.hebrew: וְאַחַר֙ יָצָ֣א אָחִ֔יו אֲשֶׁ֥ר עַל־יָד֖וֹ הַשָּׁנִ֑י
pairs.english: And then his brother came out on whose hand was the [shining] red string.
And he called his name Zarach ["shining"].
And Joseph [before the aforementioned episode] had been brought down to Egypt.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּקְנֵ֡הוּ פּוֹטִיפַר֩ סְרִ֨יס פַּרְעֹ֜ה שַׂ֤ר הַטַּבָּחִים֙ אִ֣ישׁ מִצְרִ֔י
pairs.english: And he was bought [as a slave] by Potiphar, Pharaoh's officer, the head of the slaughterers, an Egyptian man,
from the hand of the Ishmaelites, who had brought him down there.

pairs.hebrew: וַיְהִ֤י יְהֹוָה֙ אֶת־יוֹסֵ֔ף וַיְהִ֖י אִ֣ישׁ מַצְלִ֑יחַ
pairs.english: And the L rd was with Joseph, and he was a successful man,
and he remained in the house of his lord, the Egyptian.
And his master saw that the L rd was with him [(The name of the L rd was ever in his mouth)]

pairs.hebrew: וְכֹל֙ אֲשֶׁר־ה֣וּא עֹשֶׂ֔ה יְהֹוָ֖ה מַצְלִ֥יחַ בְּיָדֽוֹ׃
pairs.english: and that whatever he did the L rd prospered in his hand.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּמְצָ֨א יוֹסֵ֥ף חֵ֛ן בְּעֵינָ֖יו וַיְשָׁ֣רֶת אֹת֑וֹ
pairs.english: And Joseph found favor in his eyes, and he served him;
and he appointed him over his house,
and all that he had he placed in his hand.

pairs.hebrew: וַיְהִ֡י מֵאָז֩ הִפְקִ֨יד אֹת֜וֹ בְּבֵית֗וֹ וְעַל֙ כׇּל־אֲשֶׁ֣ר יֶשׁ־ל֔וֹ
pairs.english: And it was, from the time he appointed him over his household and over all that he had,

pairs.hebrew: וַיְבָ֧רֶךְ יְהֹוָ֛ה אֶת־בֵּ֥ית הַמִּצְרִ֖י בִּגְלַ֣ל יוֹסֵ֑ף
pairs.english: that the L rd blessed the house of the Egyptian for the sake of Joseph;

pairs.hebrew: וַיְהִ֞י בִּרְכַּ֤ת יְהֹוָה֙ בְּכׇל־אֲשֶׁ֣ר יֶשׁ־ל֔וֹ בַּבַּ֖יִת וּבַשָּׂדֶֽה׃
pairs.english: and the L rd's blessing was over all that he had, in the house and in the field.
And he left all that he had in Joseph's hand,

pairs.hebrew: וְלֹא־יָדַ֤ע אִתּוֹ֙ מְא֔וּמָה כִּ֥י אִם־הַלֶּ֖חֶם אֲשֶׁר־ה֣וּא אוֹכֵ֑ל
pairs.english: and he paid no heed to anything with him but "the bread that he ate" [i.e., his wife].
And Joseph was beautiful in form and appearance, [eating well, and primping and preening himself].

pairs.hebrew: וַיְהִ֗י אַחַר֙ הַדְּבָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֔לֶּה וַתִּשָּׂ֧א אֵֽשֶׁת־אֲדֹנָ֛יו אֶת־עֵינֶ֖יהָ אֶל־יוֹסֵ֑ף
pairs.english: And it was [immediately] after these things that his master's wife lifted her eyes to Joseph
and said: "Lie with me."

pairs.hebrew: וַיְמָאֵ֓ן ׀ וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ אֶל־אֵ֣שֶׁת אֲדֹנָ֔יו הֵ֣ן אֲדֹנִ֔י לֹא־יָדַ֥ע אִתִּ֖י מַה־בַּבָּ֑יִת
pairs.english: And he refused. And he said to his master's wife: Behold, my lord does not know what is with me in the house,
and all that he has he has placed in my hand.
There is no one greater in this house than I,

pairs.hebrew: וְלֹֽא־חָשַׂ֤ךְ מִמֶּ֙נִּי֙ מְא֔וּמָה כִּ֥י אִם־אוֹתָ֖ךְ בַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר אַתְּ־אִשְׁתּ֑וֹ
pairs.english: and he has withheld nothing from me but you, in that you are his wife.

pairs.hebrew: וְאֵ֨יךְ אֶֽעֱשֶׂ֜ה הָרָעָ֤ה הַגְּדֹלָה֙ הַזֹּ֔את וְחָטָ֖אתִי לֵֽאלֹהִֽים׃
pairs.english: And how can I do this great evil and sin against G d? [illicit relations being forbidden to the Noachides].
And it was, as she spoke to Joseph day after day,

pairs.hebrew: וְלֹא־שָׁמַ֥ע אֵלֶ֛יהָ לִשְׁכַּ֥ב אֶצְלָ֖הּ לִהְי֥וֹת עִמָּֽהּ׃
pairs.english: and he did not heed her to lie with her [even without intercourse] to be with her [(in Gehinnom) in the world to come],

pairs.hebrew: וַֽיְהִי֙ כְּהַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֔ה וַיָּבֹ֥א הַבַּ֖יְתָה לַעֲשׂ֣וֹת מְלַאכְתּ֑וֹ
pairs.english: it happened, on a certain [festival] day [when all had gone to the house of idolatry], when he came to the house to do his work,

pairs.hebrew: וְאֵ֨ין אִ֜ישׁ מֵאַנְשֵׁ֥י הַבַּ֛יִת שָׁ֖ם בַּבָּֽיִת׃
pairs.english: and none of the men of the household were there in the house,
that she grabbed him by his garment, saying: "Lie with me!"
And he left his garment in her hand
and he fled and ran outside.
And it was, when she saw that he had left his garment in her hand
and had run outside,

pairs.hebrew: וַתִּקְרָ֞א לְאַנְשֵׁ֣י בֵיתָ֗הּ וַתֹּ֤אמֶר לָהֶם֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר
pairs.english: that she called to the men of her house and said to them:

pairs.hebrew: רְא֗וּ הֵ֥בִיא לָ֛נוּ אִ֥ישׁ עִבְרִ֖י לְצַ֣חֶק בָּ֑נוּ
pairs.english: See, he [i.e., her husband] brought to us an Ivri [from ever hanahar, the other side of the river (Euphrates), of the sons of Ever] to disport himself with us [i.e., me].

pairs.hebrew: בָּ֤א אֵלַי֙ לִשְׁכַּ֣ב עִמִּ֔י וָאֶקְרָ֖א בְּק֥וֹל גָּדֽוֹל׃
pairs.english: He came to me to lie with me and I made great outcry.
And it was, when he heard me lifting my voice and calling out,

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּעֲזֹ֤ב בִּגְדוֹ֙ אֶצְלִ֔י וַיָּ֖נׇס וַיֵּצֵ֥א הַחֽוּצָה׃
pairs.english: that he left his garment with me, and he fled and ran outside.
And she left his garment with her
until his lord came to his house.
And she spoke to him such things, saying:

pairs.hebrew: בָּֽא־אֵלַ֞י הָעֶ֧בֶד הָֽעִבְרִ֛י אֲשֶׁר־הֵבֵ֥אתָ לָּ֖נוּ לְצַ֥חֶק בִּֽי׃
pairs.english: The Ivri slave that you brought to us came to me to disport himself with me.
And it was, when I raised my voice and called out,
that he left his garment with me and fled outside.

pairs.hebrew: וַיְהִי֩ כִשְׁמֹ֨עַ אֲדֹנָ֜יו אֶת־דִּבְרֵ֣י אִשְׁתּ֗וֹ אֲשֶׁ֨ר דִּבְּרָ֤ה אֵלָיו֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר
pairs.english: And it was, when his master heard [during intercourse] the words of his wife, who spoke to him, saying:
Such [(intimate) things] did your slave do with me,
that his wrath burned.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּקַּח֩ אֲדֹנֵ֨י יוֹסֵ֜ף אֹת֗וֹ וַֽיִּתְּנֵ֙הוּ֙ אֶל־בֵּ֣ית הַסֹּ֔הַר
pairs.english: And Joseph's master took him and placed him in the prison house,
the place where the king's prisoners were incarcerated;
and he remained there in the prison house.

pairs.hebrew: וַיְהִ֤י יְהֹוָה֙ אֶת־יוֹסֵ֔ף וַיֵּ֥ט אֵלָ֖יו חָ֑סֶד
pairs.english: And the L rd was with Joseph, and He conferred grace upon him,
and He granted him favor in the eyes of the overseer of the prison house.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּתֵּ֞ן שַׂ֤ר בֵּית־הַסֹּ֙הַר֙ בְּיַד־יוֹסֵ֔ף אֵ֚ת כׇּל־הָ֣אֲסִירִ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֖ר בְּבֵ֣ית הַסֹּ֑הַר
pairs.english: And the overseer of the prison house placed all of the prisoners in the prison house in Joseph's charge;

pairs.hebrew: וְאֵ֨ת כׇּל־אֲשֶׁ֤ר עֹשִׂים֙ שָׁ֔ם ה֖וּא הָיָ֥ה עֹשֶֽׂה׃
pairs.english: and all that was done there was done at his bidding.

pairs.hebrew: אֵ֣ין ׀ שַׂ֣ר בֵּית־הַסֹּ֗הַר רֹאֶ֤ה אֶֽת־כׇּל־מְא֙וּמָה֙ בְּיָד֔וֹ בַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר יְהֹוָ֖ה אִתּ֑וֹ
pairs.english: The overseer of the prison house looked after nothing in his hand in that the L rd was with him,
and whatever he did, the L rd prospered.
And it was, after these things, [(G d diverting talk against Joseph to talk against the king's stewards)]

pairs.hebrew: חָ֥טְא֛וּ מַשְׁקֵ֥ה מֶֽלֶךְ־מִצְרַ֖יִם וְהָאֹפֶ֑ה לַאֲדֹנֵיהֶ֖ם לְמֶ֥לֶךְ מִצְרָֽיִם׃
pairs.english: that the butler of the king of Egypt and the baker [of his bread] offended their lord, the king of Egypt [(a fly was found in the wine, and a pebble in the bread)].
And Pharaoh grew wroth with his two eunuchs,

pairs.hebrew: עַ֚ל שַׂ֣ר הַמַּשְׁקִ֔ים וְעַ֖ל שַׂ֥ר הָאוֹפִֽים׃
pairs.english: the chief butler and the chief baker.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּתֵּ֨ן אֹתָ֜ם בְּמִשְׁמַ֗ר בֵּ֛ית שַׂ֥ר הַטַּבָּחִ֖ים אֶל־בֵּ֣ית הַסֹּ֑הַר
pairs.english: And he placed them in custody in the house of the head of the slaughterers, in the prison house
where Joseph was incarcerated.

pairs.hebrew: וַ֠יִּפְקֹ֠ד שַׂ֣ר הַטַּבָּחִ֧ים אֶת־יוֹסֵ֛ף אִתָּ֖ם וַיְשָׁ֣רֶת אֹתָ֑ם
pairs.english: And the head of the slaughterers charged Joseph [to be] with them, and he ministered to them,
and they were days [twelve months] in ward.

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּֽחַלְמוּ֩ חֲל֨וֹם שְׁנֵיהֶ֜ם אִ֤ישׁ חֲלֹמוֹ֙ בְּלַ֣יְלָה אֶחָ֔ד
pairs.english: And the two of them dreamed a dream, each his dream in one night,
each according to the [eventual] materialization of his dream,

pairs.hebrew: הַמַּשְׁקֶ֣ה וְהָאֹפֶ֗ה אֲשֶׁר֙ לְמֶ֣לֶךְ מִצְרַ֔יִם אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֲסוּרִ֖ים בְּבֵ֥ית הַסֹּֽהַר׃
pairs.english: the butler and the baker of the king of Egypt, who were bound in the prison house.
And Joseph came to them in the morning
and he saw them, and they were distraught.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּשְׁאַ֞ל אֶת־סְרִיסֵ֣י פַרְעֹ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר אִתּ֧וֹ בְמִשְׁמַ֛ר בֵּ֥ית אֲדֹנָ֖יו לֵאמֹ֑ר
pairs.english: And he asked the eunuchs of Pharaoh who were in ward with him in his master's house:
Why are your faces downcast today?

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ אֵלָ֔יו חֲל֣וֹם חָלַ֔מְנוּ וּפֹתֵ֖ר אֵ֣ין אֹת֑וֹ
pairs.english: And they said to him: We dreamed a dream, and there is no interpreter of it.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֲלֵהֶ֜ם יוֹסֵ֗ף הֲל֤וֹא לֵֽאלֹהִים֙ פִּתְרֹנִ֔ים
pairs.english: And Joseph said to them: Are not interpretations unto G d?
Tell it, I pray you, to me.

pairs.hebrew: וַיְסַפֵּ֧ר שַֽׂר־הַמַּשְׁקִ֛ים אֶת־חֲלֹמ֖וֹ לְיוֹסֵ֑ף וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ל֔וֹ
pairs.english: And the chief butler told his dream to Joseph, saying to him:
In my dream, behold, a grapevine before me.
And on the grapevine, three shoots,
which seemed to bud. And its blossom sprouted;
and its clusters brought forth grapes.
And Pharaoh's goblet was in my hand.

pairs.hebrew: וָאֶקַּ֣ח אֶת־הָֽעֲנָבִ֗ים וָֽאֶשְׂחַ֤ט אֹתָם֙ אֶל־כּ֣וֹס פַּרְעֹ֔ה
pairs.english: And I took the grapes and squeezed them into Pharaoh's goblet;
and I placed the goblet on Pharaoh's hand.
And Joseph said to him: This is its interpretation:
The three shoots are three days.

pairs.hebrew: בְּע֣וֹד ׀ שְׁלֹ֣שֶׁת יָמִ֗ים יִשָּׂ֤א פַרְעֹה֙ אֶת־רֹאשֶׁ֔ךָ וַהֲשִֽׁיבְךָ֖ עַל־כַּנֶּ֑ךָ
pairs.english: In three more days, Pharaoh will count you [with his other attendants], and he will restore you to your post,

pairs.hebrew: וְנָתַתָּ֤ כוֹס־פַּרְעֹה֙ בְּיָד֔וֹ כַּמִּשְׁפָּט֙ הָֽרִאשׁ֔וֹן אֲשֶׁ֥ר הָיִ֖יתָ מַשְׁקֵֽהוּ׃
pairs.english: and you will place the cup of Pharaoh in his hand as at first, when you would give him drink.

pairs.hebrew: כִּ֧י אִם־זְכַרְתַּ֣נִי אִתְּךָ֗ כַּאֲשֶׁר֙ יִ֣יטַב לָ֔ךְ
pairs.english: So that if you remember me with you when it is well with you,
then do lovingkindness with me, I pray you,
and mention me to Pharaoh, and take me out of this house.
For I have been stolen from the land of the Hebrews.

pairs.hebrew: וְגַם־פֹּה֙ לֹא־עָשִׂ֣יתִֽי מְא֔וּמָה כִּֽי־שָׂמ֥וּ אֹתִ֖י בַּבּֽוֹר׃
pairs.english: And here, too, I did nothing that they should put me into the pit.
And the chief baker saw that he had interpreted well,
and he said to Joseph: I, too, in my dream;
and behold, three wicker baskets on my head.

pairs.hebrew: וּבַסַּ֣ל הָֽעֶלְי֗וֹן מִכֹּ֛ל מַאֲכַ֥ל פַּרְעֹ֖ה מַעֲשֵׂ֣ה אֹפֶ֑ה
pairs.english: And in the top basket, of all the food of Pharaoh, the work of a baker.

pairs.hebrew: וְהָע֗וֹף אֹכֵ֥ל אֹתָ֛ם מִן־הַסַּ֖ל מֵעַ֥ל רֹאשִֽׁי׃
pairs.english: And the birds ate them from the basket on my head.
And Joseph answered and he said: This is its interpretation:
The three baskets are three days.

pairs.hebrew: בְּע֣וֹד ׀ שְׁלֹ֣שֶׁת יָמִ֗ים יִשָּׂ֨א פַרְעֹ֤ה אֶת־רֹֽאשְׁךָ֙ מֵֽעָלֶ֔יךָ
pairs.english: In another three days, Pharaoh will lift your head from you
and hang you upon a tree;
and the birds will eat your flesh from you.

pairs.hebrew: וַיְהִ֣י ׀ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשְּׁלִישִׁ֗י י֚וֹם הֻלֶּ֣דֶת אֶת־פַּרְעֹ֔ה
pairs.english: And it was on the third day, Pharaoh's birthday,
that he made a feast for all his servants.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּשָּׂ֞א אֶת־רֹ֣אשׁ ׀ שַׂ֣ר הַמַּשְׁקִ֗ים וְאֶת־רֹ֛אשׁ שַׂ֥ר הָאֹפִ֖ים בְּת֥וֹךְ עֲבָדָֽיו׃
pairs.english: And he counted the chief butler and the chief baker in the midst of his servants.
And he restored the chief butler (to officiate) over his drink,
and he placed the goblet on Pharaoh's hand.
And the chief baker he hanged,
as Joseph had interpreted for them.
And the chief butler did not remember Joseph [on that day],
and he forgot him [afterwards].

pairs.hebrew: וַיְהִ֕י מִקֵּ֖ץ שְׁנָתַ֣יִם יָמִ֑ים וּפַרְעֹ֣ה חֹלֵ֔ם
pairs.english: And it was at the end of two years that Pharaoh dreamt.
And, behold, he was standing by the Nile.
And, behold, from the Nile there came up seven kine
of good appearance and fat flesh,
and they fed in the reed grass.

pairs.hebrew: וְהִנֵּ֞ה שֶׁ֧בַע פָּר֣וֹת אֲחֵר֗וֹת עֹל֤וֹת אַחֲרֵיהֶן֙ מִן־הַיְאֹ֔ר
pairs.english: And, behold, seven other kine came up after them from the Nile,
of bad appearance and thin flesh.
And they stood near the kine on the bank of the Nile.

pairs.hebrew: וַתֹּאכַ֣לְנָה הַפָּר֗וֹת רָע֤וֹת הַמַּרְאֶה֙ וְדַקֹּ֣ת הַבָּשָׂ֔ר
pairs.english: And the seven kine of bad appearance and of thin flesh ate

pairs.hebrew: אֵ֚ת שֶׁ֣בַע הַפָּר֔וֹת יְפֹ֥ת הַמַּרְאֶ֖ה וְהַבְּרִיאֹ֑ת
pairs.english: the seven kine of good appearance and of fat flesh [(signifying the forgetting of the years of plenty in the years of famine)],
and Pharaoh awoke.
And he slept and he dreamed a second time,

pairs.hebrew: וְהִנֵּ֣ה ׀ שֶׁ֣בַע שִׁבֳּלִ֗ים עֹל֛וֹת בְּקָנֶ֥ה אֶחָ֖ד
pairs.english: and, behold, seven ears of corn arose upon one stalk,
healthy and good.

pairs.hebrew: וְהִנֵּה֙ שֶׁ֣בַע שִׁבֳּלִ֔ים דַּקּ֖וֹת וּשְׁדוּפֹ֣ת קָדִ֑ים
pairs.english: And, behold, seven ears of corn, thin, and beaten by the east wind
sprouted after them.

pairs.hebrew: וַתִּבְלַ֙עְנָה֙ הַשִּׁבֳּלִ֣ים הַדַּקּ֔וֹת אֵ֚ת שֶׁ֣בַע הַֽשִּׁבֳּלִ֔ים הַבְּרִיא֖וֹת וְהַמְּלֵא֑וֹת
pairs.english: And the seven thin ears swallowed up the seven healthy, full ears.
And Pharaoh awoke,
and behold, it was a [completed] dream [demanding an interpretation].
And it was in the morning that his spirit was agitated,
and he sent and called all the necromancers of Egypt and all its wise men;
and Pharaoh told his dream to them,
but none could interpret them to Pharaoh [i.e., to Pharaoh's satisfaction.]
And the chief butler spoke to Pharaoh, saying:
I make mention of my faults this day.
Pharaoh was wroth with his servants,

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּתֵּ֨ן אֹתִ֜י בְּמִשְׁמַ֗ר בֵּ֚ית שַׂ֣ר הַטַּבָּחִ֔ים
pairs.english: and he placed me in custody in the house of the head of the slaughterers —
me and the chief baker.

pairs.hebrew: וַנַּֽחַלְמָ֥ה חֲל֛וֹם בְּלַ֥יְלָה אֶחָ֖ד אֲנִ֣י וָה֑וּא
pairs.english: And we dreamed a dream in one night, I and he;
each according to [i.e., in consonance with] the [subsequent] interpretation of his dream did we dream.

pairs.hebrew: וְשָׁ֨ם אִתָּ֜נוּ נַ֣עַר עִבְרִ֗י עֶ֚בֶד לְשַׂ֣ר הַטַּבָּחִ֔ים
pairs.english: And there was with us a youth [a simpleton], an Ivri, [who does not even know our language], a slave [(unworthy of royal regard)] to the head of the slaughterers,
and we told him and he interpreted our dreams;
each according to [the nature of] his dream did he interpret.
And it was, [just] as he interpreted it to us did it come to pass.
I, he [Pharaoh] restored to my post,
and him he hanged.
And Pharaoh sent and called (for) Joseph,
and they hastened him out of the pit,
and he cut his hair [in deference to the king], and he changed his garments,
and he came to Pharaoh.
And Pharaoh said to Joseph:
I dreamed a dream and none can interpret it.
And I have heard about you that
you understand a dream to interpret it.
And Joseph answered Pharaoh, saying:
It [the interpretation of dreams] is not mine;
G d will answer [through my mouth] for the peace of Pharaoh.
And Pharaoh spoke to Joseph:
In my dream, behold, I was standing on the bank of the Nile.
And, behold, from the Nile there came up seven kine
of fat flesh and good appearance,
and they fed in the reed grass.
And, behold, seven other kine came up after them,

pairs.hebrew: דַּלּ֨וֹת וְרָע֥וֹת תֹּ֛אַר מְאֹ֖ד וְרַקּ֣וֹת בָּשָׂ֑ר
pairs.english: lean, of very bad appearance and thin-fleshed.
I never saw such in all the land of Egypt for badness.
And the thin, bad kine ate
the first fat kine.
And they came into their midst,
but it could not be known that they had come into their midst,
for their appearance was bad as in the beginning —
and I awoke.
And I saw in my dream,

pairs.hebrew: וְהִנֵּ֣ה ׀ שֶׁ֣בַע שִׁבֳּלִ֗ים עֹלֹ֛ת בְּקָנֶ֥ה אֶחָ֖ד
pairs.english: and, behold, seven ears of corn came up on one stalk,
full and good.

pairs.hebrew: וְהִנֵּה֙ שֶׁ֣בַע שִׁבֳּלִ֔ים צְנֻמ֥וֹת דַּקּ֖וֹת שְׁדֻפ֣וֹת קָדִ֑ים
pairs.english: And, behold, seven ears of corn, parched thin, beaten by the east wind,
sprouted after them.

pairs.hebrew: וַתִּבְלַ֙עְןָ֙ הַשִּׁבֳּלִ֣ים הַדַּקֹּ֔ת אֵ֛ת שֶׁ֥בַע הַֽשִּׁבֳּלִ֖ים הַטֹּב֑וֹת
pairs.english: And the thin ears swallowed the seven good ears.
And I related this to the magicians,
and none could tell me (what it meant).
And Joseph said to Pharaoh:
The dream of Pharaoh is one.

pairs.hebrew: אֵ֣ת אֲשֶׁ֧ר הָאֱלֹהִ֛ים עֹשֶׂ֖ה הִגִּ֥יד לְפַרְעֹֽה׃
pairs.english: What G d is to do He has told to Pharaoh.

pairs.hebrew: שֶׁ֧בַע פָּרֹ֣ת הַטֹּבֹ֗ת שֶׁ֤בַע שָׁנִים֙ הֵ֔נָּה
pairs.english: The seven good kine are seven years,

pairs.hebrew: וְשֶׁ֤בַע הַֽשִּׁבֳּלִים֙ הַטֹּבֹ֔ת שֶׁ֥בַע שָׁנִ֖ים הֵ֑נָּה
pairs.english: and the seven good ears are [the same] seven years.
It is one dream.

pairs.hebrew: וְשֶׁ֣בַע הַ֠פָּר֠וֹת הָֽרַקּ֨וֹת וְהָרָעֹ֜ת הָעֹלֹ֣ת אַחֲרֵיהֶ֗ן שֶׁ֤בַע שָׁנִים֙ הֵ֔נָּה
pairs.english: And the seven thin, bad kine that came up after them are seven years.
And the seven thin ears beaten by the east wind
will be seven years of famine.
This is the thing that I have spoken to Pharaoh.
What G d is to do He has shown to Pharaoh.
Behold, seven years are coming —
great plenty in all the land of Egypt.
And seven years of famine will arise after them,
and all the plenty in the land of Egypt will be forgotten, [thus, the "swallowing" (24)],
and the famine will consume the land.
And the plenty will not be known in the land
because of that famine afterwards [thus, "And it was not noticeable, etc." (21)]
because it will be very sore.
And as to the repeating of the dream to Pharaoh twice,
it is because the thing is readied from G d,
and G d is hastening to do it.

pairs.hebrew: וְעַתָּה֙ יֵרֶ֣א פַרְעֹ֔ה אִ֖ישׁ נָב֣וֹן וְחָכָ֑ם
pairs.english: And now, let Pharaoh see (to find) an understanding, wise man,
and let him place him over the land of Egypt.
Let Pharaoh do this, and let him appoint overseers for the land,

pairs.hebrew: וְחִמֵּשׁ֙ אֶת־אֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם בְּשֶׁ֖בַע שְׁנֵ֥י הַשָּׂבָֽע׃
pairs.english: and let him spur on the (people of) the land of Egypt in the seven years of plenty.

pairs.hebrew: וְיִקְבְּצ֗וּ אֶת־כׇּל־אֹ֙כֶל֙ הַשָּׁנִ֣ים הַטֹּב֔וֹת הַבָּאֹ֖ת הָאֵ֑לֶּה
pairs.english: And let them gather up all the food of these coming good years,
and let them store up grain under the hand of Pharaoh,
food in the cities, and let them guard it.
And the [stored-up] food will be a reserve for the land

pairs.hebrew: לְשֶׁ֙בַע֙ שְׁנֵ֣י הָרָעָ֔ב אֲשֶׁ֥ר תִּהְיֶ֖יןָ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם
pairs.english: for the seven years of famine which will prevail in the land of Egypt,
and the land will not be cut off in the famine.
And the thing was good in the eyes of Pharaoh
and in the eyes of all his servants.
And Pharaoh said to his servants:
Can there be found such a one!
a man invested with the spirit of G d.
And Pharaoh said to Joseph:
Since G d has apprised you of all this,
there is none so understanding and wise as you [(Pharaoh's response to 33)].
You will be over my house,
and by your word shall all my people be fed.
Only (in) the throne [i.e., the name of "king"] shall I be greater than you.
And Pharaoh said to Joseph:

pairs.hebrew: רְאֵה֙ נָתַ֣תִּי אֹֽתְךָ֔ עַ֖ל כׇּל־אֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃
pairs.english: See, I have set you over all the land of Egypt.
And Pharaoh removed his ring from his hand
and placed it on Joseph's hand, [thus making him second to himself],
and he robed him in vestments of fine linen,
and he placed the golden chain on his neck.
And he had him ride in the chariot next to his,
and they called before him "Avrech!" ["This is the father (i.e., counselor) of the king"],
and he set him over all the land of Egypt.
And Pharaoh said to Joseph: I am Pharaoh [and I am empowered to decree],
and [I decree that] without your consent no man may lift his hand [to arm himself], or his foot [to mount a horse]
in the whole land of Egypt.
And Pharaoh called Joseph "Tzafnath Pa'aneach" ["the unraveler of the hidden"],

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּתֶּן־ל֣וֹ אֶת־אָֽסְנַ֗ת בַּת־פּ֥וֹטִי פֶ֛רַע כֹּהֵ֥ן אֹ֖ן לְאִשָּׁ֑ה
pairs.english: and he gave him as a wife Asnath the daughter of Poti Fera, the priest of On, [Pothiphar, called "Poti Fera" because, having designs on Joseph, he was rendered impotent (fera).]
And Joseph went out over the land of Egypt.

pairs.hebrew: וְיוֹסֵף֙ בֶּן־שְׁלֹשִׁ֣ים שָׁנָ֔ה בְּעׇמְד֕וֹ לִפְנֵ֖י פַּרְעֹ֣ה מֶֽלֶךְ־מִצְרָ֑יִם
pairs.english: And Joseph was thirty years old when he stood before Pharaoh king of Egypt.
And Joseph went out from before Pharaoh,
and he passed through all the land of Egypt.
And the land was made in the seven years of plenty
into fistfuls [i.e., the inhabitants gathered grain, fist upon fist, for storage].

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּקְבֹּ֞ץ אֶת־כׇּל־אֹ֣כֶל ׀ שֶׁ֣בַע שָׁנִ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֤ר הָיוּ֙ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם
pairs.english: And he gathered all the food of the seven years which were in the land of Egypt,
and he placed food in the cities.

pairs.hebrew: אֹ֧כֶל שְׂדֵה־הָעִ֛יר אֲשֶׁ֥ר סְבִיבֹתֶ֖יהָ נָתַ֥ן בְּתוֹכָֽהּ׃
pairs.english: The food [i.e., the soil] of the field of the city which was around it, he placed in it [into the gathered food, to preserve it, (food being best preserved by local soil)].

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּצְבֹּ֨ר יוֹסֵ֥ף בָּ֛ר כְּח֥וֹל הַיָּ֖ם הַרְבֵּ֣ה מְאֹ֑ד
pairs.english: And Joseph laid up grain as the sand of the sea, in great quantity,
until he [the counter] stopped counting,
for there was no count.
And unto Joseph were born two sons
before the advent of the years of famine [(whence we derive that it is forbidden to cohabit in years of famine)],

pairs.hebrew: אֲשֶׁ֤ר יָֽלְדָה־לּוֹ֙ אָֽסְנַ֔ת בַּת־פּ֥וֹטִי פֶ֖רַע כֹּהֵ֥ן אֽוֹן׃
pairs.english: which were begotten to him by Asnath the daughter of Poti Fera, the priest of On.
And Joseph called the name of the first-born Menasheh:
"for G d has made me forget (nashani) all of my toil
and all of my father's house."
And the name of the second he called Ephraim:
"for G d has made me fruitful (hifrani) in the land of my affliction."
And there ended the seven years of plenty
which were in the land of Egypt.

pairs.hebrew: וַתְּחִלֶּ֜ינָה שֶׁ֣בַע שְׁנֵ֤י הָרָעָב֙ לָב֔וֹא כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר אָמַ֣ר יוֹסֵ֑ף
pairs.english: And the seven years of famine began to arrive, as Joseph had said.
And there was famine in all of the lands,
but in all the land of Egypt there was bread.
And the whole land of Egypt hungered.
And the people cried out to Pharaoh for bread.
And Pharaoh said to all of Egypt: Go to Joseph.
Whatever he tells you, do.
And the famine was on the "face of all the land" [i.e., the rich],
and Joseph opened all (the granaries) where there was (grain),
and he sold to Egypt;
and the famine waxed strong in the land of Egypt.
And all the land came to Egypt to Joseph to buy,
for the famine was strong in all the land.
And Jacob saw that there was a grain sale in Egypt.
And Jacob said to his sons:
Why should you be looked upon [strangely by others for not stocking up before your food gives out]?

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֕אמֶר הִנֵּ֣ה שָׁמַ֔עְתִּי כִּ֥י יֶשׁ־שֶׁ֖בֶר בְּמִצְרָ֑יִם
pairs.english: And he said: Behold, I have heard that there is a (grain) sale in Egypt.
Go down (redu) there [(the gematria of "redu" is 210, intimating the years of servitude in Egypt)], and buy grain for us from there
so that we live and not die.
And the brothers of Joseph [(They went as "the brothers of Joseph," determined to redeem him)], ten, went down
to buy grain from Egypt.

pairs.hebrew: וְאֶת־בִּנְיָמִין֙ אֲחִ֣י יוֹסֵ֔ף לֹא־שָׁלַ֥ח יַעֲקֹ֖ב אֶת־אֶחָ֑יו
pairs.english: And Benjamin, the brother of Joseph, Jacob did not send with his brothers,
saying: Lest he come to harm, [Satan "prosecuting" in time of danger (i.e., on the road)].

pairs.hebrew: וַיָּבֹ֙אוּ֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לִשְׁבֹּ֖ר בְּת֣וֹךְ הַבָּאִ֑ים
pairs.english: And the children of Israel came, [mingling] in the midst of those who came [(Jacob having instructed them to enter separately so that their strength and beauty not arouse "the evil eye")],
for the famine held sway in the land of Canaan.
And Joseph — he ruled the land.
He sold (grain) to all the people of the land.
And the brothers of Joseph came,
and they prostrated themselves to him with their faces to the ground.
And Joseph saw his brothers and he recognized them,
and he acted like a stranger to them, speaking harshly to them:
"Where did you come from!"
And they said: From the land of Canaan to buy food.
And Joseph recognized his brothers, [for they were already bearded when he left them],
but they did not recognize him, [for he was unbearded when they parted].

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּזְכֹּ֣ר יוֹסֵ֔ף אֵ֚ת הַחֲלֹמ֔וֹת אֲשֶׁ֥ר חָלַ֖ם לָהֶ֑ם
pairs.english: And Joseph remembered the dreams which he had dreamed of them, [and he realized that they had been fulfilled (for they had bowed down to him)].
And he said to them: You are spies;
you have come to see the nakedness ("the weak spots") of the land.
And they said to him: No, my lord,
for your servants have come to buy food.
We are all [including Joseph] the sons of one man, [(the Holy Spirit animating their words)].
We are honest;
your servants were not spies.
And He said to them: No,
but you came to see the nakedness of the land. [For, otherwise, why would you have come through ten different gates and not through one?]

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּאמְר֗וּ שְׁנֵ֣ים עָשָׂר֩ עֲבָדֶ֨יךָ אַחִ֧ים ׀ אֲנַ֛חְנוּ בְּנֵ֥י אִישׁ־אֶחָ֖ד בְּאֶ֣רֶץ כְּנָ֑עַן
pairs.english: And they said: We, your twelve servants, are brothers, the sons of one man in the land of Canaan,
and the youngest is with our father this day,
and one is not with us, [and we "scattered" to seek him].
And Joseph said to them:

pairs.hebrew: ה֗וּא אֲשֶׁ֨ר דִּבַּ֧רְתִּי אֲלֵכֶ֛ם לֵאמֹ֖ר מְרַגְּלִ֥ים אַתֶּֽם׃
pairs.english: What I spoke of you, that you are spies, [is the truth].
By this shall you be proved —
by the life of Pharaoh, [(Joseph utilizing Pharaoh's name in swearing falsely)] —

pairs.hebrew: אִם־תֵּצְא֣וּ מִזֶּ֔ה כִּ֧י אִם־בְּב֛וֹא אֲחִיכֶ֥ם הַקָּטֹ֖ן הֵֽנָּה׃
pairs.english: You shall not go out of here unless your youngest brother comes here.
Send one of you and let him take your brother;
and you shall be sequestered
and your words be proved — Is truth with you?

pairs.hebrew: וְאִם־לֹ֕א חֵ֣י פַרְעֹ֔ה כִּ֥י מְרַגְּלִ֖ים אַתֶּֽם׃
pairs.english: And if not [i.e., if you do not bring him], then, by the life of Pharaoh, you are spies.
And he sequestered them together
for three days.
And Joseph said to them on the third day:
Do this and you shall live;
I fear G d.
If you are honest,
let one of you be confined in your prison-house,

pairs.hebrew: וְאַתֶּם֙ לְכ֣וּ הָבִ֔יאוּ שֶׁ֖בֶר רַעֲב֥וֹן בָּתֵּיכֶֽם׃
pairs.english: and you, go and bring [to your father's house] provisions [to alleviate] the hunger of [the people of] your houses.
And your youngest brother bring to me,
so that your words be confirmed and you not die.
And they did so.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּאמְר֞וּ אִ֣ישׁ אֶל־אָחִ֗יו אֲבָל֮ אֲשֵׁמִ֣ים ׀ אֲנַ֘חְנוּ֮ עַל־אָחִ֒ינוּ֒
pairs.english: And they said one to the other: In truth, we are guilty over our brother

pairs.hebrew: אֲשֶׁ֨ר רָאִ֜ינוּ צָרַ֥ת נַפְשׁ֛וֹ בְּהִתְחַֽנְנ֥וֹ אֵלֵ֖ינוּ וְלֹ֣א שָׁמָ֑עְנוּ
pairs.english: for having seen the trouble of his soul in his entreating us and not having listened.
Therefore, this trouble is come upon us.
And Reuven answered them, saying:
Did I not say to you: "Do not sin against the child?"
and you did not heed me;
and now his blood is also being demanded ["also," including the blood of "the old one" (Jacob)].

pairs.hebrew: וְהֵם֙ לֹ֣א יָֽדְע֔וּ כִּ֥י שֹׁמֵ֖עַ יוֹסֵ֑ף
pairs.english: And they did not know that Joseph understood (what they were saying),
for the interpreter [Menasheh] was (i.e., interpreted) between them [and Joseph (when they spoke with him)].
And he walked off some distance from them and he wept.
And he returned and spoke to them,
and he took Shimon from them [(It was Shimon who had cast him into the pit and who had said to Levi (37:19): "Behold, this dreamer comes")],
and he imprisoned him before their eyes [— and when they left, he released him and gave him food and drink.]
And Joseph commanded that their vessels be filled with grain,
that their money be returned, each to his sack,
and that they be given provision for the way.
And he did so to them.
And they lifted their grain onto their asses
and they went from there.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּפְתַּ֨ח הָאֶחָ֜ד אֶת־שַׂקּ֗וֹ לָתֵ֥ת מִסְפּ֛וֹא לַחֲמֹר֖וֹ בַּמָּל֑וֹן
pairs.english: And the one [Levi] opened his sack to give feed to his ass in the night-lodging,
and he saw his money,
and, behold, it was in the mouth of his sack.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֶל־אֶחָיו֙ הוּשַׁ֣ב כַּסְפִּ֔י וְגַ֖ם הִנֵּ֣ה בְאַמְתַּחְתִּ֑י
pairs.english: And he said to his brothers: My money has been returned, and it, too, [along with the grain] is in my sack.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֵּצֵ֣א לִבָּ֗ם וַיֶּֽחֶרְד֞וּ אִ֤ישׁ אֶל־אָחִיו֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר
pairs.english: And their hearts went out, and each trembled to his brothers, saying:
What is this that G d has done to us [to bring this libel (that we stole the money) upon us]?
And they came to Jacob their father to the land of Canaan,

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּגִּ֣ידוּ ל֔וֹ אֵ֛ת כׇּל־הַקֹּרֹ֥ת אֹתָ֖ם לֵאמֹֽר׃
pairs.english: and they told him all that had befallen them, saying:

pairs.hebrew: דִּ֠בֶּ֠ר הָאִ֨ישׁ אֲדֹנֵ֥י הָאָ֛רֶץ אִתָּ֖נוּ קָשׁ֑וֹת
pairs.english: The man, the lord of the land, spoke roughly to us,
and he accused us of spying out the land.
And we said to him: We are honest;
we were not spies.
We are twelve, brothers, sons of our father.
One is not with us,
and the youngest this day is with our father in the land of Canaan.
And the man, the lord of the land, said to us:
By this shall I know that you are honest.
Your one brother leave with me,
and (food for) the hunger of your houses take and go.
And bring your young brother to me,

pairs.hebrew: וְאֵֽדְעָ֗ה כִּ֣י לֹ֤א מְרַגְּלִים֙ אַתֶּ֔ם כִּ֥י כֵנִ֖ים אַתֶּ֑ם
pairs.english: and I will know that you are not spies and that you are honest.
Your brother will I give to you,
and you will go about the land [in trade].
And, as they emptied their sacks,
behold, each (found) his money bundle in his sack.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּרְא֞וּ אֶת־צְרֹר֧וֹת כַּסְפֵּיהֶ֛ם הֵ֥מָּה וַאֲבִיהֶ֖ם וַיִּירָֽאוּ׃
pairs.english: And they saw their money bundles, they and their father, and they were afraid.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֲלֵהֶם֙ יַעֲקֹ֣ב אֲבִיהֶ֔ם אֹתִ֖י שִׁכַּלְתֶּ֑ם
pairs.english: And Jacob their father said to them: You have bereaved me [of children. He suspected that they may have killed Shimon or sold him as they did Joseph.]

pairs.hebrew: יוֹסֵ֤ף אֵינֶ֙נּוּ֙ וְשִׁמְע֣וֹן אֵינֶ֔נּוּ וְאֶת־בִּנְיָמִ֣ן תִּקָּ֔חוּ
pairs.english: Joseph is not, and Shimon is not, and you would take Benjamin!
Upon me have all of them been.
And Reuven said to his father:

pairs.hebrew: אֶת־שְׁנֵ֤י בָנַי֙ תָּמִ֔ית אִם־לֹ֥א אֲבִיאֶ֖נּוּ אֵלֶ֑יךָ
pairs.english: You may kill my two sons if I do not bring him back to you.

pairs.hebrew: תְּנָ֤ה אֹתוֹ֙ עַל־יָדִ֔י וַאֲנִ֖י אֲשִׁיבֶ֥נּוּ אֵלֶֽיךָ׃
pairs.english: Entrust him to me and I will return him to you.
And he said: My son shall not go down with you,
for his brother is dead and he alone remains,
and if an accident befall him on the way on which you go,
then you will bring down my grey hairs with sorrow to the grave.
And the famine was sore
in the land.

pairs.hebrew: וַיְהִ֗י כַּאֲשֶׁ֤ר כִּלּוּ֙ לֶאֱכֹ֣ל אֶת־הַשֶּׁ֔בֶר אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֵבִ֖יאוּ מִמִּצְרָ֑יִם
pairs.english: And it was, when they had finished eating the grain they had brought from Egypt,
that their father said to them:
Return, buy for us a little food.
And Judah said to him:
The man warned us, saying:
You shall not see my face unless your brother is with you.
If you send our brother with us,
we shall go down and buy grain for you.
And if you do not send, we shall not go down.
For the man said to us:
You will not see my face unless your brother is with you.
And Israel said: Why did you do evil unto me
to tell the man that you had another brother?

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּאמְר֡וּ שָׁא֣וֹל שָֽׁאַל־הָ֠אִ֠ישׁ לָ֣נוּ וּלְמֽוֹלַדְתֵּ֜נוּ לֵאמֹ֗ר
pairs.english: And they said: The man inquired about us and about our families, saying:

pairs.hebrew: הַע֨וֹד אֲבִיכֶ֥ם חַי֙ הֲיֵ֣שׁ לָכֶ֣ם אָ֔ח
pairs.english: Is your father still living? Do you have a brother?
And we answered him in response to these words.

pairs.hebrew: הֲיָד֣וֹעַ נֵדַ֔ע כִּ֣י יֹאמַ֔ר הוֹרִ֖ידוּ אֶת־אֲחִיכֶֽם׃
pairs.english: Could we know that he would say "Bring down your brother"?
And Judah said to Israel his father:
Send the child with me and let us arise and go;

pairs.hebrew: וְנִֽחְיֶה֙ וְלֹ֣א נָמ֔וּת גַּם־אֲנַ֥חְנוּ גַם־אַתָּ֖ה גַּם־טַפֵּֽנוּ׃
pairs.english: and we shall live [(the Holy Spirit presaging Jacob's "revival" (45:27)] and we shall not die [of hunger], both we, you, and our little ones, [of a certainty, whereas Benjamin's seizure is only a possibility].
I will go surety for him; you will require him at my hand.
If I do not bring him to you and present him to you [alive],
then I shall have sinned against you all of the days [in the world to come].
For had we not been delayed [by you]
we could now have returned twice [with Shimon, and you would have been spared all this suffering].

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֲלֵהֶ֜ם יִשְׂרָאֵ֣ל אֲבִיהֶ֗ם אִם־כֵּ֣ן ׀ אֵפוֹא֮ זֹ֣את עֲשׂוּ֒
pairs.english: And Israel their father said to them: If so, [i.e., if I must send him with you] then do this:
Take of the choicest fruits of the land in your vessels,
and take a present down to the man:

pairs.hebrew: מְעַ֤ט צֳרִי֙ וּמְעַ֣ט דְּבַ֔שׁ נְכֹ֣את וָלֹ֔ט בׇּטְנִ֖ים וּשְׁקֵדִֽים׃
pairs.english: a little balm, and a little honey, resin and laudanum, pistachios and almonds.
And twice as much money [as you took before] take in your hands, [for the grain price might have risen],

pairs.hebrew: וְאֶת־הַכֶּ֜סֶף הַמּוּשָׁ֨ב בְּפִ֤י אַמְתְּחֹֽתֵיכֶם֙ תָּשִׁ֣יבוּ בְיֶדְכֶ֔ם
pairs.english: and the money returned in the mouth of your bags, return with your hands,
for it might have been [forgotten by the overseer] in error.
And your brother take,
and arise, return to the man.

pairs.hebrew: וְאֵ֣ל שַׁדַּ֗י יִתֵּ֨ן לָכֶ֤ם רַחֲמִים֙ לִפְנֵ֣י הָאִ֔ישׁ
pairs.english: And may the All-Sufficient grant you mercy before the man,
and may he release your "other" [(the Holy Spirit presaging the "release" of Joseph)] brother [Shimon] and Benjamin;
and I, [until you return], as I have been bereaved [of Joseph and Shimon], so will I be bereaved [of Benjamin].

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּקְח֤וּ הָֽאֲנָשִׁים֙ אֶת־הַמִּנְחָ֣ה הַזֹּ֔את וּמִשְׁנֶה־כֶּ֛סֶף לָקְח֥וּ בְיָדָ֖ם וְאֶת־בִּנְיָמִ֑ן
pairs.english: And the men took this gift, and double the money they took in their hand, and Benjamin,
and they arose and went down to Egypt,
and they stood before Joseph.
And Joseph saw Benjamin with them,

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ לַֽאֲשֶׁ֣ר עַל־בֵּית֔וֹ הָבֵ֥א אֶת־הָאֲנָשִׁ֖ים הַבָּ֑יְתָה
pairs.english: and he said to the overseer of his house: Bring these men into the house,
and [see to it] to slaughter something (for a meal) and prepare it,
for with me will these men dine.
And the man did as Joseph said,
and the man brought the men into Joseph's house.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּֽירְא֣וּ הָֽאֲנָשִׁ֗ים כִּ֣י הֽוּבְאוּ֮ בֵּ֣ית יוֹסֵף֒
pairs.english: And the men were afraid, for they were brought into the house of Joseph, [this not being customary for those who had come to purchase grain.]

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּאמְר֗וּ עַל־דְּבַ֤ר הַכֶּ֙סֶף֙ הַשָּׁ֤ב בְּאַמְתְּחֹתֵ֙ינוּ֙ בַּתְּחִלָּ֔ה אֲנַ֖חְנוּ מֽוּבָאִ֑ים
pairs.english: And they said: It is because of the money which was returned to our sacks in the beginning that we were brought [into the house],
to cast a libel upon us, and to fall upon us,
and to take us as slaves, and our asses.
And they drew near to the man who was over Joseph's house,
and they spoke to him at the entrance to the house.
And they said: We entreat you, my lord.
Down did we descend, [we, who were accustomed to feed others,] in the beginning, to buy food.
And it was, when we came to the inn and we opened our sacks,

pairs.hebrew: וְהִנֵּ֤ה כֶֽסֶף־אִישׁ֙ בְּפִ֣י אַמְתַּחְתּ֔וֹ כַּסְפֵּ֖נוּ בְּמִשְׁקָל֑וֹ
pairs.english: that, behold, each one's money was in the mouth of his sack, in (full) weight,
and we have brought it back in our hand.
And other money have we brought in our hand to buy grain.
We do not know who put our money in our sacks.
And he said: Peace unto you; do not fear.

pairs.hebrew: אֱלֹ֨הֵיכֶ֜ם וֵֽאלֹהֵ֤י אֲבִיכֶם֙ נָתַ֨ן לָכֶ֤ם מַטְמוֹן֙ בְּאַמְתְּחֹ֣תֵיכֶ֔ם
pairs.english: Your G d [in your merit], and [if that were not sufficient], the G d of your father [in his merit], has given you a prize in your sacks.
Your money has come to me.
And he brought Shimon out to them.
And the man [after having been gradually pushed to the entrance of the house] brought the men [again] into Joseph's house.
And he gave (them) water, and they washed their feet,
and he gave feed to their asses.
And they decorated the gift, [laying it out in fine vessels] until Joseph came to dine,
for they heard that they would take bread [i.e., dine] there.
And Joseph came to the house,
and they brought him the gift in their hands into the house [from the outer hall into the parlor],
and they prostrated themselves to him to the ground.
And he greeted them,

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר הֲשָׁל֛וֹם אֲבִיכֶ֥ם הַזָּקֵ֖ן אֲשֶׁ֣ר אֲמַרְתֶּ֑ם
pairs.english: and he said: Is your old father well of whom you spoke?
Is he still alive?
And they said: Your servant, our father, is well;
he still lives.
And they bowed [their heads in response to his greeting] and they prostrated themselves [to the ground].

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּשָּׂ֣א עֵינָ֗יו וַיַּ֞רְא אֶת־בִּנְיָמִ֣ין אָחִיו֮ בֶּן־אִמּוֹ֒
pairs.english: And he lifted up his eyes and he saw Benjamin his brother, the son of his mother,

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר הֲזֶה֙ אֲחִיכֶ֣ם הַקָּטֹ֔ן אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֲמַרְתֶּ֖ם אֵלָ֑י
pairs.english: and he said: Is this your younger brother of whom you spoke to me?
And he said: "May G d grace you, my son," [it already having been said of the other tribes (33:5): "with which G d graced your servant"].
And Joseph hastened, for his mercies had become enkindled for his brother
and he wished to cry,
and he went into his chamber and he wept there.
And he washed his face, and he went out
and he "fortified" himself, and he said: Serve bread.

pairs.hebrew: וַיָּשִׂ֥ימוּ ל֛וֹ לְבַדּ֖וֹ וְלָהֶ֣ם לְבַדָּ֑ם וְלַמִּצְרִ֞ים הָאֹכְלִ֤ים אִתּוֹ֙ לְבַדָּ֔ם
pairs.english: And they served him by himself, and them by themselves, and the Egyptians who ate with him, by themselves.

pairs.hebrew: כִּי֩ לֹ֨א יוּכְל֜וּן הַמִּצְרִ֗ים לֶאֱכֹ֤ל אֶת־הָֽעִבְרִים֙ לֶ֔חֶם
pairs.english: For the Egyptians could not eat with the Hebrews,
for it was an abomination to the Egyptians, [the Hebrews eating sheep, which the Egyptians worshiped].
And they sat [i.e., he sat them in order] before him,
the first-born according to his seniority, and the youngest, according to his youth;
and the men expressed amaze one to the other.
And he took portions from before him to them,

pairs.hebrew: וַתֵּ֜רֶב מַשְׂאַ֧ת בִּנְיָמִ֛ן מִמַּשְׂאֹ֥ת כֻּלָּ֖ם חָמֵ֣שׁ יָד֑וֹת
pairs.english: and the portion of Benjamin was five times that of the others, [Benjamin receiving his own portion, and, in addition, those sent him by Joseph, Asnath, Menasheh, and Ephraim],
and they drank and became inebriated with him, [neither he nor they having drunk wine from the day he was sold].
And he charged the one over his house, saying:

pairs.hebrew: מַלֵּ֞א אֶת־אַמְתְּחֹ֤ת הָֽאֲנָשִׁים֙ אֹ֔כֶל כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר יוּכְל֖וּן שְׂאֵ֑ת
pairs.english: Fill the sacks of the men with food, as much as they can carry,
and place each one's money in the mouth of his sack.

pairs.hebrew: וְאֶת־גְּבִיעִ֞י גְּבִ֣יעַ הַכֶּ֗סֶף תָּשִׂים֙ בְּפִי֙ אַמְתַּ֣חַת הַקָּטֹ֔ן וְאֵ֖ת כֶּ֣סֶף שִׁבְר֑וֹ
pairs.english: And my goblet, the silver goblet, place in the mouth of the sack of the youngest and the money of his grain purchase.
And he did according to the word of Joseph, who had spoken.
Morning dawned
and the men were sent away, they and their asses.
They had left the city and had not gone far
when Joseph said to the one over his house:
Arise, pursue the men,

pairs.hebrew: וְהִשַּׂגְתָּם֙ וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ אֲלֵהֶ֔ם לָ֛מָּה שִׁלַּמְתֶּ֥ם רָעָ֖ה תַּ֥חַת טוֹבָֽה׃
pairs.english: and when you overtake them, say to them: Why did you pay evil for good?

pairs.hebrew: הֲל֣וֹא זֶ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר יִשְׁתֶּ֤ה אֲדֹנִי֙ בּ֔וֹ
