pairs.english: And Aaron spoke all the things that the L-rd spoke to Moses,
and he performed the signs before the eyes of the people.

pairs.hebrew: וַֽיַּאֲמֵ֖ן הָעָ֑ם וַֽיִּשְׁמְע֡וּ כִּֽי־פָקַ֨ד יְהֹוָ֜ה אֶת־בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל
pairs.english: And the people believed when they heard that the L-rd had remembered the children of Israel
and that He had seen their affliction.
And they bowed and they prostrated themselves.

pairs.hebrew: וְאַחַ֗ר בָּ֚אוּ מֹשֶׁ֣ה וְאַהֲרֹ֔ן וַיֹּאמְר֖וּ אֶל־פַּרְעֹ֑ה
pairs.english: And afterwards Moses and Aaron came [(but the elders, in fear of going, fell off one by one)], and they said to Pharaoh:
Thus said the L-rd, the G-d of Israel:
Send My people that they may make a festival unto Me in the desert.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר פַּרְעֹ֔ה מִ֤י יְהֹוָה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אֶשְׁמַ֣ע בְּקֹל֔וֹ לְשַׁלַּ֖ח אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל
pairs.english: And Pharaoh said: Who is the L-rd that I should hearken to His voice to send out Israel?
I do not know the L-rd
and I shall also not send out Israel.
And they said: The G-d of the Hebrews revealed Himself to us.

pairs.hebrew: נֵ֣לְכָה נָּ֡א דֶּ֩רֶךְ֩ שְׁלֹ֨שֶׁת יָמִ֜ים בַּמִּדְבָּ֗ר וְנִזְבְּחָה֙ לַֽיהֹוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֔ינוּ
pairs.english: Let us go, we pray you, a three days' distance in the desert and sacrifice to the L-rd our G-d
lest He smite us [(instead of "smite you," in deference to royalty)] with pestilence or with the sword.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֲלֵהֶם֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ מִצְרַ֔יִם לָ֚מָּה מֹשֶׁ֣ה וְאַהֲרֹ֔ן תַּפְרִ֥יעוּ אֶת־הָעָ֖ם מִֽמַּעֲשָׂ֑יו
pairs.english: And the king of Egypt said to them: Why, Moses and Aaron, would you distance the people from their work?
Go to your labors [at home (the tribe of Levi being exempt from the servitude of Egypt)].

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר פַּרְעֹ֔ה הֵן־רַבִּ֥ים עַתָּ֖ה עַ֣ם הָאָ֑רֶץ
pairs.english: And Pharaoh said: The people of the land are many now,
and you would quit them of their toils.
And Pharaoh commanded on that day
the taskmasters [Egyptians] of the people and its officers [Hebrews], saying:

pairs.hebrew: לֹ֣א תֹאסִפ֞וּן לָתֵ֨ת תֶּ֧בֶן לָעָ֛ם לִלְבֹּ֥ן הַלְּבֵנִ֖ים כִּתְמ֣וֹל שִׁלְשֹׁ֑ם
pairs.english: Do not continue to give stubble to the people [to knead with clay] to make bricks as heretofore.
Let them go and collect stubble for themselves.

pairs.hebrew: וְאֶת־מַתְכֹּ֨נֶת הַלְּבֵנִ֜ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר הֵם֩ עֹשִׂ֨ים תְּמ֤וֹל שִׁלְשֹׁם֙ תָּשִׂ֣ימוּ עֲלֵיהֶ֔ם לֹ֥א תִגְרְע֖וּ מִמֶּ֑נּוּ
pairs.english: And the quota of bricks which they made heretofore you shall impose upon them. Do not reduce it.
For they are idling.

pairs.hebrew: עַל־כֵּ֗ן הֵ֤ם צֹֽעֲקִים֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר נֵלְכָ֖ה נִזְבְּחָ֥ה לֵאלֹהֵֽינוּ׃
pairs.english: That is why are they crying out: "Let us go and sacrifice to our G-d!"
Let the labor be heavy on the men and let them do it,
and let them not speak vain words.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֵּ֨צְא֜וּ נֹגְשֵׂ֤י הָעָם֙ וְשֹׁ֣טְרָ֔יו וַיֹּאמְר֥וּ אֶל־הָעָ֖ם לֵאמֹ֑ר
pairs.english: And the taskmasters of the people went out, and its officers, and they said to the people:

pairs.hebrew: כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר פַּרְעֹ֔ה אֵינֶ֛נִּי נֹתֵ֥ן לָכֶ֖ם תֶּֽבֶן׃
pairs.english: Thus has Pharaoh said: I shall not give you stubble.

pairs.hebrew: אַתֶּ֗ם לְכ֨וּ קְח֤וּ לָכֶם֙ תֶּ֔בֶן מֵאֲשֶׁ֖ר תִּמְצָ֑אוּ
pairs.english: You, go [quickly]; take for yourselves stubble wherever you find it.
For nothing must be diminished from your work [quota].
And the people spread out throughout the land of Egypt
to gather straw for the stubble.
And the taskmasters pressed [upon them], saying:

pairs.hebrew: כַּלּ֤וּ מַעֲשֵׂיכֶם֙ דְּבַר־י֣וֹם בְּיוֹמ֔וֹ כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר בִּהְי֥וֹת הַתֶּֽבֶן׃
pairs.english: Finish your work, the [entire] day's quota in its day, as it was when the stubble was [supplied to you].

pairs.hebrew: וַיֻּכּ֗וּ שֹֽׁטְרֵי֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֲשֶׁר־שָׂ֣מוּ עֲלֵהֶ֔ם נֹגְשֵׂ֥י פַרְעֹ֖ה לֵאמֹ֑ר
pairs.english: And the officers of the children of Israel, whom the taskmasters of Pharaoh placed over them, were smitten, (the taskmasters) saying:

pairs.hebrew: מַדּ֡וּעַ לֹא֩ כִלִּיתֶ֨ם חׇקְכֶ֤ם לִלְבֹּן֙ כִּתְמ֣וֹל שִׁלְשֹׁ֔ם
pairs.english: Why did you not finish your brick-making quota as of three days ago,
both yesterday and today?

pairs.hebrew: וַיָּבֹ֗אוּ שֹֽׁטְרֵי֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַיִּצְעֲק֥וּ אֶל־פַּרְעֹ֖ה לֵאמֹ֑ר
pairs.english: And the officers of the children of Israel came and they cried out to Pharaoh, saying:
Why should you do thus to your servants!
Stubble is not given to your servants,
and bricks they say to us: Make!
And, behold, your servants are smitten, and [this thing brings] sin upon your people.
And he said: You are idlers, idlers!

pairs.hebrew: עַל־כֵּן֙ אַתֶּ֣ם אֹֽמְרִ֔ים נֵלְכָ֖ה נִזְבְּחָ֥ה לַֽיהֹוָֽה׃
pairs.english: That is why you say: Let us go and sacrifice to the L-rd.
And now, go and work.
And stubble will not be given to you,
and produce the quota of bricks!

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּרְא֞וּ שֹֽׁטְרֵ֧י בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל אֹתָ֖ם בְּרָ֣ע לֵאמֹ֑ר
pairs.english: And the officers of the children of Israel saw them [their fellow Jews who were under them] in misfortune, [the officers being constrained] to say:
Do not diminish from your bricks the quota of each day in its day.
And they [(men of Israel)] met Moses and Aaron standing opposite them
when they left Pharaoh.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ אֲלֵהֶ֔ם יֵ֧רֶא יְהֹוָ֛ה עֲלֵיכֶ֖ם וְיִשְׁפֹּ֑ט
pairs.english: And they said to them: May the L-rd reveal Himself to you and judge

pairs.hebrew: אֲשֶׁ֧ר הִבְאַשְׁתֶּ֣ם אֶת־רֵיחֵ֗נוּ בְּעֵינֵ֤י פַרְעֹה֙ וּבְעֵינֵ֣י עֲבָדָ֔יו
pairs.english: how you have made us contemptible in the eyes of Pharaoh and in the eyes of his servants
to put a sword in their hands to kill us!
And Moses returned to the L-rd and he said:
O L-rd, why have You done evil to this people [and]
why have You sent me!
And from the time I came to Pharaoh to speak in Your name,
he has done [increasingly greater] evil to this people,
and You have not saved Your people.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהֹוָה֙ אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֔ה עַתָּ֣ה תִרְאֶ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֶֽעֱשֶׂ֖ה לְפַרְעֹ֑ה
pairs.english: And the L-rd said to Moses: [Because you questioned My providence,] now you shall see — what I shall do to Pharaoh, [but not what shall be done to the seven nations when I bring Israel into Eretz Yisrael].
For with a strong hand [that I shall wield against him] he shall send them out,
and with a strong hand he shall drive them out of his land [against their will (the Jews not having time to prepare their food)].
And G-d spoke ["strong words"] to Moses [for his presumptuousness (5:22)]
and He said to him: I am the L-rd [Yod-Keh-Vav-Keh (connoting "trusted for recompense," for which reason I sent you)].

pairs.hebrew: וָאֵרָ֗א אֶל־אַבְרָהָ֛ם אֶל־יִצְחָ֥ק וְאֶֽל־יַעֲקֹ֖ב בְּאֵ֣ל שַׁדָּ֑י
pairs.english: And I appeared to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob as Kel shakkai ("the All-Sufficient G-d");
but [by] My name Yod-Keh-Vav-Keh I was not realized for them, [for I promised them but did not fulfill].
And also [when I appeared to them as Kel Shakkai], I set up My covenant with them

pairs.hebrew: לָתֵ֥ת לָהֶ֖ם אֶת־אֶ֣רֶץ כְּנָ֑עַן אֵ֛ת אֶ֥רֶץ מְגֻרֵיהֶ֖ם אֲשֶׁר־גָּ֥רוּ בָֽהּ׃
pairs.english: to give them the land of Canaan [(see Genesis 17:1 and 8, 26:3, 35:9, 11, 12)], the land of their sojournings, where they dwelt.

pairs.hebrew: וְגַ֣ם ׀ אֲנִ֣י שָׁמַ֗עְתִּי אֶֽת־נַאֲקַת֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר מִצְרַ֖יִם מַעֲבִדִ֣ים אֹתָ֑ם
pairs.english: And also, [having set up the covenant and being obliged to fulfill it], I have heard the groaning of the children of Israel under the Egyptian servitude,
and I have remembered My covenant [(Genesis 15:14) wherein I promised to punish the enslaving nation].
Therefore, [by that oath] tell the children of Israel that I am the L-rd [trusted to fulfill],
and I shall take you out from under the toils of Egypt [for thus did I promise (Genesis 15:14)],
and I will deliver you from their labors,

pairs.hebrew: וְגָאַלְתִּ֤י אֶתְכֶם֙ בִּזְר֣וֹעַ נְטוּיָ֔ה וּבִשְׁפָטִ֖ים גְּדֹלִֽים׃
pairs.english: and I will redeem you with an outstretched arm and with great judgments.

pairs.hebrew: וְלָקַחְתִּ֨י אֶתְכֶ֥ם לִי֙ לְעָ֔ם וְהָיִ֥יתִי לָכֶ֖ם לֵֽאלֹהִ֑ים
pairs.english: And I will take you to Me as a people, and I will be to you as a G-d;
and you will know that I am the L-rd your G-d
who took you out from under the toils of Egypt.

pairs.hebrew: וְהֵבֵאתִ֤י אֶתְכֶם֙ אֶל־הָאָ֔רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֤ר נָשָׂ֙אתִי֙ אֶת־יָדִ֔י לָתֵ֣ת אֹתָ֔הּ לְאַבְרָהָ֥ם לְיִצְחָ֖ק וּֽלְיַעֲקֹ֑ב
pairs.english: And I shall bring you to the land which I lifted My hand [i.e., which I swore by My throne] to give to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
And I shall give it to you as an inheritance.
I am the L-rd.
And Moses spoke thus to the children of Israel

pairs.hebrew: וְלֹ֤א שָֽׁמְעוּ֙ אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֔ה מִקֹּ֣צֶר ר֔וּחַ וּמֵעֲבֹדָ֖ה קָשָֽׁה׃ {פ}
pairs.english: and they did not hearken to Moses [i.e., they were not comforted by him], for shortness of breath [in anguish] and soreness of toil.
And the L-rd spoke
to Moses, saying:
Come and speak to Pharaoh, king of Egypt,
that he send the children of Israel out of his land.

pairs.hebrew: וַיְדַבֵּ֣ר מֹשֶׁ֔ה לִפְנֵ֥י יְהֹוָ֖ה לֵאמֹ֑ר הֵ֤ן בְּנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ לֹֽא־שָׁמְע֣וּ אֵלַ֔י
pairs.english: And Moses spoke before the L-rd, saying: If the children of Israel did not heed me,
how should Pharaoh heed me!
And I am of uncircumcised [i.e., occluded] lips.
And the L-rd spoke to Moses and to Aaron [who, because of Moses' demurral (above) was made his spokesman],

pairs.hebrew: וַיְצַוֵּם֙ אֶל־בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְאֶל־פַּרְעֹ֖ה מֶ֣לֶךְ מִצְרָ֑יִם
pairs.english: and He charged them concerning the children of Israel and concerning [their embassy to] Pharaoh, king of Egypt [(the charge continuing, Ibid. 29)]
to take the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt.
These are the heads of their fathers' houses:

pairs.hebrew: בְּנֵ֨י רְאוּבֵ֜ן בְּכֹ֣ר יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל חֲנ֤וֹךְ וּפַלּוּא֙ חֶצְרֹ֣ן וְכַרְמִ֔י
pairs.english: the sons of Reuven, the first-born of Israel [(The genealogy of Moses and Aaron is traced from its beginning in the line of Jacob)]: Chanoch and Falu, Chetzron and Carmi.
These are the families of Reuven.

pairs.hebrew: וּבְנֵ֣י שִׁמְע֗וֹן יְמוּאֵ֨ל וְיָמִ֤ין וְאֹ֙הַד֙ וְיָכִ֣ין וְצֹ֔חַר וְשָׁא֖וּל בֶּן־הַֽכְּנַעֲנִ֑ית
pairs.english: And the sons of Shimon: Yemuel and Yamin and Ohad and Yachin and Tzochar and Shaul the son of the Canaanitess.
These are the families of Shimon.

pairs.hebrew: וְאֵ֨לֶּה שְׁמ֤וֹת בְּנֵֽי־לֵוִי֙ לְתֹ֣לְדֹתָ֔ם גֵּרְשׁ֕וֹן וּקְהָ֖ת וּמְרָרִ֑י
pairs.english: And these are the names of the sons of Levi according to their births: Gershon and Kehoth and Merari.

pairs.hebrew: וּשְׁנֵי֙ חַיֵּ֣י לֵוִ֔י שֶׁ֧בַע וּשְׁלֹשִׁ֛ים וּמְאַ֖ת שָׁנָֽה׃
pairs.english: And the years of the life of Levi were one hundred and thirty-seven years [(Levi's years being mentioned to apprise us of the years of the bondage, there being no bondage while any of Jacob's sons lived, and Levi being the longest-lived of them)].
The sons of Gershon:
Livni and Shimi, according to their families.

pairs.hebrew: וּבְנֵ֣י קְהָ֔ת עַמְרָ֣ם וְיִצְהָ֔ר וְחֶבְר֖וֹן וְעֻזִּיאֵ֑ל
pairs.english: And the sons of Kehoth: Amram and Yitzhar and Chevron and Uziel.

pairs.hebrew: וּשְׁנֵי֙ חַיֵּ֣י קְהָ֔ת שָׁלֹ֧שׁ וּשְׁלֹשִׁ֛ים וּמְאַ֖ת שָׁנָֽה׃
pairs.english: And the years of the life of Kehoth were one hundred and thirty-three years [(whence it is derived that the four hundred years of Israel's servitude (Genesis 15:13) date from the birth of Isaac)].
And the sons of Merari: Machli and Mushi.
These are the families of Levi according to their births.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּקַּ֨ח עַמְרָ֜ם אֶת־יוֹכֶ֤בֶד דֹּֽדָתוֹ֙ ל֣וֹ לְאִשָּׁ֔ה
pairs.english: And Amram took Yocheved his aunt [his father's sister; the daughter of Levi, the sister of Kehoth] to himself as a wife.
And she bore to him Aaron and Moses.

pairs.hebrew: וּשְׁנֵי֙ חַיֵּ֣י עַמְרָ֔ם שֶׁ֧בַע וּשְׁלֹשִׁ֛ים וּמְאַ֖ת שָׁנָֽה׃
pairs.english: And the years of the life of Amram were one hundred and thirty-seven years.
And the sons of Yitzhar:
Korach and Nefeg and Zichri.
And the sons of Uziel:
Mishael and Eltzafan and Zichri.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּקַּ֨ח אַהֲרֹ֜ן אֶת־אֱלִישֶׁ֧בַע בַּת־עַמִּינָדָ֛ב אֲח֥וֹת נַחְשׁ֖וֹן ל֣וֹ לְאִשָּׁ֑ה
pairs.english: And Aaron took Elisheva the daughter of Aminadav, the sister of Nachshon, to himself as a wife [(whence it is derived that in taking a wife one should inquire about her brothers)],

pairs.hebrew: וַתֵּ֣לֶד ל֗וֹ אֶת־נָדָב֙ וְאֶת־אֲבִיה֔וּא אֶת־אֶלְעָזָ֖ר וְאֶת־אִֽיתָמָֽר׃
pairs.english: and she bore to him Nadav and Avihu and Elazar and Ithamar.
And the sons of Korach: Assir and Elkanah and Aviasaf.
These are the families of the Korchi.

pairs.hebrew: וְאֶלְעָזָ֨ר בֶּֽן־אַהֲרֹ֜ן לָקַֽח־ל֨וֹ מִבְּנ֤וֹת פּֽוּטִיאֵל֙ ל֣וֹ לְאִשָּׁ֔ה
pairs.english: And Elazar the son of Aaron took one of the daughters of Putiel [(of the seed of Yithro, who fattened (pitem) calves for idolatry, and of the seed of Joseph, who made light of (pitpet) his evil inclination (in resisting Potiphar's wife)] to himself as a wife,
and she bore Pinchas unto him.
These are the heads of the fathers of the Levites according to their families.

pairs.hebrew: ה֥וּא אַהֲרֹ֖ן וּמֹשֶׁ֑ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר אָמַ֤ר יְהֹוָה֙ לָהֶ֔ם
pairs.english: It [i.e., the afore-mentioned] are [the] Aaron and Moses whom the L-rd told:

pairs.hebrew: הוֹצִ֜יאוּ אֶת־בְּנֵ֧י יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל מֵאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרַ֖יִם עַל־צִבְאֹתָֽם׃
pairs.english: Take the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt with their hosts [(all of their hosts according to their tribes)].

pairs.hebrew: הֵ֗ם הַֽמְדַבְּרִים֙ אֶל־פַּרְעֹ֣ה מֶֽלֶךְ־מִצְרַ֔יִם לְהוֹצִ֥יא אֶת־בְּנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל מִמִּצְרָ֑יִם
pairs.english: They were the ones who spoke to Pharaoh, king of Egypt, to take the children of Israel out of Egypt. [Those who were commanded — those are the ones who fulfilled.]
It was [the same] Moses and Aaron [(single-minded) in their mission and in their righteousness].
And it was on the day that the L-rd spoke to Moses
in the land of Egypt

pairs.hebrew: וַיְדַבֵּ֧ר יְהֹוָ֛ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֥ה לֵּאמֹ֖ר אֲנִ֣י יְהֹוָ֑ה
pairs.english: that the L-rd spoke to Moses saying [(a reversion to (11) after the genealogical hiatus)]: I am the L-rd [trusted to send you and to fulfill My embassy].
Speak to Pharaoh, king of Egypt,
all that I speak to you.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֖ה לִפְנֵ֣י יְהֹוָ֑ה הֵ֤ן אֲנִי֙ עֲרַ֣ל שְׂפָתַ֔יִם
pairs.english: And Moses said before the L-rd: I am uncircumcised [i.e., occluded] of lips.
How, then, will Pharaoh heed me! [(a reversion to (12)].

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהֹוָה֙ אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֔ה רְאֵ֛ה נְתַתִּ֥יךָ אֱלֹהִ֖ים לְפַרְעֹ֑ה
pairs.english: And the L-rd said to Moses: See, I have made you an overlord to Pharaoh,
and Aaron your brother shall be your spokesman.
You speak [(once, for each embassy)] all that I shall command you,
and Aaron your brother shall speak to Pharaoh, [elaborating on what you have said],
that he send the children of Israel from his land.
And I shall harden the heart of Pharaoh [since he has inveighed against Me and since I know that he is not inclined to repent wholeheartedly],
and I shall [in consequence] increase My signs and My wonders in the land of Egypt [for the "edification" of Israel].
And Pharaoh will not pay heed to you
and I shall place My hand against Egypt [to smite them],

pairs.hebrew: וְהוֹצֵאתִ֨י אֶת־צִבְאֹתַ֜י אֶת־עַמִּ֤י בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם בִּשְׁפָטִ֖ים גְּדֹלִֽים׃
pairs.english: and I shall bring forth My hosts, My people, the children of Israel, from the land of Egypt with great judgments.
And Egypt will know that I am the L-rd
when I stretch forth My hand against Egypt;
and I shall take out the children of Israel from their midst.

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּ֥עַשׂ מֹשֶׁ֖ה וְאַהֲרֹ֑ן כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר צִוָּ֧ה יְהֹוָ֛ה אֹתָ֖ם
pairs.english: And Moses and Aaron did as the L-rd commanded them;
so did they do.
And Moses was eighty years old
and Aaron was eighty-three years old
when they spoke to Pharaoh.
And the L-rd said
to Moses and to Aaron:

pairs.hebrew: כִּי֩ יְדַבֵּ֨ר אֲלֵכֶ֤ם פַּרְעֹה֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר תְּנ֥וּ לָכֶ֖ם מוֹפֵ֑ת
pairs.english: When Pharaoh speaks to you, saying: Give us a wonder [i.e., a sign proving the potency of your sender],

pairs.hebrew: וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ אֶֽל־אַהֲרֹ֗ן קַ֧ח אֶֽת־מַטְּךָ֛ וְהַשְׁלֵ֥ךְ לִפְנֵֽי־פַרְעֹ֖ה
pairs.english: then say to Aaron: Take your staff and cast it before Pharaoh;
it shall be a serpent.

pairs.hebrew: וַיָּבֹ֨א מֹשֶׁ֤ה וְאַהֲרֹן֙ אֶל־פַּרְעֹ֔ה וַיַּ֣עֲשׂוּ כֵ֔ן כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר צִוָּ֣ה יְהֹוָ֑ה
pairs.english: And Moses and Aaron came to Pharaoh and they did thus, as the L-rd had commanded.

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּשְׁלֵ֨ךְ אַהֲרֹ֜ן אֶת־מַטֵּ֗הוּ לִפְנֵ֥י פַרְעֹ֛ה וְלִפְנֵ֥י עֲבָדָ֖יו
pairs.english: And Aaron cast his staff before Pharaoh and before his servants
and it became a serpent.
And Pharaoh, too, called to the wise men and the magicians;

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּֽעֲשׂ֨וּ גַם־הֵ֜ם חַרְטֻמֵּ֥י מִצְרַ֛יִם בְּלַהֲטֵיהֶ֖ם כֵּֽן׃
pairs.english: and the necromancers of Egypt did likewise through their charms.
And each cast down his staff and they became serpents,
and the staff of Aaron [(i.e., after the serpent had reverted to a staff)] swallowed their staffs.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֶּֽחֱזַק֙ לֵ֣ב פַּרְעֹ֔ה וְלֹ֥א שָׁמַ֖ע אֲלֵהֶ֑ם
pairs.english: And Pharaoh's heart became strong and he did not pay heed to them,
as the L-rd had spoken.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהֹוָה֙ אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֔ה כָּבֵ֖ד לֵ֣ב פַּרְעֹ֑ה
pairs.english: And the L-rd said to Moses: The heart of Pharaoh is hard.
He refuses to send the people.

pairs.hebrew: לֵ֣ךְ אֶל־פַּרְעֹ֞ה בַּבֹּ֗קֶר הִנֵּה֙ יֹצֵ֣א הַמַּ֔יְמָה
pairs.english: Go to Pharaoh in the morning. Behold, he goes out to the water in the morning [to ease himself by the Nile (in secret, so that his people not be disabused of his godhood)].
And stand opposite him on the bank of the Nile;
and the staff which turned into a serpent take in your hand.

pairs.hebrew: וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ אֵלָ֗יו יְהֹוָ֞ה אֱלֹהֵ֤י הָעִבְרִים֙ שְׁלָחַ֤נִי אֵלֶ֙יךָ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר
pairs.english: And you shall say to him: The L-rd, the G-d of the Hebrews, has sent me to you, saying:
Send out My people that they may serve Me in the desert;
and you have not heeded (this) until now.

pairs.hebrew: כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהֹוָ֔ה בְּזֹ֣את תֵּדַ֔ע כִּ֖י אֲנִ֣י יְהֹוָ֑ה
pairs.english: Thus says the L-rd: By this you will know that I am the L-rd.

pairs.hebrew: הִנֵּ֨ה אָנֹכִ֜י מַכֶּ֣ה ׀ בַּמַּטֶּ֣ה אֲשֶׁר־בְּיָדִ֗י עַל־הַמַּ֛יִם אֲשֶׁ֥ר בַּיְאֹ֖ר
pairs.english: Behold, I will strike with the staff in my hand the waters of the Nile
and they shall turn to blood, [G-d first smiting their god, the Nile (their water source in the absence of rain), and then, they themselves.]
And the fish in the Nile shall die, and the Nile shall reek,
and the Egyptians shall weary themselves [in quest of a "cure"] to drink water from the Nile.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהֹוָ֜ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֗ה אֱמֹ֣ר אֶֽל־אַהֲרֹ֡ן קַ֣ח מַטְּךָ֣ וּנְטֵֽה־יָדְךָ֩ עַל־מֵימֵ֨י מִצְרַ֜יִם
pairs.english: And the L-rd said to Moses: Say to Aaron: Take your staff and stretch out your hand over the waters of Egypt [(Because the Nile "protected" Moses when he was cast into it (as an infant), it was not smitten through him, but through Aaron for the plagues of blood and frogs)],

pairs.hebrew: עַֽל־נַהֲרֹתָ֣ם ׀ עַל־יְאֹרֵיהֶ֣ם וְעַל־אַגְמֵיהֶ֗ם וְעַ֛ל כׇּל־מִקְוֵ֥ה מֵימֵיהֶ֖ם וְיִֽהְיוּ־דָ֑ם
pairs.english: over their rivers, over their canals, over their standing waters, and over all their gatherings of water, and they shall be blood.

pairs.hebrew: וְהָ֤יָה דָם֙ בְּכׇל־אֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם וּבָעֵצִ֖ים וּבָאֲבָנִֽים׃
pairs.english: And there will be blood in all the land of Egypt [even in the bath-houses and house-tubs] and in [water in] wood and stone [vessels].

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּֽעֲשׂוּ־כֵן֩ מֹשֶׁ֨ה וְאַהֲרֹ֜ן כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר ׀ צִוָּ֣ה יְהֹוָ֗ה
pairs.english: And Moses and Aaron did thus, as the L-rd had commanded.

pairs.hebrew: וַיָּ֤רֶם בַּמַּטֶּה֙ וַיַּ֤ךְ אֶת־הַמַּ֙יִם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בַּיְאֹ֔ר לְעֵינֵ֣י פַרְעֹ֔ה וּלְעֵינֵ֖י עֲבָדָ֑יו
pairs.english: And he raised the staff and he smote the waters in the Nile before the eyes of Pharaoh and before the eyes of his servants.
And all the water in the Nile turned to blood.
And the fish in the Nile died, and the Nile reeked,
and the Egyptians could not drink water from the Nile.
And the blood was throughout the land of Egypt.
And the necromancers of Egypt did likewise through their charms.
And Pharaoh's heart was strengthened and he did not pay heed to them,
as the L-rd had spoken.
And Pharaoh turned and came to his house,
and he did not set his heart to this [the plague of blood], too, [as well as (not) to the staff's turning into a serpent].

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּחְפְּר֧וּ כׇל־מִצְרַ֛יִם סְבִיבֹ֥ת הַיְאֹ֖ר מַ֣יִם לִשְׁתּ֑וֹת
pairs.english: And all of Egypt dug around the Nile for water to drink,

pairs.hebrew: כִּ֣י לֹ֤א יָֽכְלוּ֙ לִשְׁתֹּ֔ת מִמֵּימֵ֖י הַיְאֹֽר׃
pairs.english: for they could not drink from the waters of the Nile.
And seven days [of plague] were completed
after the L-rd had smitten the Nile [before it returned to its original state, each plague obtaining for a quarter of a month, and three-quarters for warning.]

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהֹוָה֙ אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֔ה בֹּ֖א אֶל־פַּרְעֹ֑ה וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ אֵלָ֗יו
pairs.english: And the L-rd said to Moses: Come to Pharaoh and say to him:

pairs.hebrew: כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהֹוָ֔ה שַׁלַּ֥ח אֶת־עַמִּ֖י וְיַֽעַבְדֻֽנִי׃
pairs.english: Thus said the L-rd: Send out My people and let them serve Me.
And if you are a refuser, (not) to send out,
behold, I shall smite all of your border with frogs.
And the Nile shall swarm frogs,

pairs.hebrew: וְעָלוּ֙ וּבָ֣אוּ בְּבֵיתֶ֔ךָ וּבַחֲדַ֥ר מִשְׁכָּבְךָ֖ וְעַל־מִטָּתֶ֑ךָ
pairs.english: and they shall go up [from the Nile] and come [first] into your house, [Pharaoh having counseled first against the Jews (1:9)], and into your bed chamber and upon your bed, and
[then] into the house of your servants, and into your people, and into your ovens and into your kneading troughs.
And in you [i.e., in your innards] and in your people and in all of your servants
shall the frogs go up.
And the L-rd said to Moses: Say to Aaron:

pairs.hebrew: נְטֵ֤ה אֶת־יָדְךָ֙ בְּמַטֶּ֔ךָ עַ֨ל־הַנְּהָרֹ֔ת עַל־הַיְאֹרִ֖ים וְעַל־הָאֲגַמִּ֑ים
pairs.english: Stretch your hand with the staff over the rivers, over the water courses, and over the ponds,
and bring up the frogs upon the land of Egypt.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֵּ֤ט אַהֲרֹן֙ אֶת־יָד֔וֹ עַ֖ל מֵימֵ֣י מִצְרָ֑יִם
pairs.english: And Aaron stretched forth his hand over the waters of Egypt,
and the frog [swarm] came up and covered the land of Egypt.
And the necromancers did likewise through their charms,
and the frogs came up upon the land of Egypt.
And Pharaoh called to Moses and to Aaron and he said:

pairs.hebrew: הַעְתִּ֣ירוּ אֶל־יְהֹוָ֔ה וְיָסֵר֙ הַֽצְפַרְדְּעִ֔ים מִמֶּ֖נִּי וּמֵֽעַמִּ֑י
pairs.english: Entreat the L-rd that he remove the frogs from me and from my people,
and I will send out the people and they will sacrifice to the L-rd.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֣ה לְפַרְעֹה֮ הִתְפָּאֵ֣ר עָלַי֒ לְמָתַ֣י ׀ אַעְתִּ֣יר לְךָ֗ וְלַעֲבָדֶ֙יךָ֙ וּֽלְעַמְּךָ֔
pairs.english: And Moses said to Pharaoh: "Presume" over me as to when I should entreat for you and for your servants and for your people
to cut off the frogs from you and from your houses.
Only in the Nile shall they remain.
And he said: [Entreat today] for tomorrow [i.e., that they be cut off tomorrow].
And he said: As you say.
So that you know that there is none like the L-rd our G-d.

pairs.hebrew: וְסָר֣וּ הַֽצְפַרְדְּעִ֗ים מִמְּךָ֙ וּמִבָּ֣תֶּ֔יךָ וּמֵעֲבָדֶ֖יךָ וּמֵעַמֶּ֑ךָ
pairs.english: And the frogs will depart from you and from your houses and from your servants and from your people;
only in the Nile shall they remain.
And Moses and Aaron went out from Pharaoh

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּצְעַ֤ק מֹשֶׁה֙ אֶל־יְהֹוָ֔ה עַל־דְּבַ֥ר הַֽצְפַרְדְּעִ֖ים אֲשֶׁר־שָׂ֥ם לְפַרְעֹֽה׃
pairs.english: and Moses cried out to the L-rd over the frogs which He had brought upon Pharaoh.
And the L-rd did according to the word of Moses
and the frogs died out of the houses, out of the courtyards, and out of the fields.
And they piled them up in heaps,
and the land reeked.
And Pharaoh saw that there was relief,
and his heart was hardened and he did not heed them,
as the L-rd had spoken [(7:4)].
And the L-rd said to Moses: Say to Aaron:

Stretch out your staff and strike the dust of the earth [(It was not fitting that the earth be struck by Moses, for it had "protected" him when he had killed the Egyptian, for which reason Aaron was bidden to strike it)],
and it will be lice in all the land of Egypt.

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּֽעֲשׂוּ־כֵ֗ן וַיֵּט֩ אַהֲרֹ֨ן אֶת־יָד֤וֹ בְמַטֵּ֙הוּ֙ וַיַּךְ֙ אֶת־עֲפַ֣ר הָאָ֔רֶץ
pairs.english: And they did so. And Aaron stretched forth his hand with his staff and he struck the dust of the earth,
and the louse [swarm] was in man and beast.

pairs.hebrew: כׇּל־עֲפַ֥ר הָאָ֛רֶץ הָיָ֥ה כִנִּ֖ים בְּכׇל־אֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃
pairs.english: All the dust of the earth was lice in the whole land of Egypt.

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּעֲשׂוּ־כֵ֨ן הַחַרְטֻמִּ֧ים בְּלָטֵיהֶ֛ם לְהוֹצִ֥יא אֶת־הַכִּנִּ֖ים וְלֹ֣א יָכֹ֑לוּ
pairs.english: And the necromancers did likewise with their charms to bring forth the lice, [attempting to create them and bring them forth from some other place], but they could not do so, [for the demon (of their art) is ineffective with a creature smaller than a barley corn].
And the louse [swarm] was in man and beast.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּאמְר֤וּ הַֽחַרְטֻמִּם֙ אֶל־פַּרְעֹ֔ה אֶצְבַּ֥ע אֱלֹהִ֖ים הִ֑וא
pairs.english: And the necromancers said to Pharaoh: It is the finger of G-d, [and not magic].
And the heart of Pharaoh was strengthened and he did not heed them,
as the L-rd had spoken [(7:4)].

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהֹוָ֜ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֗ה הַשְׁכֵּ֤ם בַּבֹּ֙קֶר֙ וְהִתְיַצֵּב֙ לִפְנֵ֣י פַרְעֹ֔ה הִנֵּ֖ה יוֹצֵ֣א הַמָּ֑יְמָה
pairs.english: And the L-rd said to Moses: Rise early in the morning and appear before Pharaoh. Behold, he goes out to the water.
And you shall say to him: Thus said the L-rd:
Send out My people and let them serve Me.
For if you do not send My people,

pairs.hebrew: הִנְנִי֩ מַשְׁלִ֨יחַ בְּךָ֜ וּבַעֲבָדֶ֧יךָ וּֽבְעַמְּךָ֛ וּבְבָתֶּ֖יךָ אֶת־הֶעָרֹ֑ב
pairs.english: I shall incite, against you and your servants and your people and your houses, the mixed multitude [of wild animals, serpents, and scorpions].

pairs.hebrew: וּמָ֨לְא֜וּ בָּתֵּ֤י מִצְרַ֙יִם֙ אֶת־הֶ֣עָרֹ֔ב וְגַ֥ם הָאֲדָמָ֖ה אֲשֶׁר־הֵ֥ם עָלֶֽיהָ׃
pairs.english: And the houses of Egypt will be filled with the mixed multitude, and also the ground on which they are.

pairs.hebrew: וְהִפְלֵיתִי֩ בַיּ֨וֹם הַה֜וּא אֶת־אֶ֣רֶץ גֹּ֗שֶׁן אֲשֶׁ֤ר עַמִּי֙ עֹמֵ֣ד עָלֶ֔יהָ
pairs.english: And I will set apart on that day the land of Goshen on which My people stands,
that there be no mixed multitude there.

pairs.hebrew: לְמַ֣עַן תֵּדַ֔ע כִּ֛י אֲנִ֥י יְהֹוָ֖ה בְּקֶ֥רֶב הָאָֽרֶץ׃
pairs.english: So that you know that I am the L-rd [whose decree is fulfilled] in the midst of the land [though My shechinah is in the heavens].

pairs.hebrew: וְשַׂמְתִּ֣י פְדֻ֔ת בֵּ֥ין עַמִּ֖י וּבֵ֣ין עַמֶּ֑ךָ
pairs.english: And I will make a deliverance [which shall distinguish] between My people and your people.
Tomorrow will this sign be.
And the L-rd did so,

pairs.hebrew: וַיָּבֹא֙ עָרֹ֣ב כָּבֵ֔ד בֵּ֥יתָה פַרְעֹ֖ה וּבֵ֣ית עֲבָדָ֑יו
pairs.english: and a sore mixed multitude came into the house of Pharaoh and into the house of his servants;

pairs.hebrew: וּבְכׇל־אֶ֧רֶץ מִצְרַ֛יִם תִּשָּׁחֵ֥ת הָאָ֖רֶץ מִפְּנֵ֥י הֶעָרֹֽב׃
pairs.english: and in all the land of Egypt the land was being ravaged by the mixed multitude.
And Pharaoh called to Moses and to Aaron and he said:
Go and slaughter to G-d in the land, [in your place; not in the desert].

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֗ה לֹ֤א נָכוֹן֙ לַעֲשׂ֣וֹת כֵּ֔ן
pairs.english: And Moses said: It is not right to do this,

pairs.hebrew: כִּ֚י תּוֹעֲבַ֣ת מִצְרַ֔יִם נִזְבַּ֖ח לַיהֹוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֑ינוּ
pairs.english: for the abomination of Egypt [i.e., what they hold sacred] we will slaughter to the L-rd our G-d.

pairs.hebrew: הֵ֣ן נִזְבַּ֞ח אֶת־תּוֹעֲבַ֥ת מִצְרַ֛יִם לְעֵינֵיהֶ֖ם וְלֹ֥א יִסְקְלֻֽנוּ׃
pairs.english: Will we slaughter the abomination of Egypt before their eyes and they not stone us?
We shall go a three days' journey into the desert,

pairs.hebrew: וְזָבַ֙חְנוּ֙ לַֽיהֹוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֔ינוּ כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר יֹאמַ֥ר אֵלֵֽינוּ׃
pairs.english: and we shall sacrifice to the L-rd our G-d, as He shall say to us.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר פַּרְעֹ֗ה אָנֹכִ֞י אֲשַׁלַּ֤ח אֶתְכֶם֙ וּזְבַחְתֶּ֞ם לַיהֹוָ֤ה אֱלֹֽהֵיכֶם֙ בַּמִּדְבָּ֔ר
pairs.english: And Pharaoh said: I shall send you, and you shall sacrifice to the L-rd your G-d in the desert.
Only do not go too far;
entreat for me.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֗ה הִנֵּ֨ה אָנֹכִ֜י יוֹצֵ֤א מֵֽעִמָּךְ֙ וְהַעְתַּרְתִּ֣י אֶל־יְהֹוָ֔ה
pairs.english: And Moses said: Behold, I am leaving you, and I shall entreat the L-rd,

pairs.hebrew: וְסָ֣ר הֶעָרֹ֗ב מִפַּרְעֹ֛ה מֵעֲבָדָ֥יו וּמֵעַמּ֖וֹ מָחָ֑ר
pairs.english: and the mixed multitude shall depart from Pharaoh, from his servants, and from his people tomorrow.

pairs.hebrew: רַ֗ק אַל־יֹסֵ֤ף פַּרְעֹה֙ הָתֵ֔ל לְבִלְתִּי֙ שַׁלַּ֣ח אֶת־הָעָ֔ם לִזְבֹּ֖חַ לַֽיהֹוָֽה׃
pairs.english: Only let Pharaoh not continue to dissemble, not to send the people to sacrifice to the L-rd.
And Moses went out from Pharaoh
and he prayed [devoutly] to the L-rd.
And the L-rd did as Moses spoke
and He removed the mixed multitude from Pharaoh, from his servants, and from his people;
not one remained. [(But they did not die, as the frogs did, so that no benefit be derived from their hides.)]

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּכְבֵּ֤ד פַּרְעֹה֙ אֶת־לִבּ֔וֹ גַּ֖ם בַּפַּ֣עַם הַזֹּ֑את
pairs.english: And Pharaoh hardened his heart this time as well,
and he did not send out the people.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהֹוָה֙ אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֔ה בֹּ֖א אֶל־פַּרְעֹ֑ה וְדִבַּרְתָּ֣ אֵלָ֗יו
pairs.english: And the L-rd said to Moses: Come to Pharaoh and speak to him:
Thus said the L-rd, the G-d of the Hebrews:
Send out My people and let them serve Me.
For if you refuse to send (them)
and continue holding them,

pairs.hebrew: הִנֵּ֨ה יַד־יְהֹוָ֜ה הוֹיָ֗ה בְּמִקְנְךָ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בַּשָּׂדֶ֔ה
pairs.english: Behold, the hand of the L-rd is in your cattle in the field,
in the horses, in the asses, in the camels, in the herd, and in the flock —
a very sore pestilence.

pairs.hebrew: וְהִפְלָ֣ה יְהֹוָ֔ה בֵּ֚ין מִקְנֵ֣ה יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וּבֵ֖ין מִקְנֵ֣ה מִצְרָ֑יִם
pairs.english: And the L-rd will distinguish between the cattle of Israel and the cattle of Egypt,
and there will die naught of all that appertains to the children of Israel.
And the L-rd set a time, saying:

pairs.hebrew: מָחָ֗ר יַעֲשֶׂ֧ה יְהֹוָ֛ה הַדָּבָ֥ר הַזֶּ֖ה בָּאָֽרֶץ׃
pairs.english: Tomorrow the L-rd shall do this thing in the land.
And the L-rd did this thing on the morrow,
and all the cattle of Egypt died.
And of the cattle of the children of Israel, not one died.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּשְׁלַ֣ח פַּרְעֹ֔ה וְהִנֵּ֗ה לֹא־מֵ֛ת מִמִּקְנֵ֥ה יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל עַד־אֶחָ֑ד
pairs.english: And Pharaoh sent and, behold, not even one had died of the cattle of Israel;

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּכְבַּד֙ לֵ֣ב פַּרְעֹ֔ה וְלֹ֥א שִׁלַּ֖ח אֶת־הָעָֽם׃ {פ}
pairs.english: and Pharaoh's heart was hardened and he did not send out the people.
And the L-rd said to Moses and to Aaron:

pairs.hebrew: קְח֤וּ לָכֶם֙ מְלֹ֣א חׇפְנֵיכֶ֔ם פִּ֖יחַ כִּבְשָׁ֑ן
pairs.english: Take for yourselves your full handfuls of furnace-soot,
and let Moses fling it heavenwards before the eyes of Pharaoh.
And it shall be dust over all the land of Egypt.

pairs.hebrew: וְהָיָ֨ה עַל־הָאָדָ֜ם וְעַל־הַבְּהֵמָ֗ה לִשְׁחִ֥ין פֹּרֵ֛חַ אֲבַעְבֻּעֹ֖ת בְּכׇל־אֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃
pairs.english: And it will be upon man and beast, boils sprouting blisters in all the land of Egypt.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּקְח֞וּ אֶת־פִּ֣יחַ הַכִּבְשָׁ֗ן וַיַּֽעַמְדוּ֙ לִפְנֵ֣י פַרְעֹ֔ה
pairs.english: And they took the furnace-soot and stood before Pharaoh,
and Moses flung it heavenwards,

pairs.hebrew: וַיְהִ֗י שְׁחִין֙ אֲבַעְבֻּעֹ֔ת פֹּרֵ֕חַ בָּאָדָ֖ם וּבַבְּהֵמָֽה׃
pairs.english: and it became blister-sprouting boils in man and beast [(those beasts which the G-d-fearing among the Egyptians had taken into their houses during the pestilence (compare 20), only those in the field dying (3)].

pairs.hebrew: וְלֹֽא־יָכְל֣וּ הַֽחַרְטֻמִּ֗ים לַעֲמֹ֛ד לִפְנֵ֥י מֹשֶׁ֖ה מִפְּנֵ֣י הַשְּׁחִ֑ין
pairs.english: And the necromancers could not stand before Moses because of the boils;
for the boils were in the necromancers and in all of Egypt.

pairs.hebrew: וַיְחַזֵּ֤ק יְהֹוָה֙ אֶת־לֵ֣ב פַּרְעֹ֔ה וְלֹ֥א שָׁמַ֖ע אֲלֵהֶ֑ם
pairs.english: And the L-rd strengthened Pharaoh's heart and he did not heed them,
as the L-rd had said to Moses.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהֹוָה֙ אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֔ה הַשְׁכֵּ֣ם בַּבֹּ֔קֶר וְהִתְיַצֵּ֖ב לִפְנֵ֣י פַרְעֹ֑ה וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ אֵלָ֗יו
pairs.english: And the L-rd said to Moses: Rise early in the morning and appear before Pharaoh, and say to him:
Thus said the L-rd, the G-d of the Hebrews:
Send out My people and let them serve Me.

pairs.hebrew: כִּ֣י ׀ בַּפַּ֣עַם הַזֹּ֗את אֲנִ֨י שֹׁלֵ֜חַ אֶת־כׇּל־מַגֵּפֹתַי֙ אֶֽל־לִבְּךָ֔ וּבַעֲבָדֶ֖יךָ וּבְעַמֶּ֑ךָ
pairs.english: For this time I am sending all of My plagues against your heart and in your servants and in your people,

pairs.hebrew: בַּעֲב֣וּר תֵּדַ֔ע כִּ֛י אֵ֥ין כָּמֹ֖נִי בְּכׇל־הָאָֽרֶץ׃
pairs.english: so that you know that there is none like Me in the whole land.

pairs.hebrew: כִּ֤י עַתָּה֙ שָׁלַ֣חְתִּי אֶת־יָדִ֔י וָאַ֥ךְ אוֹתְךָ֛ וְאֶֽת־עַמְּךָ֖ בַּדָּ֑בֶר
pairs.english: For now [in the plague of pestilence] I could have stretched forth My hand and smitten you and your people with pestilence,
and you would have gone lost from the earth.

pairs.hebrew: וְאוּלָ֗ם בַּעֲב֥וּר זֹאת֙ הֶעֱמַדְתִּ֔יךָ בַּעֲב֖וּר הַרְאֹתְךָ֣ אֶת־כֹּחִ֑י
pairs.english: But, because of this I have preserved you, in order to show you My might,
and that My name be spoken in all the land.
You still tread My people down,
not letting them go.

pairs.hebrew: הִנְנִ֤י מַמְטִיר֙ כָּעֵ֣ת מָחָ֔ר בָּרָ֖ד כָּבֵ֣ד מְאֹ֑ד
pairs.english: Behold, I shall rain down as at this time tomorrow [(when the sun reaches this mark that I have inscribed on the wall)] a very sore hail,

pairs.hebrew: אֲשֶׁ֨ר לֹא־הָיָ֤ה כָמֹ֙הוּ֙ בְּמִצְרַ֔יִם לְמִן־הַיּ֥וֹם הִוָּסְדָ֖הֿ וְעַד־עָֽתָּה׃
pairs.english: the like of which has not been in Egypt from the day of its founding until now.

pairs.hebrew: וְעַתָּ֗ה שְׁלַ֤ח הָעֵז֙ אֶֽת־מִקְנְךָ֔ וְאֵ֛ת כׇּל־אֲשֶׁ֥ר לְךָ֖ בַּשָּׂדֶ֑ה
pairs.english: And now, send, gather in your cattle and everything you have in the field.

pairs.hebrew: כׇּל־הָאָדָ֨ם וְהַבְּהֵמָ֜ה אֲשֶֽׁר־יִמָּצֵ֣א בַשָּׂדֶ֗ה וְלֹ֤א יֵֽאָסֵף֙ הַבַּ֔יְתָה
pairs.english: Every man and beast found in the field which will not be taken into the house —
the hail will descend upon them and they will die.
Those who feared the word of the L-rd among the servants of Pharaoh
drove their servants and their cattle into the houses.
And whoever did not take to heart the word of the L-rd
left his servants and his cattle in the field.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהֹוָ֜ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֗ה נְטֵ֤ה אֶת־יָֽדְךָ֙ עַל־הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם
pairs.english: And the L-rd said to Moses: Stretch your hand towards the heavens
and there will be hail in all the land of Egypt,

pairs.hebrew: עַל־הָאָדָ֣ם וְעַל־הַבְּהֵמָ֗ה וְעַ֛ל כׇּל־עֵ֥שֶׂב הַשָּׂדֶ֖ה בְּאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃
pairs.english: on man and on beast, and on all the grass in the field in the land of Egypt.
And Moses stretched his staff towards the heavens,

pairs.hebrew: וַֽיהֹוָ֗ה נָתַ֤ן קֹלֹת֙ וּבָרָ֔ד וַתִּ֥הֲלַךְ אֵ֖שׁ אָ֑רְצָה
pairs.english: and the L-rd sent thunders and hail, and fire coursed to the ground,
and the L-rd rained hail on the land of Egypt.

pairs.hebrew: וַיְהִ֣י בָרָ֔ד וְאֵ֕שׁ מִתְלַקַּ֖חַת בְּת֣וֹךְ הַבָּרָ֑ד
pairs.english: And there was hail, and fire flaming within the hail,
extremely sore,

pairs.hebrew: אֲ֠שֶׁ֠ר לֹֽא־הָיָ֤ה כָמֹ֙הוּ֙ בְּכׇל־אֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם מֵאָ֖ז הָיְתָ֥ה לְגֽוֹי׃
pairs.english: the like of which had not been in the land of Egypt since it had become a nation.

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּ֨ךְ הַבָּרָ֜ד בְּכׇל־אֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֗יִם אֵ֚ת כׇּל־אֲשֶׁ֣ר בַּשָּׂדֶ֔ה מֵאָדָ֖ם וְעַד־בְּהֵמָ֑ה
pairs.english: And the hail smote in all the land of Egypt all that was in the field, from man until beast.
And the hail smote all the grass in the field
and broke all the trees in the field.

pairs.hebrew: רַ֚ק בְּאֶ֣רֶץ גֹּ֔שֶׁן אֲשֶׁר־שָׁ֖ם בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל
pairs.english: Only in the land of Goshen, where the children of Israel were,
was there no hail.
And Pharaoh sent and he called to Moses and to Aaron,
and he said to them: I have sinned this time.
The L-rd is the righteous one and I and my people are the wicked ones.

pairs.hebrew: הַעְתִּ֙ירוּ֙ אֶל־יְהֹוָ֔ה וְרַ֕ב מִֽהְיֹ֛ת קֹלֹ֥ת אֱלֹהִ֖ים וּבָרָ֑ד
pairs.english: Entreat the L-rd, and enough of thunders of G-d and hail!
And I will send you and you will be detained no longer.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלָיו֙ מֹשֶׁ֔ה כְּצֵאתִי֙ אֶת־הָעִ֔יר אֶפְרֹ֥שׂ אֶת־כַּפַּ֖י אֶל־יְהֹוָ֑ה
pairs.english: And Moses said to him: When I leave the city [(which was full of idolatry)], I shall spread out my hands to the L-rd.
The thunders will stop and there will be no more hail,
so that you will know that the earth is the L-rd's.
But you and your servants,

pairs.hebrew: יָדַ֕עְתִּי כִּ֚י טֶ֣רֶם תִּֽירְא֔וּן מִפְּנֵ֖י יְהֹוָ֥ה אֱלֹהִֽים׃
pairs.english: I know that you do not yet fear the L-rd G-d [and that you will revert to your perverseness with the cessation of the hail.]
And the flax and the barley were broken [by the hail],
for the barley was ripe [and hard] and the flax was in stalk.
But the wheat and the spelt were not broken,
for they were late growths [and, therefore, soft].

pairs.hebrew: וַיֵּצֵ֨א מֹשֶׁ֜ה מֵעִ֤ם פַּרְעֹה֙ אֶת־הָעִ֔יר וַיִּפְרֹ֥שׂ כַּפָּ֖יו אֶל־יְהֹוָ֑ה
pairs.english: And Moses went away from Pharaoh out of the city, and he spread out his hands to the L-rd,
and the thunders stopped and the hail,
and rain did not reach the ground.

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּ֣רְא פַּרְעֹ֗ה כִּֽי־חָדַ֨ל הַמָּטָ֧ר וְהַבָּרָ֛ד וְהַקֹּלֹ֖ת וַיֹּ֣סֶף לַחֲטֹ֑א
pairs.english: And Pharaoh saw that the rain stopped, and the hail and the thunders, and he continued to sin;
and he hardened his heart, he and his servants.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֶּֽחֱזַק֙ לֵ֣ב פַּרְעֹ֔ה וְלֹ֥א שִׁלַּ֖ח אֶת־בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל
pairs.english: And Pharaoh's heart was strengthened and he did not send out the children of Israel,
as the L-rd had spoken by the hand of Moses.
And the L-rd said to Moses: Come to Pharaoh [and warn him],
for I have hardened his heart and the heart of his servants
in order to set these signs in his midst.
And so that you tell in the ears of your son and the son of your son,

pairs.hebrew: אֵ֣ת אֲשֶׁ֤ר הִתְעַלַּ֙לְתִּי֙ בְּמִצְרַ֔יִם וְאֶת־אֹתֹתַ֖י אֲשֶׁר־שַׂ֣מְתִּי בָ֑ם
pairs.english: of My setting Egypt to scorn and of My signs that I placed in them,
and you will know that I am the L-rd.

pairs.hebrew: וַיָּבֹ֨א מֹשֶׁ֣ה וְאַהֲרֹן֮ אֶל־פַּרְעֹה֒ וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ אֵלָ֗יו כֹּֽה־אָמַ֤ר יְהֹוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י הָֽעִבְרִ֔ים
pairs.english: And Moses and Aaron came to Pharaoh and they said to him: Thus said the L-rd, the G-d of the Hebrews:
How long will you refuse to be humbled before Me?
Send out My people and let them serve Me.
For if you refuse to send out My people,
tomorrow I shall bring a locust swarm in your boundaries.

pairs.hebrew: וְכִסָּה֙ אֶת־עֵ֣ין הָאָ֔רֶץ וְלֹ֥א יוּכַ֖ל לִרְאֹ֣ת אֶת־הָאָ֑רֶץ
pairs.english: And it will cover the face of the land so that the land cannot be seen,

pairs.hebrew: וְאָכַ֣ל ׀ אֶת־יֶ֣תֶר הַפְּלֵטָ֗ה הַנִּשְׁאֶ֤רֶת לָכֶם֙ מִן־הַבָּרָ֔ד
pairs.english: and it will devour the remainder of the remnant left to you from the hail.
And it will devour every tree that sprouts for you from the ground.

pairs.hebrew: וּמָלְא֨וּ בָתֶּ֜יךָ וּבָתֵּ֣י כׇל־עֲבָדֶ֘יךָ֮ וּבָתֵּ֣י כׇל־מִצְרַ֒יִם֒
pairs.english: And they will fill your houses, and the houses of all of your servants, and the houses of all of Egypt,

pairs.hebrew: אֲשֶׁ֨ר לֹֽא־רָא֤וּ אֲבֹתֶ֙יךָ֙ וַאֲב֣וֹת אֲבֹתֶ֔יךָ מִיּ֗וֹם הֱיוֹתָם֙ עַל־הָ֣אֲדָמָ֔ה עַ֖ד הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֑ה
pairs.english: which your fathers have not seen, and the fathers of your fathers, from the day they were upon the ground until this day.
And he turned and went out from before Pharaoh.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּאמְרוּ֩ עַבְדֵ֨י פַרְעֹ֜ה אֵלָ֗יו עַד־מָתַי֙ יִהְיֶ֨ה זֶ֥ה לָ֙נוּ֙ לְמוֹקֵ֔שׁ
pairs.english: And the servants of Pharaoh said to him: How long will this one be a stumbling block to us?
Send out the people and let them serve the L-rd their G-d.
Do you not yet know that Egypt is lost?
And Moses and Aaron were returned [by messenger] to Pharaoh.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲלֵהֶ֔ם לְכ֥וּ עִבְד֖וּ אֶת־יְהֹוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶ֑ם
pairs.english: And he said to them: Go serve the L-rd your G-d.
Who and who are the goers?
And Moses said: With our youth and with our elders will we go;
with our sons and with our daughters, with our flocks and with our herds will we go.
For it is a feast of the L-rd to us.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲלֵהֶ֗ם יְהִ֨י כֵ֤ן יְהֹוָה֙ עִמָּכֶ֔ם כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר אֲשַׁלַּ֥ח אֶתְכֶ֖ם וְאֶֽת־טַפְּכֶ֑ם
pairs.english: And he said to them: May the L-rd thus be with you as I will send you and your children. [How much more so will I not send your flocks and herds!]
See, that [your intended] evil will turn against you.

pairs.hebrew: לֹ֣א כֵ֗ן לְכֽוּ־נָ֤א הַגְּבָרִים֙ וְעִבְד֣וּ אֶת־יְהֹוָ֔ה
pairs.english: Not so, [as you say, to take the children with you, but], let the men now go and serve the L-rd,
for that [to sacrifice to the L-rd (3:18, 5:3)] is what you ask.
And he [(It is not indicated who)] drove them away from Pharaoh's presence.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהֹוָ֜ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֗ה נְטֵ֨ה יָדְךָ֜ עַל־אֶ֤רֶץ מִצְרַ֙יִם֙ בָּֽאַרְבֶּ֔ה
pairs.english: And the L-rd said to Moses: Stretch out your hand over the land of Egypt for the locust swarm.
And it shall come up upon the land of Egypt

pairs.hebrew: וְיֹאכַל֙ אֶת־כׇּל־עֵ֣שֶׂב הָאָ֔רֶץ אֵ֛ת כׇּל־אֲשֶׁ֥ר הִשְׁאִ֖יר הַבָּרָֽד׃
pairs.english: and it shall devour all the grass in the land, all that was left by the hail.
And Moses stretched out his staff over the land of Egypt,

pairs.hebrew: וַֽיהֹוָ֗ה נִהַ֤ג רֽוּחַ־קָדִים֙ בָּאָ֔רֶץ כׇּל־הַיּ֥וֹם הַה֖וּא וְכׇל־הַלָּ֑יְלָה
pairs.english: and the L-rd swept an east wind over the land all that day and all that night.

pairs.hebrew: הַבֹּ֣קֶר הָיָ֔ה וְר֙וּחַ֙ הַקָּדִ֔ים נָשָׂ֖א אֶת־הָאַרְבֶּֽה׃
pairs.english: Morning came and the east wind bore the locust swarm, [Egypt being in the south-west of Eretz Yisrael].

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּ֣עַל הָֽאַרְבֶּ֗ה עַ֚ל כׇּל־אֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם וַיָּ֕נַח בְּכֹ֖ל גְּב֣וּל מִצְרָ֑יִם כָּבֵ֣ד מְאֹ֔ד
pairs.english: And the locust swarm came up on all the land of Egypt, and it rested in the entire boundary of Egypt — very sore.
Before it there had never been a locust swarm of its like,
and after it there will not be such.
And it covered the face of the whole land and the land was darkened,

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֜אכַל אֶת־כׇּל־עֵ֣שֶׂב הָאָ֗רֶץ וְאֵת֙ כׇּל־פְּרִ֣י הָעֵ֔ץ אֲשֶׁ֥ר הוֹתִ֖יר הַבָּרָ֑ד
pairs.english: and it devoured all the grass of the earth and all the fruit of the trees which the hail had left.

pairs.hebrew: וְלֹא־נוֹתַ֨ר כׇּל־יֶ֧רֶק בָּעֵ֛ץ וּבְעֵ֥שֶׂב הַשָּׂדֶ֖ה בְּכׇל־אֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃
pairs.english: And there remained no green on a tree or in the grass of the field in all the land of Egypt.
And Pharaoh hastened to call Moses and Aaron,
and he said: I have sinned to the L-rd your G-d and to you.

pairs.hebrew: וְעַתָּ֗ה שָׂ֣א נָ֤א חַטָּאתִי֙ אַ֣ךְ הַפַּ֔עַם
pairs.english: And now, forgive my sin, I pray you, just this time,

pairs.hebrew: וְהַעְתִּ֖ירוּ לַיהֹוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶ֑ם וְיָסֵר֙ מֵֽעָלַ֔י רַ֖ק אֶת־הַמָּ֥וֶת הַזֶּֽה׃
pairs.english: and entreat the L-rd your G-d that He remove from me just this death.
And Moses went out from before Pharaoh
and he prayed to the L-rd.
And the L-rd turned a very strong west wind,
and it lifted the locust swarm and cast it into the Red Sea.

pairs.hebrew: לֹ֤א נִשְׁאַר֙ אַרְבֶּ֣ה אֶחָ֔ד בְּכֹ֖ל גְּב֥וּל מִצְרָֽיִם׃
pairs.english: There remained not one locust [(even of those they had salted)] in all the border of Egypt.
And the L-rd strengthened Pharaoh's heart
and he did not send out the children of Israel.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהֹוָ֜ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֗ה נְטֵ֤ה יָֽדְךָ֙ עַל־הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם
pairs.english: And the L-rd said to Moses: Stretch forth your hand towards the heavens,

pairs.hebrew: וִ֥יהִי חֹ֖שֶׁךְ עַל־אֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם וְיָמֵ֖שׁ חֹֽשֶׁךְ׃
pairs.english: and there will be darkness over the land of Egypt, which shall darken darkness.
And Moses stretched forth his hand towards the heavens,

pairs.hebrew: וַיְהִ֧י חֹֽשֶׁךְ־אֲפֵלָ֛ה בְּכׇל־אֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרַ֖יִם שְׁלֹ֥שֶׁת יָמִֽים׃
pairs.english: and there was thick darkness in all the land of Egypt a triad of days.

One man did not see another [for one triad of days (when the wicked among the Jews who refused to leave Egypt were killed — in darkness, so the Egyptians could not say: "These are being smitten as we are")],

and no man rose from his place [(One who was sitting could not stand, and one who was standing could not sit)] for [another] triad of days [(when the Jews could search their houses at will for vessels to take with them during the exodus)],
and for all the children of Israel there was light in their habitations.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּקְרָ֨א פַרְעֹ֜ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֗ה וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ לְכוּ֙ עִבְד֣וּ אֶת־יְהֹוָ֔ה
pairs.english: And Pharaoh called to Moses and he said: Go serve the L-rd;
only your flocks and herds leave in place.
Also your children shall go with you.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֔ה גַּם־אַתָּ֛ה תִּתֵּ֥ן בְּיָדֵ֖נוּ זְבָחִ֣ים וְעֹלֹ֑ת
pairs.english: And Moses said: [Not only shall our cattle go with us, but] you, too, shall place in our hands sacrifices and burnt-offerings,
and we shall offer them to the L-rd our G-d.

pairs.hebrew: וְגַם־מִקְנֵ֜נוּ יֵלֵ֣ךְ עִמָּ֗נוּ לֹ֤א תִשָּׁאֵר֙ פַּרְסָ֔ה
pairs.english: Our cattle, too, shall go with us; a hoof will not remain.

pairs.hebrew: כִּ֚י מִמֶּ֣נּוּ נִקַּ֔ח לַעֲבֹ֖ד אֶת־יְהֹוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֑ינוּ
pairs.english: For we will take thereof to serve the L-rd our G-d.

pairs.hebrew: וַאֲנַ֣חְנוּ לֹֽא־נֵדַ֗ע מַֽה־נַּעֲבֹד֙ אֶת־יְהֹוָ֔ה עַד־בֹּאֵ֖נוּ שָֽׁמָּה׃
pairs.english: For we do not know what [i.e., how much we will need] to serve the L-rd until we come there.
And the L-rd strengthened Pharaoh's heart
and he did not want to send them.
And Pharaoh said to him: Go from me.
Take heed to yourself. Do not see my face again.
For on the day you see my face you will die.
And Moses said: True have you spoken, [and in the proper time. Indeed,]
I shall not see your face again!

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהֹוָ֜ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֗ה ע֣וֹד נֶ֤גַע אֶחָד֙ אָבִ֤יא עַל־פַּרְעֹה֙ וְעַל־מִצְרַ֔יִם
pairs.english: And the L-rd said to Moses: Yet one more plague shall I bring upon Pharaoh and upon Egypt.
After that, he shall send you hence.

pairs.hebrew: כְּשַׁ֨לְּח֔וֹ כָּלָ֕ה גָּרֵ֛שׁ יְגָרֵ֥שׁ אֶתְכֶ֖ם מִזֶּֽה׃
pairs.english: When he sends (you), [he shall send] all [of you]; he shall drive you hence.
Speak, I pray you, in the ears of the people,

pairs.hebrew: וְיִשְׁאֲל֞וּ אִ֣ישׁ ׀ מֵאֵ֣ת רֵעֵ֗הוּ וְאִשָּׁה֙ מֵאֵ֣ת רְעוּתָ֔הּ
pairs.english: that every man ask of his (Egyptian) neighbor and every woman ask of her neighbor

vessels of silver and vessels of gold, [so that the righteous one, Abraham, not say "and they shall serve them and they shall afflict them" (Genesis 15:3) He did fulfill, but "and afterwards they shall go out with great wealth" (Ibid. 14) He did not fulfill.]

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּתֵּ֧ן יְהֹוָ֛ה אֶת־חֵ֥ן הָעָ֖ם בְּעֵינֵ֣י מִצְרָ֑יִם
pairs.english: And the L-rd put the favor of the people in the eyes of Egypt.

pairs.hebrew: גַּ֣ם ׀ הָאִ֣ישׁ מֹשֶׁ֗ה גָּד֤וֹל מְאֹד֙ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם
pairs.english: The man Moses, too, was very great in the land of Egypt
in the eyes of the servants of Pharaoh and in the eyes of the people.
And Moses said [to Pharaoh]: Thus said the L-rd:

pairs.hebrew: כַּחֲצֹ֣ת הַלַּ֔יְלָה אֲנִ֥י יוֹצֵ֖א בְּת֥וֹךְ מִצְרָֽיִם׃
pairs.english: When the night is divided [i.e., at midnight] I shall go out into the midst of Egypt.
And every first-born in the land of Egypt will die,
from the first-born of Pharaoh who sits on his throne [(and down)]

pairs.hebrew: עַ֚ד בְּכ֣וֹר הַשִּׁפְחָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֖ר אַחַ֣ר הָרֵחָ֑יִם
pairs.english: until the first-born of the maidservant behind the mill-stones [(and up. The captive first-born (see 12:29) died so that they not say that their gods "claimed their shame" and brought destruction upon the Egyptians. The sons of the maidservants died, for they, too, worked the Jews and rejoiced in their affliction)]
and all the first-born of beasts, [these having been served as objects of idolatry. ("When the Holy One Blessed be He exacts punishment of a nation, He exacts punishment of its gods.")]
And there will be a great outcry in the whole land of Egypt,

pairs.hebrew: אֲשֶׁ֤ר כָּמֹ֙הוּ֙ לֹ֣א נִהְיָ֔תָה וְכָמֹ֖הוּ לֹ֥א תֹסִֽף׃
pairs.english: the like of which had never been and the like of which will not be again.

pairs.hebrew: וּלְכֹ֣ל ׀ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל לֹ֤א יֶֽחֱרַץ־כֶּ֙לֶב֙ לְשֹׁנ֔וֹ לְמֵאִ֖ישׁ וְעַד־בְּהֵמָ֑ה
pairs.english: And against all the children of Israel a dog shall not sharpen its tongue — from man until beast —

pairs.hebrew: לְמַ֙עַן֙ תֵּֽדְע֔וּן אֲשֶׁר֙ יַפְלֶ֣ה יְהֹוָ֔ה בֵּ֥ין מִצְרַ֖יִם וּבֵ֥ין יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
pairs.english: so that you will know that the L-rd distinguished between Egypt and Israel.

pairs.hebrew: וְיָרְד֣וּ כׇל־עֲבָדֶ֩יךָ֩ אֵ֨לֶּה אֵלַ֜י וְהִשְׁתַּֽחֲווּ־לִ֣י לֵאמֹ֗ר
pairs.english: And all these servants of yours will come down and bow down to me, saying:
Go out! you and all your followers;
and then I will go out.
And [after he finished what he had to say] he went out from before Pharaoh in great wrath [over his having said (10:28): "You shall not see my face again!"]
And the L-rd said to Moses:
Pharaoh will not pay heed to you,
so that My wonders be multiplied in the land of Egypt [viz.: the plague of the first-born, the splitting of the Red Sea, and the "shaking out" of the Egyptians therein.]

pairs.hebrew: וּמֹשֶׁ֣ה וְאַהֲרֹ֗ן עָשׂ֛וּ אֶת־כׇּל־הַמֹּפְתִ֥ים הָאֵ֖לֶּה לִפְנֵ֣י פַרְעֹ֑ה
pairs.english: And Moses and Aaron performed all of these wonders before Pharaoh,
and the L-rd strengthened Pharaoh's heart
and he did not send the children of Israel from his land.
And the L-rd said to Moses and to Aaron [(Aaron being accorded honor in this first mitzvah (2) for having participated and exerted himself along with Moses in the embassy of the signs)]
in the land of Egypt [outside the city (see 11:29)], saying:
This month [this stage of the moon (the L-rd "pointing it out" to Moses)] [Nissan] shall be to you the beginning of months.
It is the first for you of the months of the year.
Speak [today, on Rosh Chodesh] to the whole congregation of Israel, saying:
On the tenth day of this month [(the "taking" of the paschal lamb of Egypt was on the tenth, but not that of future generations)]
shall they take for themselves, each man a lamb for a family [(and, in the event that the family is large and one lamb will not suffice for it)],
a lamb for a household [(i.e., for each household within that family)].
And if the household is too small for one lamb [so that some of it would be left over (nothar, which is forbidden)],

pairs.hebrew: וְלָקַ֣ח ה֗וּא וּשְׁכֵנ֛וֹ הַקָּרֹ֥ב אֶל־בֵּית֖וֹ בְּמִכְסַ֣ת נְפָשֹׁ֑ת
pairs.english: then he and his neighbor next to his house shall take it according to the count of souls.
Each according to his eating [(excluding one who is so sick or old that he cannot eat at least an olive size)] shall you [include in the] count for the lamb.

pairs.hebrew: שֶׂ֥ה תָמִ֛ים זָכָ֥ר בֶּן־שָׁנָ֖ה יִהְיֶ֣ה לָכֶ֑ם
pairs.english: A lamb, unblemished, a one-year-old male [i.e., in its first year] shall it be to you.
Of the lambs or of the goats shall you take it, [a (young) goat, too, being regarded as a "lamb"].
And it shall be to you for a keeping [i.e., surveillance against blemish]

pairs.hebrew: עַ֣ד אַרְבָּעָ֥ה עָשָׂ֛ר י֖וֹם לַחֹ֣דֶשׁ הַזֶּ֑ה
pairs.english: until the fourteenth day of this month [(Israel being given two mitzvoth on that night — the blood of the paschal lamb and the blood of circumcision — to make them worthy of redemption)],

pairs.hebrew: וְשָׁחֲט֣וּ אֹת֗וֹ כֹּ֛ל קְהַ֥ל עֲדַֽת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בֵּ֥ין הָעַרְבָּֽיִם׃
pairs.english: and the entire congregation of Israel shall slaughter it [(whence it is derived that one's messenger is reckoned as the sender himself)], from midday (on).
And they shall take from the blood [in the basin]
and place it on the two side posts and on the lintel
of the houses where they shall eat it, [but not on non-dwellings].
And they shall eat the flesh, [but not sinews and bones] on this night,
roasted in fire.
And matzoth with merorim [(Every bitter herb is called maror)] shall they eat it, [in commemoration of (1:10): "And they embittered (vayemararu) their lives."]

pairs.hebrew: אַל־תֹּאכְל֤וּ מִמֶּ֙נּוּ֙ נָ֔א וּבָשֵׁ֥ל מְבֻשָּׁ֖ל בַּמָּ֑יִם
pairs.english: Do not eat of it not entirely roasted or cooked in water [or any other liquid],
but roasted in fire [(a negative commandment here being added to the positive (8)]; [it is to be roasted entire],
its head, with its legs, with its inner parts, [and its entrails placed therein after rinsing].
And you shall not leave over anything of it until the morning [(sunrise)];
and what is left over of it until morning [(dawn)], in fire shall you burn it.
And thus shall you eat it:

pairs.hebrew: מׇתְנֵיכֶ֣ם חֲגֻרִ֔ים נַֽעֲלֵיכֶם֙ בְּרַגְלֵיכֶ֔ם וּמַקֶּלְכֶ֖ם בְּיֶדְכֶ֑ם
pairs.english: your thighs girded ["ready for the road"], your shoes on your feet, and your staff in your hand.
And you shall eat it in haste —
it is a pesach ("skipping over") offering to the L-rd [see 27].
And I shall pass through the land of Egypt in this night,

pairs.hebrew: וְהִכֵּיתִ֤י כׇל־בְּכוֹר֙ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם מֵאָדָ֖ם וְעַד־בְּהֵמָ֑ה
pairs.english: and I shall smite every first-born in the land of Egypt [(even first-born of other nations in the land of Egypt)], from man until beast;
and upon all the gods of Egypt I shall wreak judgments, [wooden idols rotting and metal ones melting];
I am the L-rd [I shall do this Myself and not through a messenger.]

pairs.hebrew: וְהָיָה֩ הַדָּ֨ם לָכֶ֜ם לְאֹ֗ת עַ֤ל הַבָּתִּים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אַתֶּ֣ם שָׁ֔ם
pairs.english: And the blood shall be for you as a sign [("for you" and not "for others" — whence it is inferred that the blood was placed on the inside)] upon the houses where you are,
and I shall see the blood [i.e., I shall "give heart" to your performance of My mitzvoth], and I shall skip over you,

pairs.hebrew: וְלֹֽא־יִֽהְיֶ֨ה בָכֶ֥ם נֶ֙גֶף֙ לְמַשְׁחִ֔ית בְּהַכֹּתִ֖י בְּאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃
pairs.english: and there will be no destroying plague in you when I smite the land of Egypt [(even if you are found in an Egyptian house — but there will be plague in an Egyptian found in an Israelite house)].
And this day [of the exodus] shall be for you as a remembrance [for the coming generations],
and you shall celebrate it [the fifteenth of Nissan] as a festival of the L-rd.
For your generations as an everlasting statute shall you celebrate it.
Seven days [lit., "a septet of days"] shall you eat matzoth. [(Eating matzoth on the first night is obligatory, and, thereafter, optional)]

pairs.hebrew: אַ֚ךְ בַּיּ֣וֹם הָרִאשׁ֔וֹן תַּשְׁבִּ֥יתוּ שְּׂאֹ֖ר מִבָּתֵּיכֶ֑ם
pairs.english: But on the first day [i.e., on the eve of Pesach] you shall eliminate leaven from your houses.

pairs.hebrew: כִּ֣י ׀ כׇּל־אֹכֵ֣ל חָמֵ֗ץ וְנִכְרְתָ֞ה הַנֶּ֤פֶשׁ הַהִוא֙ מִיִּשְׂרָאֵ֔ל
pairs.english: For whoever eats chametz, that soul [(one who has volition, but not one who is forced)] shall be cut off from Israel [and from My presence] —
from the first day until the seventh day.

pairs.hebrew: וּבַיּ֤וֹם הָרִאשׁוֹן֙ מִקְרָא־קֹ֔דֶשׁ וּבַיּוֹם֙ הַשְּׁבִיעִ֔י מִקְרָא־קֹ֖דֶשׁ יִהְיֶ֣ה לָכֶ֑ם
pairs.english: And on the first day a calling of holiness and on the seventh day a calling of holiness shall there be unto you. [Call it "holy" for purposes of eating, drinking, and raiment.]
No labor shall be done in them [even through a non-Jew].

pairs.hebrew: אַ֚ךְ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יֵאָכֵ֣ל לְכׇל־נֶ֔פֶשׁ ה֥וּא לְבַדּ֖וֹ יֵעָשֶׂ֥ה לָכֶֽם׃
pairs.english: Only what is to be eaten by all souls, that [labor] alone may be done for you, [and not any preparatory labor which could have been done before the festival].
And you shall watch over the matzoth [that they not become chametz];

pairs.hebrew: כִּ֗י בְּעֶ֙צֶם֙ הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֔ה הוֹצֵ֥אתִי אֶת־צִבְאוֹתֵיכֶ֖ם מֵאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם
pairs.english: for on this very same day I took your hosts out from the land of Egypt.

pairs.hebrew: וּשְׁמַרְתֶּ֞ם אֶת־הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּ֛ה לְדֹרֹתֵיכֶ֖ם חֻקַּ֥ת עוֹלָֽם׃
pairs.english: And you shall guard this day [against performing labor thereon] unto your generations as an everlasting statute.

pairs.hebrew: בָּרִאשֹׁ֡ן בְּאַרְבָּעָה֩ עָשָׂ֨ר י֤וֹם לַחֹ֙דֶשׁ֙ בָּעֶ֔רֶב תֹּאכְל֖וּ מַצֹּ֑ת
pairs.english: On the first day, on the fourteenth day of the month, in the evening shall you eat matzoth,

pairs.hebrew: עַ֠ד י֣וֹם הָאֶחָ֧ד וְעֶשְׂרִ֛ים לַחֹ֖דֶשׁ בָּעָֽרֶב׃
pairs.english: until the twenty-first day of the month in the evening [(whence it is derived that the mitzvah obtains in the evenings, too)].

pairs.hebrew: שִׁבְעַ֣ת יָמִ֔ים שְׂאֹ֕ר לֹ֥א יִמָּצֵ֖א בְּבָתֵּיכֶ֑ם
pairs.english: Seven days, se'or [a leavening agent] shall not be found in your houses [i.e., under your control — to exclude liability for chametz of a non-Jew which is found in a Jew's property.]

pairs.hebrew: כִּ֣י ׀ כׇּל־אֹכֵ֣ל מַחְמֶ֗צֶת וְנִכְרְתָ֞ה הַנֶּ֤פֶשׁ הַהִוא֙ מֵעֲדַ֣ת יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל
pairs.english: For whoever eats leavening, that soul shall be cut off from the congregation of Israel,
whether he be a proselyte [(for whom the miracle was not performed)] or a citizen of the land.
All leavening [(including an admixture — this is the exhortation against the eating of se'or)] you shall not eat.
In all of your habitations shall you eat matzoth [(to exclude — as satisfying the mitzvah— matzoth of ma'aser sheni and thanksgiving challoth, which may be eaten only in Jerusalem)].

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּקְרָ֥א מֹשֶׁ֛ה לְכׇל־זִקְנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲלֵהֶ֑ם
pairs.english: And Moses called to all the elders of Israel, and he said to them:
Draw forth [if you have your own,] and take unto yourselves [i.e., buy, if you do not have your own,] sheep for your families [a lamb for a family],
and slaughter the pesach.
And you shall take a bundle [three stalks] of hyssop
and dip it in the blood which is in the basin,

pairs.hebrew: וְהִגַּעְתֶּ֤ם אֶל־הַמַּשְׁקוֹף֙ וְאֶל־שְׁתֵּ֣י הַמְּזוּזֹ֔ת מִן־הַדָּ֖ם אֲשֶׁ֣ר בַּסָּ֑ף
pairs.english: and touch the lintel and the two doorposts (with some) of the blood which is in the basin, [a new dipping for each touching];

pairs.hebrew: וְאַתֶּ֗ם לֹ֥א תֵצְא֛וּ אִ֥ישׁ מִפֶּֽתַח־בֵּית֖וֹ עַד־בֹּֽקֶר׃
pairs.english: and you, do not go out, a man from the door of his house until morning. ["Once 'the destroyer' has been granted leave to destroy, he does not distinguish between righteous and wicked."]
And the L-rd will pass through to smite Egypt,

pairs.hebrew: וְרָאָ֤ה אֶת־הַדָּם֙ עַל־הַמַּשְׁק֔וֹף וְעַ֖ל שְׁתֵּ֣י הַמְּזוּזֹ֑ת
pairs.english: and He will see the blood on the lintel and on the two door posts,
and the L-rd will skip over the door,

pairs.hebrew: וְלֹ֤א יִתֵּן֙ הַמַּשְׁחִ֔ית לָבֹ֥א אֶל־בָּתֵּיכֶ֖ם לִנְגֹּֽף׃
pairs.english: and He will not permit the destroyer to come to your houses to smite.
And you shall keep this thing
as a statute for you and for your children forever.

pairs.hebrew: וְהָיָ֞ה כִּֽי־תָבֹ֣אוּ אֶל־הָאָ֗רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֨ר יִתֵּ֧ן יְהֹוָ֛ה לָכֶ֖ם כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבֵּ֑ר
pairs.english: And it shall be, when you come to the land that the L-rd will give you, as He has spoken [6:8],
then you shall observe this service. [The service is contingent upon their entering the land. (In the desert they were obliged to observe only one Pesach, in the second year, by Divine command.)]
And it shall be, if your sons say to you:
"What is this service to you?" [an allusion to the question of "the wicked son" (see 13:8)],
then you shall say: It is a paschal sacrifice to the L-rd,
who skipped over the houses of the children of Israel in Egypt
when He smote Egypt, and our houses He saved.
And the people bowed down and they prostrated themselves [for the tidings of deliverance and entry to the land and for the tidings of the children that would be born to them,]
And the children of Israel went and they did [(their intent to do being regarded as doing, and their going being rewarded as well as their doing)]

pairs.hebrew: כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר צִוָּ֧ה יְהֹוָ֛ה אֶת־מֹשֶׁ֥ה וְאַהֲרֹ֖ן כֵּ֥ן עָשֽׂוּ׃ {ס}
pairs.english: as the L-rd commanded Moses and Aaron, [exactly, leaving nothing undone.] So did they [Moses and Aaron also] do.
And it was in the middle of the night,
and the L-rd [He and His "tribunal"] smote every first-born [even a non-Egyptian] in the land of Egypt,
from the first-born of Pharaoh sitting on his throne

pairs.hebrew: עַ֚ד בְּכ֣וֹר הַשְּׁבִ֔י אֲשֶׁ֖ר בְּבֵ֣ית הַבּ֑וֹר
pairs.english: until the captive first-born in the dungeon [see 11:5 (The first-born of the maid-servant is subsumed in "until the captive first-born")],
and every first-born of the beast.

pairs.hebrew: וַיָּ֨קׇם פַּרְעֹ֜ה לַ֗יְלָה ה֤וּא וְכׇל־עֲבָדָיו֙ וְכׇל־מִצְרַ֔יִם
pairs.english: And Pharaoh arose [from his bed] at night [and not in the third hour of the morning in the manner of kings], he and all his servants [(Pharaoh awakened them)] and all of Egypt.
And there was a great outcry in Egypt,
for there was no house where no one had died. [If there were no first-born there, the eldest in the house died.]
And he called to Moses and to Aaron at night, and he said:

pairs.hebrew: ק֤וּמוּ צְּאוּ֙ מִתּ֣וֹךְ עַמִּ֔י גַּם־אַתֶּ֖ם גַּם־בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל
pairs.english: Arise, go out from the midst of my people, both you [the adults] and the children of Israel [the children],
and go serve the L-rd as you have spoken [and not as I have spoken].

pairs.hebrew: גַּם־צֹאנְכֶ֨ם גַּם־בְּקַרְכֶ֥ם קְח֛וּ כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר דִּבַּרְתֶּ֖ם וָלֵ֑כוּ
pairs.english: Also your flocks and also your herds take, as you have spoken [i.e., Take also of mine as you have spoken (10:25): "You, too, etc"], and go
and bless also me [Pray for me that I not die, for I, too, am a first-born.]

pairs.hebrew: וַתֶּחֱזַ֤ק מִצְרַ֙יִם֙ עַל־הָעָ֔ם לְמַהֵ֖ר לְשַׁלְּחָ֣ם מִן־הָאָ֑רֶץ
pairs.english: And Egypt bore down upon the people, hastening to send them out of the land,
for they said: We are all dead, [even non first-born dying, beyond the decree of Moses].
And the people took their dough before it leavened, [the Egyptians pressing them to leave],
their [matzoh and maror] remnants bound up in their clothes, on their shoulders [and not upon their beasts, in the love of the mitzvah].
And the children of Israel did as Moses had bid them [11:2]

pairs.hebrew: וַֽיִּשְׁאֲלוּ֙ מִמִּצְרַ֔יִם כְּלֵי־כֶ֛סֶף וּכְלֵ֥י זָהָ֖ב וּשְׂמָלֹֽת׃
pairs.english: and they asked of Egypt vessels of silver and vessels of gold and raiment.

pairs.hebrew: וַֽיהֹוָ֞ה נָתַ֨ן אֶת־חֵ֥ן הָעָ֛ם בְּעֵינֵ֥י מִצְרַ֖יִם
pairs.english: And the L-rd placed the favor of the people in the eyes of Egypt,
and they lent them [even more than they asked],
and they emptied out Egypt.
And the children of Israel journeyed from Ramses to Succoth [a distance of one hundred and twenty miles, "on eagle's wings" (19:4)],

pairs.hebrew: כְּשֵׁשׁ־מֵא֨וֹת אֶ֧לֶף רַגְלִ֛י הַגְּבָרִ֖ים לְבַ֥ד מִטָּֽף׃
pairs.english: six hundred thousand men on foot, aside from the children.
And also a great mixture [of proselytes] went up with them.
And flocks and herds, a great crush of cattle.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּאפ֨וּ אֶת־הַבָּצֵ֜ק אֲשֶׁ֨ר הוֹצִ֧יאוּ מִמִּצְרַ֛יִם עֻגֹ֥ת מַצּ֖וֹת
pairs.english: And they baked the dough which they had taken out of Egypt, cakes of matzoh,
for it had not leavened.
For they were driven out of Egypt and they could not tarry;
and provisions, too, they could not make for themselves [(a tribute to Israel's belief in the L-rd, venturing forth into the desert without provisions)].

pairs.hebrew: וּמוֹשַׁב֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר יָשְׁב֖וּ בְּמִצְרָ֑יִם
pairs.english: And the habitation of the children of Israel in the land of Egypt [and their habitations outside it after "Your seed shall be a stranger, etc." (Genesis 15:13)]
was [all together] four hundred and thirty years.

pairs.hebrew: וַיְהִ֗י מִקֵּץ֙ שְׁלֹשִׁ֣ים שָׁנָ֔ה וְאַרְבַּ֥ע מֵא֖וֹת שָׁנָ֑ה
pairs.english: And it was at the end of four hundred and thirty years,

and it was on this very same day [the fifteenth of Nissan, (the date of the angels' tidings to Abraham on the birth of a son, the date of Isaac's birth, the date of the covenant between the pieces — the L-rd not delaying an instant after the arrival of the foretold time)]
that all the hosts of the L-rd went out of the land of Egypt.
It is a night of guarding for the L-rd, ["guarded" by the L-rd]
to take them out from the land of Egypt;
it is "this night" of the L-rd [i.e., of His saying to Abraham: "On this night I shall redeem your children"],
guarded [against destructive agents] for all the children of Israel for (all) their generations [see 33].
And the L-rd said to Moses and Aaron [(on the fourteenth of Nissan)]:
This is the statute of the paschal offering:
No stranger [(Both a heretical Jew and a non-Jew are implied)] may eat of it.
And every man-servant acquired by money —
you shall circumcise him;
then shall he [(according to one view, the master; according to another, the servant)] eat of it.
A sojourner [a ger toshav (one who does not convert fully, but who undertakes not to serve idols and to observe the seven Noahide laws)] and a hired man [a non-Jew]
may not eat of it. [The above applies (even) to a circumcised Arab or a circumcised Giveonite who is a sojourner or a hired man.]
In one house [i.e., group] shall it be eaten.
Do not take from the house [i.e., from the group] of the flesh outside.
And a bone [which has an olive-size of meat on it] shall you not break in it.
The entire congregation of Israel [in any groups]
shall offer it [in future generations, (as opposed to the Pesach of Egypt, when it was offered by family groups)].

pairs.hebrew: וְכִֽי־יָג֨וּר אִתְּךָ֜ גֵּ֗ר וְעָ֣שָׂה פֶ֘סַח֮ לַיהֹוָה֒
pairs.english: And if there live with you a stranger (i.e., a proselyte) and he would offer a paschal offering to the L-rd [on the fourteenth of Nissan],

pairs.hebrew: הִמּ֧וֹל ל֣וֹ כׇל־זָכָ֗ר וְאָז֙ יִקְרַ֣ב לַעֲשֹׂת֔וֹ
pairs.english: let all of his males be circumcised and then he shall draw near to offer it.
And he shall be as the citizen of the land,
and no uncircumcised one shall eat of it [(including one who is not circumcised because his brothers have died as a result of circumcision)].
One Torah shall there be for the citizen
and for the stranger that lives in your midst. [The proselyte is hereby equated with the citizen for all of the other mitzvoth of the Torah.]
And all the children of Israel did

pairs.hebrew: כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר צִוָּ֧ה יְהֹוָ֛ה אֶת־מֹשֶׁ֥ה וְאֶֽת־אַהֲרֹ֖ן כֵּ֥ן עָשֽׂוּ׃ {ס}
pairs.english: as the L-rd commanded Moses and Aaron; thus did they do.
And it was in this very same day

pairs.hebrew: הוֹצִ֨יא יְהֹוָ֜ה אֶת־בְּנֵ֧י יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל מֵאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרַ֖יִם עַל־צִבְאֹתָֽם׃ {פ}
pairs.english: that the L-rd took the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt by their hosts.
And the L-rd said to Moses,
saying:
Sanctify unto Me every first-born,

pairs.hebrew: פֶּ֤טֶר כׇּל־רֶ֙חֶם֙ בִּבְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל בָּאָדָ֖ם וּבַבְּהֵמָ֑ה
pairs.english: the [first] opener of each womb among the children of Israel in man and beast;
he is Mine, [acquired by Me when I smote the first-born of Egypt].
And Moses said to the people:

pairs.hebrew: זָכ֞וֹר אֶת־הַיּ֤וֹם הַזֶּה֙ אֲשֶׁ֨ר יְצָאתֶ֤ם מִמִּצְרַ֙יִם֙ מִבֵּ֣ית עֲבָדִ֔ים
pairs.english: Remember this day when you went out of Egypt from the house of bondage [(We are hereby taught to make mention of the exodus every day)].

pairs.hebrew: כִּ֚י בְּחֹ֣זֶק יָ֔ד הוֹצִ֧יא יְהֹוָ֛ה אֶתְכֶ֖ם מִזֶּ֑ה
pairs.english: For with might of hand did the L-rd take you hence,
and chametz shall not be eaten.
This day you go out,
in the month of spring [an equable month: neither hot, nor cold, nor rainy.]

pairs.hebrew: וְהָיָ֣ה כִֽי־יְבִיאֲךָ֣ יְהֹוָ֡ה אֶל־אֶ֣רֶץ הַֽ֠כְּנַעֲנִ֠י וְהַחִתִּ֨י וְהָאֱמֹרִ֜י וְהַחִוִּ֣י וְהַיְבוּסִ֗י
pairs.english: And it shall be, when the L-rd brings you to the land of Canaan [(a particular nation of the seven nations generically called "Canaanites")], the Chitti, the Emori, the Chivi, and the Yevussi,

pairs.hebrew: אֲשֶׁ֨ר נִשְׁבַּ֤ע לַאֲבֹתֶ֙יךָ֙ לָ֣תֶת לָ֔ךְ אֶ֛רֶץ זָבַ֥ת חָלָ֖ב וּדְבָ֑שׁ
pairs.english: which He swore to your forefathers to give to you [(Abraham — Genesis 15:18; Isaac — 26:3; Jacob — 28:13)], a land flowing with milk [from goats] and honey [from dates and figs],
then you shall perform this service [of Pesach] on this month.
Seven days shall you eat matzoth,
and on the seventh day, a festival to the L-rd.
Matzoth shall be eaten the seven days;
and chametz (leaven) shall not be seen unto you,
and se'or (leavening) shall not be seen unto you in all of your boundaries.
And you shall tell [vehigadeta] your son [(an allusion to "the son who does not know how to ask." "Open for him" with words of aggadah (narration), which stimulate questioning)] on that day, saying:
Because of this [i.e., so that I fulfill His mitzvoth, e.g., pesach, matzoth, and maror]

the L-rd wrought for me when I went out of Egypt [(an allusion to the answer to "the wicked son," (see 12:26), viz.: "The L-rd wrought for me and not for you. Had you been there, you would not have merited redemption.")]

pairs.hebrew: וְהָיָה֩ לְךָ֨ לְא֜וֹת עַל־יָדְךָ֗ וּלְזִכָּרוֹן֙ בֵּ֣ין עֵינֶ֔יךָ
pairs.english: And it [the account of the exodus from Egypt] shall be to you as a sign upon your [left] hand [in the hand phylactery] and as a memorial between your eyes [in the head phylactery],
so that the Torah of the L-rd be in your mouth;

pairs.hebrew: כִּ֚י בְּיָ֣ד חֲזָקָ֔ה הוֹצִֽאֲךָ֥ יְהֹוָ֖ה מִמִּצְרָֽיִם׃
pairs.english: for with a mighty hand did the L-rd take you out of Egypt.
And you shall keep this statute in its time,
from year to year.
And it shall be, when the L-rd brings you to the land of the Canaanite

pairs.hebrew: כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר נִשְׁבַּ֥ע לְךָ֖ וְלַֽאֲבֹתֶ֑יךָ וּנְתָנָ֖הּ לָֽךְ׃
pairs.english: as He swore to you [6:8] and to your forefathers and gives it to you [(Let it be in your eyes as if it is given to you on that day and not as an inheritance from your fathers)],
then you shall set apart every firstling of the womb for the L-rd.

pairs.hebrew: וְכׇל־פֶּ֣טֶר ׀ שֶׁ֣גֶר בְּהֵמָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר יִהְיֶ֥ה לְךָ֛ הַזְּכָרִ֖ים לַיהֹוָֽה׃
pairs.english: And every firstling of the cast-off [i.e., the premature birth] of a beast that shall be to you, the males are the L-rd's.

And every firstling of an ass [and not of any other unclean beast, the first-born of the Egyptians being compared to asses, and, also, because the asses "assisted" Israel in taking out the spoils of Egypt)] shall you redeem with a lamb. [The lamb is given to the Cohein, benefit may then be derived from the firstling, and the lamb is chullin (non-sacred) for the Cohein.]
And if you do not redeem it, then you shall break its neck [with a hatchet from behind (He caused the Cohein a loss; therefore, he suffers a loss)],
and every human first-born among your sons shall you redeem [by giving five selaim to the Cohein].

pairs.hebrew: וְהָיָ֞ה כִּֽי־יִשְׁאָלְךָ֥ בִנְךָ֛ מָחָ֖ר לֵאמֹ֣ר מַה־זֹּ֑את
pairs.english: And it shall be, if your son asks you in after time, saying "What is this?" [(an allusion to the question of "the simple son")],

pairs.hebrew: וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ אֵלָ֔יו בְּחֹ֣זֶק יָ֗ד הוֹצִיאָ֧נוּ יְהֹוָ֛ה מִמִּצְרַ֖יִם מִבֵּ֥ית עֲבָדִֽים׃
pairs.english: then you shall say to him: With might of hand did the L-rd take us out of Egypt from the house of bondage.
And it was, when Pharaoh resisted sending us out,

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּהֲרֹ֨ג יְהֹוָ֤ה כׇּל־בְּכוֹר֙ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם מִבְּכֹ֥ר אָדָ֖ם וְעַד־בְּכ֣וֹר בְּהֵמָ֑ה
pairs.english: that the L-rd killed every first-born in the land of Egypt, from the first-born of man until the first-born of beast.

pairs.hebrew: עַל־כֵּן֩ אֲנִ֨י זֹבֵ֜חַ לַֽיהֹוָ֗ה כׇּל־פֶּ֤טֶר רֶ֙חֶם֙ הַזְּכָרִ֔ים
pairs.english: Therefore, I sacrifice to the L-rd every male firstling of the womb,
and every firstling of my sons, I redeem.
And it shall be as a sign upon your hand
and as a frontlet [totafoth (signifying "four" — the four compartments of the head phylactery)] between your eyes;
for with might of hand did the L-rd take us out of Egypt.
And it was, when Pharaoh sent out the people,

pairs.hebrew: וְלֹא־נָחָ֣ם אֱלֹהִ֗ים דֶּ֚רֶךְ אֶ֣רֶץ פְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים כִּ֥י קָר֖וֹב ה֑וּא
pairs.english: that G-d did not lead them by the way of the land of the Philistines, for it was near [and afforded "easy return" to Egypt].

pairs.hebrew: כִּ֣י ׀ אָמַ֣ר אֱלֹהִ֗ים פֶּֽן־יִנָּחֵ֥ם הָעָ֛ם בִּרְאֹתָ֥ם מִלְחָמָ֖ה וְשָׁ֥בוּ מִצְרָֽיְמָה׃
pairs.english: For G-d said: Lest the people bethink themselves [about having left Egypt] when they see war [e.g., Numbers 14:45] and they return to Egypt.
And G-d led the people circuitously by way of the desert to the Red Sea.
And the children of Israel went up armed from the land of Egypt.
And Moses took the bones of Joseph with him.

pairs.hebrew: כִּי֩ הַשְׁבֵּ֨עַ הִשְׁבִּ֜יעַ אֶת־בְּנֵ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר
pairs.english: For he had made the children of Israel swear, saying:
G-d will surely remember you,
and you shall bring up my bones from here with you, [the tribes, (the bones of all the tribes also being brought up with them)].
And they journeyed from Succoth [on the second day]
and they encamped in Etham at the edge of the desert.

pairs.hebrew: וַֽיהֹוָ֡ה הֹלֵךְ֩ לִפְנֵיהֶ֨ם יוֹמָ֜ם בְּעַמּ֤וּד עָנָן֙ לַנְחֹתָ֣ם הַדֶּ֔רֶךְ
pairs.english: And the L-rd went before them by day with [i.e., leading] a pillar of cloud to guide them on the way,
and at night, with a pillar of fire to light them,
to go by day and by night.
He did not dispel the pillar of cloud in the day
and the pillar of light at night before the people. [Before the one "set," the other rose.]
And the L-rd said to Moses,
saying:
Speak to the children of Israel

that they return [The L-rd turned them back to Egypt to deceive Pharaoh into thinking they had lost their way (3)] and encamp before Pi Hachiroth [Pithom, called "Pi Hachiroth" because the Jews became freemen (bnei chorin) there],

pairs.hebrew: בֵּ֥ין מִגְדֹּ֖ל וּבֵ֣ין הַיָּ֑ם לִפְנֵי֙ בַּ֣עַל צְפֹ֔ן
pairs.english: between Migdol and the sea, before Baal Tzefon [the only remaining Egyptian idol (left over to deceive the Egyptians into relying on its potency)].
Over against it shall you encamp by the sea.
And Pharaoh will say about the children of Israel:
They are trapped in the land;
the desert has shut them in.
And I shall strengthen Pharaoh's heart and he will pursue them,
and I will be honored through [the downfall of] Pharaoh and all of his host [(Pharaoh being mentioned first in that he was the "initiator")],
and Egypt will know that I am the L-rd.
And they did so. [(a tribute to Israel, who did not ask: "How can we turn back towards our pursuers!")]

pairs.hebrew: וַיֻּגַּד֙ לְמֶ֣לֶךְ מִצְרַ֔יִם כִּ֥י בָרַ֖ח הָעָ֑ם
pairs.english: And it was told to the king of Egypt [on the fourth day, by officers that he had sent with them (after seeing that they did not return to Egypt on the stipulated third day)] that the people had fled. [(On the fifth and sixth days they pursued them; on the night of the seventh Israel went down to the sea; and in the morning — the seventh day of Pesach — they sang (15:1)],
and the heart of Pharaoh (12:31) and of his servants (10:7) was reversed against the people. [Now they pursued them for the wealth that they had lent them],

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּֽאמְרוּ֙ מַה־זֹּ֣את עָשִׂ֔ינוּ כִּֽי־שִׁלַּ֥חְנוּ אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל מֵעׇבְדֵֽנוּ׃
pairs.english: and they said: What is this that we did in sending Israel away from serving us!
And he [Pharaoh himself] harnessed his chariot,
and he "took" [by suasion] his people with him.
And he took six hundred choice chariots
and all [the other] chariots of Egypt,
and officers upon all of them.

pairs.hebrew: וַיְחַזֵּ֣ק יְהֹוָ֗ה אֶת־לֵ֤ב פַּרְעֹה֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ מִצְרַ֔יִם
pairs.english: And the L-rd strengthened the heart of Pharaoh king of Egypt [Pharaoh wavering between pursuing and not pursuing]
and he pursued the children of Israel,
and the children of Israel went out with a high hand [i.e., with manifest might].

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּרְדְּפ֨וּ מִצְרַ֜יִם אַחֲרֵיהֶ֗ם וַיַּשִּׂ֤יגוּ אוֹתָם֙ חֹנִ֣ים עַל־הַיָּ֔ם
pairs.english: And Egypt pursued them, and they overtook them camping by the sea,
every horse of Pharaoh's chariots and his horsemen and his host,
by Pi Hachiroth, before Baal Tzefon.
And Pharaoh pressed ahead [of the others],

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּשְׂאוּ֩ בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֨ל אֶת־עֵינֵיהֶ֜ם וְהִנֵּ֥ה מִצְרַ֣יִם ׀ נֹסֵ֣עַ אַחֲרֵיהֶ֗ם
pairs.english: and the children of Israel lifted their eyes, and, behold, Egypt coming after them [with one heart, as one man],
and they were exceedingly afraid,
and the children of Israel cried out to the L-rd, ["embracing the trade" (prayer) of their fathers: (Abraham — Genesis 19:27; Isaac — 24:63; Jacob — 28:11)].
And they said to Moses:

pairs.hebrew: הֲֽמִבְּלִ֤י אֵין־קְבָרִים֙ בְּמִצְרַ֔יִם לְקַחְתָּ֖נוּ לָמ֣וּת בַּמִּדְבָּ֑ר
pairs.english: Is it for lack of graves in Egypt that you have taken us to die in the desert!
What is this that you did to us to take us out of Egypt.

pairs.hebrew: הֲלֹא־זֶ֣ה הַדָּבָ֗ר אֲשֶׁר֩ דִּבַּ֨רְנוּ אֵלֶ֤יךָ בְמִצְרַ֙יִם֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר
pairs.english: Is not this the thing that we spoke to you in Egypt [5:21], saying:
Let us be and let us serve Egypt,

pairs.hebrew: כִּ֣י ט֥וֹב לָ֙נוּ֙ עֲבֹ֣ד אֶת־מִצְרַ֔יִם מִמֻּתֵ֖נוּ בַּמִּדְבָּֽר׃
pairs.english: for it is better for us to serve Egypt than to die in the desert.
And Moses said to the people: Do not fear.

pairs.hebrew: הִֽתְיַצְּב֗וּ וּרְאוּ֙ אֶת־יְשׁוּעַ֣ת יְהֹוָ֔ה אֲשֶׁר־יַעֲשֶׂ֥ה לָכֶ֖ם הַיּ֑וֹם
pairs.english: Stand ready to see the salvation of the L-rd, which He shall work for you this day.
For your seeing Egypt is [only] this day;
you shall see them no more, forever.
The L-rd will war for you,
and you will be still.
And the L-rd said to Moses:
Why do you cry out to Me? [i.e., Why do you prolong your prayer when Israel are stepped in affliction?]
Speak to the children of Israel and have them go forward [(There is nothing standing in their way. The merits of their fathers and their belief in Me will suffice to split the sea.)]
And you, raise your staff,
and stretch out your hand over the sea, and split it.
And the children of Israel shall come in the midst of the sea on the dry land.
And I, behold, I shall strengthen the heart of Egypt,
and they shall come after them,
and I shall be glorified through Pharaoh and through all his host, through his chariots and through his horsemen.
And Egypt will know that I am the L-rd
when I am glorified through Pharaoh, through his chariots and through his horsemen.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּסַּ֞ע מַלְאַ֣ךְ הָאֱלֹהִ֗ים הַהֹלֵךְ֙ לִפְנֵי֙ מַחֲנֵ֣ה יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַיֵּ֖לֶךְ מֵאַחֲרֵיהֶ֑ם
pairs.english: And the angel of G-d (Elokim), who went before the camp of Israel, turned and went behind them [to separate the Israelites from the Egyptians and to receive the projectiles intended for them. ("Elokim" connotes justice. Israel was being judged at that moment for survival or for destruction along with the Egyptians)].
And [when it became dark and the pillar of fire supervened], the pillar of cloud turned from before them
and stood behind them [to "darken things" for the Egyptians].
