pairs.english: and the festival of the ingathering [Succoth] at the going out of the year, when you gather your labor from the field [against the rain].
Three times in the year
shall appear all the males among you in the presence of the Master, the L-rd, [the festivals not lapsing in the sabbatical year].
You shall not offer alongside chametz the blood of My sacrifice [i.e., Do not slaughter the Pesach offering on the fourteenth of Nissan until the chametz has been removed],
and there shall not remain [unplaced on the altar] the fat of My festival offering until morning.

pairs.hebrew: רֵאשִׁ֗ית בִּכּוּרֵי֙ אַדְמָ֣תְךָ֔ תָּבִ֕יא בֵּ֖ית יְהֹוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֑יךָ
pairs.english: The first of the first-fruits of your land [even in the sabbatical year] you shall bring to the house of the L-rd your G-d.

You shall not cook a kid [any young, tender animal] in its mother's milk. [This is written three times in the Torah: (here, 34:26, and Deuteronomy 14:21), once to forbid eating (milk and meat together), once to forbid derivation of benefit, and once to forbid cooking.]
Behold, I shall send an angel before you [(the L-rd here apprising them that they would sin, that He would not go up among them (33:3) and that they would require an intermediary)],

pairs.hebrew: לִשְׁמׇרְךָ֖ בַּדָּ֑רֶךְ וְלַהֲבִ֣יאֲךָ֔ אֶל־הַמָּק֖וֹם אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֲכִנֹֽתִי׃
pairs.english: to watch over you on the way, and to bring you to the place that I have readied [for you].

pairs.hebrew: הִשָּׁ֧מֶר מִפָּנָ֛יו וּשְׁמַ֥ע בְּקֹל֖וֹ אַל־תַּמֵּ֣ר בּ֑וֹ
pairs.english: Take heed of him and hearken to his voice. Do not rebel against him,

pairs.hebrew: כִּ֣י לֹ֤א יִשָּׂא֙ לְפִשְׁעֲכֶ֔ם כִּ֥י שְׁמִ֖י בְּקִרְבּֽוֹ׃
pairs.english: for he will not forgive your offenses, [sin being foreign to his nature and forgiveness not being deputed to him. "Take heed of him"] for My name is within him [i.e., associated with him].

pairs.hebrew: כִּ֣י אִם־שָׁמ֤וֹעַ תִּשְׁמַע֙ בְּקֹל֔וֹ וְעָשִׂ֕יתָ כֹּ֖ל אֲשֶׁ֣ר אֲדַבֵּ֑ר
pairs.english: But if you hearken to his voice and do all that I shall speak,
then I shall hate your enemies and oppress your oppressors.
For My angel shall go before you,

pairs.hebrew: וֶהֱבִֽיאֲךָ֗ אֶל־הָֽאֱמֹרִי֙ וְהַ֣חִתִּ֔י וְהַפְּרִזִּי֙ וְהַֽכְּנַעֲנִ֔י הַחִוִּ֖י וְהַיְבוּסִ֑י וְהִכְחַדְתִּֽיו׃
pairs.english: and he will bring you to the Emori, and the Chitti and the Perizi and the Canaani and the Chivi and the Yevussi, and I will annihilate them.

pairs.hebrew: לֹֽא־תִשְׁתַּחֲוֶ֤ה לֵאלֹֽהֵיהֶם֙ וְלֹ֣א תׇֽעׇבְדֵ֔ם וְלֹ֥א תַעֲשֶׂ֖ה כְּמַֽעֲשֵׂיהֶ֑ם
pairs.english: Do not bow down to their gods and do not worship them and do not emulate their deeds,

pairs.hebrew: כִּ֤י הָרֵס֙ תְּהָ֣רְסֵ֔ם וְשַׁבֵּ֥ר תְּשַׁבֵּ֖ר מַצֵּבֹתֵיהֶֽם׃
pairs.english: but raze them [their idols] and break down their [stone] monuments [which they set up to bow down to].
And you shall serve the L-rd your G-d,
and He will bless your bread and your water,
and I shall remove sickness from your midst.
There shall not be [if you do My will] a woman bereft [(of her young, miscarrying or burying them)] or barren in your land;
the number of your days shall I complete.
My fright shall I send before you,
and I shall confound all the people among whom you come,
and I shall set the nape of all your foes before you [in fleeing you].
And I shall send the hornet before you,
and it shall drive out the Chivvi, the Canaani, and the Chitti before you.
I will not drive them out before you in one year

pairs.hebrew: פֶּן־תִּהְיֶ֤ה הָאָ֙רֶץ֙ שְׁמָמָ֔ה וְרַבָּ֥ה עָלֶ֖יךָ חַיַּ֥ת הַשָּׂדֶֽה׃
pairs.english: lest the land be left desolate and the animals of the field increase against you.
Little by little I will drive them out before you
until you multiply and inherit the land.

pairs.hebrew: וְשַׁתִּ֣י אֶת־גְּבֻלְךָ֗ מִיַּם־סוּף֙ וְעַד־יָ֣ם פְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים וּמִמִּדְבָּ֖ר עַד־הַנָּהָ֑ר
pairs.english: And I shall set your boundaries from the Red Sea until the sea of the Philistines, and from the desert until the river.

pairs.hebrew: כִּ֣י ׀ אֶתֵּ֣ן בְּיֶדְכֶ֗ם אֵ֚ת יֹשְׁבֵ֣י הָאָ֔רֶץ
pairs.english: For I will put in your hand the inhabitants of the land,
and you will drive them out before you.
You shall not make a covenant with them
or with their gods.

pairs.hebrew: לֹ֤א יֵשְׁבוּ֙ בְּאַרְצְךָ֔ פֶּן־יַחֲטִ֥יאוּ אֹתְךָ֖ לִ֑י
pairs.english: They shall not dwell in your land lest they cause you to sin against Me,

pairs.hebrew: כִּ֤י תַעֲבֹד֙ אֶת־אֱלֹ֣הֵיהֶ֔ם כִּֽי־יִהְיֶ֥ה לְךָ֖ לְמוֹקֵֽשׁ׃ {פ}
pairs.english: that you serve their gods and they be a stumbling block to you.

pairs.hebrew: וְאֶל־מֹשֶׁ֨ה אָמַ֜ר עֲלֵ֣ה אֶל־יְהֹוָ֗ה אַתָּה֙ וְאַהֲרֹן֙ נָדָ֣ב וַאֲבִיה֔וּא וְשִׁבְעִ֖ים מִזִּקְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל
pairs.english: And to Moses He said [(before the Ten Commandments) on the fourth of Sivan]: Go up to the L-rd, you and Aaron, Nadav and Avihu, and seventy of the elders of Israel,
and bow down from afar.
And Moses alone shall draw near [to the mist] to the L-rd,

pairs.hebrew: וְהֵ֖ם לֹ֣א יִגָּ֑שׁוּ וְהָעָ֕ם לֹ֥א יַעֲל֖וּ עִמּֽוֹ׃
pairs.english: but they shall not draw near, and the people shall not go up with him.

pairs.hebrew: וַיָּבֹ֣א מֹשֶׁ֗ה וַיְסַפֵּ֤ר לָעָם֙ אֵ֚ת כׇּל־דִּבְרֵ֣י יְהֹוָ֔ה וְאֵ֖ת כׇּל־הַמִּשְׁפָּטִ֑ים
pairs.english: And Moses came and he told the people [on that day] all the words of the L-rd [the commandment of separation (from conjugal relations) and the keeping of bounds (from Mount Sinai)] and all of the judgments [the seven Noachide laws, Sabbath, honoring of father and mother, and the administration of justice, which had been related to them at Marah].
And the people answered with one voice and said:
All of the things which the L-rd has spoken we shall do.
And Moses wrote all the words of the L-rd [from the creation until the giving of the Torah, and he wrote down the mitzvoth given at Marah]

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּשְׁכֵּ֣ם בַּבֹּ֔קֶר וַיִּ֥בֶן מִזְבֵּ֖חַ תַּ֣חַת הָהָ֑ר
pairs.english: and he arose early in the morning [on the fifth of Sivan] and he built an altar at the foot of the mountain

pairs.hebrew: וּשְׁתֵּ֤ים עֶשְׂרֵה֙ מַצֵּבָ֔ה לִשְׁנֵ֥ים עָשָׂ֖ר שִׁבְטֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
pairs.english: and twelve monuments for the twelve tribes of Israel.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּשְׁלַ֗ח אֶֽת־נַעֲרֵי֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַֽיַּעֲל֖וּ עֹלֹ֑ת
pairs.english: And he sent the youths [i.e., the first-born] of the children of Israel, and they offered up burnt-offerings
and slaughtered sacrifices, peace-offerings to the L-rd, bullocks.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּקַּ֤ח מֹשֶׁה֙ חֲצִ֣י הַדָּ֔ם וַיָּ֖שֶׂם בָּאַגָּנֹ֑ת
pairs.english: And Moses took half of the blood [(an angel coming and halving it)] and he placed it in basins [(two basins: one for half the blood of the burnt-offering; the other, for half the blood of the peace-offering to sprinkle upon the people (whence our sages infer that our ancestors entered the covenant through circumcision, immersion, and the sprinkling of blood, there being no sprinkling without immersion)],
and half the blood he sprinkled upon the altar.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּקַּח֙ סֵ֣פֶר הַבְּרִ֔ית וַיִּקְרָ֖א בְּאׇזְנֵ֣י הָעָ֑ם
pairs.english: And he took the book of the covenant [(from the creation until the giving of the Torah and the mitzvoth given at Marah)], and he read (it) in the ears of the people,

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ כֹּ֛ל אֲשֶׁר־דִּבֶּ֥ר יְהֹוָ֖ה נַעֲשֶׂ֥ה וְנִשְׁמָֽע׃
pairs.english: and they said: All that the L-rd has spoken we shall do and we shall hear.
And Moses took the blood and sprinkled it upon the people,

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר הִנֵּ֤ה דַֽם־הַבְּרִית֙ אֲשֶׁ֨ר כָּרַ֤ת יְהֹוָה֙ עִמָּכֶ֔ם
pairs.english: and he said: Behold, the blood of the covenant, which the L-rd has made with you
over all these words.
And there went up Moses and Aaron,
Nadav and Avihu, and seventy of the elders of Israel.

And they saw the G-d of Israel [They "peeked" and were liable to death, but the Holy One Blessed be He, desiring not to dampen the joy of (receiving the) Torah "waited" for Nadav and Avihu until the consecration of the tabernacle, and for the elders until the episode of the complainers (Numbers 11:16)],

pairs.hebrew: וְתַ֣חַת רַגְלָ֗יו כְּמַעֲשֵׂה֙ לִבְנַ֣ת הַסַּפִּ֔יר וּכְעֶ֥צֶם הַשָּׁמַ֖יִם לָטֹֽהַר׃
pairs.english: and under His feet, as the work of a sapphire brick [This was before Him at the time of the (Egyptian) bondage to "keep Him in mind" of the brick-toil of the Jews] and as the appearance of the heavens in brightness. [When they were redeemed, there was light and rejoicing before Him.]

pairs.hebrew: וְאֶל־אֲצִילֵי֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לֹ֥א שָׁלַ֖ח יָד֑וֹ
pairs.english: And against the nobles of the children of Israel [Nadav, Avihu, and the elders], He did not send forth His hand [(whence it is to be derived that it would have been warranted)],
and they gazed upon G-d [grossly] while eating and drinking.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהֹוָ֜ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֗ה עֲלֵ֥ה אֵלַ֛י הָהָ֖רָה וֶהְיֵה־שָׁ֑ם
pairs.english: And the L-rd said to Moses [after the giving of the Torah]: Go up to Me to the mountain and be there [forty days],

pairs.hebrew: וְאֶתְּנָ֨ה לְךָ֜ אֶת־לֻחֹ֣ת הָאֶ֗בֶן וְהַתּוֹרָה֙ וְהַמִּצְוָ֔ה
pairs.english: and I shall give you the tablets of stone and the Torah and the mitzvah
which I have written to teach them. [All the six hundred and thirteen mitzvoth are contained in the Ten Commandments.]
And Moses arose and Joshua his attendant,
and Moses went up to the mountain of G-d, [Joshua accompanying him as far as he was permitted to go, pitching his tent there and awaiting Moses' return].

pairs.hebrew: וְאֶל־הַזְּקֵנִ֤ים אָמַר֙ שְׁבוּ־לָ֣נוּ בָזֶ֔ה עַ֥ד אֲשֶׁר־נָשׁ֖וּב אֲלֵיכֶ֑ם
pairs.english: And to the elders he said [upon leaving the encampment]: Abide for us here [with the rest of the people to be "on call" for judging their disputes] until we return to you,
and, behold, Aaron and Chur [(the son of Miriam and Calev ben Yefuneh)] are with you.
Whoever has a claim (against his fellow) shall draw near to them.
And Moses went up to the mountain,
and the cloud covered the mountain.
And the glory of the L-rd reposed upon Mount Sinai,
and the cloud covered it for six days

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּקְרָ֧א אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֛ה בַּיּ֥וֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִ֖י מִתּ֥וֹךְ הֶעָנָֽן׃
pairs.english: and He called to Moses on the seventh day from the midst of the cloud. [Or, according to another view, him. ("it"): "And the glory of the L-rd reposed upon Mount Sinai and the cloud covered it for six days [from Rosh Chodesh Sivan], and He called to Moses [(all of Israel standing there, but Moses being singled out for special honor)] on the seventh day [to declare the Ten Commandments] from the midst of the cloud." ("him"): "And the glory of the L-rd reposed upon Mount Sinai and the cloud covered him for six days [after the Ten Commandments, the beginning of the forty days of Moses' going up to receive the tablets (Scripture teaching that entrance into the "Divine Encampment" (later, the Holy of Holies) requires a six-day separation period)], and He called to Moses on the seventh day from the midst of the cloud."]
And the sight of the glory of the L-rd

pairs.hebrew: כְּאֵ֥שׁ אֹכֶ֖לֶת בְּרֹ֣אשׁ הָהָ֑ר לְעֵינֵ֖י בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
pairs.english: was like a consuming fire on the top of the mountain in the eyes of the children of Israel.

pairs.hebrew: וַיָּבֹ֥א מֹשֶׁ֛ה בְּת֥וֹךְ הֶעָנָ֖ן וַיַּ֣עַל אֶל־הָהָ֑ר
pairs.english: And Moses came in the midst of the cloud, [G d making a kind of path for him in its midst], and he went up to the mountain.

pairs.hebrew: וַיְהִ֤י מֹשֶׁה֙ בָּהָ֔ר אַרְבָּעִ֣ים י֔וֹם וְאַרְבָּעִ֖ים לָֽיְלָה׃ {פ}
pairs.english: And Moses was in the mountain forty days and forty nights.
And the L-rd spoke to Moses,
saying:
Speak to the children of Israel and let them take for Me [i.e., for My Name's sake] terumah [a tithe].

pairs.hebrew: מֵאֵ֤ת כׇּל־אִישׁ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יִדְּבֶ֣נּוּ לִבּ֔וֹ תִּקְח֖וּ אֶת־תְּרוּמָתִֽי׃
pairs.english: From every man whose heart prompts him shall you take My terumah. [Three terumoth are referred to here: the terumah of a beka for a head, of which the sockets were made; the terumah of the altar, a beka for a head, for the communal offering funds; and the terumah of the mishkan (the tabernacle), an individual gift. (The thirteen articles mentioned below were needed either for the work of the mishkan or for the priestly garments)].
And this is the terumah that you shall take from them:
gold, silver, and copper [all voluntary gifts, except silver, a half-shekel for each individual (Additional offerings of silver were used for making the ministering vessels)].
And tcheleth [wool died with the blood of the chilazon, of a greenish hue], and argaman [wool colored with a dye of that name],
and crimson, and linen, and goats' hair.
And skins of rams dyed red [after tanning]
and skins of techashim [a kind of animal found only at that time],

and acacia wood. [Jacob foresaw that they would build a tabernacle in the desert (where there is no wood). Accordingly, he brought cedars to Egypt, planted them and bade his sons take them when they left Egypt.]
Oil for the light [pure olive oil to make the flame ascend continuously],

spices for the anointing oil [used to anoint the vessels of the mishkan itself, to sanctify it] and for the burning [ketoreth (the rising of a smoke column)] of the incense, [which was burned every evening and morning].
[Two] onyx stones [for the ephod (28:6)] and stones for filling [the golden settings in the breastplate (choshen)],
for the ephod and the choshen [respectively].
And they shall make for Me mikdash [beth kedushah — "a house of holiness"]
and I shall dwell in their midst.

pairs.hebrew: כְּכֹ֗ל אֲשֶׁ֤ר אֲנִי֙ מַרְאֶ֣ה אוֹתְךָ֔ אֵ֚ת תַּבְנִ֣ית הַמִּשְׁכָּ֔ן וְאֵ֖ת תַּבְנִ֣ית כׇּל־כֵּלָ֑יו
pairs.english: ["And they shall make for Me mikdash"] according to all that I show you, the design of the tabernacle and the design of all its vessels.
And so [according to this design] shall you do [in future generations when any of the Temple vessels are lost].
And they shall make an ark [without legs] of acacia wood:
two and a half cubits, its length;

pairs.hebrew: וְאַמָּ֤ה וָחֵ֙צִי֙ רׇחְבּ֔וֹ וְאַמָּ֥ה וָחֵ֖צִי קֹמָתֽוֹ׃
pairs.english: one and a half cubits, its breadth; and one and a half cubits, its height.

pairs.hebrew: וְצִפִּיתָ֤ אֹתוֹ֙ זָהָ֣ב טָה֔וֹר מִבַּ֥יִת וּמִח֖וּץ תְּצַפֶּ֑נּוּ
pairs.english: And you shall cover it with pure gold. From inside and from outside shall you cover it. [Bezalel made three arks: two of gold and one of wood, each having four walls and a base, and open from above. He placed the wooden one in a golden one, and a golden one in the wooden one and covered the top with gold so that it was found to be covered with gold "from inside and from outside."]

And you shall make a rim of gold roundabout it. [He made the outer ark higher than the inner so that it projected above the kaporeth (the ark cover) and formed a rim roundabout, symbolizing the "crown of Torah"].
And you shall cast for it four golden rings,

and you shall place them on its four [upper] corners [near the kaporeth, two on each side along the breadth of the ark, into which the staves were placed, this allowing space (the two and a half cubits of the length) for two carriers to walk between them] —

pairs.hebrew: וּשְׁתֵּ֣י טַבָּעֹ֗ת עַל־צַלְעוֹ֙ הָֽאֶחָ֔ת וּשְׁתֵּי֙ טַבָּעֹ֔ת עַל־צַלְע֖וֹ הַשֵּׁנִֽית׃
pairs.english: two rings on one side and two rings on the other.
And you shall make staves of acacia wood
and cover them with gold.

pairs.hebrew: וְהֵבֵאתָ֤ אֶת־הַבַּדִּים֙ בַּטַּבָּעֹ֔ת עַ֖ל צַלְעֹ֣ת הָאָרֹ֑ן
pairs.english: And you shall insert the staves in the rings on the sides of the ark
to carry the ark therewith.
In the rings of the ark shall the staves remain;
they shall never depart from it.
And you shall place in the ark the Testimony [(the Torah, which serves as testimony between you and Me that I have charged you with the mitzvoth written therein)]
that I shall give you.
And you shall make a kaporeth [an ark-cover (the ark was open on top and the kaporeth was placed upon it like a board)] of pure gold:

pairs.hebrew: אַמָּתַ֤יִם וָחֵ֙צִי֙ אׇרְכָּ֔הּ וְאַמָּ֥ה וָחֵ֖צִי רׇחְבָּֽהּ׃
pairs.english: two and a half cubits its length and a cubit and a half its width [(corresponding to the length and width of the ark, the kaporeth resting on the thickness of its four walls. The thickness of the kaporeth was a tefach, a hand-breadth)].
And you shall make two golden cherubs.

pairs.hebrew: מִקְשָׁה֙ תַּעֲשֶׂ֣ה אֹתָ֔ם מִשְּׁנֵ֖י קְצ֥וֹת הַכַּפֹּֽרֶת׃
pairs.english: Of beaten work shall you make them, at the two [front] ends of the kaporeth.

pairs.hebrew: וַ֠עֲשֵׂ֠ה כְּר֨וּב אֶחָ֤ד מִקָּצָה֙ מִזֶּ֔ה וּכְרוּב־אֶחָ֥ד מִקָּצָ֖ה מִזֶּ֑ה
pairs.english: Make one cherub at one end and one cherub at the other end.
From the kaporeth [itself] shall you make the cherubs at its two ends.

pairs.hebrew: וְהָי֣וּ הַכְּרֻבִים֩ פֹּרְשֵׂ֨י כְנָפַ֜יִם לְמַ֗עְלָה סֹכְכִ֤ים בְּכַנְפֵיהֶם֙ עַל־הַכַּפֹּ֔רֶת
pairs.english: And the cherubs shall have their wings spread on high [parallel to their heads], covering the kaporeth with their wings from above [a space of ten tefachim between the wings and the kaporeth].
And their faces shall be towards each other.
Towards the kaporeth shall the faces of the cherubs be.
And you shall place the kaporeth on the ark from above,

pairs.hebrew: וְאֶל־הָ֣אָרֹ֔ן תִּתֵּן֙ אֶת־הָ֣עֵדֻ֔ת אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֶתֵּ֖ן אֵלֶֽיךָ׃
pairs.english: and in the ark shall you place the Testimony that I shall give you.
And I will be appointed for you [to speak to you] there,

pairs.hebrew: וְדִבַּרְתִּ֨י אִתְּךָ֜ מֵעַ֣ל הַכַּפֹּ֗רֶת מִבֵּין֙ שְׁנֵ֣י הַכְּרֻבִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֖ר עַל־אֲר֣וֹן הָעֵדֻ֑ת
pairs.english: and I will speak to you from above the kaporeth between the two cherubs on the ark of testimony,

pairs.hebrew: אֵ֣ת כׇּל־אֲשֶׁ֧ר אֲצַוֶּ֛ה אוֹתְךָ֖ אֶל־בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ {פ}
pairs.english: all that I shall charge you with to the children of Israel.
And you shall make a table of acacia wood:
two cubits, its length; one cubit, its breadth;
and a cubit and a half, its height [the combined height of its legs and the thickness of the table].
And you shall cover it with pure gold,
and you shall make for it a rim of gold roundabout, [symbolizing the "crown of kingdom"].
And you shall make a frame for it, a hand-breadth roundabout,
and you shall make a golden rim [the aforementioned (24)] for its frame, roundabout.
And you shall make for it four golden rings,

pairs.hebrew: וְנָתַתָּ֙ אֶת־הַטַּבָּעֹ֔ת עַ֚ל אַרְבַּ֣ע הַפֵּאֹ֔ת אֲשֶׁ֖ר לְאַרְבַּ֥ע רַגְלָֽיו׃
pairs.english: and you shall place the rings in the four corners of its four legs.
Opposite the [corners of the] frame shall the rings be,
as housings for the staves for the carrying of the table.
And you shall make the staves of acacia wood,
and you shall cover them with gold,
and the table shall be carried with them.

And you shall make its [bread-] moulds [for the show-bread], its censers [for the frankincense], its (hollow) canes [canes split lengthwise on which the loaves were placed to separate one from another so that they not mold], and its staves, [the framework for the canes]
by which [canes] it [the show-bread] shall be covered.
Of pure gold shall you make them.
And you shall place upon the table show-bread
before Me always. ["show-bread," lit., "face-bread," so called because it had "faces" (i.e., surfaces) facing two (opposite) sides of the sanctuary].
And you shall make a menorah [candelabrum] of pure gold;
of beaten work shall the menorah be made, ["of itself." Moses being "stymied" by the task, the Holy One Blessed be He said to him: "Cast the talent into the fire and it shall be made of itself."]

pairs.hebrew: יְרֵכָ֣הּ וְקָנָ֔הּ גְּבִיעֶ֛יהָ כַּפְתֹּרֶ֥יהָ וּפְרָחֶ֖יהָ מִמֶּ֥נָּה יִהְיֽוּ׃
pairs.english: Its base, its [central] shaft [surmounted by the middle lamp, made in the form of a cup (for the oil and the wick)], its bowls [golden ornaments projecting from the branches], its bulbs [apple-shaped ornaments around the central branch], and its flowers [flower-shaped figures], from it [the one piece of gold] shall be [fashioned (without breaking anything off)].
And six branches projecting from its [the central shaft's] sides,
three branches of the menorah from one side,
and three branches of the menorah from the other side [slantwise, one above the other, all rising to the height of the middle branch].

pairs.hebrew: שְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה גְ֠בִעִ֠ים מְֽשֻׁקָּדִ֞ים בַּקָּנֶ֣ה הָאֶחָד֮ כַּפְתֹּ֣ר וָפֶ֒רַח֒
pairs.english: Three chased bowls on one branch, with bulb and flower;

pairs.hebrew: וּשְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה גְבִעִ֗ים מְשֻׁקָּדִ֛ים בַּקָּנֶ֥ה הָאֶחָ֖ד כַּפְתֹּ֣ר וָפָ֑רַח
pairs.english: and three chased bowls on the other branch, with bulb and flower.
And so with (all) six branches that project from the menorah.
And on the [central shaft of the] menorah were four bowls [one projecting under the branches, and three (respectively) above the origin of the branches],
chased, its bulbs and its flowers [(The phrase is ambiguous, i.e., either "bowls chased, its bulbs and its flowers," or "…bowls, its bulbs and its flowers chased")]
And a bulb under the two branches from it [the one piece of gold],
and a bulb under the (next) two branches from it,

pairs.hebrew: וְכַפְתֹּ֕ר תַּחַת־שְׁנֵ֥י הַקָּנִ֖ים מִמֶּ֑נָּה לְשֵׁ֙שֶׁת֙ הַקָּנִ֔ים הַיֹּצְאִ֖ים מִן־הַמְּנֹרָֽה׃
pairs.english: and a bulb under the (next) two branches from it, (thus) for (all) the six branches that project from the menorah.
Their bulbs and their branches from it shall be,
all one (piece of) beaten work of pure gold.
And you shall make its lamps [small bowls into which oil and wicks were placed], seven,
and he (the artificer) shall fashion its lamps so that their light is directed at its face [the central shaft].
And its tongs [for manipulating and positioning the wicks] and its snuff-dishes [small bowls into which the high-priest raked the ashes every morning],
pure gold.
(Of) a talent of pure gold shall he make it
[together] with all these vessels.
And see, and make (them)
according to their design which you are shown [here] in the mountain.
And the tabernacle (the mishkan) shall you make with ten curtains [to serve it as a roof and as partitions outside the boards, the curtains being hung behind them to cover them]:

pairs.hebrew: שֵׁ֣שׁ מׇשְׁזָ֗ר וּתְכֵ֤לֶת וְאַרְגָּמָן֙ וְתֹלַ֣עַת שָׁנִ֔י
pairs.english: twisted linen (shesh) and blue (wool) and purple and scarlet, [four varieties in each thread, one of linen and three of wool and each thread twisted six (shesh) times, giving a twenty-four-fold thread],
cherubs of artistic work [(figures interwoven on both sides)] shall you make them.

pairs.hebrew: אֹ֣רֶךְ ׀ הַיְרִיעָ֣ה הָֽאַחַ֗ת שְׁמֹנֶ֤ה וְעֶשְׂרִים֙ בָּֽאַמָּ֔ה
pairs.english: The length of one curtain, twenty-eight cubits;
and the width, four cubits for one curtain —
one measure for all the curtains.

pairs.hebrew: חֲמֵ֣שׁ הַיְרִיעֹ֗ת תִּֽהְיֶ֙יןָ֙ חֹֽבְרֹ֔ת אִשָּׁ֖ה אֶל־אֲחֹתָ֑הּ
pairs.english: Five curtains shall be attached [by sewing] one to the other,
and five curtains, one to the other.

pairs.hebrew: וְעָשִׂ֜יתָ לֻֽלְאֹ֣ת תְּכֵ֗לֶת עַ֣ל שְׂפַ֤ת הַיְרִיעָה֙ הָאֶחָ֔ת מִקָּצָ֖ה בַּחֹבָ֑רֶת
pairs.english: And you shall make loops of purple wool at the edge of the end curtain of one (five-curtain) joining,

pairs.hebrew: וְכֵ֤ן תַּעֲשֶׂה֙ בִּשְׂפַ֣ת הַיְרִיעָ֔ה הַקִּ֣יצוֹנָ֔ה בַּמַּחְבֶּ֖רֶת הַשֵּׁנִֽית׃
pairs.english: and, likewise, at the edge of the end curtain of the other joining.
Fifty loops shall you make in the one (end) curtain,

pairs.hebrew: וַחֲמִשִּׁ֣ים לֻֽלָאֹ֗ת תַּעֲשֶׂה֙ בִּקְצֵ֣ה הַיְרִיעָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֖ר בַּמַּחְבֶּ֣רֶת הַשֵּׁנִ֑ית
pairs.english: and fifty loops shall you make at the edge of the (end) curtain in the second joining,
the loops [on the respective joinings] directly aligned one with the other.
And you shall make fifty golden hooks,
and you shall join the curtains one to the other by the hooks, [inserting one end of the hook into one loop, and the other end, into its corresponding loop],
and the tabernacle shall be one.
And you shall make curtains of goats' hair to tent over the [lower curtains of the] tabernacle;
eleven curtains shall you make them.
The length of one curtain, thirty cubits;
and the width, four cubits for one curtain —
one measure for the eleven curtains.

pairs.hebrew: וְחִבַּרְתָּ֞ אֶת־חֲמֵ֤שׁ הַיְרִיעֹת֙ לְבָ֔ד וְאֶת־שֵׁ֥שׁ הַיְרִיעֹ֖ת לְבָ֑ד
pairs.english: And you shall join five curtains separately and six curtains separately,

pairs.hebrew: וְכָפַלְתָּ֙ אֶת־הַיְרִיעָ֣ה הַשִּׁשִּׁ֔ית אֶל־מ֖וּל פְּנֵ֥י הָאֹֽהֶל׃
pairs.english: and you shall double [two cubits of] the sixth curtain [the "surplus" vis-à-vis the lower curtains] over the face of the tent [the screen on the east (as a bride's face is veiled in modesty)].

pairs.hebrew: וְעָשִׂ֜יתָ חֲמִשִּׁ֣ים לֻֽלָאֹ֗ת עַ֣ל שְׂפַ֤ת הַיְרִיעָה֙ הָֽאֶחָ֔ת הַקִּיצֹנָ֖ה בַּחֹבָ֑רֶת
pairs.english: And you shall make fifty loops at the edge of the end curtain in (one) joining,

pairs.hebrew: וַחֲמִשִּׁ֣ים לֻֽלָאֹ֗ת עַ֚ל שְׂפַ֣ת הַיְרִיעָ֔ה הַחֹבֶ֖רֶת הַשֵּׁנִֽית׃
pairs.english: and fifty loops at the edge of the curtain in the second joining.
And you shall make fifty copper hooks,
and you shall insert the hooks into the loops,
and you shall join the tent [the goats' hair covering], and it shall be one.

pairs.hebrew: וְסֶ֙רַח֙ הָעֹדֵ֔ף בִּירִיעֹ֖ת הָאֹ֑הֶל חֲצִ֤י הַיְרִיעָה֙ הָעֹדֶ֔פֶת
pairs.english: And the additional draping in the curtains of the tent, half of the additional curtain [i.e., two cubits],
you shall hang over the back [the west] of the tabernacle [to cover the two cubits of exposed beams.]

pairs.hebrew: וְהָאַמָּ֨ה מִזֶּ֜ה וְהָאַמָּ֤ה מִזֶּה֙ בָּעֹדֵ֔ף בְּאֹ֖רֶךְ יְרִיעֹ֣ת הָאֹ֑הֶל
pairs.english: And the cubit on one side and the cubit on the other side in excess [of the length of the lower curtains] in the length of the curtains of the tent,

pairs.hebrew: יִהְיֶ֨ה סָר֜וּחַ עַל־צִדֵּ֧י הַמִּשְׁכָּ֛ן מִזֶּ֥ה וּמִזֶּ֖ה לְכַסֹּתֽוֹ׃
pairs.english: shall be spread over both sides [north and south] of the tabernacle [curtains] to cover it [(for purposes of adornment)].

pairs.hebrew: וְעָשִׂ֤יתָ מִכְסֶה֙ לָאֹ֔הֶל עֹרֹ֥ת אֵילִ֖ם מְאׇדָּמִ֑ים
pairs.english: And you shall make a cover for the tent [(the goats' hair roof)] of rams' skins dyed red,
and a cover of tachash skins above.
And you shall make the beams of the tabernacle [those that have been designated for the purpose (Jacob, prophetically, having planted acacia trees to this end)]
of standing acacia wood. [The beams of the tabernacle walls are to be stood up vertically, and not placed horizontally one atop the other.]
Ten cubits the length of the beam [(so that the height of the tabernacle was ten cubits)],

pairs.hebrew: וְאַמָּה֙ וַחֲצִ֣י הָֽאַמָּ֔ה רֹ֖חַב הַקֶּ֥רֶשׁ הָאֶחָֽד׃
pairs.english: and a cubit and a half the breadth of each beam [(so that the length of the tabernacle was thirty cubits)].

pairs.hebrew: שְׁתֵּ֣י יָד֗וֹת לַקֶּ֙רֶשׁ֙ הָאֶחָ֔ד מְשֻׁ֨לָּבֹ֔ת אִשָּׁ֖ה אֶל־אֲחֹתָ֑הּ
pairs.english: Two prongs (wooden projections) for each beam [(the beam being hollowed out at the bottom to form these prongs)], rung-like, one near the other [like the rungs of a ladder].
So shall you do for all the beams of the tabernacle.
And you shall make the beams for the tabernacle,
twenty beams for the southern side.

pairs.hebrew: וְאַרְבָּעִים֙ אַדְנֵי־כֶ֔סֶף תַּעֲשֶׂ֕ה תַּ֖חַת עֶשְׂרִ֣ים הַקָּ֑רֶשׁ
pairs.english: And forty silver sockets shall you make under the twenty beams;

pairs.hebrew: שְׁנֵ֨י אֲדָנִ֜ים תַּֽחַת־הַקֶּ֤רֶשׁ הָאֶחָד֙ לִשְׁתֵּ֣י יְדֹתָ֔יו
pairs.english: two sockets under one beam for its two prongs,

pairs.hebrew: וּשְׁנֵ֧י אֲדָנִ֛ים תַּֽחַת־הַקֶּ֥רֶשׁ הָאֶחָ֖ד לִשְׁתֵּ֥י יְדֹתָֽיו׃
pairs.english: and two sockets under the next beam for its two prongs.
And for the second side of the tabernacle, the northern side,
twenty beams.
And their forty silver sockets,
two sockets under one beam
and two sockets under the next beam.
And for the ends [i.e., the back] of the tabernacle on the west,
you shall make six beams, [accounting for nine cubits of width.]
And two beams shall you make
for the corners of the tabernacle at the ends, [(so that the interior width is ten cubits)].
And they (the beams) shall be fitted against each other at the bottom,

pairs.hebrew: וְיַחְדָּ֗ו יִהְי֤וּ תַמִּים֙ עַל־רֹאשׁ֔וֹ אֶל־הַטַּבַּ֖עַת הָאֶחָ֑ת
pairs.english: and together shall they be fitted at its top into one ring. [Two adjacent beams were fixed together by a ring placed in grooves along their breadth.]

pairs.hebrew: כֵּ֚ן יִהְיֶ֣ה לִשְׁנֵיהֶ֔ם לִשְׁנֵ֥י הַמִּקְצֹעֹ֖ת יִהְיֽוּ׃
pairs.english: So shall it be for the two of them [for the two beams at the end, the beam at the northern end and the western beam, and so,] for the two corners shall they be.

pairs.hebrew: וְהָיוּ֙ שְׁמֹנָ֣ה קְרָשִׁ֔ים וְאַדְנֵיהֶ֣ם כֶּ֔סֶף שִׁשָּׁ֥ה עָשָׂ֖ר אֲדָנִ֑ים
pairs.english: And [on the western side] there shall be eight beams and their silver sockets, sixteen sockets;
two sockets under one beam
and two sockets under the next beam.
And you shall make bars of acacia wood,

five for the beams of one side of the tabernacle [These "five" are three, the upper and lower bars, respectively, consisting of two equal (fifteen cubit segments) running along the side wall, and one bar running the entire length through a hole bored in each beam.]
And five bars for the beams of the second side of the tabernacle,

pairs.hebrew: וַחֲמִשָּׁ֣ה בְרִיחִ֗ם לְקַרְשֵׁי֙ צֶ֣לַע הַמִּשְׁכָּ֔ן לַיַּרְכָתַ֖יִם יָֽמָּה׃
pairs.english: and five bars for the beams of the side of the tabernacle at the western ends.
And the middle bar in the midst of the beams
shall extend from end to end.
And the beams shall you cover with gold,
and their rings shall you make of gold [to serve as] housings for the bars,
and you shall cover the bars with gold [i.e., They will be "covered" with gold when they are inserted into the golden rings flanked by the golden half-reeds on either side.]
And you shall set up the tabernacle
after the manner which will have been shown to you [by the L-rd] in the mountain.

pairs.hebrew: וְעָשִׂ֣יתָ פָרֹ֗כֶת תְּכֵ֧לֶת וְאַרְגָּמָ֛ן וְתוֹלַ֥עַת שָׁנִ֖י וְשֵׁ֣שׁ מׇשְׁזָ֑ר
pairs.english: And you shall make a parocheth (partition) of blue wool and purple wool and scarlet wool and twisted linen.
Artistic work shall he make it, cherubs. [See Rashi on verse 1].

pairs.hebrew: וְנָתַתָּ֣ה אֹתָ֗הּ עַל־אַרְבָּעָה֙ עַמּוּדֵ֣י שִׁטִּ֔ים מְצֻפִּ֣ים זָהָ֔ב
pairs.english: And you shall place it on four pillars of acacia wood covered with gold,
their hooks of gold [(Hooks bent upwards were set in the pillars on which to place the pole on which the top of the parocheth was wrapped)] (the pillars standing) upon four sockets of silver.
And you shall put the parocheth under the hooks,

pairs.hebrew: וְהֵבֵאתָ֥ שָׁ֙מָּה֙ מִבֵּ֣ית לַפָּרֹ֔כֶת אֵ֖ת אֲר֣וֹן הָעֵד֑וּת
pairs.english: and you shall bring there, inside the parocheth, the ark of testimony;

pairs.hebrew: וְהִבְדִּילָ֤ה הַפָּרֹ֙כֶת֙ לָכֶ֔ם בֵּ֣ין הַקֹּ֔דֶשׁ וּבֵ֖ין קֹ֥דֶשׁ הַקֳּדָשִֽׁים׃
pairs.english: and the parocheth shall separate for you between the holy and the holy of holies.
And you shall put the kaporeth (the lid) upon the ark of testimony
in the holy of holies.
And you shall place the table outside the parocheth,

pairs.hebrew: וְאֶת־הַמְּנֹרָה֙ נֹ֣כַח הַשֻּׁלְחָ֔ן עַ֛ל צֶ֥לַע הַמִּשְׁכָּ֖ן תֵּימָ֑נָה
pairs.english: and the menorah opposite the table on the southern side of the tabernacle;
and the table shall you place on the northern side.
And you shall make a screen [a curtain] for the entrance of the tent,

pairs.hebrew: תְּכֵ֧לֶת וְאַרְגָּמָ֛ן וְתוֹלַ֥עַת שָׁנִ֖י וְשֵׁ֣שׁ מׇשְׁזָ֑ר מַעֲשֵׂ֖ה רֹקֵֽם׃
pairs.english: of blue wool, purple wool, scarlet wool, and twisted linen, the work of an embroiderer [needlework, the figures on one side being the same as those on the other.]
And you shall make for the screen five pillars of acacia wood,
and you shall cover them with gold, and their hooks (shall be) of gold;
and you shall cast for them five copper sockets.
And you shall make the altar of acacia wood,

pairs.hebrew: חָמֵשׁ֩ אַמּ֨וֹת אֹ֜רֶךְ וְחָמֵ֧שׁ אַמּ֣וֹת רֹ֗חַב
pairs.english: five cubits long and five cubits wide.

pairs.hebrew: רָב֤וּעַ יִהְיֶה֙ הַמִּזְבֵּ֔חַ וְשָׁלֹ֥שׁ אַמּ֖וֹת קֹמָתֽוֹ׃
pairs.english: The altar shall be square and three cubits high.

pairs.hebrew: וְעָשִׂ֣יתָ קַרְנֹתָ֗יו עַ֚ל אַרְבַּ֣ע פִּנֹּתָ֔יו מִמֶּ֖נּוּ תִּהְיֶ֣יןָ קַרְנֹתָ֑יו
pairs.english: And you shall make its horns on its four corners. From it [the altar itself] shall its horns be, [and not first made and then attached to it.]
and you shall cover it with copper [to atone for brazenness (see Isaiah 48:4)].

pairs.hebrew: וְעָשִׂ֤יתָ סִּֽירֹתָיו֙ לְדַשְּׁנ֔וֹ וְיָעָיו֙ וּמִזְרְקֹתָ֔יו וּמִזְלְגֹתָ֖יו וּמַחְתֹּתָ֑יו
pairs.english: And you shall make its pots (into which) to empty its ashes, and its shovels [with which to remove its ashes], and its sprinkling basins [in which to receive the blood of the sacrifices], and its spits, and its fire-pans [for taking coals from the outer altar to the inner altar for the burning of the incense].
All of its implements shall you make of copper.

pairs.hebrew: וְעָשִׂ֤יתָ לּוֹ֙ מִכְבָּ֔ר מַעֲשֵׂ֖ה רֶ֣שֶׁת נְחֹ֑שֶׁת
pairs.english: And you shall make for it a copper lattice, netting work.

pairs.hebrew: וְעָשִׂ֣יתָ עַל־הָרֶ֗שֶׁת אַרְבַּע֙ טַבְּעֹ֣ת נְחֹ֔שֶׁת עַ֖ל אַרְבַּ֥ע קְצוֹתָֽיו׃
pairs.english: And you shall make on the netting four copper rings at its four edges.

pairs.hebrew: וְנָתַתָּ֣ה אֹתָ֗הּ תַּ֛חַת כַּרְכֹּ֥ב הַמִּזְבֵּ֖חַ מִלְּמָ֑טָּה
pairs.english: And you shall place it under the karkov of the altar [an encircling, decorative band] below.
And the netting shall extend until the mid-point of the altar [for distinguishing between the (placing of the) "upper blood" and the "lower blood"].

pairs.hebrew: וְעָשִׂ֤יתָ בַדִּים֙ לַמִּזְבֵּ֔חַ בַּדֵּ֖י עֲצֵ֣י שִׁטִּ֑ים
pairs.english: And you shall make staves for the altar of acacia wood,
and you shall cover them with copper.
And its staves shall be brought into the [four] rings [made in the lattice].

pairs.hebrew: וְהָי֣וּ הַבַּדִּ֗ים עַל־שְׁתֵּ֛י צַלְעֹ֥ת הַמִּזְבֵּ֖חַ בִּשְׂאֵ֥ת אֹתֽוֹ׃
pairs.english: And the staves shall be on the two sides of the altar when it is carried.
A hollow of boards shall you make it,
as He showed you on the mountain; so shall they do.
And you shall make the court of the tabernacle:

pairs.hebrew: לִפְאַ֣ת נֶֽגֶב־תֵּ֠ימָ֠נָה קְלָעִ֨ים לֶחָצֵ֜ר שֵׁ֣שׁ מׇשְׁזָ֗ר
pairs.english: On the south side, curtains for the court, of twisted linen,
a hundred cubits long on one side.
And its pillars, twenty, [five cubits between the pillars], and their sockets twenty, of copper;
the hooks of the pillars and their belts [(threads by which the pillars were encircled)] of silver.

pairs.hebrew: וְכֵ֨ן לִפְאַ֤ת צָפוֹן֙ בָּאֹ֔רֶךְ קְלָעִ֖ים מֵ֣אָה אֹ֑רֶךְ
pairs.english: And so for the northern side in length. Curtains a hundred (cubits) long,
and its pillars, twenty, and their sockets twenty, of copper;
the hooks of the pillars and their belts, of silver.

pairs.hebrew: וְרֹ֤חַב הֶֽחָצֵר֙ לִפְאַת־יָ֔ם קְלָעִ֖ים חֲמִשִּׁ֣ים אַמָּ֑ה
pairs.english: And the width of the court on the west side: Curtains, fifty cubits (long),
their pillars, ten, and their sockets, ten.
And the width of the court on the front side, to the east,
fifty cubits.
And fifteen cubits of curtains on the shoulder [(on one side of the opening)],
their pillars three and their sockets three.
And on the second shoulder, fifteen (cubits) of curtains,
their pillars three and their sockets three.
And for the gate of the court, a screen [a curtain] of twenty cubits:

pairs.hebrew: תְּכֵ֨לֶת וְאַרְגָּמָ֜ן וְתוֹלַ֧עַת שָׁנִ֛י וְשֵׁ֥שׁ מׇשְׁזָ֖ר מַעֲשֵׂ֣ה רֹקֵ֑ם
pairs.english: blue wool, and purple wool, and scarlet wool, and twisted linen, the work of an embroiderer,
their pillars four and their sockets four.
All the pillars of the court roundabout, belted with silver,
their hooks of silver and their sockets of copper.

pairs.hebrew: אֹ֣רֶךְ הֶֽחָצֵר֩ מֵאָ֨ה בָֽאַמָּ֜ה וְרֹ֣חַב ׀ חֲמִשִּׁ֣ים בַּחֲמִשִּׁ֗ים
pairs.english: The length of the court, a hundred cubits, and the width, fifty by fifty,
and the height, five cubits of twisted linen,
and their sockets [(including the sockets for the pillars of the screen)] of copper.
All the implements of the tabernacle for all of its labor [for erecting and dismantling it],
and all of its pegs, and all the pegs of the courtyard, of copper.
And you shall command the children of Israel

pairs.hebrew: וְיִקְח֨וּ אֵלֶ֜יךָ שֶׁ֣מֶן זַ֥יִת זָ֛ךְ כָּתִ֖ית לַמָּא֑וֹר
pairs.english: that they take for you olive oil, clear [without lees], (the olives) crushed [(in a mortar and not ground in a mill, so that there be no lees)], for illumination [(but the olives may be ground in a mill for the (oil of the) meal-offering)],
to raise a light [(the flame rising of itself)] continually [i.e., each night].

pairs.hebrew: בְּאֹ֣הֶל מוֹעֵד֩ מִח֨וּץ לַפָּרֹ֜כֶת אֲשֶׁ֣ר עַל־הָעֵדֻ֗ת
pairs.english: In the tent of meeting outside the parocheth which is before the Testimony,

pairs.hebrew: יַעֲרֹךְ֩ אֹת֨וֹ אַהֲרֹ֧ן וּבָנָ֛יו מֵעֶ֥רֶב עַד־בֹּ֖קֶר לִפְנֵ֣י יְהֹוָ֑ה
pairs.english: Aaron and his sons shall arrange it [so that it burn] from evening until morning before the L-rd,
an eternal statute for their generations, from the children of Israel.

pairs.hebrew: וְאַתָּ֡ה הַקְרֵ֣ב אֵלֶ֩יךָ֩ אֶת־אַהֲרֹ֨ן אָחִ֜יךָ וְאֶת־בָּנָ֣יו אִתּ֗וֹ מִתּ֛וֹךְ בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לְכַהֲנוֹ־לִ֑י
pairs.english: And you, draw near to yourself [after completing the work of the tabernacle] Aaron your brother and his sons with him from the midst of the children of Israel to be a priest unto Me —

pairs.hebrew: אַהֲרֹ֕ן נָדָ֧ב וַאֲבִיה֛וּא אֶלְעָזָ֥ר וְאִיתָמָ֖ר בְּנֵ֥י אַהֲרֹֽן׃
pairs.english: Aaron, Nadav and Avihu, Elazar and Ithamar, the sons of Aaron.
And you shall make consecrated garments for Aaron your brother,
for honor and for glory.

pairs.hebrew: וְאַתָּ֗ה תְּדַבֵּר֙ אֶל־כׇּל־חַכְמֵי־לֵ֔ב אֲשֶׁ֥ר מִלֵּאתִ֖יו ר֣וּחַ חׇכְמָ֑ה
pairs.english: And you shall speak to all the wise of heart whom I have filled with the spirit of wisdom,
that they make the vestments of Aaron to sanctify him, to make him a Cohein [a ministering priest] unto Me.
And these are the garments which they shall make:

pairs.hebrew: חֹ֤שֶׁן וְאֵפוֹד֙ וּמְעִ֔יל וּכְתֹ֥נֶת תַּשְׁבֵּ֖ץ מִצְנֶ֣פֶת וְאַבְנֵ֑ט
pairs.english: a choshen [an ornament worn on the heart], an ephod [a kind of apron], a me'il [an outer robe], a kethoneth [an inner robe worn on the skin] with checkered indentations, a mitznefeth [a dome-like hat], and an avnet [the belt over the kethoneth].

pairs.hebrew: וְעָשׂ֨וּ בִגְדֵי־קֹ֜דֶשׁ לְאַהֲרֹ֥ן אָחִ֛יךָ וּלְבָנָ֖יו לְכַהֲנוֹ־לִֽי׃
pairs.english: And they shall make garments of kodesh [i.e., from the contribution that has been consecrated (mekudesheth) for My name] for Aaron your brother and for his sons to make him a Cohein unto Me.
And they [the wise of heart] shall take [from the donors] the gold,
the blue wool, the purple wool, the scarlet wool, and the linen [whereof to make the garments].
And they shall make the ephod

pairs.hebrew: זָ֠הָ֠ב תְּכֵ֨לֶת וְאַרְגָּמָ֜ן תּוֹלַ֧עַת שָׁנִ֛י וְשֵׁ֥שׁ מׇשְׁזָ֖ר מַעֲשֵׂ֥ה חֹשֵֽׁב׃
pairs.english: of gold, blue wool, purple wool, scarlet wool, and twisted linen, artistic work. [See Rashi on 26:1.]

pairs.hebrew: שְׁתֵּ֧י כְתֵפֹ֣ת חֹֽבְרֹ֗ת יִֽהְיֶה־לּ֛וֹ אֶל־שְׁנֵ֥י קְצוֹתָ֖יו
pairs.english: Two shoulder straps, attached, shall it [the ephod] have to its two ends [(to the ends of the width of the ephod, which is the width of the Cohein's back)],
and it [the ephod with the two shoulder straps] shall be connected [to the cheishev (8) (by needle, and not woven together with it)].

pairs.hebrew: וְחֵ֤שֶׁב אֲפֻדָּתוֹ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָלָ֔יו כְּמַעֲשֵׂ֖הוּ מִמֶּ֣נּוּ יִהְיֶ֑ה
pairs.english: And the cheishev [the belt] of his adornment which is above it [i.e., which is on the upper edge of the ephod], after its manner [i.e., artistic work, of the five varieties (of material)], of it [i.e., woven together with the ephod] shall it be:

pairs.hebrew: זָהָ֗ב תְּכֵ֧לֶת וְאַרְגָּמָ֛ן וְתוֹלַ֥עַת שָׁנִ֖י וְשֵׁ֥שׁ מׇשְׁזָֽר׃
pairs.english: gold, blue wool, purple wool, scarlet wool, and twisted linen.
And you shall take the two shoham stones
and engrave thereon the names of the children of Israel.
Six of their names on the one stone,

pairs.hebrew: וְאֶת־שְׁמ֞וֹת הַשִּׁשָּׁ֧ה הַנּוֹתָרִ֛ים עַל־הָאֶ֥בֶן הַשֵּׁנִ֖ית כְּתוֹלְדֹתָֽם׃
pairs.english: and the names of the remaining six on the second stone, in order of their birth [i.e., on the first stone: Reuven, Shimon, Levi, Yehudah, Dan, Naftali; on the second: Gad, Asher, Yissachar, Zevulun, Yosef, Binyamin].

pairs.hebrew: מַעֲשֵׂ֣ה חָרַשׁ֮ אֶ֒בֶן֒ פִּתּוּחֵ֣י חֹתָ֗ם תְּפַתַּח֙ אֶת־שְׁתֵּ֣י הָאֲבָנִ֔ים עַל־שְׁמֹ֖ת בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל
pairs.english: The work of a stone artisan (a lapidary), [with script as clear as] the engraving of a signet shall you engrave the two stones with the names of the children of Israel;
surrounded by golden settings shall you make them [(the settings then to be attached to the shoulder straps of the ephod)].

pairs.hebrew: וְשַׂמְתָּ֞ אֶת־שְׁתֵּ֣י הָאֲבָנִ֗ים עַ֚ל כִּתְפֹ֣ת הָֽאֵפֹ֔ד
pairs.english: And you shall place the two stones on the shoulder straps of the ephod,
stones of remembrance for the children of Israel.

pairs.hebrew: וְנָשָׂא֩ אַהֲרֹ֨ן אֶת־שְׁמוֹתָ֜ם לִפְנֵ֧י יְהֹוָ֛ה עַל־שְׁתֵּ֥י כְתֵפָ֖יו לְזִכָּרֹֽן׃ {ס}
pairs.english: And Aaron shall carry their names before the L-rd on his two shoulders as a remembrance [i.e., so that the Holy One see the tribes inscribed before Him and remember their righteousness].
And you shall make
[two] golden settings.
And (you shall make) two chains of pure gold.

pairs.hebrew: מִגְבָּלֹ֛ת תַּעֲשֶׂ֥ה אֹתָ֖ם מַעֲשֵׂ֣ה עֲבֹ֑ת וְנָתַתָּ֛ה אֶת־שַׁרְשְׁרֹ֥ת הָעֲבֹתֹ֖ת עַל־הַֽמִּשְׁבְּצֹֽת׃ {ס}
pairs.english: At the edge [of the choshen] shall you make them, braided chains on the settings [of the ephod].
And you shall make a choshen of judgment [i.e., a choshen which atones for subversion of judgment]; artistic work,
like the work of the ephod shall you make it:

pairs.hebrew: זָ֠הָ֠ב תְּכֵ֨לֶת וְאַרְגָּמָ֜ן וְתוֹלַ֧עַת שָׁנִ֛י וְשֵׁ֥שׁ מׇשְׁזָ֖ר תַּעֲשֶׂ֥ה אֹתֽוֹ׃
pairs.english: gold, blue wool, purple wool, scarlet wool, and twisted linen shall you make it.
Square shall it be, folded (into a square),
a zereth (half a cubit) its length, and a zereth its width.

pairs.hebrew: וּמִלֵּאתָ֥ בוֹ֙ מִלֻּ֣אַת אֶ֔בֶן אַרְבָּעָ֖ה טוּרִ֣ים אָ֑בֶן
pairs.english: And you shall fill it [its indentations] with stone filling, four rows of stone.

pairs.hebrew: ט֗וּר אֹ֤דֶם פִּטְדָה֙ וּבָרֶ֔קֶת הַטּ֖וּר הָאֶחָֽד׃
pairs.english: A row of odem, pitedah, and bareketh — the one row.
The second row —
nofech, sapir, and yahalom.
The third row —
leshem, shevo, and achlamah.
And the fourth row — tarshish, shoham, and yashfeh.
Set in gold shall they [the rows] be with their [exact] fillings [i.e., They shall be surrounded by golden settings of a depth to accommodate the exact thickness of the stone.]

pairs.hebrew: וְ֠הָאֲבָנִ֠ים תִּֽהְיֶ֜יןָ עַל־שְׁמֹ֧ת בְּנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל שְׁתֵּ֥ים עֶשְׂרֵ֖ה עַל־שְׁמֹתָ֑ם
pairs.english: And the stones shall be according to the names of the children of Israel, twelve, according to their names,

pairs.hebrew: פִּתּוּחֵ֤י חוֹתָם֙ אִ֣ישׁ עַל־שְׁמ֔וֹ תִּֽהְיֶ֕יןָ לִשְׁנֵ֥י עָשָׂ֖ר שָֽׁבֶט׃
pairs.english: like the engraving of a signet, each by his name shall they be, for the twelve tribes [in order of their birth: odem for Reuven, pitedah for Shimon, etc.]
And you shall make for the choshen chains at the edge,
braidwork of pure gold.
And you shall make for the choshen two rings of gold,

pairs.hebrew: וְנָתַתָּ֗ אֶת־שְׁתֵּי֙ הַטַּבָּע֔וֹת עַל־שְׁנֵ֖י קְצ֥וֹת הַחֹֽשֶׁן׃
pairs.english: and you shall put the two rings on the two ends of the choshen [on the two corners opposite the neck.]

pairs.hebrew: וְנָתַתָּ֗ה אֶת־שְׁתֵּי֙ עֲבֹתֹ֣ת הַזָּהָ֔ב עַל־שְׁתֵּ֖י הַטַּבָּעֹ֑ת
pairs.english: And you shall place the two golden braids on the two rings
at the ends of the choshen.

pairs.hebrew: וְאֵ֨ת שְׁתֵּ֤י קְצוֹת֙ שְׁתֵּ֣י הָעֲבֹתֹ֔ת תִּתֵּ֖ן עַל־שְׁתֵּ֣י הַֽמִּשְׁבְּצ֑וֹת
pairs.english: And the two ends of the two braids [i.e., the two heads of each braid] you shall place on the two settings (verses 12-13) [the right braid on the right setting, and the left braid on the left],
and you shall place [the settings] on the shoulder straps of the ephod on its face [i.e., on the topside of the (shoulder strap of the) ephod.]
And you shall make two golden rings,
and you shall place them on the two ends of the choshen [the two lower corners]
on its edge which faces the ephod [i.e., the lower, apron part], inwards [(whereas the rings on top of the choshen face outwards)].
And you shall make two golden rings,

pairs.hebrew: וְנָתַתָּ֣ה אֹתָ֡ם עַל־שְׁתֵּי֩ כִתְפ֨וֹת הָאֵפ֤וֹד מִלְּמַ֙טָּה֙ מִמּ֣וּל פָּנָ֔יו לְעֻמַּ֖ת מַחְבַּרְתּ֑וֹ
pairs.english: and you shall place them on the (origin of the) two shoulder straps of the ephod below, on its face [i.e., on the topside of the ephod], opposite [i.e., near] where it [the shoulder strap] is attached [to the ephod],
above the cheishev of the ephod.

pairs.hebrew: וְיִרְכְּס֣וּ אֶת־הַ֠חֹ֠שֶׁן מִֽטַּבְּעֹתָ֞ו אֶל־טַבְּעֹ֤ת הָאֵפוֹד֙ בִּפְתִ֣יל תְּכֵ֔לֶת לִֽהְי֖וֹת עַל־חֵ֣שֶׁב הָאֵפ֑וֹד
pairs.english: And they shall bind the choshen from its rings to the rings of the ephod with a string of blue wool to be on [i.e., fastened to] the cheishev of the ephod.
And the choshen shall not be detached from the ephod.

pairs.hebrew: וְנָשָׂ֣א אַ֠הֲרֹ֠ן אֶת־שְׁמ֨וֹת בְּנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל בְּחֹ֧שֶׁן הַמִּשְׁפָּ֛ט עַל־לִבּ֖וֹ בְּבֹא֣וֹ אֶל־הַקֹּ֑דֶשׁ
pairs.english: And Aaron shall bear the names of the children of Israel on the choshen of judgment on his heart when he enters the sanctuary,
as a remembrance before the L-rd, always.

And you shall place into the [fold of the] choshen of judgment, the urim and the tumim [the (written) Tetragrammaton, by means of which the choshen illuminates (meir) and brings to perfection (metamem) its words].

pairs.hebrew: וְהָיוּ֙ עַל־לֵ֣ב אַהֲרֹ֔ן בְּבֹא֖וֹ לִפְנֵ֣י יְהֹוָ֑ה
pairs.english: And they shall be on Aaron's heart when he comes before the L-rd.

pairs.hebrew: וְנָשָׂ֣א אַ֠הֲרֹ֠ן אֶת־מִשְׁפַּ֨ט בְּנֵי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֧ל עַל־לִבּ֛וֹ לִפְנֵ֥י יְהֹוָ֖ה תָּמִֽיד׃ {ס}
pairs.english: And Aaron shall bear the judgment of the children of Israel [(i.e., the choshen, which they consult for judgment and direction)] on his heart before the L-rd, always.
And you shall make the me'il (the outer robe) of the ephod [i.e., belted by the ephod]
entirely of blue wool.
And its head-opening shall be [folded over] within it [as a hem].

pairs.hebrew: שָׂפָ֡ה יִֽהְיֶה֩ לְפִ֨יו סָבִ֜יב מַעֲשֵׂ֣ה אֹרֵ֗ג
pairs.english: Its opening shall have a border roundabout, the work of a weaver [and not needlework].
As the opening of a suit of armor shall it [its neck-opening] be for it, so that it not be torn [(Tearing it constitutes transgression of a negative commandment.]

pairs.hebrew: וְעָשִׂ֣יתָ עַל־שׁוּלָ֗יו רִמֹּנֵי֙ תְּכֵ֤לֶת וְאַרְגָּמָן֙ וְתוֹלַ֣עַת שָׁנִ֔י עַל־שׁוּלָ֖יו סָבִ֑יב
pairs.english: And you shall make on its (lower) hem pomegranates [(they were round and hollow)] of blue wool and purple wool and scarlet wool on its hem roundabout,
and golden bells [with clappers within them] in their [the pomegranates'] midst roundabout, [one bell between every two pomegranates].
A golden bell and a pomegranate [next to it],
a golden bell and a pomegranate
on the hem of the me'il roundabout.
And it will be on Aaron for ministering,

pairs.hebrew: וְנִשְׁמַ֣ע ק֠וֹל֠וֹ בְּבֹא֨וֹ אֶל־הַקֹּ֜דֶשׁ לִפְנֵ֧י יְהֹוָ֛ה וּבְצֵאת֖וֹ
pairs.english: and its sound will be heard when he comes to the sanctuary before the L-rd and when he leaves,
and he will not die [(the implication being that if he enters lacking one of the priestly garments he is subject to death at the hands of Heaven)].
And you shall make a tzitz [a kind of plate, two fingerbreadths wide, which went round his forehead from ear to ear], of pure gold,
and you shall engrave it as the engraving of a signet:
"Holy to the L-rd."
And you shall place it on a string of blue wool,
and it [the middle string of three (two at the sides and one in the middle)] shall be on the mitznefeth (the mitre).
Opposite the face of [i.e., on top of] the mitznefeth shall it be.
And it [the tzitz] shall be on Aaron's forehead.

pairs.hebrew: וְנָשָׂ֨א אַהֲרֹ֜ן אֶת־עֲוֺ֣ן הַקֳּדָשִׁ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֤ר יַקְדִּ֙ישׁוּ֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לְכׇֽל־מַתְּנֹ֖ת קׇדְשֵׁיהֶ֑ם
pairs.english: And Aaron shall bear [(towards atonement)] the sin of the holy (offerings) which the children of Israel consecrate of all the gifts of their holy offerings [(the tzitz atones for offerings of impure blood and fats)].

pairs.hebrew: וְהָיָ֤ה עַל־מִצְחוֹ֙ תָּמִ֔יד לְרָצ֥וֹן לָהֶ֖ם לִפְנֵ֥י יְהֹוָֽה׃
pairs.english: And it shall be on his forehead [to atone for them] always, for (the conferring of) favor upon them before the L-rd.
And you shall checker [with indentations] the kethoneth (the inner robe) [which is made of] linen.
And you shall make a mitznefeth of linen;
and an avneit (a belt) shall you make, the work of an embroiderer.
And for the sons of Aaron you shall make [(these four garments, including michnasayim (42), and no more:)] kutanoth;
and you shall make for them avneitim;
and migbaoth [mitznafoth] shall you make for them for honor and for glory.

pairs.hebrew: וְהִלְבַּשְׁתָּ֤ אֹתָם֙ אֶת־אַהֲרֹ֣ן אָחִ֔יךָ וְאֶת־בָּנָ֖יו אִתּ֑וֹ
pairs.english: And you shall dress with them [the eight garments] Aaron your brother, and [with the four garments] his sons with him,
and you shall anoint them [Aaron and his sons (with the anointing oil)], and you shall fill their hands [i.e., you shall invest them],
and you shall sanctify them, and they shall minister unto Me.

pairs.hebrew: וַעֲשֵׂ֤ה לָהֶם֙ מִכְנְסֵי־בָ֔ד לְכַסּ֖וֹת בְּשַׂ֣ר עֶרְוָ֑ה
pairs.english: And you shall make for them [for Aaron and for his sons] pants (michnasayim) of linen to cover the flesh of nakedness.
From the hips to the thighs shall they be.

pairs.hebrew: וְהָיוּ֩ עַל־אַהֲרֹ֨ן וְעַל־בָּנָ֜יו בְּבֹאָ֣ם ׀ אֶל־אֹ֣הֶל מוֹעֵ֗ד א֣וֹ בְגִשְׁתָּ֤ם אֶל־הַמִּזְבֵּ֙חַ֙ לְשָׁרֵ֣ת בַּקֹּ֔דֶשׁ
pairs.english: And they [their respective garments] shall be on Aaron and on his sons when they come to the tent of meeting [to the heichal (Temple); likewise, to the mishkan (tabernacle)] or when they draw near to the altar to serve in holiness,
that they not bear a sin and die [ — whence it is derived that a Cohein who ministers lacking one of the priestly garments incurs death (at the hands of Heaven)],
an eternal statute [categorical (for validity of the service) immediately and for future generations], for him and for his seed after him.

pairs.hebrew: וְזֶ֨ה הַדָּבָ֜ר אֲשֶֽׁר־תַּעֲשֶׂ֥ה לָהֶ֛ם לְקַדֵּ֥שׁ אֹתָ֖ם לְכַהֵ֣ן לִ֑י
pairs.english: And this is the thing that you shall do to them to sanctify them to minister unto Me:
Take one young bullock [to atone for the sin of the golden calf (that "calf" being a bullock)]
and two unblemished rams.
And [(ten of each of the following kinds:)] matzah bread [(later referred to as "challah of oil bread" (23) because he puts as much oil into it as into the loaves and wafers combined)],
and matzah challoth mixed with oil [when they are still flour],
and matzah wafers anointed with oil. [After they are baked, he anoints them in the shape of the Greek letter chi, similar to our nun.]
Of fine wheat flour shall you make them.
And you shall place them in one basket,
and you shall bring them near in the basket [to the court of the mishkan on the day it is erected],
and the bullock and the two rams.

pairs.hebrew: וְאֶת־אַהֲרֹ֤ן וְאֶת־בָּנָיו֙ תַּקְרִ֔יב אֶל־פֶּ֖תַח אֹ֣הֶל מוֹעֵ֑ד
pairs.english: And Aaron and his sons you shall bring near to the entrance of the tent of meeting,
and you shall wash them in water [(This is immersion of the entire body)].
And you shall take the garments

pairs.hebrew: וְהִלְבַּשְׁתָּ֤ אֶֽת־אַהֲרֹן֙ אֶת־הַכֻּתֹּ֔נֶת וְאֵת֙ מְעִ֣יל הָאֵפֹ֔ד וְאֶת־הָאֵפֹ֖ד וְאֶת־הַחֹ֑שֶׁן
pairs.english: and you shall dress Aaron with the kutoneth and the me'il of the ephod and the ephod and the choshen.
And you shall adorn him with the cheishev of the ephod.
And you shall place the mitznefeth on his head,
and you shall place the crown of sanctity [the tzitz] on the mitznefeth. [See 28:37].
And you shall take the oil of anointment,
and you shall pour it on his head,
and you shall anoint him.
And his sons shall you bring near
and dress them in kutanoth.
And you shall gird them with an avneit, Aaron and his sons,
and you shall bind migbaoth upon them,
and the kehunah (the priesthood) shall be for them an everlasting statute;
and you shall fill the hand of Aaron and the hand of his sons. [i.e., You shall thereby invest them into the priesthood.]
And you shall bring the bullock before the tent of meeting,

pairs.hebrew: וְסָמַ֨ךְ אַהֲרֹ֧ן וּבָנָ֛יו אֶת־יְדֵיהֶ֖ם עַל־רֹ֥אשׁ הַפָּֽר׃
pairs.english: and Aaron and his sons shall place their hands on the head of the bullock.
And you shall slaughter the bullock before the L-rd
at the entrance of the tent of meeting [i.e., in the court of the mishkan before the entrance].
And you shall take of the blood of the bullock
and you shall place it on [top of] the horns of the altar with your finger,
and all of the [remnants of the] blood you shall pour at the base of the altar.
And you shall take all of the fat that covers the innards [i.e., the stomach membrane]

pairs.hebrew: וְאֵ֗ת הַיֹּתֶ֙רֶת֙ עַל־הַכָּבֵ֔ד וְאֵת֙ שְׁתֵּ֣י הַכְּלָיֹ֔ת וְאֶת־הַחֵ֖לֶב אֲשֶׁ֣ר עֲלֵיהֶ֑ן
pairs.english: and the lobe [the liver membrane] with [some of] the liver, and the two kidneys and the fat that is upon them,
and you shall smoke (them) upon the altar.

pairs.hebrew: וְאֶת־בְּשַׂ֤ר הַפָּר֙ וְאֶת־עֹר֣וֹ וְאֶת־פִּרְשׁ֔וֹ תִּשְׂרֹ֣ף בָּאֵ֔שׁ מִח֖וּץ לַֽמַּחֲנֶ֑ה
pairs.english: And the flesh of the bullock and its hide and its waste you shall burn in a fire outside the camp
— it is a sin-offering [This is the only outer-altar sin-offering which is (entirely) burnt].
And you shall take the one ram

pairs.hebrew: וְסָ֨מְכ֜וּ אַהֲרֹ֧ן וּבָנָ֛יו אֶת־יְדֵיהֶ֖ם עַל־רֹ֥אשׁ הָאָֽיִל׃
pairs.english: and Aaron and his sons shall place their hands on the head of the ram.
And you shall slaughter the ram
and you shall take its blood

and you shall toss it [from a vessel] on the [corners of the] altar [so that the blood is seen on both sides of each corner] roundabout. [He tosses it on two opposite diagonal corners, so that the blood is seen on all four sides of the altar.]
And you shall cut the ram into its pieces,
and you shall wash its innards and its feet,
and you shall place them with its [other] pieces and with its head.
And you shall smoke the entire ram upon the altar.
It is a burnt-offering to the L-rd,
a fragrance that is pleasing [in that His will was done], a fire-offering [i.e., the smoking of the limbs on the fire] to the L-rd.
And you shall take the second ram,

pairs.hebrew: וְסָמַ֨ךְ אַהֲרֹ֧ן וּבָנָ֛יו אֶת־יְדֵיהֶ֖ם עַל־רֹ֥אשׁ הָאָֽיִל׃
pairs.english: and Aaron and his sons shall place their hands on the head of the ram.
And you shall slaughter the ram, and you shall take of its blood

pairs.hebrew: וְנָֽתַתָּ֡ה עַל־תְּנוּךְ֩ אֹ֨זֶן אַהֲרֹ֜ן וְעַל־תְּנ֨וּךְ אֹ֤זֶן בָּנָיו֙ הַיְמָנִ֔ית
pairs.english: and you shall place it on the t'nuch of the ear [the cartilage of the middle section inside the ear] of Aaron, and on the t'nuch of the ear of his sons — the right (ear) —

pairs.hebrew: וְעַל־בֹּ֤הֶן יָדָם֙ הַיְמָנִ֔ית וְעַל־בֹּ֥הֶן רַגְלָ֖ם הַיְמָנִ֑ית
pairs.english: and on the thumb of their right hand and on the big toe of their right foot.
And you shall toss the blood on the altar roundabout.

pairs.hebrew: וְלָקַחְתָּ֞ מִן־הַדָּ֨ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר עַֽל־הַמִּזְבֵּ֘חַ֮ וּמִשֶּׁ֣מֶן הַמִּשְׁחָה֒
pairs.english: And you shall take some of the blood which is on the altar and some of the anointment oil,

pairs.hebrew: וְהִזֵּיתָ֤ עַֽל־אַהֲרֹן֙ וְעַל־בְּגָדָ֔יו וְעַל־בָּנָ֛יו וְעַל־בִּגְדֵ֥י בָנָ֖יו אִתּ֑וֹ
pairs.english: and you shall sprinkle it upon Aaron and upon his garments and upon his sons and upon the garments of his sons with him.

pairs.hebrew: וְקָדַ֥שׁ הוּא֙ וּבְגָדָ֔יו וּבָנָ֛יו וּבִגְדֵ֥י בָנָ֖יו אִתּֽוֹ׃
pairs.english: And he and his garments and his sons and the garments of his sons with him shall be sanctified.

pairs.hebrew: וְלָקַחְתָּ֣ מִן־הָ֠אַ֠יִל הַחֵ֨לֶב וְהָֽאַלְיָ֜ה וְאֶת־הַחֵ֣לֶב ׀ הַֽמְכַסֶּ֣ה אֶת־הַקֶּ֗רֶב
pairs.english: And you shall take from the ram the fat [of the small intestines, or (according to another opinion) the stomach], and the fat-tail, [from the kidneys and below], and the fat that covers the innards,

pairs.hebrew: וְאֵ֨ת יֹתֶ֤רֶת הַכָּבֵד֙ וְאֵ֣ת ׀ שְׁתֵּ֣י הַכְּלָיֹ֗ת וְאֶת־הַחֵ֙לֶב֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עֲלֵיהֶ֔ן וְאֵ֖ת שׁ֣וֹק הַיָּמִ֑ין
pairs.english: and the lobe with [some of] the liver and the two kidneys and the fat that is on them and the right thigh [(This is the only instance of the smoking of the right thigh with the eimurim [the consecrated parts])];

for it is the ram of miluim (completeness) [a peace-offering (shelamim), complete in that all share in it: the altar, the officiator (in this instance, Moses, who receives the breast), and the owners (in this instance, Aaron and his sons, who eat the rest of it)].

pairs.hebrew: וְכִכַּ֨ר לֶ֜חֶם אַחַ֗ת וְֽחַלַּ֨ת לֶ֥חֶם שֶׁ֛מֶן אַחַ֖ת וְרָקִ֣יק אֶחָ֑ד
pairs.english: And one loaf of bread [from the (matzah) challoth (see 2)], and one challah of oil bread, and one wafer
from the basket of matzoth which is before the L-rd. [(This is the only instance of a bread offering accompanying an animal offering, being burned on the altar)].

pairs.hebrew: וְשַׂמְתָּ֣ הַכֹּ֔ל עַ֚ל כַּפֵּ֣י אַהֲרֹ֔ן וְעַ֖ל כַּפֵּ֣י בָנָ֑יו
pairs.english: And you shall place all of it on the palms of Aaron and on the palms of his sons,

and you shall wave them a waving before the L-rd. [The Cohein (in this instance, Moses) places his hand under that of the owner (in this instance, Aaron and his sons, who held the parts), and he moves them back and forth (to the Owner of the four winds of the world). Waving staves off punishment and ill winds. In "lifting" (27), he lifts and lowers them (to the Owner of heaven and earth). Lifting staves off harmful dews.]
And you shall take them from their hand
and you shall smoke them on the altar after the [first ram which you brought as a] burnt-offering,

pairs.hebrew: לְרֵ֤יחַ נִיח֙וֹחַ֙ לִפְנֵ֣י יְהֹוָ֔ה אִשֶּׁ֥ה ה֖וּא לַיהֹוָֽה׃
pairs.english: a pleasing fragrance before the L-rd. It is a fire-offering to the L-rd [i.e., in His name].

pairs.hebrew: וְלָקַחְתָּ֣ אֶת־הֶֽחָזֶ֗ה מֵאֵ֤יל הַמִּלֻּאִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לְאַהֲרֹ֔ן
pairs.english: And you shall take the breast of the ram of miluim which is Aaron's,
and you shall wave it, a waving before the L-rd,
and it shall be a portion for you.

pairs.hebrew: וְקִדַּשְׁתָּ֞ אֵ֣ת ׀ חֲזֵ֣ה הַתְּנוּפָ֗ה וְאֵת֙ שׁ֣וֹק הַתְּרוּמָ֔ה
pairs.english: And you shall consecrate [for waving and lifting in peace-offerings of future generations] the breast of the waving and the thigh of the lifting,
which was waved and which was lifted,

pairs.hebrew: מֵאֵיל֙ הַמִּלֻּאִ֔ים מֵאֲשֶׁ֥ר לְאַהֲרֹ֖ן וּמֵאֲשֶׁ֥ר לְבָנָֽיו׃
pairs.english: from the ram of the miluim which is Aaron's and his sons'.

pairs.hebrew: וְהָיָה֩ לְאַהֲרֹ֨ן וּלְבָנָ֜יו לְחׇק־עוֹלָ֗ם מֵאֵת֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל
pairs.english: [But you shall not consecrate it for burning in future generations, for] it shall be for Aaron and his sons as an everlasting share from the children of Israel [to whom the peace-offerings belong].
For it [breast and thigh] is a devotion.

pairs.hebrew: וּתְרוּמָ֞ה יִהְיֶ֨ה מֵאֵ֤ת בְּנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ מִזִּבְחֵ֣י שַׁלְמֵיהֶ֔ם תְּרוּמָתָ֖ם לַיהֹוָֽה׃
pairs.english: And it shall be set aside by the children of Israel from the sacrifices of their peace-offerings, their devotion to the L-rd.

pairs.hebrew: וּבִגְדֵ֤י הַקֹּ֙דֶשׁ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לְאַהֲרֹ֔ן יִהְי֥וּ לְבָנָ֖יו אַחֲרָ֑יו
pairs.english: And the consecrated garments which are Aaron's shall be to his sons [of the high-priesthood] after him,
to be exalted through them
and to be invested [in the high-priesthood] through them.

pairs.hebrew: שִׁבְעַ֣ת יָמִ֗ים יִלְבָּשָׁ֧ם הַכֹּהֵ֛ן תַּחְתָּ֖יו מִבָּנָ֑יו
pairs.english: Seven [consecutive] days shall he don them, he who officiates in his stead, of his sons,

pairs.hebrew: אֲשֶׁ֥ר יָבֹ֛א אֶל־אֹ֥הֶל מוֹעֵ֖ד לְשָׁרֵ֥ת בַּקֹּֽדֶשׁ׃
pairs.english: who comes to the tent of meeting [i.e., who is qualified to enter the Holy of Holies on Yom Kippur, viz. the high-priest], to minister in the holy place.
And the miluim ram shall you take
and you shall cook its flesh in a holy place [i.e., in the court of the tent of meeting, these peace-offerings being holy of holies].

pairs.hebrew: וְאָכַ֨ל אַהֲרֹ֤ן וּבָנָיו֙ אֶת־בְּשַׂ֣ר הָאַ֔יִל וְאֶת־הַלֶּ֖חֶם אֲשֶׁ֣ר בַּסָּ֑ל
pairs.english: And Aaron and his sons shall eat the flesh of the ram and the bread that is in the basket
at the entrance [i.e., in the court] of the tent of meeting.
And they [Aaron and his sons, the owners,] shall eat them, so that there be atoned through them [any impurity they (Aaron and his sons) possess],
to invest them [through the ram and the bread] and to consecrate them [in the priesthood].
And a stranger (i.e., a non-Cohein) may not eat, for they are holy [i.e., holy of holies (whence is derived the exhortation against a non-Cohein eating holy of holies)].
And if anything be left over from the flesh of the miluim or from the bread until morning,
you shall burn what is left over in fire.
It shall not be eaten, for it is consecrated.

pairs.hebrew: וְעָשִׂ֜יתָ לְאַהֲרֹ֤ן וּלְבָנָיו֙ כָּ֔כָה כְּכֹ֥ל אֲשֶׁר־צִוִּ֖יתִי אֹתָ֑כָה
pairs.english: And you shall do thus to Aaron and to his sons, according to everything I have commanded you [(The repetition renders the commandment categorical, so that if even one detail is omitted they are not invested.)]
Seven days [i.e., on each of the seven days] shall you invest them [as indicated].
And a bullock sin-offering shall you make each day for the cleansings [of the altar of any impurity],
and you shall purify the altar [by application of blood with the finger] when you cleanse it.
And you shall anoint it [with the anointing oil] to consecrate it.

pairs.hebrew: שִׁבְעַ֣ת יָמִ֗ים תְּכַפֵּר֙ עַל־הַמִּזְבֵּ֔חַ וְקִדַּשְׁתָּ֖ אֹת֑וֹ
pairs.english: Seven days shall you cleanse the altar and you shall consecrate it.
And the altar shall be holy of holies [in that]
whatever touches the altar [(even an unfit offering)] shall be consecrated.

And this is what you shall offer upon the altar [("this": something like the burnt-offering which follows, i.e., an animal which was fit when it entered the Temple court — even if it became unfit thereafter. Such animals (but not those which were unfit before they entered), once they ascend the altar are not taken down)]:
sheep in their first year, two each day, always.
The one sheep shall you offer in the morning

pairs.hebrew: וְאֵת֙ הַכֶּ֣בֶשׂ הַשֵּׁנִ֔י תַּעֲשֶׂ֖ה בֵּ֥ין הָעַרְבָּֽיִם׃
pairs.english: and the second sheep shall you offer in the afternoon.

pairs.hebrew: וְעִשָּׂרֹ֨ן סֹ֜לֶת בָּל֨וּל בְּשֶׁ֤מֶן כָּתִית֙ רֶ֣בַע הַהִ֔ין
pairs.english: And a tenth of [an ephah of] fine flour mixed with oil of crushing [i.e., extracted by crushing olives in a mortar (although it is also valid if the olives are ground in a mill. See 27:20)], a quarter of a hin;

pairs.hebrew: וְנֵ֕סֶךְ רְבִיעִ֥ת הַהִ֖ין יָ֑יִן לַכֶּ֖בֶשׂ הָאֶחָֽד׃
pairs.english: and a libation, a quarter of a hin of wine, for the one sheep.

pairs.hebrew: וְאֵת֙ הַכֶּ֣בֶשׂ הַשֵּׁנִ֔י תַּעֲשֶׂ֖ה בֵּ֣ין הָעַרְבָּ֑יִם
pairs.english: And the second sheep shall you offer in the afternoon.
As the meal-offering of the morning and as its libation shall you offer it,
a pleasing fragrance [(this, referring to the libation meal-offering, which is entirely burnt)], a fire-offering to the L-rd.
A continual [daily] burnt-offering for your generations,
at the entrance of the tent of meeting before the L-rd,

pairs.hebrew: אֲשֶׁ֨ר אִוָּעֵ֤ד לָכֶם֙ שָׁ֔מָּה לְדַבֵּ֥ר אֵלֶ֖יךָ שָֽׁם׃
pairs.english: where I shall appoint a time for you to speak to you [i.e., When I set a time to speak with you, I shall set it for that place.]
And I shall be appointed there for the children of Israel [to speak to them],
and it [the mishkan] will be sanctified through My glory, [My shechinah resting therein.]
And I shall consecrate the tent of meeting and the altar;
and Aaron and his sons shall I consecrate to minister unto Me.
And I shall dwell in the midst of the children of Israel,
and I shall be a G-d to them.
And they shall know that I am the L-rd their G-d

pairs.hebrew: אֲשֶׁ֨ר הוֹצֵ֧אתִי אֹתָ֛ם מֵאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרַ֖יִם לְשׇׁכְנִ֣י בְתוֹכָ֑ם
pairs.english: who took them out of the land of Egypt so that I should dwell in their midst;
I am the L-rd their G-d.
And you shall make an altar for the smoking of the spices;
of acacia wood shall you make it.

pairs.hebrew: אַמָּ֨ה אׇרְכּ֜וֹ וְאַמָּ֤ה רׇחְבּוֹ֙ רָב֣וּעַ יִהְיֶ֔ה
pairs.english: A cubit its length and a cubit its width — square shall it be;
and two cubits its height.
From it shall its horns be (made).

pairs.hebrew: וְצִפִּיתָ֨ אֹת֜וֹ זָהָ֣ב טָה֗וֹר אֶת־גַּגּ֧וֹ וְאֶת־קִירֹתָ֛יו סָבִ֖יב וְאֶת־קַרְנֹתָ֑יו
pairs.english: And you shall cover it with pure gold, its roof and its walls roundabout and its horns;
and you shall make for it a rim of gold roundabout [symbolizing "the crown of kehunah"].
And two golden rings shall you make for it.

pairs.hebrew: מִתַּ֣חַת לְזֵר֗וֹ עַ֚ל שְׁתֵּ֣י צַלְעֹתָ֔יו תַּעֲשֶׂ֖ה עַל־שְׁנֵ֣י צִדָּ֑יו
pairs.english: Beneath its rim at its two corners shall you make (them), on its two sides.

pairs.hebrew: וְהָיָה֙ לְבָתִּ֣ים לְבַדִּ֔ים לָשֵׂ֥את אֹת֖וֹ בָּהֵֽמָּה׃
pairs.english: And it [the ring-work] shall be for housings for the staves to carry it thereby.
And you shall make the staves of acacia wood,
and you shall cover them with gold.

pairs.hebrew: וְנָתַתָּ֤ה אֹתוֹ֙ לִפְנֵ֣י הַפָּרֹ֔כֶת אֲשֶׁ֖ר עַל־אֲרֹ֣ן הָעֵדֻ֑ת
pairs.english: And you shall place it before the parocheth which is by the ark of testimony,
before the lid on the testimony [i.e., aligned directly opposite the ark, on the outside of the parocheth],
where I shall be appointed for you.

pairs.hebrew: וְהִקְטִ֥יר עָלָ֛יו אַהֲרֹ֖ן קְטֹ֣רֶת סַמִּ֑ים בַּבֹּ֣קֶר בַּבֹּ֗קֶר
pairs.english: And Aaron shall smoke incense upon it every morning.
When he cleans the lamps [the cups of the menorah (He would clean them of their ashes every morning)], he shall smoke it.

pairs.hebrew: וּבְהַעֲלֹ֨ת אַהֲרֹ֧ן אֶת־הַנֵּרֹ֛ת בֵּ֥ין הָעַרְבַּ֖יִם יַקְטִירֶ֑נָּה
pairs.english: And when Aaron kindles the lamps in the afternoon, he shall smoke it, [every day, half a portion in the morning, half in the afternoon],
a continual incense before the L-rd for your generations.
You shall not bring up upon it strange [i.e., donated] incense,
nor burnt-offering [any offering of animal or fowl], nor meal-offering [any offering of bread];
nor may you pour a libation upon it.

pairs.hebrew: וְכִפֶּ֤ר אַהֲרֹן֙ עַל־קַרְנֹתָ֔יו אַחַ֖ת בַּשָּׁנָ֑ה מִדַּ֞ם חַטַּ֣את הַכִּפֻּרִ֗ים
pairs.english: And Aaron will make atonement [by application of the blood] upon its horns once a year [on Yom Kippur] with the blood of the sin-offering of the atonements [the bullock and the goat of Yom Kippur, which atone for impurity of the sanctuary and its sacred objects].
Once a year shall he make atonement upon it for your generations;
it is holy of holies to the L-rd [It is consecrated for these things alone and for no other service.]
And the L-rd spoke
to Moses, saying:
When you [wish to] take [a count of] the heads of the children of Israel according to their numbers, [do not count them by heads, but]

pairs.hebrew: וְנָ֨תְנ֜וּ אִ֣ישׁ כֹּ֧פֶר נַפְשׁ֛וֹ לַיהֹוָ֖ה בִּפְקֹ֣ד אֹתָ֑ם
pairs.english: let each man give [a half-shekel] as an atonement for his soul to the L-rd in counting them,
so that there be no plague among them in counting them. [And count the shekalim, for the evil eye prevails over what is counted and makes it vulnerable to pestilence (See II Samuel 24:1-10)].
This is what they shall give [(The L-rd showed Moses a coin of fire whose weight was half a shekel and said to him: "Let them give a coin like this")], everyone who passes among the counted,
half a shekel by the [standard] shekel [weight] for consecration,

pairs.hebrew: עֶשְׂרִ֤ים גֵּרָה֙ הַשֶּׁ֔קֶל מַחֲצִ֣ית הַשֶּׁ֔קֶל תְּרוּמָ֖ה לַֽיהֹוָֽה׃
pairs.english: twenty gerah the shekel. [Let them give] half this shekel as an offering to the L-rd.

pairs.hebrew: כֹּ֗ל הָעֹבֵר֙ עַל־הַפְּקֻדִ֔ים מִבֶּ֛ן עֶשְׂרִ֥ים שָׁנָ֖ה וָמָ֑עְלָה
pairs.english: Everyone who passes among the counted, from the age of twenty years and above [(the army age)]
shall give the offering of the L-rd.

pairs.hebrew: הֶֽעָשִׁ֣יר לֹֽא־יַרְבֶּ֗ה וְהַדַּל֙ לֹ֣א יַמְעִ֔יט מִֽמַּחֲצִ֖ית הַשָּׁ֑קֶל
pairs.english: The rich shall not give more and the poor shall not give less than the half-shekel,
to give the offering of the L-rd
to atone for your souls [i.e., so that you not be plague-smitten because of the count.]

pairs.hebrew: וְלָקַחְתָּ֞ אֶת־כֶּ֣סֶף הַכִּפֻּרִ֗ים מֵאֵת֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל
pairs.english: And you shall take the silver of the atonements from the children of Israel

and give it for the work of the tent of meeting [(whence it is seen that Moses was commanded to count them at the beginning of the erection of the mishkan. It was from this counting that the sockets for the mishkan were made.)]

pairs.hebrew: וְהָיָה֩ לִבְנֵ֨י יִשְׂרָאֵ֤ל לְזִכָּרוֹן֙ לִפְנֵ֣י יְהֹוָ֔ה לְכַפֵּ֖ר עַל־נַפְשֹׁתֵיכֶֽם׃ {פ}
pairs.english: And it shall be for the children of Israel a remembrance before the L-rd to atone for your souls.
And the L-rd spoke
to Moses, saying:

pairs.hebrew: וְעָשִׂ֜יתָ כִּיּ֥וֹר נְחֹ֛שֶׁת וְכַנּ֥וֹ נְחֹ֖שֶׁת לְרׇחְצָ֑ה
pairs.english: And you shall make a kiyyor [an urn with spigots] of copper, and its pedestal of copper, for washing.

pairs.hebrew: וְנָתַתָּ֣ אֹת֗וֹ בֵּֽין־אֹ֤הֶל מוֹעֵד֙ וּבֵ֣ין הַמִּזְבֵּ֔חַ
pairs.english: And you shall place it between the tent of meeting and the altar [(not directly between them but drawn off towards the south)],
and you shall put water there.
And Aaron and his sons
shall wash their hands and their feet from it [(at one and the same time, placing the right hand on the right foot and the left hand on the left foot.)]

pairs.hebrew: בְּבֹאָ֞ם אֶל־אֹ֧הֶל מוֹעֵ֛ד יִרְחֲצוּ־מַ֖יִם וְלֹ֣א יָמֻ֑תוּ
pairs.english: When they come to the tent of meeting [to smoke incense morning and evening, or to sprinkle of the blood of the bullock of the high-priest and the "idolatry goats"], they shall wash with water and they will not die, [(the implication being that if they do not wash they will die],

pairs.hebrew: א֣וֹ בְגִשְׁתָּ֤ם אֶל־הַמִּזְבֵּ֙חַ֙ לְשָׁרֵ֔ת לְהַקְטִ֥יר אִשֶּׁ֖ה לַֽיהֹוָֽה׃
pairs.english: or when they draw near to the [outer] altar to serve, to smoke a fire-offering to the L-rd.
And they shall wash their hands and feet and not die, [the implication being that if they do not wash (this, in reference to service on the outer altar) they will die].

pairs.hebrew: וְהָיְתָ֨ה לָהֶ֧ם חׇק־עוֹלָ֛ם ל֥וֹ וּלְזַרְע֖וֹ לְדֹרֹתָֽם׃ {פ}
pairs.english: And it shall be for them an eternal statute, for him and his seed for their generations.
And the L-rd spoke
to Moses, saying:
And you, take for yourself choice spices:
pure myrrh, five hundred (shekel-weights)];
aromatic cinnamon — half of it, two hundred and fifty [(It was weighed twice to amount to five hundred and a little more (a small amount being added each time to tip the scale above 250)];
and aromatic cane, two hundred and fifty [(its total weight)].
And kiddah, five hundred in the shekel-weight of the sanctuary,
and a hin of olive oil.
And you shall make of it oil of sacred anointment,
a mixed blend, the work of the spice-blender.
Oil of sacred anointment shall it be.
And you shall anoint with it [(in the shape of the Greek letter chi)] the tent of meeting
and the ark of testimony.
And the table and all of its implements,
the menorah and all of its implements,
and the incense altar.
And the burnt-offering altar and all of its implements,
and the kiyyor and its pedestal.
And [by this anointment] you shall consecrate them and they shall be holy of holies [in that]
everything [fit for (use in) a ministering vessel] that touches them [i.e., that enters into them] shall become consecrated.
And Aaron and his sons shall you anoint,
and you shall consecrate them to minister unto Me.
And to the children of Israel shall you speak, saying:

pairs.hebrew: שֶׁ֠מֶן מִשְׁחַת־קֹ֨דֶשׁ יִהְיֶ֥ה זֶ֛ה לִ֖י לְדֹרֹתֵיכֶֽם׃
pairs.english: Oil of sacred anointment shall this (zeh) be to Me [(The gematria of zeh is twelve; there were twelve lugin of anointing oil)], for your generations [All of it remains for future generations.]
On the flesh of man it shall not be smeared,
and you shall not compound another like it.
It is holy. Holy shall it be to you.

pairs.hebrew: אִ֚ישׁ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יִרְקַ֣ח כָּמֹ֔הוּ וַאֲשֶׁ֥ר יִתֵּ֛ן מִמֶּ֖נּוּ עַל־זָ֑ר
pairs.english: One who compounds its like or who puts of it [(of that made by Moses)] upon a stranger [(one not requiring anointment for priesthood or royalty)]
shall be cut off from his people.
And the L-rd said to Moses:

pairs.hebrew: קַח־לְךָ֣ סַמִּ֗ים נָטָ֤ף ׀ וּשְׁחֵ֙לֶת֙ וְחֶלְבְּנָ֔ה סַמִּ֖ים וּלְבֹנָ֣ה זַכָּ֑ה
pairs.english: Take for yourself [two] spices [and] stacte, onycha, galbanum [(a foul-smelling spice, included in the incense to teach us not to belittle inclusion of sinners in our fasts and prayers)], [and an additional five] spices, and pure frankincense.
They [the stacte, onycha, galbanum, and frankincense] shall be equal [in weight] to one another.
And you shall make it into incense,
a compound, the work of a spice-blender,
thoroughly mixed, [and it shall be] pure [and] holy.
And you shall grind some of it fine,

pairs.hebrew: וְנָתַתָּ֨ה מִמֶּ֜נָּה לִפְנֵ֤י הָעֵדֻת֙ בְּאֹ֣הֶל מוֹעֵ֔ד אֲשֶׁ֛ר אִוָּעֵ֥ד לְךָ֖ שָׁ֑מָּה
pairs.english: and you shall place some of it [daily, on the inner altar] before the [ark of] testimony in the tent of meeting where I shall be appointed for you [to speak to you] there.
Holy of holies shall it be to you.

pairs.hebrew: וְהַקְּטֹ֙רֶת֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר תַּעֲשֶׂ֔ה בְּמַ֨תְכֻּנְתָּ֔הּ לֹ֥א תַעֲשׂ֖וּ לָכֶ֑ם
pairs.english: And the incense that you make, in its composition [(the number of its spices)] you shall not make for yourselves.
Holy shall it be to you for the L-rd. [You shall make it only for His name alone.]
One who makes its like to smell it
shall be cut off from his people. [But one may make it of what he owns, in its composition, for Temple use.]
And the L-rd spoke
to Moses, saying:
See, I have called by name [to do My work]
Betzalel the son of Uri the son of Chur of the tribe of Judah.
And I have filled him with the spirit of G-d,
with wisdom [to learn from others], with understanding [to learn from what he has learned], with knowledge [the holy spirit], and with (skill in) all work.
To do [the] artistic work [of a weaver],
to work in gold, silver, and copper.
And in stone work, to fill [the stone into its setting],
and in wood work, to do all (kinds of) work.

pairs.hebrew: וַאֲנִ֞י הִנֵּ֧ה נָתַ֣תִּי אִתּ֗וֹ אֵ֣ת אׇהֳלִיאָ֞ב בֶּן־אֲחִֽיסָמָךְ֙ לְמַטֵּה־דָ֔ן
pairs.english: And I, behold, I have placed with him Ahaliav the son of Achisamach of the tribe of Dan.
And in the heart of all the wise of heart [who are among you] I have placed wisdom,
and they shall make all that I have commanded you:
The tent of meeting and the ark for the [tablets of the] testimony,
and the lid that is on it
and all the implements of the tent.
And the table and its implements,
and the menorah [made of] pure [gold], and all its implements,
and the incense altar.
And the burnt-offering altar and all its implements,
and the kiyyor, and its pedestal.
And the mesh vestments [see Numbers 4]
and the consecrated garments of Aaron the Cohein,
and the garments of his sons for ministering.

pairs.hebrew: וְאֵ֨ת שֶׁ֧מֶן הַמִּשְׁחָ֛ה וְאֶת־קְטֹ֥רֶת הַסַּמִּ֖ים לַקֹּ֑דֶשׁ
pairs.english: And the anointing oil, and the spice incense for [smoking in the sanctuary, which is] holy.
As all that I have commanded you shall they make.
And the L-rd said
to Moses, saying:

pairs.hebrew: וְאַתָּ֞ה דַּבֵּ֨ר אֶל־בְּנֵ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר אַ֥ךְ אֶת־שַׁבְּתֹתַ֖י תִּשְׁמֹ֑רוּ
pairs.english: And you, speak to the children of Israel, saying […Even though I commanded you to charge them concerning the work of the mishkan, do not make light of the Sabbath to override it by that work], but [though you be eager and zealous in that work], My Sabbaths shall you keep.

pairs.hebrew: כִּי֩ א֨וֹת הִ֜וא בֵּינִ֤י וּבֵֽינֵיכֶם֙ לְדֹרֹ֣תֵיכֶ֔ם
pairs.english: For it is a [great] sign between Me and you for your generations [that I chose you, by bequeathing to you My day of rest for your rest],
[for the nations] to know that I, the L-rd, sanctify you.

pairs.hebrew: וּשְׁמַרְתֶּם֙ אֶת־הַשַּׁבָּ֔ת כִּ֛י קֹ֥דֶשׁ הִ֖וא לָכֶ֑ם
pairs.english: And you shall keep the Sabbath, for it is holy to you.
Those who profane it, [treating it like a weekday] shall be put to death [(if there were witnesses and warning)].

pairs.hebrew: כִּ֗י כׇּל־הָעֹשֶׂ֥ה בָהּ֙ מְלָאכָ֔ה וְנִכְרְתָ֛ה הַנֶּ֥פֶשׁ הַהִ֖וא מִקֶּ֥רֶב עַמֶּֽיהָ׃
pairs.english: For whoever does work upon it, that soul [(in the absence of warning)] shall be cut off from the midst of its people.
Six days may work be done,

pairs.hebrew: וּבַיּ֣וֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִ֗י שַׁבַּ֧ת שַׁבָּת֛וֹן קֹ֖דֶשׁ לַיהֹוָ֑ה
pairs.english: and on the seventh day (there shall be) a Sabbath of resting [(not merely casual resting, but complete resting, where all work, even for preparation of food, is forbidden)], holy unto the L-rd, [the keeping of its sanctity being for His name and by His charge.]

pairs.hebrew: כׇּל־הָעֹשֶׂ֧ה מְלָאכָ֛ה בְּי֥וֹם הַשַּׁבָּ֖ת מ֥וֹת יוּמָֽת׃
pairs.english: Whoever does work on the Sabbath day shall be put to death.
And the children of Israel shall keep the Sabbath
to observe the Sabbath for their generations, an eternal covenant.

pairs.hebrew: בֵּינִ֗י וּבֵין֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל א֥וֹת הִ֖וא לְעֹלָ֑ם
pairs.english: Between Me and the children of Israel it is a sign forever.

pairs.hebrew: כִּי־שֵׁ֣שֶׁת יָמִ֗ים עָשָׂ֤ה יְהֹוָה֙ אֶת־הַשָּׁמַ֣יִם וְאֶת־הָאָ֔רֶץ
pairs.english: For six days the L-rd made the heavens and the earth,
and on the seventh day He rested and [His spirit] was restored [(G-d using human terms that can be "assimilated by the ear" (of flesh and blood)].

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּתֵּ֣ן אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֗ה כְּכַלֹּתוֹ֙ לְדַבֵּ֤ר אִתּוֹ֙ בְּהַ֣ר סִינַ֔י
pairs.english: And He gave to Moses when He finished speaking with him [(the statutes and the judgments in Mishpatim)] on Mount Sinai,
the two tablets of the testimony,

stone tablets written by the finger of G-d. ["There is no 'earlier' and 'later' in the Torah" (This section is out of chronological order.) The incident of the golden calf preceded the charge to build the mishkan. For on the seventeenth of Tammuz the tablets were broken, and on Yom Kippur the L-rd was reconciled with Israel. And the next day they began donating for the mishkan, which was erected on the first of Nissan.] ("when He finished (kechalotho) speaking with him") ["kechalotho" is written defective (without the vav).
