pairs.english: And [when] the Canaanite heard [(The Amalekites changed their language to that of Canaan, so that the Israelites pray for victory over the Canaanites" (which they were not)], the king of Arad, the dweller in the south [i.e., Amalek (see 13:29)] — [when he heard that Aaron had died and the clouds of glory had departed and] that Israel was coming by way of Atharim [the southern route, by which the spies had come (see 13:22)],
he fought with Israel, and he captured from them a captive [a single maidservant].

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּדַּ֨ר יִשְׂרָאֵ֥ל נֶ֛דֶר לַֽיהֹוָ֖ה וַיֹּאמַ֑ר אִם־נָתֹ֨ן תִּתֵּ֜ן אֶת־הָעָ֤ם הַזֶּה֙ בְּיָדִ֔י
pairs.english: And Israel vowed a vow unto the L-rd and said: If You give this people into my hand [(When Israel saw them dressed as Amalekites and speaking the Canaanite tongue, they said "this people" — whoever they are],
then I shall consecrate [the spoils of] their cities [to the L-rd].

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּשְׁמַ֨ע יְהֹוָ֜ה בְּק֣וֹל יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל וַיִּתֵּן֙ אֶת־הַֽכְּנַעֲנִ֔י וַיַּחֲרֵ֥ם אֶתְהֶ֖ם וְאֶת־עָרֵיהֶ֑ם
pairs.english: And the L-rd hearkened to the voice of Israel, and He delivered up the Canaanites, and he (Israel) exterminated them and [he plundered] their cities [(as per 2 above)],
and he called the name of the place Charmah ["devastation"].

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּסְע֞וּ מֵהֹ֤ר הָהָר֙ דֶּ֣רֶךְ יַם־ס֔וּף לִסְבֹ֖ב אֶת־אֶ֣רֶץ אֱד֑וֹם
pairs.english: And they journeyed from Hor Hahar by way of the Red Sea [(the same way they had turned back by G-d's decree (see Deuteronomy 1:40) in the episode of the spies)] to go around the land of Edom, [(having been refused permission to pass through it)],

and the soul of the people became constricted [(i.e., unable to "contain" their distress)] by the [duress of the] way [(being "so near and yet so far," and likening their situation to that of their fathers, who turned back thus and languished in the desert for thirty-eight years)].

pairs.hebrew: וַיְדַבֵּ֣ר הָעָ֗ם בֵּֽאלֹהִים֮ וּבְמֹשֶׁה֒ לָמָ֤ה הֶֽעֱלִיתֻ֙נוּ֙ מִמִּצְרַ֔יִם לָמ֖וּת בַּמִּדְבָּ֑ר
pairs.english: And the people spoke against G-d and against Moses ["they likened the servant to his Master"]: Why did you ["both of you"] bring us up from Egypt to die in the desert?

pairs.hebrew: כִּ֣י אֵ֥ין לֶ֙חֶם֙ וְאֵ֣ין מַ֔יִם וְנַפְשֵׁ֣נוּ קָ֔צָה בַּלֶּ֖חֶם הַקְּלֹקֵֽל׃
pairs.english: For there is no bread and there is no water, and our souls are constricted by this flimsy bread [(which is absorbed in our limbs and which must ultimately make us "burst")].

pairs.hebrew: וַיְשַׁלַּ֨ח יְהֹוָ֜ה בָּעָ֗ם אֵ֚ת הַנְּחָשִׁ֣ים הַשְּׂרָפִ֔ים וַֽיְנַשְּׁכ֖וּ אֶת־הָעָ֑ם
pairs.english: And the L-rd sent against the people the fiery serpents [(which burn by their venom)], and they bit the people,
and a large number died of Israel.

pairs.hebrew: וַיָּבֹא֩ הָעָ֨ם אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֜ה וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ חָטָ֗אנוּ כִּֽי־דִבַּ֤רְנוּ בַֽיהֹוָה֙ וָבָ֔ךְ
pairs.english: And the people came to Moses and they said: We have sinned, for we spoke against the L-rd and against you.
Pray to the L-rd that He remove the serpent from us;
and Moses prayed on behalf of the people.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהֹוָ֜ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֗ה עֲשֵׂ֤ה לְךָ֙ שָׂרָ֔ף וְשִׂ֥ים אֹת֖וֹ עַל־נֵ֑ס
pairs.english: And the L-rd said to Moses: Make for yourself a fiery serpent (nachash) and place it on a pole.
And it shall be, whoever is bitten [(Even if he were bitten by a dog or an ass, he would waste away)], if he sees it [(even without gazing at it intently)], he shall live.

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּ֤עַשׂ מֹשֶׁה֙ נְחַ֣שׁ נְחֹ֔שֶׁת וַיְשִׂמֵ֖הוּ עַל־הַנֵּ֑ס
pairs.english: And Moses made a serpent of copper (nechosheth) [(Since the L-rd called it "nachash," he made it of nechosheth)], and he placed it on a pole.

pairs.hebrew: וְהָיָ֗ה אִם־נָשַׁ֤ךְ הַנָּחָשׁ֙ אֶת־אִ֔ישׁ וְהִבִּ֛יט אֶל־נְחַ֥שׁ הַנְּחֹ֖שֶׁת וָחָֽי׃
pairs.english: And it was, if the snake had bitten a man, when he gazed [intently] at the copper snake, he lived.
And the children of Israel journeyed,
and they encamped in Ovoth.
And they journeyed from Ovoth,

pairs.hebrew: וַֽיַּחֲנ֞וּ בְּעִיֵּ֣י הָֽעֲבָרִ֗ים בַּמִּדְבָּר֙ אֲשֶׁר֙ עַל־פְּנֵ֣י מוֹאָ֔ב מִמִּזְרַ֖ח הַשָּֽׁמֶשׁ׃
pairs.english: and they encamped in Iyei Ha'avarim [so called because of those who pass (ovrim) Har Nevo there on the way to the land of Canaan, (Har Nevo separating the land of Moav from the land of the Emori)], in the desert, before Moav toward the rising of the sun [i.e., to the east of Moav].
From there they journeyed,
and they encamped in Nachal Zared.

pairs.hebrew: מִשָּׁם֮ נָסָ֒עוּ֒ וַֽיַּחֲנ֗וּ מֵעֵ֤בֶר אַרְנוֹן֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בַּמִּדְבָּ֔ר הַיֹּצֵ֖א מִגְּבֻ֣ל הָֽאֱמֹרִ֑י
pairs.english: From there they journeyed, [around the entire southern and eastern border of Moav, (Moav not permitting them to pass through their land)] and they encamped on the [other, northern,] side [of Moav in] Arnon, [Emori territory] which is in the desert, which juts out from the boundary of the Emori.

pairs.hebrew: כִּ֤י אַרְנוֹן֙ גְּב֣וּל מוֹאָ֔ב בֵּ֥ין מוֹאָ֖ב וּבֵ֥ין הָאֱמֹרִֽי׃
pairs.english: For Arnon is the boundary of Moav, between Moav and the Emori.
Of this [encampment and the miracles wrought therein] it will be stated in recounting the wars of the L-rd [i.e., the miracles wrought by the L-rd for our forefathers],
what He gave them [i.e., the miracles He performed for them] at the Red Sea and at the valleys of Arnon. [Just as the former miracles are recounted, so should the latter be.]

[And what are these miracles?] The spilling [of the blood of the Emorites] in the valleys. [The Emorites secreted themselves in mountain crypts on the Moavite side to waylay the Israelites as they passed through, and the mountain on the Emorite side moved forward and crushed them with its projections] —

pairs.hebrew: אֲשֶׁ֥ר נָטָ֖ה לְשֶׁ֣בֶת עָ֑ר וְנִשְׁעַ֖ן לִגְב֥וּל מוֹאָֽב׃
pairs.english: which [mountain] moved [from its place] to fix itself [i.e., its projections] in Ar [of Moav]; it leaned on the boundary of Moav.

And from there [it (the blood flow) came] to the well. [The well (that followed the Israelites) descended into the valley and brought up from there the blood and the limbs of the slain to apprise Israel of the miracle that had been wrought for them] —

pairs.hebrew: הִ֣וא הַבְּאֵ֗ר אֲשֶׁ֨ר אָמַ֤ר יְהֹוָה֙ לְמֹשֶׁ֔ה אֱסֹף֙ אֶת־הָעָ֔ם וְאֶתְּנָ֥ה לָהֶ֖ם מָֽיִם׃ {ס}
pairs.english: the well of which the L-rd said to Moses: Gather the people and I will give them water.
Then Israel sang this song:
"Bring up, O well, [what you are bringing up from the valley]; sing to it.

pairs.hebrew: בְּאֵ֞ר חֲפָר֣וּהָ שָׂרִ֗ים כָּר֙וּהָ֙ נְדִיבֵ֣י הָעָ֔ם בִּמְחֹקֵ֖ק בְּמִשְׁעֲנֹתָ֑ם
pairs.english: The well which princes [Moses and Aaron] dug, which the nobles of the people hollowed by (word of) the lawgiver, [Moses] with their staff;
and from the desert [it was given to them as] a gift.
And after it had been given to them, [it descended with them] to the valley,
and from the valley [it ascended with them] to the heights.

pairs.hebrew: וּמִבָּמ֗וֹת הַגַּיְא֙ אֲשֶׁר֙ בִּשְׂדֵ֣ה מוֹאָ֔ב רֹ֖אשׁ הַפִּסְגָּ֑ה
pairs.english: And from the heights [it descended] to the valley in the field of Moav, the top of the height [(where Moses died and the well ceased flowing)],
which [height] looks out on the face of Yeshimon" [lit., "the waste" (i.e., the desert)].
And Israel [i.e., Moses — the leader of the generation being "Israel" (see Deuteronomy 2:26 and Numbers 20:14)] sent messengers to Sichon, king of the Emori,
saying:

pairs.hebrew: אֶעְבְּרָ֣ה בְאַרְצֶ֗ךָ לֹ֤א נִטֶּה֙ בְּשָׂדֶ֣ה וּבְכֶ֔רֶם לֹ֥א נִשְׁתֶּ֖ה מֵ֣י בְאֵ֑ר
pairs.english: Let me pass through your land [(They opened with an offer of peace though not having been commanded to do so)]; we shall not turn into field or into vineyard. We shall not drink water from the wells.

pairs.hebrew: בְּדֶ֤רֶךְ הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ נֵלֵ֔ךְ עַ֥ד אֲשֶֽׁר־נַעֲבֹ֖ר גְּבֻלֶֽךָ׃
pairs.english: On the king's way shall we go until we pass your boundary.
And Sichon did not allow Israel to pass through his boundary,

pairs.hebrew: וַיֶּאֱסֹ֨ף סִיחֹ֜ן אֶת־כׇּל־עַמּ֗וֹ וַיֵּצֵ֞א לִקְרַ֤את יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ הַמִּדְבָּ֔רָה
pairs.english: and Sichon gathered together all his people, and he went out against Israel to the desert,
and he came to Yahatz and he fought against Israel.

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּכֵּ֥הוּ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לְפִי־חָ֑רֶב וַיִּירַ֨שׁ אֶת־אַרְצ֜וֹ מֵֽאַרְנֹ֗ן עַד־יַבֹּק֙ עַד־בְּנֵ֣י עַמּ֔וֹן
pairs.english: And Israel smote him with the sword and inherited his land from Arnon until Yabbok until the children of Ammon;
for the boundary of the children of Ammon was strong, [fortified in the L-rd's monition to Israel (Deuteronomy 2:19): "Do not besiege them (Ammon)"].
And Israel took all these cities,

pairs.hebrew: וַיֵּ֤שֶׁב יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ בְּכׇל־עָרֵ֣י הָֽאֱמֹרִ֔י בְּחֶשְׁבּ֖וֹן וּבְכׇל־בְּנֹתֶֽיהָ׃
pairs.english: and Israel dwelt in all the cities of the Emori in Cheshbon and in all of its neighboring villages.

pairs.hebrew: כִּ֣י חֶשְׁבּ֔וֹן עִ֗יר סִיחֹ֛ן מֶ֥לֶךְ הָאֱמֹרִ֖י הִ֑וא
pairs.english: For Cheshbon was the city of Sichon the king of the Emori,

pairs.hebrew: וְה֣וּא נִלְחַ֗ם בְּמֶ֤לֶךְ מוֹאָב֙ הָֽרִאשׁ֔וֹן וַיִּקַּ֧ח אֶת־כׇּל־אַרְצ֛וֹ מִיָּד֖וֹ עַד־אַרְנֹֽן׃
pairs.english: and he had fought against the first king of Moav and had taken all of his land from his possession until Arnon, [so that Israel was not in violation of (Deuteronomy 2:9): "Do not besiege Moav" in taking Cheshbon from Sichon.]
About this [war that Sichon waged with Moav] those who speak in parables [Bilam (see 23:7) and Beor] said [when Sichon hired Bilam to curse Moav]: Come to Cheshbon;
it shall be built and established as the city of Sichon.

pairs.hebrew: כִּי־אֵשׁ֙ יָֽצְאָ֣ה מֵֽחֶשְׁבּ֔וֹן לֶהָבָ֖ה מִקִּרְיַ֣ת סִיחֹ֑ן
pairs.english: For a fire has gone forth from Cheshbon [after its capture by Sichon], a flame from the city of Sichon.

pairs.hebrew: אָֽכְלָה֙ עָ֣ר מוֹאָ֔ב בַּעֲלֵ֖י בָּמ֥וֹת אַרְנֹֽן׃
pairs.english: It has consumed Ar [a province of] Moav, the possessors of the heights of Arnon.
Woe unto you, Moav! [(Bilam and Beor here cursing Moav to fall by the hand of Sichon)] You are lost, people of Kemosh [(the divinity of Moav)].

pairs.hebrew: נָתַ֨ן בָּנָ֤יו פְּלֵיטִם֙ וּבְנֹתָ֣יו בַּשְּׁבִ֔ית לְמֶ֥לֶךְ אֱמֹרִ֖י סִיחֽוֹן׃
pairs.english: He has yielded his sons as fugitives and his daughters as captives to the king of the Emori, Sichon.
And their [Moav's] sovereignty over Cheshbon is lost; lost is [their sovereignty over] Divon,
and [those who speak in parables will say]: We have laid it waste until Nofach, which reaches until Medva.
And Israel dwelt
in the land of the Emori.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּשְׁלַ֤ח מֹשֶׁה֙ לְרַגֵּ֣ל אֶת־יַעְזֵ֔ר וַֽיִּלְכְּד֖וּ בְּנֹתֶ֑יהָ
pairs.english: And Moses sent to spy out Yazer and they [the spies] took its neighboring villages [(these spies, unlike the first, relying on Moses' prayers to give them victory)],
and they drove out the Emori who were there.
And they turned and went up by way of the Bashan,

pairs.hebrew: וַיֵּצֵ֣א עוֹג֩ מֶֽלֶךְ־הַבָּשָׁ֨ן לִקְרָאתָ֜ם ה֧וּא וְכׇל־עַמּ֛וֹ לַמִּלְחָמָ֖ה אֶדְרֶֽעִי׃
pairs.english: and Og, king of the Bashan, went out against them, he and all of his people, to do battle at Edrei.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהֹוָ֤ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁה֙ אַל־תִּירָ֣א אֹת֔וֹ כִּ֣י בְיָדְךָ֞ נָתַ֧תִּי אֹת֛וֹ וְאֶת־כׇּל־עַמּ֖וֹ וְאֶת־אַרְצ֑וֹ
pairs.english: And the L-rd said to Moses: Do not fear him [Do not fear that the merit of Abraham (see Genesis 14:13) will protect him)], for I have given him into your hand, and all of his people, and his land.

pairs.hebrew: וְעָשִׂ֣יתָ לּ֔וֹ כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשִׂ֗יתָ לְסִיחֹן֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ הָֽאֱמֹרִ֔י אֲשֶׁ֥ר יוֹשֵׁ֖ב בְּחֶשְׁבּֽוֹן׃
pairs.english: And you shall do to him as you did to Sichon king of the Emori who dwells at Cheshbon.

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּכּ֨וּ אֹת֤וֹ וְאֶת־בָּנָיו֙ וְאֶת־כׇּל־עַמּ֔וֹ עַד־בִּלְתִּ֥י הִשְׁאִֽיר־ל֖וֹ שָׂרִ֑יד
pairs.english: And they smote him [(Moses himself smiting Og)] and his sons and all his people, until no remnant was left of him,
and they inherited his land.
And the children of Israel journeyed,
and they encamped in the plains of Moav across the Jordan from Jericho.
And Balak the son of Tzippor saw
all that Israel had done to the Emori [He said: If these two kings (Sichon and Og) on whom we relied, could not withstand them, how much more so we alone! — wherefore:]

pairs.hebrew: וַיָּ֨גׇר מוֹאָ֜ב מִפְּנֵ֥י הָעָ֛ם מְאֹ֖ד כִּ֣י רַב־ה֑וּא
pairs.english: And Moav greatly feared the people, for they were many,
and Moav despaired [of their lives] before the children of Israel.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר מוֹאָ֜ב אֶל־זִקְנֵ֣י מִדְיָ֗ן עַתָּ֞ה יְלַחֲכ֤וּ הַקָּהָל֙ אֶת־כׇּל־סְבִ֣יבֹתֵ֔ינוּ כִּלְחֹ֣ךְ הַשּׁ֔וֹר אֵ֖ת יֶ֣רֶק הַשָּׂדֶ֑ה
pairs.english: And Moav said to the elders of Midian: Now this horde will lap up everything around us as an ox laps up the greens of the field —

pairs.hebrew: וּבָלָ֧ק בֶּן־צִפּ֛וֹר מֶ֥לֶךְ לְמוֹאָ֖ב בָּעֵ֥ת הַהִֽוא׃
pairs.english: and Balak the son of Tzippor [one of the princes of Midian] was [made] king of Moav at that time [because of the exigency of the time, though he was not of the royal line].

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּשְׁלַ֨ח מַלְאָכִ֜ים אֶל־בִּלְעָ֣ם בֶּן־בְּעֹ֗ר פְּ֠ת֠וֹרָה אֲשֶׁ֧ר עַל־הַנָּהָ֛ר אֶ֥רֶץ בְּנֵי־עַמּ֖וֹ לִקְרֹא־ל֑וֹ לֵאמֹ֗ר
pairs.english: And he sent messengers to Bilam the son of Beor to Pethor, which is by the river of the land of the children of his people to call for him [i.e., for his (Bilam's) benefit, Balak promising to enrich him], saying:

pairs.hebrew: הִ֠נֵּ֠ה עַ֣ם יָצָ֤א מִמִּצְרַ֙יִם֙ הִנֵּ֤ה כִסָּה֙ אֶת־עֵ֣ין הָאָ֔רֶץ
pairs.english: Behold, a people has gone forth from Egypt; behold, it has covered "the eye of the land" [Sichon and Moav, who were our protectors — Israel rose against them and killed them],
and it abides opposite me, [against me, to cut me off].

pairs.hebrew: וְעַתָּה֩ לְכָה־נָּ֨א אָֽרָה־לִּ֜י אֶת־הָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֗ה כִּֽי־עָצ֥וּם הוּא֙ מִמֶּ֔נִּי
pairs.english: And now, come, I pray you, and curse this people for me, for it is too strong for me.
Perhaps I shall be able to smite it and drive it from the land.

pairs.hebrew: כִּ֣י יָדַ֗עְתִּי אֵ֤ת אֲשֶׁר־תְּבָרֵךְ֙ מְבֹרָ֔ךְ וַאֲשֶׁ֥ר תָּאֹ֖ר יוּאָֽר׃
pairs.english: For I know [by your having helped Sichon to defeat Moav (see 21:27)] that what you bless is blessed and what you curse is cursed.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֵּ֨לְכ֜וּ זִקְנֵ֤י מוֹאָב֙ וְזִקְנֵ֣י מִדְיָ֔ן וּקְסָמִ֖ים בְּיָדָ֑ם
pairs.english: And the elders of Moav went, and the elders of Midian, with [all kinds of] charms in their hand [(so that Bilam not plead lack of "tools")],

pairs.hebrew: וַיָּבֹ֙אוּ֙ אֶל־בִּלְעָ֔ם וַיְדַבְּר֥וּ אֵלָ֖יו דִּבְרֵ֥י בָלָֽק׃
pairs.english: and they came to Bilam and they related to him the words of Balak.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲלֵיהֶ֗ם לִ֤ינוּ פֹה֙ הַלַּ֔יְלָה וַהֲשִׁבֹתִ֤י אֶתְכֶם֙ דָּבָ֔ר כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר יְדַבֵּ֥ר יְהֹוָ֖ה אֵלָ֑י
pairs.english: And he said to them: Lodge here this night [(The Holy Spirit reposes on the prophets of the nations only at night (as one "steals into" his concubine)], and I will return to you a word, as the L-rd speaks to me [(Perhaps He will consider it beneath His dignity to permit me to go with emissaries of your (lowly) rank)],
and the officers of Moav abode with Bilam.
And G-d came to Bilam
and He said: Who are these people with you? [(G-d's purpose was to delude Bilam into thinking that there were some "gaps" in His knowledge and that he might seize upon one of them to curse Israel.)]
And Bilam said to G-d:

pairs.hebrew: בָּלָ֧ק בֶּן־צִפֹּ֛ר מֶ֥לֶךְ מוֹאָ֖ב שָׁלַ֥ח אֵלָֽי׃
pairs.english: Balak the son of Tzippor, the king of Moav, sent to me [(I may not "rate" with You, but I do rate with kings)]:

pairs.hebrew: הִנֵּ֤ה הָעָם֙ הַיֹּצֵ֣א מִמִּצְרַ֔יִם וַיְכַ֖ס אֶת־עֵ֣ין הָאָ֑רֶץ
pairs.english: Behold, the people that has gone forth from Egypt and covers the eye of the land.

pairs.hebrew: עַתָּ֗ה לְכָ֤ה קָֽבָה־לִּי֙ אֹת֔וֹ אוּלַ֥י אוּכַ֛ל לְהִלָּ֥חֶם בּ֖וֹ וְגֵרַשְׁתִּֽיו׃
pairs.english: Now, go and curse (kavah) it for me [("kavah" is more "pointed" and explicit than Balak's "arah" (6)]. Perhaps I will be able to war against it and drive it out ["of the world," whereas Balak had said (6): "and drive it from the land," Balak desiring only to free himself of them.]

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֱלֹהִים֙ אֶל־בִּלְעָ֔ם לֹ֥א תֵלֵ֖ךְ עִמָּהֶ֑ם
pairs.english: And G-d said to Bilam: "Do not go with them." [Bilam: "If so, I will curse them in my place."]

pairs.hebrew: לֹ֤א תָאֹר֙ אֶת־הָעָ֔ם כִּ֥י בָר֖וּךְ הֽוּא׃
pairs.english: (G-d): "Do not curse the people" [Bilam: "If so, I will bless them." (G-d): "They do not need your blessing], for it is blessed." ["Neither your honey nor your sting!"]

pairs.hebrew: וַיָּ֤קׇם בִּלְעָם֙ בַּבֹּ֔קֶר וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ אֶל־שָׂרֵ֣י בָלָ֔ק לְכ֖וּ אֶֽל־אַרְצְכֶ֑ם
pairs.english: And Bilam arose in the morning and he said to the officers of Balak: Go to your land,

pairs.hebrew: כִּ֚י מֵאֵ֣ן יְהֹוָ֔ה לְתִתִּ֖י לַהֲלֹ֥ךְ עִמָּכֶֽם׃
pairs.english: for the L-rd refuses to allow me to go with you, [but only with men of higher station, (Bilam shrouding his impotence in his arrogance)].
And the officers of Moav arose and came to Balak
and they said: Bilam refuses to go with us.
And Balak sent officers yet again —
more, and more honorable than these.

pairs.hebrew: וַיָּבֹ֖אוּ אֶל־בִּלְעָ֑ם וַיֹּ֣אמְרוּ ל֗וֹ כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ בָּלָ֣ק בֶּן־צִפּ֔וֹר
pairs.english: And they came to Bilam and said to him: Thus said Balak the son of Tzippor:
Do not, I pray you, refrain from going to me.

pairs.hebrew: כִּֽי־כַבֵּ֤ד אֲכַבֶּדְךָ֙ מְאֹ֔ד וְכֹ֛ל אֲשֶׁר־תֹּאמַ֥ר אֵלַ֖י אֶֽעֱשֶׂ֑ה
pairs.english: For I will honor you greatly [(I will give you more than you were wont to receive in the past)], and whatever you tell me I will do;
but go, I pray you, and curse this people for me.

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּ֣עַן בִּלְעָ֗ם וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ אֶל־עַבְדֵ֣י בָלָ֔ק אִם־יִתֶּן־לִ֥י בָלָ֛ק מְלֹ֥א בֵית֖וֹ כֶּ֣סֶף וְזָהָ֑ב
pairs.english: And Bilam answered and said to the servants of Balak: If Balak gives me his house full of silver and gold [— and he really should, for if he hired armies, he would have to pay them; and their success is in doubt, whereas mine is assured (Bilam here "gives away" his lust for the wealth of others)],

pairs.hebrew: לֹ֣א אוּכַ֗ל לַעֲבֹר֙ אֶת־פִּי֙ יְהֹוָ֣ה אֱלֹהָ֔י לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת קְטַנָּ֖ה א֥וֹ גְדוֹלָֽה׃
pairs.english: I will not be able to countermand the word of the L-rd my G-d to do (anything) small or great [(Bilam here perforce reveals that he is not his own master and prophesies that he will not be able to annul the L-rd's blessings to the patriarchs)].

pairs.hebrew: וְעַתָּ֗ה שְׁב֨וּ נָ֥א בָזֶ֛ה גַּם־אַתֶּ֖ם הַלָּ֑יְלָה
pairs.english: And now, abide here, I pray you — you, too [(His mouth "foiled" him — "you, too," like the first, are destined to leave in frustration)],
and I shall know what more the L-rd will say to me. [He will not change His blessings to curses — would that He would not bless them more! (Bilam here prophesies that He will!)]

pairs.hebrew: וַיָּבֹ֨א אֱלֹהִ֥ים ׀ אֶל־בִּלְעָם֮ לַ֒יְלָה֒ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ל֗וֹ אִם־לִקְרֹ֤א לְךָ֙ בָּ֣אוּ הָאֲנָשִׁ֔ים ק֖וּם לֵ֣ךְ אִתָּ֑ם
pairs.english: And G-d came to Bilam at night and He said to Him: If the men came to call for you [i.e., if their calling is for your benefit; if you think you can turn it toward your profit], arise and go with them,

pairs.hebrew: וְאַ֗ךְ אֶת־הַדָּבָ֛ר אֲשֶׁר־אֲדַבֵּ֥ר אֵלֶ֖יךָ אֹת֥וֹ תַעֲשֶֽׂה׃
pairs.english: but [perforce] what I speak to you that shall you do [ — in spite of which Bilam went, hoping to "win over" the L-rd].
And Bilam arose in the morning and he [himself] saddled his donkey ["Hatred undermines the proprieties"],
and he went [of one accord] with the officers of Moav.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּֽחַר־אַ֣ף אֱלֹהִים֮ כִּֽי־הוֹלֵ֣ךְ הוּא֒ וַיִּתְיַצֵּ֞ב מַלְאַ֧ךְ יְהֹוָ֛ה בַּדֶּ֖רֶךְ לְשָׂטָ֣ן ל֑וֹ
pairs.english: And the L-rd was wroth that He went [(for though Bilam saw that G-d objected (12), he persisted in going)], and an angel of the L-rd [an angel of mercy] stood in the way to turn him aside [to prevent him from sinning and going lost];

pairs.hebrew: וְהוּא֙ רֹכֵ֣ב עַל־אֲתֹנ֔וֹ וּשְׁנֵ֥י נְעָרָ֖יו עִמּֽוֹ׃
pairs.english: and he was riding on his donkey and his two youths with him [(whence it is derived that a man of eminence going on a journey should take two men to attend him (who relieve each other in turn)].

pairs.hebrew: וַתֵּ֣רֶא הָאָתוֹן֩ אֶת־מַלְאַ֨ךְ יְהֹוָ֜ה נִצָּ֣ב בַּדֶּ֗רֶךְ וְחַרְבּ֤וֹ שְׁלוּפָה֙ בְּיָד֔וֹ
pairs.english: And the donkey saw the angel of the L-rd [(but Bilam did not, G-d allowing animals to see more than men, who, possessing intellect, would become "unhinged" at the sight of mazzikin (destructive agents)], standing on the way with his sword drawn in his hand,
and the donkey turned aside from the way and walked in the field,
and Bilam struck the donkey to turn it back upon the road.
And the angel of the L-rd stood in the path of the vineyards,
a [stone] fence on one side and a fence on the other.

pairs.hebrew: וַתֵּ֨רֶא הָאָת֜וֹן אֶת־מַלְאַ֣ךְ יְהֹוָ֗ה וַתִּלָּחֵץ֙ אֶל־הַקִּ֔יר
pairs.english: And the donkey saw the angel of the L-rd, and it pinned itself against the fence,

pairs.hebrew: וַתִּלְחַ֛ץ אֶת־רֶ֥גֶל בִּלְעָ֖ם אֶל־הַקִּ֑יר וַיֹּ֖סֶף לְהַכֹּתָֽהּ׃
pairs.english: and it pinned Bilam's leg against the fence, and he struck her again.
And the angel of the L-rd passed on [before him] again,

pairs.hebrew: וַֽיַּעֲמֹד֙ בְּמָק֣וֹם צָ֔ר אֲשֶׁ֛ר אֵֽין־דֶּ֥רֶךְ לִנְט֖וֹת יָמִ֥ין וּשְׂמֹֽאול׃
pairs.english: and he stood in a narrow place where there was no way to turn to the right or to the left.

pairs.hebrew: וַתֵּ֤רֶא הָֽאָתוֹן֙ אֶת־מַלְאַ֣ךְ יְהֹוָ֔ה וַתִּרְבַּ֖ץ תַּ֣חַת בִּלְעָ֑ם
pairs.english: And the donkey saw the angel of the L-rd, and it sank under Bilam,
and Bilam was wroth, and he struck the donkey with the rod.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּפְתַּ֥ח יְהֹוָ֖ה אֶת־פִּ֣י הָאָת֑וֹן וַתֹּ֤אמֶר לְבִלְעָם֙
pairs.english: And the L-rd opened the donkey's mouth and it said to Bilam:

pairs.hebrew: מֶה־עָשִׂ֣יתִֽי לְךָ֔ כִּ֣י הִכִּיתַ֔נִי זֶ֖ה שָׁלֹ֥שׁ רְגָלִֽים׃
pairs.english: What have I done to you that you have struck me this three times? [Would you uproot a nation that celebrates three times (i.e., festivals) in the year?]

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר בִּלְעָם֙ לָֽאָת֔וֹן כִּ֥י הִתְעַלַּ֖לְתְּ בִּ֑י
pairs.english: And Bilam said to the donkey: Because you mocked me!

pairs.hebrew: ל֤וּ יֶשׁ־חֶ֙רֶב֙ בְּיָדִ֔י כִּ֥י עַתָּ֖ה הֲרַגְתִּֽיךְ׃
pairs.english: Would there were a sword in my hand and I would slay you now!

pairs.hebrew: וַתֹּ֨אמֶר הָאָת֜וֹן אֶל־בִּלְעָ֗ם הֲלוֹא֩ אָנֹכִ֨י אֲתֹֽנְךָ֜ אֲשֶׁר־רָכַ֣בְתָּ עָלַ֗י מֵעֽוֹדְךָ֙ עַד־הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֔ה
pairs.english: And the donkey said to Bilam: Am I not your donkey, on which you have ridden from the very beginning until this day?
Was I ever wont to do thus unto you?
And he said: No.

pairs.hebrew: וַיְגַ֣ל יְהֹוָה֮ אֶת־עֵינֵ֣י בִלְעָם֒ וַיַּ֞רְא אֶת־מַלְאַ֤ךְ יְהֹוָה֙ נִצָּ֣ב בַּדֶּ֔רֶךְ וְחַרְבּ֥וֹ שְׁלֻפָ֖ה בְּיָד֑וֹ
pairs.english: And the L-rd uncovered Bilam's eyes, and he saw the angel of the L-rd standing in the way with his sword drawn in his hand,
and he bowed down and prostrated himself on his face.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלָיו֙ מַלְאַ֣ךְ יְהֹוָ֔ה עַל־מָ֗ה הִכִּ֙יתָ֙ אֶת־אֲתֹ֣נְךָ֔ זֶ֖ה שָׁל֣וֹשׁ רְגָלִ֑ים
pairs.english: And the angel of the L-rd said to him: Why did you strike your donkey this three times?

pairs.hebrew: הִנֵּ֤ה אָנֹכִי֙ יָצָ֣אתִי לְשָׂטָ֔ן כִּֽי־יָרַ֥ט הַדֶּ֖רֶךְ לְנֶגְדִּֽי׃
pairs.english: Behold, I went out to turn [you] aside, for [I saw that] the [goer on the] way [i.e., you] hastened [(on the way] against me [i.e., in defiance of me].

pairs.hebrew: וַתִּרְאַ֙נִי֙ הָֽאָת֔וֹן וַתֵּ֣ט לְפָנַ֔י זֶ֖ה שָׁלֹ֣שׁ רְגָלִ֑ים
pairs.english: And the donkey saw me and turned aside before me this three times.

pairs.hebrew: אוּלַי֙ נָטְתָ֣ה מִפָּנַ֔י כִּ֥י עַתָּ֛ה גַּם־אֹתְכָ֥ה הָרַ֖גְתִּי וְאוֹתָ֥הּ הֶחֱיֵֽיתִי׃
pairs.english: Had it not turned aside before me, I would now [not only have delayed you, but] also have killed you and kept it alive, [but since it silenced you with its rebuke, I have killed it so that it not be pointed to as your "undoer" (the Holy One Blessed be He being solicitous of men's honor)].

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר בִּלְעָ֜ם אֶל־מַלְאַ֤ךְ יְהֹוָה֙ חָטָ֔אתִי כִּ֚י לֹ֣א יָדַ֔עְתִּי כִּ֥י אַתָּ֛ה נִצָּ֥ב לִקְרָאתִ֖י בַּדָּ֑רֶךְ
pairs.english: And Bilam said to the angel of the L-rd: I have sinned, for I did not know that you were standing against me on the way [(Bilam's own mouth here perforce "undoes" him — "I did not know," as opposed to (24:16): "And he (Bilam) knows, etc.")]
And, now, if it is evil in your eyes, I will go back [(a "dig" at the Holy One Blessed be He, viz.: He Himself commanded me to go, and you a (mere) angel countermand His word!)]

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֩אמֶר֩ מַלְאַ֨ךְ יְהֹוָ֜ה אֶל־בִּלְעָ֗ם לֵ֚ךְ עִם־הָ֣אֲנָשִׁ֔ים וְאֶ֗פֶס אֶת־הַדָּבָ֛ר אֲשֶׁר־אֲדַבֵּ֥ר אֵלֶ֖יךָ אֹת֣וֹ תְדַבֵּ֑ר
pairs.english: And the angel of the L-rd said to Bilam: Go with the men [("A man is led on the way he would travel")], but, perforce, the thing that I shall speak to you, that shall you speak.
And Bilam went with the officers of Balak [(as happy as they to curse the Jews)].
And Balak heard [through messengers sent by Bilam] that Bilam was coming,

pairs.hebrew: וַיֵּצֵ֨א לִקְרָאת֜וֹ אֶל־עִ֣יר מוֹאָ֗ב אֲשֶׁר֙ עַל־גְּב֣וּל אַרְנֹ֔ן אֲשֶׁ֖ר בִּקְצֵ֥ה הַגְּבֽוּל׃
pairs.english: and he went out towards him to the city [i.e., the metropolis] of Moav [(by way of saying: "See what these Jews would uproot!")] which borders on Arnon at the edge of the boundary.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר בָּלָ֜ק אֶל־בִּלְעָ֗ם הֲלֹא֩ שָׁלֹ֨חַ שָׁלַ֤חְתִּי אֵלֶ֙יךָ֙ לִקְרֹא־לָ֔ךְ לָ֥מָּה לֹא־הָלַ֖כְתָּ אֵלָ֑י
pairs.english: And Balak said to Bilam: Did I not send to you to call for you? Why did you not come to me?
Am I not, indeed, able to honor you? [(a prophecy that Bilam is destined to depart from him in shame)]

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר בִּלְעָ֜ם אֶל־בָּלָ֗ק הִֽנֵּה־בָ֙אתִי֙ אֵלֶ֔יךָ עַתָּ֕ה הֲיָכֹ֥ל אוּכַ֖ל דַּבֵּ֣ר מְא֑וּמָה
pairs.english: And Bilam said to Balak: Behold, I have come to you now. Is there aught that I can speak?

pairs.hebrew: הַדָּבָ֗ר אֲשֶׁ֨ר יָשִׂ֧ים אֱלֹהִ֛ים בְּפִ֖י אֹת֥וֹ אֲדַבֵּֽר׃
pairs.english: The thing that G-d shall put in my mouth, that shall I speak.
And Bilam went with Balak,
and they came to Kiryat Chutzoth [lit., "a city of (crowded) thoroughfares" — again, by way of saying: "See what the Jews would uproot!"]
And Balak slaughtered cattle and sheep [a small amount],
and he sent it to Bilam and to the officers who were with him.

pairs.hebrew: וַיְהִ֣י בַבֹּ֔קֶר וַיִּקַּ֤ח בָּלָק֙ אֶת־בִּלְעָ֔ם וַֽיַּעֲלֵ֖הוּ בָּמ֣וֹת בָּ֑עַל
pairs.english: And it was in the morning that Balak took Bilam and he brought him up to the heights of Ba'al [his deity],
and he saw from there the edge of the people (of Israel).

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר בִּלְעָם֙ אֶל־בָּלָ֔ק בְּנֵה־לִ֥י בָזֶ֖ה שִׁבְעָ֣ה מִזְבְּחֹ֑ת
pairs.english: And Bilam said to Balak: Build me here seven altars,

pairs.hebrew: וְהָכֵ֥ן לִי֙ בָּזֶ֔ה שִׁבְעָ֥ה פָרִ֖ים וְשִׁבְעָ֥ה אֵילִֽים׃
pairs.english: and prepare me here seven bullocks and seven rams.
And Balak did as Bilam had spoken,

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּ֨עַל בָּלָ֧ק וּבִלְעָ֛ם פָּ֥ר וָאַ֖יִל בַּמִּזְבֵּֽחַ׃
pairs.english: and Balak and Bilam offered a bullock and a ram on (each) altar.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר בִּלְעָ֜ם לְבָלָ֗ק הִתְיַצֵּב֮ עַל־עֹלָתֶ֒ךָ֒ וְאֵֽלְכָ֗ה אוּלַ֞י יִקָּרֵ֤ה יְהֹוָה֙ לִקְרָאתִ֔י
pairs.english: And Bilam said to Balak: Stand by your burnt-offering and I will go; perhaps the (word of) the L-rd will chance to (come to) me [(He is not wont to speak with me in the daytime)],

pairs.hebrew: וּדְבַ֥ר מַה־יַּרְאֵ֖נִי וְהִגַּ֣דְתִּי לָ֑ךְ וַיֵּ֖לֶךְ שֶֽׁפִי׃
pairs.english: and I will tell you; and he went off alone.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּקָּ֥ר אֱלֹהִ֖ים אֶל־בִּלְעָ֑ם וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלָ֗יו אֶת־שִׁבְעַ֤ת הַֽמִּזְבְּחֹת֙ עָרַ֔כְתִּי
pairs.english: And G-d chanced upon Bilam [in the daytime, "grudgingly and contemptuously," and only in order to show His love for Israel]; and he said to Him: The seven altars [corresponding to the seven altars that the patriarchs arranged before You] have I arranged,
and I have offered up a bullock and a ram on (each) altar [whereas Abraham offered up only one ram].
And the L-rd placed a word in the mouth of Bilam
and He said: Return to Balak and thus shall you speak.
And he returned to him, and, behold, he was standing by his burnt-offering,
he and all the officers of Moav.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּשָּׂ֥א מְשָׁל֖וֹ וַיֹּאמַ֑ר מִן־אֲ֠רָ֠ם יַנְחֵ֨נִי בָלָ֤ק מֶֽלֶךְ־מוֹאָב֙ מֵֽהַרְרֵי־קֶ֔דֶם
pairs.english: And he took up his parable and he said: From Aram, Balak the king of Moav brought me, from the mountains of the east (saying to me):

pairs.hebrew: לְכָה֙ אָֽרָה־לִּ֣י יַעֲקֹ֔ב וּלְכָ֖ה זֹעֲמָ֥ה יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
pairs.english: Go and curse (arah) Jacob for me, and go and curse (zoamah) Israel [(Balak using both terms, being uncertain as to the "lethal" form)].
When I would curse, the Almighty would not curse [(Even when they deserved to be cursed, they were not cursed (see citations in Rashi)],
and when I would vent wrath, the L-rd would not. [My only power is in knowing G-d's "moment of wrath," and He did not manifest that moment all of these days)].
For from [their very] beginning, I behold them [fortified as] rocks [by the patriarchs and the matriarchs]; and [fortified] as mounts, I view them.

pairs.hebrew: הֶן־עָם֙ לְבָדָ֣ד יִשְׁכֹּ֔ן וּבַגּוֹיִ֖ם לֹ֥א יִתְחַשָּֽׁב׃
pairs.english: Lo, the people (of Israel) shall dwell alone [in the world], and among the nations they shall not be reckoned [for destruction].

pairs.hebrew: מִ֤י מָנָה֙ עֲפַ֣ר יַעֲקֹ֔ב וּמִסְפָּ֖ר אֶת־רֹ֣בַע יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל
pairs.english: Who can count the dust [i.e., the offspring (see Genesis 13:16)] of Jacob or the number of [one of] the four [banners of the encampments of] Israel?

pairs.hebrew: תָּמֹ֤ת נַפְשִׁי֙ מ֣וֹת יְשָׁרִ֔ים וּתְהִ֥י אַחֲרִיתִ֖י כָּמֹֽהוּ׃
pairs.english: Let my soul die the death of the righteous [among them] and let my last end be like theirs.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר בָּלָק֙ אֶל־בִּלְעָ֔ם מֶ֥ה עָשִׂ֖יתָ לִ֑י לָקֹ֤ב אֹיְבַי֙ לְקַחְתִּ֔יךָ
pairs.english: And Balak said to Bilam: What did you do to me? To curse my foes did I take you,
and, behold, you have blessed them!
And he answered and said:

pairs.hebrew: הֲלֹ֗א אֵת֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר יָשִׂ֤ים יְהֹוָה֙ בְּפִ֔י אֹת֥וֹ אֶשְׁמֹ֖ר לְדַבֵּֽר׃
pairs.english: Must I not take heed to speak that which the L-rd places in my mouth?

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֵלָ֜יו בָּלָ֗ק (לך) [לְכָה־]נָּ֨א אִתִּ֜י אֶל־מָק֤וֹם אַחֵר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר תִּרְאֶ֣נּוּ מִשָּׁ֔ם
pairs.english: And Balak said to him: Come, I pray you, with me to another place whence you will see them.

pairs.hebrew: אֶ֚פֶס קָצֵ֣הוּ תִרְאֶ֔ה וְכֻלּ֖וֹ לֹ֣א תִרְאֶ֑ה וְקׇבְנוֹ־לִ֖י מִשָּֽׁם׃
pairs.english: But only their outermost part will you see, and you will not see all of them; and curse them for me from there.

And he took him to the field of the scouts, to the top of the height [Balak divined that a breach would break forth in Israel there and assumed it to be the effect of the curse (whereas, in reality, the "breach" was Moses' dying there)];

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּ֙בֶן֙ שִׁבְעָ֣ה מִזְבְּחֹ֔ת וַיַּ֛עַל פָּ֥ר וָאַ֖יִל בַּמִּזְבֵּֽחַ׃
pairs.english: and he built seven altars, and he offered up a bullock and a ram on (each) altar.
And he said to Balak: Stand here by your burnt-offering,
and I will be chanced upon here [by the Holy One Blessed be He].

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּקָּ֤ר יְהֹוָה֙ אֶל־בִּלְעָ֔ם וַיָּ֥שֶׂם דָּבָ֖ר בְּפִ֑יו
pairs.english: And the L-rd chanced upon Bilam, and He placed a word in his mouth, [as one places a bit in an animal's mouth (Bilam balking at what he now saw to be a futile errand, and the L-rd "bridling" him to His will)],
and He said: Return to Balak, and thus shall you speak.

pairs.hebrew: וַיָּבֹ֣א אֵלָ֗יו וְהִנּ֤וֹ נִצָּב֙ עַל־עֹ֣לָת֔וֹ וְשָׂרֵ֥י מוֹאָ֖ב אִתּ֑וֹ
pairs.english: And he came to him, and, lo, he stood by his burnt-offering, and [some of] the officers of Moav with him, [but not all of them (as opposed to (6), some of them having lost hope in him and having left)].
And Balak said to him [mockingly]: What did the L-rd (but not "you") speak? [you being nothing but His mouthpiece]

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּשָּׂ֥א מְשָׁל֖וֹ וַיֹּאמַ֑ר ק֤וּם בָּלָק֙ וּֽשְׁמָ֔ע
pairs.english: And he took up his parable and he said: Arise, Balak [(This is Bilam's "riposte" to Balak's mockery — Stand! You have no right to sit when being addressed by G-d's emissary!)];
give ear to me, son of Tzippor!

pairs.hebrew: לֹ֣א אִ֥ישׁ אֵל֙ וִֽיכַזֵּ֔ב וּבֶן־אָדָ֖ם וְיִתְנֶחָ֑ם
pairs.english: The Almighty is not a man that He should deceive [(He has sworn to give them the land, and do you think to slay them in the desert)]; nor the son of man, that He should retract.

pairs.hebrew: הַה֤וּא אָמַר֙ וְלֹ֣א יַעֲשֶׂ֔ה וְדִבֶּ֖ר וְלֹ֥א יְקִימֶֽנָּה׃
pairs.english: Would He say and not do? [Would He] speak and not fulfill?
Behold, [a fiat] to bless [them] have I received [from Him],
and He has blessed [them], and I will not reverse it.

pairs.hebrew: לֹֽא־הִבִּ֥יט אָ֙וֶן֙ בְּיַעֲקֹ֔ב וְלֹא־רָאָ֥ה עָמָ֖ל בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל
pairs.english: He does not scrutinize [exactingly] the iniquity [that is] in Jacob, and He does not see the toil [i.e., the toilsome transgression] [that is] in Israel.

pairs.hebrew: יְהֹוָ֤ה אֱלֹהָיו֙ עִמּ֔וֹ וּתְרוּעַ֥ת מֶ֖לֶךְ בּֽוֹ׃
pairs.english: The L-rd, his G-d, is with him, [not leaving them even when they are rebellious], and the King's love is in him.
The Almighty brought them forth from Egypt [(as opposed to your: "A people has gone forth from Egypt" (22:5)];
and the flight of the heights is His.
[They are worthy of blessing] for there is no [practice of] enchantment in Jacob, and there is no divination in Israel.

pairs.hebrew: כָּעֵ֗ת יֵאָמֵ֤ר לְיַעֲקֹב֙ וּלְיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל מַה־פָּ֖עַל אֵֽל׃
pairs.english: [There is destined to come] a time like this [when His love for them will be revealed, when they are seated within the Divine partition and] it will be asked of Jacob and of Israel: "What hath the Almighty wrought?"
Behold, a people that rises like a lioness [in the morning from their sleep to "snatch" mitzvoth] and which lifts itself up as a lion.

pairs.hebrew: לֹ֤א יִשְׁכַּב֙ עַד־יֹ֣אכַל טֶ֔רֶף וְדַם־חֲלָלִ֖ים יִשְׁתֶּֽה׃
pairs.english: It does not lie down [to sleep] until [by the reading of the Shema] it consumes its prey, [all of the mazzikin (destructive agents) which come to assail them], and [when armies come against them, the L-rd protects them and fights their wars], and it drinks the blood of the slain.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר בָּלָק֙ אֶל־בִּלְעָ֔ם גַּם־קֹ֖ב לֹ֣א תִקֳּבֶ֑נּוּ
pairs.english: And Balak said to Bilam: Neither curse them
nor bless them!

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּ֣עַן בִּלְעָ֔ם וַיֹּ֖אמֶר אֶל־בָּלָ֑ק הֲלֹ֗א דִּבַּ֤רְתִּי אֵלֶ֙יךָ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר
pairs.english: And Bilam answered and said to Balak: Did I not tell you:
All that the L-rd speaks, that will I do?

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר בָּלָק֙ אֶל־בִּלְעָ֔ם לְכָה־נָּא֙ אֶקָּ֣חֲךָ֔ אֶל־מָק֖וֹם אַחֵ֑ר
pairs.english: And Balak said to Bilam: Come, I pray you, let me take you to another place.

pairs.hebrew: אוּלַ֤י יִישַׁר֙ בְּעֵינֵ֣י הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים וְקַבֹּ֥תוֹ לִ֖י מִשָּֽׁם׃
pairs.english: Perhaps it will be right in the eyes of G-d, and you will curse them for me from there.
And Balak took Bilam to the top of Peor,
which looks out upon the face of the wilderness. [Balak divined that Israel would be smitten by Peor and assumed the (prospective) curse to be the cause.]

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר בִּלְעָם֙ אֶל־בָּלָ֔ק בְּנֵה־לִ֥י בָזֶ֖ה שִׁבְעָ֣ה מִזְבְּחֹ֑ת
pairs.english: And Bilam said to Balak: Build for me here seven altars

pairs.hebrew: וְהָכֵ֥ן לִי֙ בָּזֶ֔ה שִׁבְעָ֥ה פָרִ֖ים וְשִׁבְעָ֥ה אֵילִֽם׃
pairs.english: and prepare for me here seven bullocks and seven rams.
And Balak did as Bilam said,
and he offered up a bullock and a ram upon (each) altar.

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּ֣רְא בִּלְעָ֗ם כִּ֣י ט֞וֹב בְּעֵינֵ֤י יְהֹוָה֙ לְבָרֵ֣ךְ אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל
pairs.english: And Bilam saw that it was good in the eyes of the L-rd to bless Israel,

pairs.hebrew: וְלֹא־הָלַ֥ךְ כְּפַֽעַם־בְּפַ֖עַם לִקְרַ֣את נְחָשִׁ֑ים וַיָּ֥שֶׁת אֶל־הַמִּדְבָּ֖ר פָּנָֽיו׃
pairs.english: and he did not go, as [he had gone] twice before to diviners [to divine whether the L-rd would "chance upon" him as he wished; but he said to himself: Whether or not He wishes to curse them, I shall mention their sins and the curse will perforce alight upon them], and he set his face to the desert [to the sin of the golden calf that Israel had made there].

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּשָּׂ֨א בִלְעָ֜ם אֶת־עֵינָ֗יו וַיַּרְא֙ אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל שֹׁכֵ֖ן לִשְׁבָטָ֑יו
pairs.english: And Bilam lifted his eyes [seeking to cast the "evil eye" upon them], and he saw Israel dwelling according to its tribes, [each tribe by itself, and the doors of their tents non-aligned, so that none look into his neighbor's tent],
and the spirit of G-d reposed upon him. [It entered his heart not to curse them.]
And he took up his parable and he said:

pairs.hebrew: נְאֻ֤ם בִּלְעָם֙ בְּנ֣וֹ בְעֹ֔ר וּנְאֻ֥ם הַגֶּ֖בֶר שְׁתֻ֥ם הָעָֽיִן׃
pairs.english: The speech of Bilam the son of Beor and the speech of the man of the gouged-out eye.
The speech of the hearer of the words of the Almighty,

pairs.hebrew: אֲשֶׁ֨ר מַחֲזֵ֤ה שַׁדַּי֙ יֶֽחֱזֶ֔ה נֹפֵ֖ל וּגְל֥וּי עֵינָֽיִם׃
pairs.english: who sees the vision of the Almighty, fallen [on his bed at night] and his eyes uncovered [(Bilam being granted prophecy only at night)]:
How goodly are your tents, O Jacob, [the tent-entrances not being aligned with one another],
your dwelling places [i.e., your encampments], O Israel!
As brooks which stretch out [into the distance], as gardens by the river,
as the aloes planted by the L-rd [in the garden of Eden], as cedar trees by the waters.
Water shall flow from his springs [i.e., the king issuing from his sons shall flourish], and his seed in many waters [i.e., his seed will prosper],
and his [first] king (Saul) will be exalted above [i.e., he will vanquish] Agag [the king of Amalek], and his [Jacob's] kingdom will rise [ever higher, (David and Solomon following Saul)].

pairs.hebrew: אֵ֚ל מוֹצִיא֣וֹ מִמִּצְרַ֔יִם כְּתוֹעֲפֹ֥ת רְאֵ֖ם ל֑וֹ
pairs.english: [Who accorded this greatness to them?] The Almighty who brought them forth from Egypt [with His strength and grandeur]. The flight of the heights is His.

pairs.hebrew: יֹאכַ֞ל גּוֹיִ֣ם צָרָ֗יו וְעַצְמֹתֵיהֶ֛ם יְגָרֵ֖ם וְחִצָּ֥יו יִמְחָֽץ׃
pairs.english: He shall devour the nations, his oppressors, and their bones shall he strip clean, and he shall dye His arrows [in their blood.]

pairs.hebrew: כָּרַ֨ע שָׁכַ֧ב כַּאֲרִ֛י וּכְלָבִ֖יא מִ֣י יְקִימֶ֑נּוּ
pairs.english: He shall crouch and lie down as a lion [i.e., They will settle their land in strength and might], and as a lioness — Who shall make him rise?
Those who bless you will be blessed, and those who curse you will be cursed.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּֽחַר־אַ֤ף בָּלָק֙ אֶל־בִּלְעָ֔ם וַיִּסְפֹּ֖ק אֶת־כַּפָּ֑יו וַיֹּ֨אמֶר בָּלָ֜ק אֶל־בִּלְעָ֗ם לָקֹ֤ב אֹֽיְבַי֙ קְרָאתִ֔יךָ
pairs.english: And Balak's anger burned against Bilam and he smote his hands together and Balak said to Bilam: To curse my foes did I call you,

pairs.hebrew: וְהִנֵּה֙ בֵּרַ֣כְתָּ בָרֵ֔ךְ זֶ֖ה שָׁלֹ֥שׁ פְּעָמִֽים׃
pairs.english: and here you have blessed them this three times!
And now, flee to your place.

pairs.hebrew: אָמַ֙רְתִּי֙ כַּבֵּ֣ד אֲכַבֶּדְךָ֔ וְהִנֵּ֛ה מְנָעֲךָ֥ יְהֹוָ֖ה מִכָּבֽוֹד׃
pairs.english: I said that I would honor you, but the L-rd has withheld you from honor.
And Bilam said to Balak:

pairs.hebrew: הֲלֹ֗א גַּ֧ם אֶל־מַלְאָכֶ֛יךָ אֲשֶׁר־שָׁלַ֥חְתָּ אֵלַ֖י דִּבַּ֥רְתִּי לֵאמֹֽר׃
pairs.english: Did I not also speak to your messengers that you sent to me, saying:

pairs.hebrew: אִם־יִתֶּן־לִ֨י בָלָ֜ק מְלֹ֣א בֵיתוֹ֮ כֶּ֣סֶף וְזָהָב֒
pairs.english: If Balak gives me his house full of silver and gold,

pairs.hebrew: לֹ֣א אוּכַ֗ל לַעֲבֹר֙ אֶת־פִּ֣י יְהֹוָ֔ה לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת טוֹבָ֛ה א֥וֹ רָעָ֖ה מִלִּבִּ֑י
pairs.english: I will not be able to countermand the word of the L-rd [(Here he omits "my G-d," as opposed to 22:18, knowing that he has been rejected and "cast out" by Him)] to do good or evil as I wish?
What the L-rd speaks, that will I speak.
And now, behold, I go to my people, [to be as one of them (the L-rd having left him)].

pairs.hebrew: לְכָה֙ אִיעָ֣צְךָ֔ אֲשֶׁ֨ר יַעֲשֶׂ֜ה הָעָ֥ם הַזֶּ֛ה לְעַמְּךָ֖ בְּאַחֲרִ֥ית הַיָּמִֽים׃
pairs.english: Come, I will counsel you [what to do to them — to undo them by harlotry (see 31:16). And I shall reveal to you] what this people will do to your people in the end of days [viz., 17].
And he took up his parable and he said:

pairs.hebrew: נְאֻ֤ם בִּלְעָם֙ בְּנ֣וֹ בְעֹ֔ר וּנְאֻ֥ם הַגֶּ֖בֶר שְׁתֻ֥ם הָעָֽיִן׃
pairs.english: The speech of Bilam the son of Beor and the speech of the man of the gouged-out eye.

pairs.hebrew: נְאֻ֗ם שֹׁמֵ֙עַ֙ אִמְרֵי־אֵ֔ל וְיֹדֵ֖עַ דַּ֣עַת עֶלְי֑וֹן
pairs.english: The speech of the hearer of the words of the Almighty, and the knower of the knowledge of the Most High [(in that he can determine the time of His anger)].

pairs.hebrew: מַחֲזֵ֤ה שַׁדַּי֙ יֶֽחֱזֶ֔ה נֹפֵ֖ל וּגְל֥וּי עֵינָֽיִם׃
pairs.english: He sees the vision of the Almighty, fallen and his eyes uncovered [see 4].

pairs.hebrew: אֶרְאֶ֙נּוּ֙ וְלֹ֣א עַתָּ֔ה אֲשׁוּרֶ֖נּוּ וְלֹ֣א קָר֑וֹב
pairs.english: I see it [the greatness of Jacob], but [it is] not now [but after a time]; I behold it, but [it is] not near.

pairs.hebrew: דָּרַ֨ךְ כּוֹכָ֜ב מִֽיַּעֲקֹ֗ב וְקָ֥ם שֵׁ֙בֶט֙ מִיִּשְׂרָאֵ֔ל
pairs.english: A star [i.e., a king] will arise from Jacob, and a sceptre [i.e., a ruling king] will arise from Israel,
and he [David] shall smite the edges of Moav [See II Samuel 8:2] and he shall dig through all the sons of Sheth [i.e., the nations].

pairs.hebrew: וְהָיָ֨ה אֱד֜וֹם יְרֵשָׁ֗ה וְהָיָ֧ה יְרֵשָׁ֛ה שֵׂעִ֖יר אֹיְבָ֑יו
pairs.english: And Edom will be a possession [to Israel], and Seir will be a possession [to Israel] his enemies,
and Israel will do valiantly.
And there will be [yet another] ruler [the Messiah] from Jacob,
and he will destroy the remnant [of Edom] from [its capital] city [Rome].

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּרְא֙ אֶת־עֲמָלֵ֔ק וַיִּשָּׂ֥א מְשָׁל֖וֹ וַיֹּאמַ֑ר רֵאשִׁ֤ית גּוֹיִם֙ עֲמָלֵ֔ק
pairs.english: And he saw [the retribution of] Amalek, and he took up his parable and he said: The first of nations [to war against Israel] was Amalek,
and his end is to perish everlastingly [through them].

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּרְא֙ אֶת־הַקֵּינִ֔י וַיִּשָּׂ֥א מְשָׁל֖וֹ וַיֹּאמַ֑ר אֵיתָן֙ מֽוֹשָׁבֶ֔ךָ
pairs.english: And he saw the Keini [(the grandeur of the descendants of Yithro. See I Chronicles 2:55.) Having just spoken of Amalek, he now speaks of the Keini, who were situated in their midst (I Samuel 15:6)], and he took up his parable and he said: [I wonder how you have attained to this. Were you (Yithro) not together with me in the counsel against Israel? (Exodus 1:10), and now] your dwelling place is firm [within the stronghold of Israel]
and you have set your nest in the rock!

[Fortunate are you in having joined yourself to this strength, for you will thus never be driven from the world]; for though Kayin (i.e., the Keini) be destined to be removed [into exile together with the ten tribes, what of it?]
How far will Ashur carry you into captivity? [To Chalach or to Chavor? This is not extinction but removal, and you will return with the other exiles.]
And he took up his parable and he said: [(Having mentioned Ashur's conquest, he now says)]
Woe, who shall live [i.e., Who shall escape] from the Placer of these [decreeing the same things against him!]

pairs.hebrew: וְצִים֙ מִיַּ֣ד כִּתִּ֔ים וְעִנּ֥וּ אַשּׁ֖וּר וְעִנּוּ־עֵ֑בֶר
pairs.english: [For Sancherev (Ashur) will arise and confound the nations,] and, [thereafter,] great ships shall come from Kittim and they [the Romans] shall afflict Ashur, and they will afflict [those] beyond [the Euphrates],
but he, too, [i.e., the Romans] shall perish everlastingly [See Daniel 7:11].
And Bilam arose and went and returned to his place,
and Balak, too, went on his way.
And Israel dwelt in Shittim,
and the people began to stray after the daughters of Moav [(a result of Bilam's counsel)].
And they [the Moavite women] called the people to the sacrifices of their gods,
and the people ate, and they bowed down to their gods [(the Moavite women making this a condition for their consenting)].
And Israel joined itself to Ba'al Peor (the idolatry of Moav) [so called because they exposed (pa'aru) themselves and defecated before it (this being its mode of worship)],
and the L-rd was wroth with Israel. [He sent a plague against them.]

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהֹוָ֜ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֗ה קַ֚ח אֶת־כׇּל־רָאשֵׁ֣י הָעָ֔ם וְהוֹקַ֥ע אוֹתָ֛ם לַיהֹוָ֖ה נֶ֣גֶד הַשָּׁ֑מֶשׁ
pairs.english: And the L-rd said to Moses: Take all the heads of the people [to judge the worshippers of Peor] and hang them [the worshippers] up to the L-rd [after stoning them (all who are executed by stoning being hanged thereafter)] in the face of the sun [i.e., before all]
so that the wrath of the L-rd turn away from Israel.
And Moses said to the judges [88,000] of Israel:

pairs.hebrew: הִרְגוּ֙ אִ֣ישׁ אֲנָשָׁ֔יו הַנִּצְמָדִ֖ים לְבַ֥עַל פְּעֽוֹר׃
pairs.english: Slay each (of you) his [two] men that have joined themselves to Ba'al Peor.

pairs.hebrew: וְהִנֵּ֡ה אִישׁ֩ מִבְּנֵ֨י יִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל בָּ֗א וַיַּקְרֵ֤ב אֶל־אֶחָיו֙ אֶת־הַמִּדְיָנִ֔ית לְעֵינֵ֣י מֹשֶׁ֔ה וּלְעֵינֵ֖י כׇּל־עֲדַ֣ת בְּנֵי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל
pairs.english: And, behold, a man of the children of Israel [Zimri, chief of the tribe of Shimon] came, and he brought near to his brothers the Midianite woman [Kazbi, the daughter of Tzur] in the sight of Moses and in the sight of the entire congregation of the children of Israel,

and they wept at the door of the tent of meeting [(at Moses' seeming impotence to stand up against one man whereas in the incident of the golden calf he had stood up against six hundred thousand! (For a full account of what transpired here see Sanhedrin 82a)]
And Pinchas, the son of Elazar, the son of Aaron the Cohein, saw [the act, and he remembered the halachah (that zealots may kill one they see cohabiting with an Aramite woman)],

pairs.hebrew: וַיָּ֙קׇם֙ מִתּ֣וֹךְ הָֽעֵדָ֔ה וַיִּקַּ֥ח רֹ֖מַח בְּיָדֽוֹ׃
pairs.english: and he arose from the midst of the congregation and he took a spear in his hand.

pairs.hebrew: וַ֠יָּבֹ֠א אַחַ֨ר אִֽישׁ־יִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל אֶל־הַקֻּבָּ֗ה וַיִּדְקֹר֙ אֶת־שְׁנֵיהֶ֔ם אֵ֚ת אִ֣ישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְאֶת־הָאִשָּׁ֖ה אֶל־קֳבָתָ֑הּ
pairs.english: And he came after the man of Israel to the tent and he thrust both of them through, the man of Israel [precisely through his genitals] and the woman [precisely] through her genitals [so that all see that he had not slain them for nought],
and the plague was stayed from the children of Israel.
And the dead in the plague
were twenty-four thousand.
And the L-rd spoke to Moses,
saying:

pairs.hebrew: פִּֽינְחָ֨ס בֶּן־אֶלְעָזָ֜ר בֶּן־אַהֲרֹ֣ן הַכֹּהֵ֗ן הֵשִׁ֤יב אֶת־חֲמָתִי֙ מֵעַ֣ל בְּנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל בְּקַנְא֥וֹ אֶת־קִנְאָתִ֖י בְּתוֹכָ֑ם
pairs.english: Pinchas, the son of Elazar, the son of Aaron the Cohein, [(Because the tribes denigrated Pinchas — "Did you see the son of this Puti (short for Putiel (Exodus 6:25), whose mother's father (Yithro) fattened (pitem) calves for idolatry, who killed the chief (Zimri) of a tribe of Israel!" — Scripture took pains to trace his genealogy to Aaron)], (Pinchas) turned My wrath away from the children of Israel when he raged My rage [i.e., when he executed vengeance on My behalf] in their midst,
and I did not consume the children of Israel in My wrath.
Therefore, say:
Behold, I give to him My covenant [to be unto him a covenant of] peace.

pairs.hebrew: וְהָ֤יְתָה לּוֹ֙ וּלְזַרְע֣וֹ אַחֲרָ֔יו בְּרִ֖ית כְּהֻנַּ֣ת עוֹלָ֑ם
pairs.english: And it shall be unto him and to his seed after him a covenant of eternal priesthood [(Prior to this, the priesthood had been given only to Aaron and his sons who were anointed with him and to their sons born thereafter, but Pinchas had been born before)] —

pairs.hebrew: תַּ֗חַת אֲשֶׁ֤ר קִנֵּא֙ לֵֽאלֹהָ֔יו וַיְכַפֵּ֖ר עַל־בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
pairs.english: because he was wroth for his G-d and he atoned for the children of Israel.

pairs.hebrew: וְשֵׁם֩ אִ֨ישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל הַמֻּכֶּ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֤ר הֻכָּה֙ אֶת־הַמִּדְיָנִ֔ית זִמְרִ֖י בֶּן־סָל֑וּא
pairs.english: And the name of the man of Israel who was smitten, who was smitten together with the Midianite woman, was Zimri the son of Salu [(As the righteous one is cited for commendation, the wicked one is cited for condemnation)],
chief of a father's house [one of the five] in the house of Shimon.

pairs.hebrew: וְשֵׁ֨ם הָֽאִשָּׁ֧ה הַמֻּכָּ֛ה הַמִּדְיָנִ֖ית כׇּזְבִּ֣י בַת־צ֑וּר
pairs.english: And the name of the woman who was smitten, the Midianitess, was Kazbi the daughter of Tzur;

head of the peoples [chief of the five kings of Midian], of a father's house [one of the five] in Midian was he [ — in spite of which, the Midianites, in their fierce hatred of Israel, consigned her to harlotry].
And the L-rd spoke to Moses,
saying:
Afflict the Midianites
and smite them.

pairs.hebrew: כִּ֣י צֹרְרִ֥ים הֵם֙ לָכֶ֔ם בְּנִכְלֵיהֶ֛ם אֲשֶׁר־נִכְּל֥וּ לָכֶ֖ם עַל־דְּבַר־פְּע֑וֹר
pairs.english: For they afflict you with their schemes which they have schemed against you in the cause of Peor, [consigning their daughters to harlotry to turn you to Peor worship],

pairs.hebrew: וְעַל־דְּבַ֞ר כׇּזְבִּ֨י בַת־נְשִׂ֤יא מִדְיָן֙ אֲחֹתָ֔ם הַמֻּכָּ֥ה בְיוֹם־הַמַּגֵּפָ֖ה עַל־דְּבַר־פְּעֽוֹר׃
pairs.english: and in the cause of Kazbi, the daughter of a prince of Midian, their sister, who was smitten in the day of the plague in the cause of Peor.
And it was, after the plague, ["the Shepherd counting his surviving sheep after the wolf raid"],

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהֹוָה֙ אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֔ה וְאֶ֧ל אֶלְעָזָ֛ר בֶּן־אַהֲרֹ֥ן הַכֹּהֵ֖ן לֵאמֹֽר׃
pairs.english: that the L-rd said to Moses and to Elazar the son of Aaron the Cohein, saying:

pairs.hebrew: שְׂא֞וּ אֶת־רֹ֣אשׁ ׀ כׇּל־עֲדַ֣ת בְּנֵי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל מִבֶּ֨ן עֶשְׂרִ֥ים שָׁנָ֛ה וָמַ֖עְלָה לְבֵ֣ית אֲבֹתָ֑ם
pairs.english: Take the count of the entire congregation of the children of Israel from twenty years and above by their fathers' house [(the tribes being reckoned according to the fathers and not according to the mothers)],
all who go to war in Israel.
And Moses and Elazar the Cohein spoke with them [of G-d's having commanded to count them],
in the plains of Moav by the Jordan (near) Jericho, saying:
[You must be counted] from twenty years and above,

pairs.hebrew: כַּאֲשֶׁר֩ צִוָּ֨ה יְהֹוָ֤ה אֶת־מֹשֶׁה֙ וּבְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל הַיֹּצְאִ֖ים מֵאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃
pairs.english: as the L-rd commanded Moses and the children of Israel who went out of the land of Egypt [to be counted thus (Exodus 30:14)].

pairs.hebrew: רְאוּבֵ֖ן בְּכ֣וֹר יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל בְּנֵ֣י רְאוּבֵ֗ן חֲנוֹךְ֙ מִשְׁפַּ֣חַת הַחֲנֹכִ֔י
pairs.english: Reuven, the first-born of Israel, the sons of Reuven: Chanoch, the family of the Chanochi (hachanochi) [All of the family names are similarly structured (with the heh and the yod), intimating (Psalms 122:4): "The tribes of Kah ('the L-rd') testimony to Israel" — G-d Himself testifying to the (tribal) paternity of Israel (in rebuttal to those who would cast doubt upon it in view of their having been enslaved by the Egyptians)];
Falu, the family of the Palui,
Chetzron, the family of the Chetzroni;
Karmi, the family of the Karmi.
These are the families of the Reuveni.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּהְי֣וּ פְקֻדֵיהֶ֗ם שְׁלֹשָׁ֤ה וְאַרְבָּעִים֙ אֶ֔לֶף וּשְׁבַ֥ע מֵא֖וֹת וּשְׁלֹשִֽׁים׃
pairs.english: And their number was forty-three thousand and seven hundred and thirty.
And the sons of Falu,
Eliav.
And the sons of Eliav: Nemuel and Dathan and Aviram.

pairs.hebrew: הֽוּא־דָתָ֨ן וַאֲבִירָ֜ם (קרואי) [קְרִיאֵ֣י] הָעֵדָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר הִצּ֜וּ עַל־מֹשֶׁ֤ה וְעַֽל־אַהֲרֹן֙ בַּעֲדַת־קֹ֔רַח בְּהַצֹּתָ֖ם עַל־יְהֹוָֽה׃
pairs.english: This is the Dathan and Aviram, the "called" of the congregation [see 1:16], who incited [Israel] against Moses and Aaron in the congregation of Korach when they incited [Israel] against the L-rd.

pairs.hebrew: וַתִּפְתַּ֨ח הָאָ֜רֶץ אֶת־פִּ֗יהָ וַתִּבְלַ֥ע אֹתָ֛ם וְאֶת־קֹ֖רַח בְּמ֣וֹת הָעֵדָ֑ה בַּאֲכֹ֣ל הָאֵ֗שׁ אֵ֣ת חֲמִשִּׁ֤ים וּמָאתַ֙יִם֙ אִ֔ישׁ
pairs.english: And the earth opened its mouth and it swallowed them and Korach in the death of the congregation (of Korach) when the fire consumed the two hundred and fifty men,
and they became a sign [for G-d's having established the priesthood (with Aaron and his sons)].
And the sons of Korach
did not die [(Though in the plot at the outset, they repented in their hearts, so that a high place was bastioned for them in Gehinnom, where they abided.)]

pairs.hebrew: בְּנֵ֣י שִׁמְעוֹן֮ לְמִשְׁפְּחֹתָם֒ לִנְמוּאֵ֗ל מִשְׁפַּ֙חַת֙ הַנְּמ֣וּאֵלִ֔י
pairs.english: The sons of Shimon, according to their families: Nemuel, the family of the Nemueli;

pairs.hebrew: לְיָמִ֕ין מִשְׁפַּ֖חַת הַיָּמִינִ֑י לְיָכִ֕ין מִשְׁפַּ֖חַת הַיָּכִינִֽי׃
pairs.english: Yamin, the family of the Yamini; Yachin, the family of the Yachini.
Zerach [the same as Tzochar (Exodus 6:14)], the family of the Zarchi;
Shaul, the family of the Shauli.
These are the families of the Shimoni,
twenty-two thousand and two hundred.

pairs.hebrew: בְּנֵ֣י גָד֮ לְמִשְׁפְּחֹתָם֒ לִצְפ֗וֹן מִשְׁפַּ֙חַת֙ הַצְּפוֹנִ֔י
pairs.english: The sons of Gad, according to their families: Tzefon, the family of the Tzefoni;

pairs.hebrew: לְחַגִּ֕י מִשְׁפַּ֖חַת הַֽחַגִּ֑י לְשׁוּנִ֕י מִשְׁפַּ֖חַת הַשּׁוּנִֽי׃
pairs.english: Chaggi, the family of the Chaggi; Shuni, the family of the Shuni.
Azni [the same as the family of Etzbon (Genesis 46:16)], the family of the Azni;
Eiri, the family of the Eiri.
Arod, the family of the Arodi;
Arieli, the family of the Arieli.
These are the families of the sons of Gad by their numbers,
forty thousand and five hundred.
The sons of Yehudah, Er and Onan.
And Er and Onan died in the land of Canaan.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּהְי֣וּ בְנֵי־יְהוּדָה֮ לְמִשְׁפְּחֹתָם֒ לְשֵׁלָ֗ה מִשְׁפַּ֙חַת֙ הַשֵּׁ֣לָנִ֔י
pairs.english: And the sons of Yehudah were, according to their families: Shelah, the family of the Shelani;

pairs.hebrew: לְפֶ֕רֶץ מִשְׁפַּ֖חַת הַפַּרְצִ֑י לְזֶ֕רַח מִשְׁפַּ֖חַת הַזַּרְחִֽי׃
pairs.english: Peretz, the family of the Partzi; Zerach, the family of the Zarchi.
And the sons of Peretz were: Chetzron, the family of the Chetzroni;
Chamul, the family of the Chamuli.
These are the families of Yehudah by their numbers,
seventy-six thousand and five hundred.

pairs.hebrew: בְּנֵ֤י יִשָּׂשכָר֙ לְמִשְׁפְּחֹתָ֔ם תּוֹלָ֕ע מִשְׁפַּ֖חַת הַתּוֹלָעִ֑י
pairs.english: The sons of Yissachar, according to their families: Tola, the family of the Tolai;
Puvah, the family of the Puni.
Yashuv, the family of the Yashuvi [This is Yov, mentioned among those who went down to Egypt (Genesis 46:13), all the families being called by the names of those who went down to Egypt];
Shimron, the family of the Shimroni.
These are the families of Yissachar by their numbers,
sixty-four thousand and three hundred.

pairs.hebrew: בְּנֵ֣י זְבוּלֻן֮ לְמִשְׁפְּחֹתָם֒ לְסֶ֗רֶד מִשְׁפַּ֙חַת֙ הַסַּרְדִּ֔י
pairs.english: The sons of Zevulun, according to their families: Sered, the family of the Sardi;

pairs.hebrew: לְאֵל֕וֹן מִשְׁפַּ֖חַת הָאֵלֹנִ֑י לְיַ֨חְלְאֵ֔ל מִשְׁפַּ֖חַת הַיַּחְלְאֵלִֽי׃
pairs.english: Eilon, the family of the Eiloni; Yachle'el, the family of the Yachle'eli.
These are the families of the Zvuloni by their numbers,
sixty thousand and five hundred.
The sons of Joseph, according to their families:
Menasheh and Ephraim.

pairs.hebrew: בְּנֵ֣י מְנַשֶּׁ֗ה לְמָכִיר֙ מִשְׁפַּ֣חַת הַמָּכִירִ֔י וּמָכִ֖יר הוֹלִ֣יד אֶת־גִּלְעָ֑ד
pairs.english: The sons of Menasheh: Machir, the family of the Machiri, and Machir begot Gilad;
Gilad, the family of the Giladi [(this family being mentioned separately, being exceptionally large)].

pairs.hebrew: אֵ֚לֶּה בְּנֵ֣י גִלְעָ֔ד אִיעֶ֕זֶר מִשְׁפַּ֖חַת הָאִֽיעֶזְרִ֑י
pairs.english: These are the sons of Gilad: Iezer, the family of the Iezri;
Chelek, the family of the Chelki.
And Asriel, the family of the Asrieli;
and Shechem, the family of the Shichmi.
And Shmida, the family of the Shmidai;
and Chefer, the family of the Chefri.

pairs.hebrew: וּצְלׇפְחָ֣ד בֶּן־חֵ֗פֶר לֹא־הָ֥יוּ ל֛וֹ בָּנִ֖ים כִּ֣י אִם־בָּנ֑וֹת
pairs.english: And Tzelafchad the son of Chefer did not have sons but daughters.

pairs.hebrew: וְשֵׁם֙ בְּנ֣וֹת צְלׇפְחָ֔ד מַחְלָ֣ה וְנֹעָ֔ה חׇגְלָ֥ה מִלְכָּ֖ה וְתִרְצָֽה׃
pairs.english: And the names of the daughters of Tzelafchad: Machlah, Noah, Chaglah, Milkah, and Tirtzah.
These are the families of Menasheh
and their numbered ones, fifty-two thousand and seven hundred.

pairs.hebrew: אֵ֣לֶּה בְנֵי־אֶפְרַ֘יִם֮ לְמִשְׁפְּחֹתָם֒ לְשׁוּתֶ֗לַח מִשְׁפַּ֙חַת֙ הַשֻּׁ֣תַלְחִ֔י
pairs.english: These are the sons of Ephraim, according to their families: Shuthelach, the family of the Shuthalchi;

pairs.hebrew: לְבֶ֕כֶר מִשְׁפַּ֖חַת הַבַּכְרִ֑י לְתַ֕חַן מִשְׁפַּ֖חַת הַֽתַּחֲנִֽי׃
pairs.english: Becher, the family of the Bachri; Tachan, the family of the Tachani.
And these are the sons of Shuthalach:
Eran, the family of the Erani [The offspring of the other sons of Shuthelach were called by his name. Because the family of Eran was exceptionally large, they are called by his name.]

pairs.hebrew: אֵ֣לֶּה מִשְׁפְּחֹ֤ת בְּנֵי־אֶפְרַ֙יִם֙ לִפְקֻ֣דֵיהֶ֔ם שְׁנַ֧יִם וּשְׁלֹשִׁ֛ים אֶ֖לֶף וַחֲמֵ֣שׁ מֵא֑וֹת
pairs.english: These are the families of the sons of Ephraim by their numbers, thirty-two thousand and five hundred.
These are the sons of Joseph according to their families.

pairs.hebrew: בְּנֵ֣י בִנְיָמִן֮ לְמִשְׁפְּחֹתָם֒ לְבֶ֗לַע מִשְׁפַּ֙חַת֙ הַבַּלְעִ֔י
pairs.english: The sons of Binyamin, according to their families: Bela, the family of the Bal'i;

pairs.hebrew: לְאַשְׁבֵּ֕ל מִשְׁפַּ֖חַת הָֽאַשְׁבֵּלִ֑י לַאֲחִירָ֕ם מִשְׁפַּ֖חַת הָאֲחִירָמִֽי׃
pairs.english: Ashbel, the family of the Ashbeli; Achiram, the family of the Achirami [Achiram is the same as Echi (Genesis 46:21). Because he was named after Joseph, Binyamin's brother, he was called "Achi (my brother) ram" (high, i.e., greater than I)].
Shefufam, the family of the Shufami [the same as Mupim (Genesis 46:21), Joseph being downtrodden (shafuf) by the peoples],
Chufam, the family of the Chufami.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּהְי֥וּ בְנֵי־בֶ֖לַע אַ֣רְדְּ וְנַעֲמָ֑ן מִשְׁפַּ֙חַת֙ הָֽאַרְדִּ֔י
pairs.english: And the sons of Bela were Ard and Na'aman, the family of the Ardi;
Na'aman, the family of the Na'ami.
These are the sons of Binyamin according to their families;
and their numbered ones, forty-five thousand and six hundred.

pairs.hebrew: אֵ֤לֶּה בְנֵי־דָן֙ לְמִשְׁפְּחֹתָ֔ם לְשׁוּחָ֕ם מִשְׁפַּ֖חַת הַשּׁוּחָמִ֑י
pairs.english: These are the sons of Dan according to their families: Shucham, [the same as Chushim (Genesis 46:23)], the family of the Shuchami.
These are the families of Dan by their families.
All the families of the Shuchami by their numbered ones,
sixty-four thousand and four hundred.

pairs.hebrew: בְּנֵ֣י אָשֵׁר֮ לְמִשְׁפְּחֹתָם֒ לְיִמְנָ֗ה מִשְׁפַּ֙חַת֙ הַיִּמְנָ֔ה
pairs.english: The sons of Asher, according to their families: Yimnah, the family of the Yimnah;

pairs.hebrew: לְיִשְׁוִ֕י מִשְׁפַּ֖חַת הַיִּשְׁוִ֑י לִבְרִיעָ֕ה מִשְׁפַּ֖חַת הַבְּרִיעִֽי׃
pairs.english: Yishvi, the family of the Yishvi; Beriah, the family of the Beri'i.
The sons of Beriah: Chever, the family of the Chevri;
Malkiel, the family of the Malkieli.
And the name of the daughter of Asher
was Sarach [(Because she was still alive, she is mentioned here)].
These are the families of the sons of Asher by their numbered ones,
fifty-three thousand and four hundred.

pairs.hebrew: בְּנֵ֤י נַפְתָּלִי֙ לְמִשְׁפְּחֹתָ֔ם לְיַ֨חְצְאֵ֔ל מִשְׁפַּ֖חַת הַיַּחְצְאֵלִ֑י
pairs.english: The sons of Naftali, according to their families: Yachtze'el, the family of the Yachtze'eli;
Guni, the family of the Guni.
Yetzer, the family of the Yitzri;
Shilem, the family of the Shilemi.
These are the families of Naftali according to their families;

pairs.hebrew: וּפְקֻ֣דֵיהֶ֔ם חֲמִשָּׁ֧ה וְאַרְבָּעִ֛ים אֶ֖לֶף וְאַרְבַּ֥ע מֵאֽוֹת׃
pairs.english: and their numbered ones, forty-five thousand and four hundred.
These are the numbered ones of the children of Israel,

pairs.hebrew: שֵׁשׁ־מֵא֥וֹת אֶ֖לֶף וָאָ֑לֶף שְׁבַ֥ע מֵא֖וֹת וּשְׁלֹשִֽׁים׃ {פ}
pairs.english: six hundred and one thousand and seven hundred and thirty.
And the L-rd spoke to Moses,
saying:
To these shall the land be apportioned, [and not to those younger than twenty, even if they reached that age by the time of the division of the land], as an inheritance
according to the number of names.

pairs.hebrew: לָרַ֗ב תַּרְבֶּה֙ נַחֲלָת֔וֹ וְלַמְעַ֕ט תַּמְעִ֖יט נַחֲלָת֑וֹ
pairs.english: To the [more] numerous [tribe] you shall increase its inheritance [i.e., you shall give it a larger portion], and to the less [numerous] you shall decrease its inheritance.
To each, according to his numbers shall his inheritance be given.
Only [(excluding Joshua and Calev, who received special portions)] by lot shall the land be divided, [the lot actually calling out the correct division through the Holy Spirit.]

By the names of the tribes of their fathers [(proselytes and slaves hereby excluded), who came out of Egypt] shall they inherit [e.g., If two brothers who left Egypt had sons entering the land — the first, one son; the second, three — (the one son takes one portion; the three, three (as per verse 53), after which their portions revert to their fathers' father (as per verse 55), so that they (the two fathers) divide (four portions) equally.]
By the word of the lot [("word," literally, see above)] shall its inheritance be divided
between the many and the few.

pairs.hebrew: וְאֵ֨לֶּה פְקוּדֵ֣י הַלֵּוִי֮ לְמִשְׁפְּחֹתָם֒ לְגֵרְשׁ֗וֹן מִשְׁפַּ֙חַת֙ הַגֵּ֣רְשֻׁנִּ֔י
pairs.english: And these are the numbered of the Levites, according to their families: Gershon, the family of the Gershuni;

pairs.hebrew: לִקְהָ֕ת מִשְׁפַּ֖חַת הַקְּהָתִ֑י לִמְרָרִ֕י מִשְׁפַּ֖חַת הַמְּרָרִֽי׃
pairs.english: Kehath, the family of the Kehathi; Merari, the family of the Merari.

pairs.hebrew: אֵ֣לֶּה ׀ מִשְׁפְּחֹ֣ת לֵוִ֗י מִשְׁפַּ֨חַת הַלִּבְנִ֜י מִשְׁפַּ֤חַת הַֽחֶבְרֹנִי֙ מִשְׁפַּ֤חַת הַמַּחְלִי֙ מִשְׁפַּ֣חַת הַמּוּשִׁ֔י מִשְׁפַּ֖חַת הַקׇּרְחִ֑י
pairs.english: These are the families of Levi [see Exodus 16-19]: the family of the Livni, the family of the Chevroni, the family of the Machli, the family of the Mushi, the family of the Karchi;
and Kehath begot Amram.

pairs.hebrew: וְשֵׁ֣ם ׀ אֵ֣שֶׁת עַמְרָ֗ם יוֹכֶ֙בֶד֙ בַּת־לֵוִ֔י אֲשֶׁ֨ר יָלְדָ֥ה אֹתָ֛הּ לְלֵוִ֖י בְּמִצְרָ֑יִם
pairs.english: And the name of the wife of Amram was Yocheved the daughter of Levi, who (i.e., whose wife) bore her to Levi in Egypt, [just as they entered Egypt (so that she makes up the complement of the "seventy souls" who entered Egypt (Genesis 46:27)].

pairs.hebrew: וַתֵּ֣לֶד לְעַמְרָ֗ם אֶֽת־אַהֲרֹן֙ וְאֶת־מֹשֶׁ֔ה וְאֵ֖ת מִרְיָ֥ם אֲחֹתָֽם׃
pairs.english: And she bore to Amram: Aaron and Moses, and Miriam, their sister.
And there was born to Aaron: Nadav and Avihu,
Elazar and Ithamar.
And Nadav and Avihu died
when they offered strange fire before the L-rd.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּהְי֣וּ פְקֻדֵיהֶ֗ם שְׁלֹשָׁ֤ה וְעֶשְׂרִים֙ אֶ֔לֶף כׇּל־זָכָ֖ר מִבֶּן־חֹ֣דֶשׁ וָמָ֑עְלָה
pairs.english: And their (the Levites') numbered ones were twenty-three thousand, every male from one month and above.

pairs.hebrew: כִּ֣י ׀ לֹ֣א הׇתְפָּקְד֗וּ בְּתוֹךְ֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל כִּ֠י לֹא־נִתַּ֤ן לָהֶם֙ נַחֲלָ֔ה בְּת֖וֹךְ בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
pairs.english: For they were not numbered in the midst of the children of Israel [from the age of twenty]; for an inheritance was not given them [as it was to all those over twenty] in the midst of the children of Israel.

pairs.hebrew: אֵ֚לֶּה פְּקוּדֵ֣י מֹשֶׁ֔ה וְאֶלְעָזָ֖ר הַכֹּהֵ֑ן אֲשֶׁ֨ר פָּֽקְד֜וּ אֶת־בְּנֵ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙
pairs.english: These are the numbered ones of Moses and Elazar the Cohein, who numbered the children of Israel
in the plains of Moav by the Jordan (near) Jericho.

pairs.hebrew: וּבְאֵ֙לֶּה֙ לֹא־הָ֣יָה אִ֔ישׁ מִפְּקוּדֵ֣י מֹשֶׁ֔ה וְאַהֲרֹ֖ן הַכֹּהֵ֑ן
pairs.english: And among these there was not a man of those that had been counted by Moses and Aaron the Cohein,

pairs.hebrew: אֲשֶׁ֥ר פָּקְד֛וּ אֶת־בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בְּמִדְבַּ֥ר סִינָֽי׃
pairs.english: who had counted the children of Israel in the desert of Sinai. [(But the decree of the spies had not gone forth against the women, who, unlike the men, who wished to return to Egypt, desired a holding in the land (for which reason the episode of the daughters of Tzelafchad follows)].

pairs.hebrew: כִּֽי־אָמַ֤ר יְהֹוָה֙ לָהֶ֔ם מ֥וֹת יָמֻ֖תוּ בַּמִּדְבָּ֑ר
pairs.english: For the L-rd had said to them: They will surely die in the desert.

pairs.hebrew: וְלֹא־נוֹתַ֤ר מֵהֶם֙ אִ֔ישׁ כִּ֚י אִם־כָּלֵ֣ב בֶּן־יְפֻנֶּ֔ה וִיהוֹשֻׁ֖עַ בִּן־נֽוּן׃ {ס}
pairs.english: And there was left not a man of them except Calev the son of Yefuneh and Joshua the son of Nun.

pairs.hebrew: וַתִּקְרַ֜בְנָה בְּנ֣וֹת צְלׇפְחָ֗ד בֶּן־חֵ֤פֶר בֶּן־גִּלְעָד֙ בֶּן־מָכִ֣יר בֶּן־מְנַשֶּׁ֔ה לְמִשְׁפְּחֹ֖ת מְנַשֶּׁ֣ה בֶן־יוֹסֵ֑ף
pairs.english: And there drew near the daughters of Tzelafchad, the son of Chefer, the son of Gilad, the son of Machir, the son of Menasheh, of the families of Menasheh the son of Joseph. [Just as Joseph held Eretz Yisrael dear (viz., Genesis 50:25), so did the daughters of Tzelafchad (viz., 4 following). And all of them were righteous (their pedigree being traced back to Joseph, the tzaddik)].

pairs.hebrew: וְאֵ֙לֶּה֙ שְׁמ֣וֹת בְּנֹתָ֔יו מַחְלָ֣ה נֹעָ֔ה וְחׇגְלָ֥ה וּמִלְכָּ֖ה וְתִרְצָֽה׃
pairs.english: And these are the names of his daughters: Machlah, Noah, Chaglah, Milkah, and Tirtzah.

pairs.hebrew: וַֽתַּעֲמֹ֜דְנָה לִפְנֵ֣י מֹשֶׁ֗ה וְלִפְנֵי֙ אֶלְעָזָ֣ר הַכֹּהֵ֔ן וְלִפְנֵ֥י הַנְּשִׂיאִ֖ם וְכׇל־הָעֵדָ֑ה
pairs.english: And they stood [in the house of study] before Moses and before Elazar the Cohein [(This occurred in the fortieth year, after Aaron had died)] and before the leaders and the entire congregation
at the door of the tent of meeting, saying:

pairs.hebrew: אָבִ֘ינוּ֮ מֵ֣ת בַּמִּדְבָּר֒ וְה֨וּא לֹא־הָיָ֜ה בְּת֣וֹךְ הָעֵדָ֗ה הַנּוֹעָדִ֛ים עַל־יְהֹוָ֖ה בַּעֲדַת־קֹ֑רַח
pairs.english: Our father died in the desert, and he was not in the midst of the congregation that gathered against the L-rd [i.e., the cavilers (Exodus 16:2), and not] in the congregation of Korach, [who incited to rebellion],
but he died in his own sin, [without inciting others to sin], and he left no sons.

pairs.hebrew: לָ֣מָּה יִגָּרַ֤ע שֵׁם־אָבִ֙ינוּ֙ מִתּ֣וֹךְ מִשְׁפַּחְתּ֔וֹ כִּ֛י אֵ֥ין ל֖וֹ בֵּ֑ן
pairs.english: Why should the name of our father be withheld from his family because he has no son? [We stand in place of a son. And if females are not considered seed, let our mother perform levirate marriage (yibum)! ("because he has no son":) If he had a son they would claim nothing (They were sage women)].
Give us a holding in the midst of the brothers of our father.
And Moses brought forth their judgment
before the L-rd. [The halachah evaded him — retribution for his "presumptuousness," viz. (Deuteronomy 1:17): "And the thing that is too difficult for you, you shall bring near to me."]
And the L-rd said to Moses,
saying:
Rightly do the daughters of Tzelafchad speak. [Thus is this section (of inheritance) written before Me on high.]

pairs.hebrew: נָתֹ֨ן תִּתֵּ֤ן לָהֶם֙ אֲחֻזַּ֣ת נַחֲלָ֔ה בְּת֖וֹךְ אֲחֵ֣י אֲבִיהֶ֑ם וְהַֽעֲבַרְתָּ֛ אֶת־נַחֲלַ֥ת אֲבִיהֶ֖ן לָהֶֽן׃
pairs.english: Given shall be given to them [(two portions — that of their father, who was among those who left Egypt, and that of his brothers in the property of Chefer (his father, who was also one of those who left Egypt)] the holding of an inheritance in the midst of the brothers of their father, and you shall pass over (veha'avarta) [(an expression of wrath (evrah), directed against one who does not leave over a son to inherit him)] the inheritance of their father to them.

pairs.hebrew: וְאֶל־בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל תְּדַבֵּ֣ר לֵאמֹ֑ר אִ֣ישׁ כִּֽי־יָמ֗וּת וּבֵן֙ אֵ֣ין ל֔וֹ
pairs.english: And to the children of Israel shall you speak, saying: A man, if he die and he have no son,
then you shall pass over his inheritance to his daughter.
And if he has no daughter,
then you shall give his inheritance to his brothers.
And if he has no brothers,
then you shall give his inheritance to the brothers of his father.

pairs.hebrew: וְאִם־אֵ֣ין אַחִים֮ לְאָבִיו֒ וּנְתַתֶּ֣ם אֶת־נַחֲלָת֗וֹ לִשְׁאֵר֞וֹ הַקָּרֹ֥ב אֵלָ֛יו מִמִּשְׁפַּחְתּ֖וֹ וְיָרַ֣שׁ אֹתָ֑הּ
pairs.english: And if his father has no brothers, then you shall give his inheritance to his flesh who is near to him of his family [("family" denotes his father's side)], and he shall inherit it,

pairs.hebrew: וְֽהָ֨יְתָ֜ה לִבְנֵ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ לְחֻקַּ֣ת מִשְׁפָּ֔ט כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר צִוָּ֥ה יְהֹוָ֖ה אֶת־מֹשֶֽׁה׃ {פ}
pairs.english: and it shall be to the children of Israel a statute of judgment as the L-rd commanded Moses.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהֹוָה֙ אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֔ה עֲלֵ֛ה אֶל־הַ֥ר הָעֲבָרִ֖ים הַזֶּ֑ה
pairs.english: And the L-rd said to Moses: Go up to this Mount Avarim

pairs.hebrew: וּרְאֵה֙ אֶת־הָאָ֔רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֥ר נָתַ֖תִּי לִבְנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
pairs.english: and see the land that I gave to the children of Israel. [(The rationale of the juxtaposition: When the L-rd told Moses to give the daughters of Tzelafchad an inheritance, he felt that the decree against his entering the land might have been rescinded — whereupon he was apprised otherwise.)]
And you shall see it and you, too, shall be gathered to your people,
as Aaron your brother was gathered [(whence it is seen that Moses aspired to a death like Aaron's)].

pairs.hebrew: כַּאֲשֶׁר֩ מְרִיתֶ֨ם פִּ֜י בְּמִדְבַּר־צִ֗ן בִּמְרִיבַת֙ הָֽעֵדָ֔ה לְהַקְדִּישֵׁ֥נִי בַמַּ֖יִם לְעֵינֵיהֶ֑ם
pairs.english: [This, your death, was decreed] when you flouted My command in the desert of Tzin, in the contention of the congregation, (My command) to sanctify Me with the waters before their eyes.
They [(the waters alone, and no egregious sin, were the cause of their death in the desert)], the waters of Merivath-Kadesh, in the desert of Tzin.
And Moses spoke to the L-rd [(When the righteous leave the world, they put aside their own needs in favor of communal needs)]
to say [i.e., to tell him whether or not He would appoint a leader for them.)]

[When Moses was told to give Tzelafchad's inheritance to his daughters, he felt that the time was ripe to ask that his sons inherit his greatness — whereupon he said:] Let the L-rd, the G-d of the spirits of all flesh appoint
a man over the congregation [(You know that the minds of all men are different. Appoint for them a leader who can tolerate all of these minds)]

pairs.hebrew: אֲשֶׁר־יֵצֵ֣א לִפְנֵיהֶ֗ם וַאֲשֶׁ֤ר יָבֹא֙ לִפְנֵיהֶ֔ם וַאֲשֶׁ֥ר יוֹצִיאֵ֖ם וַאֲשֶׁ֣ר יְבִיאֵ֑ם
pairs.english: who will go out before them (to war) [(Not like the kings of the nations, who sit at home and send their armies to war, but like me (and like Joshua and David), who fought in the vanguard)], and who will come in before them [at their head], and who will take them out [in his merits], and who will bring them back [in his merits].

pairs.hebrew: וְלֹ֤א תִהְיֶה֙ עֲדַ֣ת יְהֹוָ֔ה כַּצֹּ֕אן אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֵין־לָהֶ֖ם רֹעֶֽה׃
pairs.english: And let the congregation of the L-rd not be as sheep without a shepherd.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהֹוָ֜ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֗ה קַח־לְךָ֙ אֶת־יְהוֹשֻׁ֣עַ בִּן־נ֔וּן אִ֖ישׁ אֲשֶׁר־ר֣וּחַ בּ֑וֹ
pairs.english: And the L-rd said to Moses: [Not as you think, but] take for yourself Joshua the son of Nun [(because "he never departed from the tent" (Exodus 33:11) — "The keeper of the fig tree shall eat its fruit" (Proverbs 27:18)], a man who has spirit in him [(as per your request (16)],
and place your hand upon him [Give him an interpreter to expound (Torah) in your lifetime, so that people not say about him (after your death): "He would never dare do this in Moses' lifetime!"]

pairs.hebrew: וְהַֽעֲמַדְתָּ֣ אֹת֗וֹ לִפְנֵי֙ אֶלְעָזָ֣ר הַכֹּהֵ֔ן וְלִפְנֵ֖י כׇּל־הָעֵדָ֑ה
pairs.english: And stand him before Elazar the Cohein and before the entire congregation,
and charge him [over Israel] before their eyes. [Impress it upon him that he is accepting the charge with full knowledge of their bothersomeness and refractoriness.]
And you shall place [some] of your glory ["shining of countenance"] upon him,
so that all the congregation of the children of Israel pay heed [to honor and fear him, as they do you.]

pairs.hebrew: וְלִפְנֵ֨י אֶלְעָזָ֤ר הַכֹּהֵן֙ יַעֲמֹ֔ד וְשָׁ֥אַל ל֛וֹ בְּמִשְׁפַּ֥ט הָאוּרִ֖ים לִפְנֵ֣י יְהֹוָ֑ה
pairs.english: And before Elazar the Cohein shall he stand [(an accession to Moses' request that all his honor not depart from his father's house — Joshua, too, having need of Elazar)], and he (Joshua) shall inquire of him [when there is a need to go out to war] as to the judgment of the urim before the L-rd.

pairs.hebrew: עַל־פִּ֨יו יֵצְא֜וּ וְעַל־פִּ֣יו יָבֹ֗אוּ ה֛וּא וְכׇל־בְּנֵי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֥ל אִתּ֖וֹ וְכׇל־הָעֵדָֽה׃
pairs.english: By his [Elazar's] word shall they go out, and by his word shall they come in, he (Joshua) and all the children of Israel with him, and the entire congregation [the Sanhedrin].

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּ֣עַשׂ מֹשֶׁ֔ה כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר צִוָּ֥ה יְהֹוָ֖ה אֹת֑וֹ
pairs.english: And Moses did as the L-rd commanded him,

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּקַּ֣ח אֶת־יְהוֹשֻׁ֗עַ וַיַּֽעֲמִדֵ֙הוּ֙ לִפְנֵי֙ אֶלְעָזָ֣ר הַכֹּהֵ֔ן וְלִפְנֵ֖י כׇּל־הָעֵדָֽה׃
pairs.english: and he "took" Joshua [with words, apprising him of the reward of the leaders of Israel in the world to come], and he charged him before Elazar the Cohein and before the entire congregation.
And he placed his hands upon him [(being even more profuse in the conferring of his wisdom than he had been commanded, viz. (18) "Place your hand upon him")], and he charged him,
as the L-rd had spoken [(even in respect to the glory" (20) — he imparted of his glory to him)] by the hand of Moses.
And the L-rd spoke to Moses,
saying:
Command the children of Israel [(Before commanding Me for My children, viz. (16): "Let the L-rd appoint a man, etc.," command My children for Me!")], and say to them:

pairs.hebrew: אֶת־קׇרְבָּנִ֨י לַחְמִ֜י לְאִשַּׁ֗י רֵ֚יחַ נִֽיחֹחִ֔י תִּשְׁמְר֕וּ לְהַקְרִ֥יב לִ֖י בְּמוֹעֲדֽוֹ׃
pairs.english: My offering [the blood], My bread [the devoted portions (see Leviticus 3:16)], for My fires [i.e., which are placed on the fires of My altar], (for) My sweet savor shall you observe [(whence is derived the institution of ma'amadoth ("watches"), Cohanim, Levites, and Israelites standing over the sacrifices)] to offer to Me in its appointed time [(Every day is the "appointed time" of the temidim (the continual offerings)].

pairs.hebrew: וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ לָהֶ֔ם זֶ֚ה הָֽאִשֶּׁ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר תַּקְרִ֖יבוּ לַיהֹוָ֑ה
pairs.english: And you shall say to them [This is an exhortation to beth-din (to charge the people)]: This is the fire-offering which you shall offer up to the L-rd:

pairs.hebrew: כְּבָשִׂ֨ים בְּנֵֽי־שָׁנָ֧ה תְמִימִ֛ם שְׁנַ֥יִם לַיּ֖וֹם עֹלָ֥ה תָמִֽיד׃
pairs.english: lambs of the first year, unblemished, two each day [(each to be slaughtered opposite the "day," i.e., the sun; the morning tamid in the west, and the evening tamid in the east)], a perpetual burnt-offering.
The one lamb shall you offer in the morning,

pairs.hebrew: וְאֵת֙ הַכֶּ֣בֶשׂ הַשֵּׁנִ֔י תַּעֲשֶׂ֖ה בֵּ֥ין הָֽעַרְבָּֽיִם׃
pairs.english: and the other lamb shall you offer towards evening. [Even though this was already stated (Exodus 29:38), there it was an exhortation for the days of investiture (of the Cohanim), whereas here it is commanded for all time.]
And a tenth of an ephah of flour for the meal-offering [the libation meal-offering]
mixed with oil of crushing (see Exodus 29:40), a fourth of a hin.
A perpetual burnt-offering [like those] offered up [in the days of the investiture] at Mount Sinai,
as a sweet savor, a fire-offering to the L-rd.
And its [wine] libation, a fourth of a hin for the one lamb.
On the holy place [i.e., the altar] shall it be poured, a pouring of strong [intoxicating] drink [as opposed to wine straight from the press] to the L-rd.

pairs.hebrew: וְאֵת֙ הַכֶּ֣בֶשׂ הַשֵּׁנִ֔י תַּעֲשֶׂ֖ה בֵּ֣ין הָֽעַרְבָּ֑יִם
pairs.english: And the second lamb shall you offer up towards evening.

pairs.hebrew: כְּמִנְחַ֨ת הַבֹּ֤קֶר וּכְנִסְכּוֹ֙ תַּעֲשֶׂ֔ה אִשֵּׁ֛ה רֵ֥יחַ נִיחֹ֖חַ לַיהֹוָֽה׃ {פ}
pairs.english: As the meal-offering of the morning and its libation shall you offer it; a fire-offering, a sweet savor [i.e., gratifying] to the L-rd [in that His will was done].
And on the Sabbath day, two lambs of the first year without blemish

pairs.hebrew: וּשְׁנֵ֣י עֶשְׂרֹנִ֗ים סֹ֧לֶת מִנְחָ֛ה בְּלוּלָ֥ה בַשֶּׁ֖מֶן וְנִסְכּֽוֹ׃
pairs.english: and two tenth measures of flour for a meal-offering, mixed with oil and its libation.
The burnt-offering of the Sabbath in its Sabbath [(and not the burnt-offering of this Sabbath on another Sabbath ["The day being past, its offering is annulled")],
in addition to the daily burnt-offering and its libation. [(These are the mussafim, the "additional" offerings, which are to be offered between the two daily offerings.)]
And in the beginning of your months, you shall offer a burnt-offering to the L-rd:

pairs.hebrew: פָּרִ֨ים בְּנֵֽי־בָקָ֤ר שְׁנַ֙יִם֙ וְאַ֣יִל אֶחָ֔ד כְּבָשִׂ֧ים בְּנֵי־שָׁנָ֛ה שִׁבְעָ֖ה תְּמִימִֽם׃
pairs.english: two young bullocks, one ram, seven one-year-old lambs, unblemished.

pairs.hebrew: וּשְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה עֶשְׂרֹנִ֗ים סֹ֤לֶת מִנְחָה֙ בְּלוּלָ֣ה בַשֶּׁ֔מֶן לַפָּ֖ר הָאֶחָ֑ד
pairs.english: And three esronim of flour for a meal-offering, [as with the fixed libations for a bullock (15:9)], mixed with oil for the one bullock,

pairs.hebrew: וּשְׁנֵ֣י עֶשְׂרֹנִ֗ים סֹ֤לֶת מִנְחָה֙ בְּלוּלָ֣ה בַשֶּׁ֔מֶן לָאַ֖יִל הָֽאֶחָֽד׃
pairs.english: and two esronim of flour for a meal-offering, mixed with oil for the one ram.

pairs.hebrew: וְעִשָּׂרֹ֣ן עִשָּׂר֗וֹן סֹ֤לֶת מִנְחָה֙ בְּלוּלָ֣ה בַשֶּׁ֔מֶן לַכֶּ֖בֶשׂ הָאֶחָ֑ד
pairs.english: And issaron, issaron of flour for a meal-offering, mixed with oil, for the one lamb,
for a burnt-offering, a sweet savor, a fire-offering to the L-rd.

pairs.hebrew: וְנִסְכֵּיהֶ֗ם חֲצִ֣י הַהִין֩ יִהְיֶ֨ה לַפָּ֜ר וּשְׁלִישִׁ֧ת הַהִ֣ין לָאַ֗יִל וּרְבִיעִ֥ת הַהִ֛ין לַכֶּ֖בֶשׂ יָ֑יִן
pairs.english: And their libations: half a hin for the bullock, a third of a hin for the ram, a fourth of a hin for the lamb, wine.

pairs.hebrew: זֹ֣את עֹלַ֥ת חֹ֙דֶשׁ֙ בְּחׇדְשׁ֔וֹ לְחׇדְשֵׁ֖י הַשָּׁנָֽה׃
pairs.english: This is the burnt-offering of the month in its month [(If the day passes, the offering is annulled and there is no restitution)], for the months of the year.

And one kid of goats as a sin-offering to the L-rd [i.e., where only the L-rd knows of the sin — this, in atonement for defiling the sanctuary or its objects without awareness of having done so (this offering serving as the prototype for all of the additional goat offerings (mussafim) as effecting such atonement)];
in addition to the continual burnt-offering shall it [the complete offering (not just the kid)] be offered, with its [the offering's (not the kid's)] libation.

pairs.hebrew: וּבַחֹ֣דֶשׁ הָרִאשׁ֗וֹן בְּאַרְבָּעָ֥ה עָשָׂ֛ר י֖וֹם לַחֹ֑דֶשׁ
pairs.english: And in the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month,
it is Pesach to the L-rd.

pairs.hebrew: וּבַחֲמִשָּׁ֨ה עָשָׂ֥ר י֛וֹם לַחֹ֥דֶשׁ הַזֶּ֖ה חָ֑ג
pairs.english: And on the fifteenth day of this month, it is a festival;
for seven days matzoth shall be eaten.
On the first day it is a calling of holiness;
all work of labor you shall not do [(Even essential work, which cannot be made up, which is permitted on Chol Hamoed, is forbidden on Yom Tov)].

pairs.hebrew: וְהִקְרַבְתֶּ֨ם אִשֶּׁ֤ה עֹלָה֙ לַֽיהֹוָ֔ה פָּרִ֧ים בְּנֵי־בָקָ֛ר שְׁנַ֖יִם וְאַ֣יִל אֶחָ֑ד
